One of them, who was Dhu'l-Khuwayṣira (may Allah split his belly), said: "Be just, for you have not been just." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Woe to you! If I am not just, who will be just? You would deem me untrustworthy over the people of the earth, but you do not trust me?"

When the man turned away, Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to kill him. In another narration it was Khalid ibn al-Walid, and there is no contradiction in combining them. He said: "Leave him, for there will emerge from his lineage (i.e., from his kind) a people whose prayer you will consider insignificant compared to their prayer, and whose fasting you will consider insignificant compared to their fasting, and whose recitation you will consider insignificant compared to their recitation. They will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through the game. Wherever you meet them, kill them, for in killing them there is a reward for whoever kills them."

Then their emergence occurred in the days of Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he fought them at al-Nahrawan. Afterwards, many groups, tribes, opinions, desires, doctrines and sects branched off from them, spreading widely. Then the Qadariyya emerged, then the Mu'tazila, then the Jahmiyya, and other innovations, about which the truthful, believed one (ﷺ) gave information in his saying: "This Ummah will split into seventy-three sects, all of which are in the Fire except one." They said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Those who are upon what I am upon and my Companions." Al-Hakim reported it in his al-Mustadrak with this addition.[[Al-Mustadrak (1/28) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr. The addition is his saying: "All of them are in the Fire except one." Ibn al-Wazir declared it weak and attributed that to Ibn Hazm. Shaykh Nasir al-Din al-Albani has a study establishing the authenticity of this addition; refer to al-Silsila al-Sahiha, no. 204.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Musa narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, from his father, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Jundab ibn Abdullah, that it reached him from Hudhayfa, or he heard it from him, narrating from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he mentioned: "Indeed, in my Ummah there will be a people who recite the Qur'an, scattering it like the scattering of dried palm fronds, interpreting it in other than its proper interpretation."[[Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani mentioned it in al-Matalib al-ʿĀliya (3/300) and attributed it to Abu Ya'la, but he mentioned it from the hadith of Aisha.]]

Allah's statement: ﴿And none knows its interpretation except Allah﴾. The reciters have differed about where to pause here. It has been said that the pause is on the divine name (Allah), as was previously reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Tafsir (exegesis) is of four kinds: an exegesis no one is excused from understanding; an exegesis that the Arabs know from their languages; an exegesis that only the rasikhun fi al-ilm (those firmly rooted in knowledge) know; and an exegesis that none knows except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." This view is also reported from Aisha, Urwa, Abu al-Sha'tha, Abu Nuhayk, and others.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Hashim ibn Mirthad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'a narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "I fear for my Ummah only three things: that wealth will increase for them, so they will envy one another and fight; that the Book will be opened to them, so the believer will take it seeking its interpretation, ﴿and none knows its interpretation except Allah, and those firmly rooted in knowledge say, 'We believe in it; all is from our Lord; and none will be reminded except the people of understanding'﴾ (the verse); and that their knowledge will increase, so they will waste it and not care about it." Gharib jiddan (very strange).[[Al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (3/292). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/128): "It contains Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash from his father, and he did not hear from his father."]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Amr informed us, Hisham ibn Ammar informed us, Ibn Abi Hatim informed us, from his father, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from Ibn al-As, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed the Qur'an was not sent down so that some of it would contradict other parts of it. So what you know of it, act upon it, and what is ambiguous in it, believe in it."[[Ibn al-Daris in Fada'il al-Qur'an, and Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (4/1/197), and its chain is hasan (good).]]

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: "And none knows its interpretation except Allah, and the rasikhun say: We believe in it."[[ʿAbd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir, no. 377.]] Similarly, Ibn Jarir reported from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and Malik ibn Anas that they believe in it without knowing its interpretation. Ibn Jarir also related that in the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud it is: "Indeed its interpretation is only with Allah, and those firmly rooted in knowledge say: We believe in it." Similarly from Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Some scholars stop at Allah's statement: ﴿and those firmly rooted in knowledge﴾. Many commentators and scholars of usul al-fiqh (principles of jurisprudence) followed them, and they said: addressing people with what they cannot understand is far-fetched.

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: "I am among those firmly rooted in knowledge who know its interpretation." Ibn Abi Najih also said, from Mujahid: "Those firmly rooted in knowledge know its interpretation and say: We believe in it." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas also said likewise.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: ﴿And none knows its interpretation﴾, meaning what He intends by it, ﴿except Allah. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say: We believe in it﴾. Then they referred the interpretation of the mutashabih (ambiguous verses) to what they knew of the interpretation of the muhkam (clear verses), which has only one interpretation for anyone. Thus the Book became consistent by their statement, its parts confirmed one another, the proof was established, the excuse was made manifest, falsehood was removed, and disbelief was repelled by it.

It is also in a hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) supplicated for Ibn Abbas, saying: "O Allah, grant him understanding in the religion and teach him the interpretation."

Among the scholars are those who gave a detailed account on this matter. They said: The word ta'wil (interpretation) is used in the Qur'an with two meanings. The first is ta'wil in the sense of the reality of a thing and what its matter ultimately comes to, as in His Exalted statement: ﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said: O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true﴾ [Yusuf: 100], and His statement: ﴿Do they await but its ta'wil? On the day its ta'wil comes﴾ [al-A'raf: 53], meaning the reality of what they were told about the matter of the Return. If ta'wil is intended in this sense, then the pause is on the divine name, because the realities of matters and their essence clearly known only to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And His statement ﴿and those firmly rooted in knowledge﴾ is then the subject, and ﴿say: We believe in it﴾ is its predicate.

As for the other meaning, which is tafsir (exegesis), explanation, and clarification of a thing, as in His Exalted statement: ﴿Inform us of its ta'wil﴾ [Yusuf: 36], meaning its tafsir, if this meaning is intended, then the pause is on ﴿and those firmly rooted in knowledge﴾, because they know and understand what they were addressed with in this respect, even if they do not comprehend the realities of things in their full essence. In this case, ﴿they say: We believe in it﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) describing them. This is permissible because it is a case where the description applies to the conjoined element and not to the element it is conjoined to, as in His statement: ﴿For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties…﴾ up to His statement: ﴿and those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith﴾ [al-Hashr: 8–10], and as in His Exalted statement: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾ [al-Fajr: 22], meaning: and the angels came, rank upon rank.

* *

As for His statement, informing about them that they ﴿say: We believe in it﴾, meaning in the mutashabih, ﴿all is from our Lord﴾, meaning the whole of the muhkam and the mutashabih is true and right, and each of them confirms and testifies to the other, because all of it is from Allah, and nothing from Allah is conflicting or contradictory. This is in accordance with His statement: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much inconsistency﴾ [al-Nisa': 82]. For this reason He said: ﴿And none will be reminded except the people of understanding﴾, meaning: only those of sound intellects and upright comprehension understand, reason, and reflect upon the meanings in their proper form.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf al-Himsi narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, Fayyad al-Raqqi narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, and he had met the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): Anas, Abu Umama, and Abu al-Darda, may Allah be pleased with them. He said: Abu al-Darda narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the rasikhun fi al-ilm, and he said: "Those whose oath is fulfilled, whose tongue is truthful, whose heart is upright, and who keep their stomach and private parts chaste, those are among those firmly rooted in knowledge."[[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/72). It was also narrated by al-Tabari (6/207) and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, as in al-Durr (2/151), through the chain of Abdullah ibn Yazid. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6/324): "Abdullah ibn Yazid is weak."]]

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a people disputing, and he said: "Those before you were destroyed only by this: they struck the Book of Allah, one part against another. Indeed the Book of Allah was sent down so that one part would confirm another. So do not deny one part by another. What you know of it, say it; and what you do not know, leave it to its knower."[[Al-Musnad (2/185). Ibn Majah reported it, no. 85, and al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunna (1/260), through Amr ibn Shu'ayb. Al-Busiri said in Zawa'id Ibn Majah (1/58): "Its chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy."]]

And the narration of Ibn Mardawayh of this hadith has already been mentioned, through the chain of Hisham ibn Ammar, from Ibn Abi Hazim, from his father, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, with the same wording.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Muthanna al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Salama, who said: I do not know it except from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Qur'an was revealed in seven ahruf (modes), and disputing about the Qur'an is kufr (disbelief)" three times. "What you know of it, act upon it; and what you do not know of it, refer it to its knower."

This is a sahih chain, but there is a defect in it due to the narrator's statement: "I do not know it except from Abu Hurayra."[[Abu Ya'la in al-Musnad, no. 6016, and from his chain Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (1/146) (al-Ihsan). Ahmad reported it in al-Musnad (2/300) and al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra (5/33) through Anas ibn Iyad. The doubt "I do not know" is not in al-Nasa'i's narration.]]

Ibn al-Mundhir said in his *Tafsir*: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam informed us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, saying: It was said: "Those firmly grounded in knowledge" are those who are humble before Allah, who abase themselves before Allah seeking His good pleasure. They do not look down upon those above them [[In ج and أ: "يتعاظمون" (they regard themselves as great).]], nor do they belittle those beneath them. [Hence Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And none will be reminded except those of understanding﴾, meaning: only those of sound intellects, or upright understanding, comprehend, reason, and reflect upon the meanings as they truly are.] [[Addition from ج، ر، أ.]]

Then Allah the Exalted said, reporting about them that they supplicated their Lord, saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾, meaning: do not turn them away from guidance after You have set them upon it, and do not make us like those in whose hearts is deviation, who follow that which is ambiguous of the Qur'an. But keep us firm upon Your straight path and Your upright religion. ﴿And grant us from Yourself mercy﴾, meaning: from Your presence, ﴿mercy﴾ by which You will strengthen our hearts, gather our scattered affairs, and increase us in faith and certainty. ﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, and Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us. They both said: Waki' narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." Then he recited: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾ Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Muhammad ibn Bakkar, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah, and she is Asma' bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan. She heard her narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to frequently say in his supplication: "O Allah, Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, does the heart indeed turn?" He said: "Yes. There is no human among the children of Adam whom Allah has created except that his heart is between two of the fingers of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. If He wills, He keeps it firm, and if He wills, He causes it to deviate." So we ask Allah, our Lord, that He not let our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to grant us mercy from Himself. Indeed, He is the Bestower.

Likewise, Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Asad ibn Musa, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with the same wording. He also narrated it from al-Muthanna, from al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with the same wording, and he added: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, will you not teach me a supplication to supplicate with for myself?' He said: 'Yes, say: O Allah, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive my sin, remove the rage of my heart, and protect me from misleading trials.'" [[Ibn Abi Hatim in his *Tafsir* (2/84), al-Tabari in his *Tafsir* (6/213), Ahmad in *al-Musnad* (6/315), al-Tirmidhi in *al-Sunan* (3522), and Ibn Abi Asim in *al-Sunnah* (no. 223) narrated it through Abu Ka'b, the seller of silk, from Shahr ibn Hawshab with the same wording. The hadith has corroborating narrations from Aisha, Anas, Jabir, and al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, may Allah be pleased with them.]]

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Bakkar al-Dimashqi narrated to us, saying: al-Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Khallal informed us, saying: Yazid ibn Yahya ibn Ubayd Allah informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn Bashir informed us, from Qatadah, from Abu Hassan al-A'raj, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ often used to supplicate: "O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how often you supplicate with this supplication!" He said: "There is no heart except that it is between two fingers of the Most Merciful. When He wills to keep it firm, He keeps it firm, and when He wills to cause it to deviate, He causes it to deviate. Do you not hear His saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.﴾" This is *gharib* (rare) through this chain, but its origin is established in the *Sahihayn* and other works through many routes, without the addition of mention of this noble verse.

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' (al-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban added: and Abd Allah ibn Wahb), both of them from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, who said: Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Tujibi narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he woke up at night, would say: "There is no god but You, glory be to You. O Allah, I ask Your forgiveness for my sin, and I ask You for mercy. O Allah, increase me in knowledge, do not let my heart deviate after You have guided me, and grant me from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower." This is the wording of Ibn Mardawayh. [[Abu Dawud in *al-Sunan* (no. 5061) and al-Nasa'i in *al-Kubra* (no. 10701).]]

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Malik, from Abu Ubayd, the freedman of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, that he informed him that he heard Qays ibn al-Harith say: Abu Abd Allah al-Sunabihi informed me that he prayed behind Abu Bakr al-Siddiq the Maghrib prayer, and Abu Bakr recited in the first two rak'ahs al-Fatihah and two short surahs from al-Mufassal (the short surahs at the end of the Qur'an) [[*Al-Mufassal*: the portion of the Qur'an from Surah Qaf (50) to its end, so called because of the many divisions (*fusul*) between its surahs by the basmalah.]], and in the third rak'ah he recited. He said: I drew close to him until my garments nearly touched his garments, and I heard him reciting al-Fatihah and this verse: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us [and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower].﴾ [[Addition from ج، ر، أ، و; in هـ: "the verse".]] [[Narrated by Malik in *al-Muwatta'* (1/79).]]

Abu Ubayd said: Ubadah ibn Nusayy also informed me that he was with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz during his caliphate, and Umar said to Qays: "How did you narrate to me about Abu Abd Allah al-Sunabihi?" He informed him of what he had heard from Abu Abd Allah the second time. Umar said: "We have not abandoned it since we heard it from him, although before that I was upon something other than that." A man said to him: "Upon what was the Commander of the Believers before that?" He said: "I used to recite ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1]." This report was also narrated by al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Malik and al-Awza'i, both of them from Abu Ubayd, with the same wording. al-Walid also narrated it from Ibn Jabir, from Yahya ibn Yahya al-Ghassani, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from al-Sunabihi, that he prayed behind Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, the Maghrib prayer, and he recited in the first two rak'ahs al-Fatihah and a short surah, aloud. When he stood for the third, he began the recitation, and I drew close to him until my garments touched his garments, and he recited this verse: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate [after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower].﴾ [[Addition from ج، أ، و; in هـ: "the verse".]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Our Lord, indeed You are the gatherer of mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.﴾ Meaning: they say in their supplication: "Indeed You, O our Lord, will gather together Your creation on the Day of their return, and You will separate them and judge among them concerning that over which they differed, and You will recompense each soul according to its deeds, and what it was upon of good and evil in the world."

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on surah 3, verses 10–11:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us that the disbelievers are the fuel of the Fire: ﴿On the Day when no excuse will benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 52]. The wealth and children that they were given in this world will not benefit them with Allah, nor will they save them from His punishment and His painful retribution. Rather, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in this world, and their souls will depart while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 85]. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the land deceive you. A brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 196–197]. As He says here: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: in the signs of Allah, and who denied His messengers, opposed His Book, and did not benefit from His revelation sent to His prophets, ﴿their wealth and their children will never avail them against Allah at all, and they are the fuel of the Fire﴾, meaning: its firewood, with which it is kindled and set ablaze, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; to it you will be brought﴾ [al-Anbiya': 98].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, Ibn al-Hadi informed me, from Hind bint al-Harith, from Umm al-Fadl, the mother of Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: "While we were in Makkah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up during the night and said, 'Have I conveyed? O Allah, have I conveyed?' ... three times. Then 'Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said, 'Yes.' Then in the morning the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Islam will certainly prevail until it drives disbelief back to its places, and men will certainly plunge into the seas with Islam. There will certainly come upon the people a time when they learn the Qur'an and recite it, then they will say: We have recited and we have learned; so who is better than us? Is there any good in those people?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who are those?' He said: 'Those are from among you, and those are the fuel of the Fire.'" And thus I saw it narrated with this wording.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Hadi, from Hind bint al-Harith, the wife of Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Umm al-Fadl, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood one night in Makkah and said: "Have I conveyed?" saying it three times. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up—and he was one who wept much—and said: "O Allah, yes, you have conveyed, and you exerted yourself, strove, and advised; so be patient." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Faith will certainly prevail until it drives disbelief back to its places, and men will certainly plunge into the seas with Islam, and there will certainly come upon the people a time when they recite the Qur'an, and they recite it and know it, and they say: We have recited, and we have known; so who is better than us? There is no good in those people." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are those?" He said: "Those are from among you, and those are the fuel of the Fire." [Note: Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/90); in its chain is Ibn Lahi'ah, but he was followed by 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Hazim from Yazid ibn al-Hadi, narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/250). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/186): "Its narrators are trustworthy, except that I have not seen anyone who authenticated or criticised Hind bint al-Harith al-Khath'amiyyah, the Successor (tabi'iyyah)."] Then he narrated it through the route of Musa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from the daughter of al-Hadi, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, with similar wording.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "like the practice of the people of Pharaoh." Similarly it was narrated from 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, and others. Some of them said: "like the way of the people of Pharaoh," "like the deed of the people of Pharaoh," and "like the likeness of the people of Pharaoh," and the wordings are close in meaning. Al-Da'b (with the vowel sukun, and also with fatha, as in nahr and nahar) is: al-sun' (the practice), al-sha'n (the affair), al-hal (the condition), al-amr (the matter), and al-'adah (the custom). As one says: "This remains my custom (da'b) and yours." Imru' al-Qays said:

"We stopped there, my companions halting their mounts over me, saying: 'Do not perish in grief, and bear yourself with composure,'
Like your custom (da'bika) concerning Umm al-Huwayrith before her, and her neighbour Umm al-Rabab at Ma'sal."

The meaning is: "like your habit regarding Umm al-Huwayrith, when you destroyed yourself in love for her, and wept over her abode and its traces."

None can escape Him, nothing eludes Him, and He is the Doer of what He wills, who has overcome everything and to whom everything is subjugated. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

Allah says: Say, O Muhammad, to the disbelievers: "You will be overcome" (sa-tughlabūn), i.e., in this world, "and you will be gathered" (wa-tuḥsharūn), i.e., on the Day of Resurrection, "to Hell, and how wretched is the resting-place" (wa-bi'sa al-mihād).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had achieved what he achieved against the people of Badr and returned to Madinah, he gathered the Jews in the marketplace of Banu Qaynuqa' and said: "O assembly of Jews, embrace Islam before Allah inflicts upon you what He inflicted upon Quraysh." They said: "O Muhammad, do not let yourself be deceived by the fact that you killed a group of Quraysh who were inexperienced and did not know how to fight. By Allah, if you were to fight us, you would know that we are the (real) men, and that you have never encountered the likes of us." So Allah revealed concerning their statement: "Say to those who disbelieve: 'You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and how wretched is the resting-place'" up to His words: "Surely there is a lesson in that for those who have vision" (li-'ibratan li-ulī al-abṣār).

Ibn Ishaq also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Sa'id or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, and mentioned it similarly. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said: "There has already been a sign for you" (qad kana lakum āyah), i.e., there has already been for you, O Jews, who said what you said, "a sign" (āyah), i.e., a proof that Allah strengthens His religion, supports His Messenger, makes His word prevail, and exalts His command. "In two groups that met" (fī fi'atayn iltaqatā), i.e., two companies that met "for battle" (lil-qital): "one fighting in the way of Allah" (fi'atun tuqātilu fī sabīl Allah), and they are the Muslims, "and another disbelieving" (wa-ukhrā kafirah), and they are the polytheists of Quraysh on the Day of Badr.

* *

As for His words: "They saw them as twice their number with the eye of sight" (yarawnahum mithlayhim ra'y al-'ayn). Some scholars said, as related by Ibn Jarir: The polytheists on the Day of Badr saw the Muslims as twice their number in quantity with their own eyes, i.e., Allah made that, in what they saw, a cause for the victory of Islam over them. This has no difficulty except from one direction: the polytheists sent 'Umar ibn Sa'd that day before the fighting to estimate the number of the Muslims for them, and he informed them that they were three hundred, give or take a little. And so it was: they were three hundred and some ten men. Then, when the fighting began, Allah reinforced them with a thousand of the chosen angels and their leaders.

The second opinion: The meaning of His words "They saw them as twice their number with the eye of sight" is that the Muslim company saw the disbelieving company as twice their number, i.e., double them in quantity, and despite this Allah gave them victory over them. There is no difficulty in this according to what al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas, that the believers on the Day of Badr were three hundred and thirteen men, and the polytheists were six hundred and twenty-six men. This opinion seems to be derived from the apparent meaning of this verse, but it contradicts what is well known among the historians, the biographers and the chroniclers of people's days, and contradicts what is known to the majority, that the polytheists were between nine hundred and a thousand, as related by Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked that black slave belonging to the sons of al-Hajjaj about the number of Quraysh, and he said: "Many." He said: "How many do they slaughter each day?" He said: "One day nine, and one day ten." The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: "The people are between nine hundred and a thousand."

Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i related from Harithah, from Ali, who said: "They were a thousand," and Ibn Mas'ud said likewise. The well-known view is that they were between nine hundred and a thousand. In any case, they were three times the number of the Muslims. On this basis, this statement is problematic, and Allah knows best. However, Ibn Jarir interpreted this and considered it sound, as one would say: "I have a thousand, and I need twice that," and you would then be in need of three thousand. Thus he said, and on this basis there is no difficulty.

But another question remains, which applies to both opinions: How is this verse to be reconciled with His words in the account of Badr: "And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes and made you appear few in their eyes, that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done" (al-Anfal: 44)? The answer: That was in one state, and the other was in another state, as as-Suddi said, from Murrah al-Tayyib, from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words: "There has already been a sign for you in two groups that met: one fighting in the way of Allah and another disbelieving, they saw them as twice their number with the eye of sight," that he said: "This is the Day of Badr." Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "We looked at the polytheists and saw them as doubled against us; then we looked at them again and did not see them exceeding us by a single man." That is His saying: "And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes and made you appear few in their eyes."

Abu Ishaq said, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "They were made to appear so few in our eyes that I said to a man beside me: 'Do you see them as seventy?' He said: 'I see them as a hundred.' Then we captured a man from them and asked him: 'How many were you?' He said: 'A thousand.'" When each of the two groups saw the other, the Muslims saw the polytheists as twice their number, i.e., more than them by double, so that they would rely upon Allah, turn to Him, and seek help from their Lord, Mighty and Majestic. And the polytheists saw the believers likewise, so that terror, fear, anxiety and dread would befall them. Then, when the battle lines were formed and the two groups met, Allah made these appear few in the eyes of those and those appear few in the eyes of these, so that each of them would advance upon the other.

"That Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done" (li-yaqḍiya Allah amran kana maf'ūlan), i.e., that He might distinguish truth from falsehood, make the word of faith prevail over disbelief, exalt the believers and humble the disbelievers, as Allah the Exalted said: "And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak" (Ali 'Imran: 123). And here He said: "And Allah supports with His help whom He wills. Surely in that is a lesson for those who have vision," i.e., surely in that is an admonition for whoever has insight and understanding, by which he may be guided to the judgment of Allah, His actions, and His decree that operates to grant victory to His believing servants in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand.

Al-Ma'murah is the one with many offspring; al-Sikkah is the lined-up palm trees; and al-Ma'burah is the pollinated one.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿That is the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾, that is: this is merely the splendor of the worldly life and its adornment, which is transient and passing away; ﴿but with Allah is the best return﴾, that is: the best destination and reward.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Ata, from Abu Bakr ibn Hafs ibn Umar ibn Sa'd, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When it was revealed: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires﴾, I said: Now, O Lord, when You have beautified them for us? Then it was revealed: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who are mindful of God are gardens with their Lord beneath which rivers flow [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W; in manuscript H: "the verse."]]﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/244).]].

Therefore He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that?﴾, that is: Say, O Muhammad, to the people: Shall I tell you of something better than what has been made attractive to people in this worldly life of its splendor and bliss, which is certainly passing away? Then He informed about that, saying: ﴿For those who are mindful of God are gardens with their Lord beneath which rivers flow﴾, that is: rivers flow through their sides and expanses, of various kinds of drinks: of honey, milk, wine, water and other things, such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has occurred to a human heart.

﴿Abiding therein﴾, that is: remaining therein forever and ever, not desiring any change from it [[In manuscripts J, R: "they will not find any turning away from it."]].

"And purified spouses" — that is, purified from filth, impurity, harm, menstruation, postnatal bleeding, and all else that afflicts the women of this world.

"And approval from Allah" — that is, His good pleasure descends upon them, so that He never becomes displeased with them thereafter, ever. For this reason, Allah said in the other verse in Surat al-Tawbah: ﴿And approval from Allah is greater﴾ [al-Tawbah: 72] — that is, greater than what He has given them of enduring bliss. Then He said [Most High] ﹛And Allah is Seeing of the servants﹜ — that is, He gives each one according to what he deserves of reward.

Ibn Kathir said, commenting on Surah Aal 'Imran, verses 16–17:

Allah, exalted is He, describes His righteous servants, to whom He has promised a great reward. He says: ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, indeed we have believed"﴾, meaning: in You, in Your Book, and in Your Messenger. ﴿So forgive us our sins﴾, meaning: because of our faith in You and in what You have prescribed for us. ﴿So forgive us our sins and our shortcomings in our affair, by Your bounty and mercy, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.﴾

Then He said: ﴿The patient﴾, meaning: in their standing in acts of worship and their abstaining from what is forbidden; ﴿and the truthful﴾, in what they report of their faith, through their commitment to difficult deeds; ﴿and the obedient﴾. Al-qunut (obedience and humility) is obedience and submission. ﴿And the spenders﴾, meaning: from their wealth in all that they have been commanded of acts of obedience, the maintenance of ties of kinship and relatives, filling the needs (of the poor), and comforting those in need. ﴿And those who seek forgiveness in the hours before dawn﴾: this indicates the virtue of seeking forgiveness at the time of the pre-dawn hours (al-asḥār).

It has been said that when Ya'qub (peace be upon him) said to his sons: ﴿I will ask my Lord to forgive you﴾ [Yusuf: 98], he delayed it until the time of suhur (the last part of the night). It is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) and others, the Masanid (musnad collections) and the Sunan, through multiple chains, from a group of the Companions, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: 'Is there anyone who asks, that I may give to him? Is there anyone who calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Is there anyone who seeks forgiveness, that I may forgive him?'" – the hadith [[It comes from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih under no. (7494) and no. (6321); narrated by Muslim in his Sahih under no. (758); Abu Dawud in his Sunan under no. (1315); and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan under no. (4398).

It also comes from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Jubayr ibn Mut'im, Rifa'ah al-Juhani, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn Mas'ud. For discussion of these, see Irwa' al-Ghalil by Shaykh Nasir al-Albani (2/450).]] The Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni devoted a separate juz' (booklet) to this subject, narrating it through multiple routes.

In the Two Sahihs, from 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would make his witr (odd-numbered prayer) at every part of the night, at its beginning, middle and end, and his witr would end at suhur." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih under no. (996) and by Muslim in his Sahih under no. (745).]]

'Abdullah ibn 'Umar would pray during the night, then say: "O Nafi', has the suhur come?" If he said, "Yes," he would turn to supplication and seeking forgiveness until morning. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn WakI' narrated to us, from his father, from Hurayth ibn Abi Mutar, from Ibrahim ibn Hatib, from his father, who said: "I heard a man in the pre-dawn hour in a corner of the mosque saying: 'My Lord, You commanded me and I obeyed You, and this is the suhur, so forgive me.' I looked and it was Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/266); in its chain is Sufyan ibn WakI', who is weak; and the hadith of Ibn Abi Mutar was weakened by Abu Hatim, Ibn Ma'in and al-Bukhari.]]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas ibn Malik who said: "When we had prayed during the night, we were commanded to seek forgiveness at the end of the pre-dawn hour seventy times."

He (Allah) bears witness, and sufficient is He as a witness. He is the most truthful of witnesses, the most just of them, and the most truthful of speakers, [[In manuscript wa: "yashhadu".]] that there is no god except Him. That is, He alone is singled out for divinity over all creation, all of creation are His servants and creatures, all are in need of Him, and He is free of need of anything other than Him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ [An-Nisa: 166]. [[In manuscripts J and R: "bihi", which is an error.]]

Then He joined the witness of His angels and of those possessed of knowledge to His own witness, saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge [bear witness]﴾. This is a great distinction for the scholars in this position.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Jubayr ibn Amr al-Qurashi narrated to me, Abu Sa'id [[In manuscripts A and W: "Abu Sa'd".]] al-Ansari narrated to us, from Abu Yahya, mawla of the family of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, from al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was at Arafah reciting this verse: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice; there is no god except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾, and [he added]: "And I am among those who bear witness to that, O Lord." [[Musnad (1/166). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6/325): "In its chain are unknown narrators."]]

[[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/146). In its chain are unknown narrators.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Abdan ibn Ahmad and Ali ibn Sa'id al-Razi narrated to us, both saying: Ammar ibn Umar ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Ghalib al-Qattan narrated to me, saying: I came to Kufah on business and stayed near al-A'mash. One night I wanted to set out, and he got up and prayed the night prayer. He passed by this verse: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice; there is no god except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise. Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾. Then al-A'mash said: "And I bear witness to what Allah has borne witness to, and I entrust Allah with this testimony, which is a deposit with Him for me: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾," repeating it several times. I said: He has surely heard something in it. So I went to him in the morning and bid him farewell. Then I said: O Abu Muhammad, I heard you repeating this verse. He said: Has it not reached you what is in it? I said: I have been with you for a month and you have not told me. He said: By Allah, I will not tell you of it for a year. So I stayed for a year, sitting at his door. When the year had passed, I said: O Abu Muhammad, the year has passed. He said: Abu Wa'il narrated to me, from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection its companion will be brought, and Allah, mighty and majestic, will say: My servant made a covenant with Me, and I am most worthy to fulfil the covenant. Admit My servant to Paradise." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/245). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/326): "In it is Umar ibn al-Mukhtar, who is weak." Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (5/36) by way of Ammar ibn Umar al-Mukhtar, and said: "None narrates it except Umar al-Mukhtar, and the extent of what he narrates is questionable."]]

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ is an informing from Allah, exalted is He, that there is no religion with Him that He accepts from anyone other than Islam, which is following the messengers in what Allah sent them with in every age, until they were sealed with Muhammad (ﷺ), who closed all the routes to Him except the route through Muhammad (ﷺ). Whoever meets Allah after His sending of Muhammad (ﷺ) with a religion other than his law, it will not be accepted. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 85]. In this verse, informing that the religion accepted with Him is confined to Islam, He said: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾.

Ibn Jarir reported that Ibn Abbas recited: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice; there is no god except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise. Indeed [innahu] the religion with Allah is Islam﴾, with the "inna" of "innahu" in the kasra [i.e., "innahu"] and the "inna" of "inna al-din" in the fatha [i.e., "anna al-din"], meaning: He bears witness, and His angels and those of knowledge among mankind bear witness, that the religion with Allah is Islam. The majority read it with a kasra as an informative statement, and both meanings are sound. However, this is more apparent according to the view of the majority, and Allah knows best.

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed that those given the Scripture before differed only after the proof had been established against them, through the sending of messengers to them and the sending down of books to them. He said: ﴿And those given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾. That is, some of them transgressed against others, so they differed about the truth due to their jealousy, hatred and enmity toward one another, so that the hatred of some of them toward others led them to oppose them in all their statements and actions, even if those were true. Then He said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, then indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. That is, whoever denies what Allah has sent down in His Book, Allah will requite him for that, will call him to account for his denial, and will punish him for opposing His Book. [[In manuscripts A and W: "anzalahu" and "bi-kitabihi".]]

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they argue with you﴾, that is, they dispute with you about monotheism, ﴿then say: I have submitted myself entirely to Allah, and so have those who follow me﴾. That is, say: I have sincerely devoted my worship to Allah alone, with no partner, no equal, no son and no consort for Him. ﴿And those who follow me﴾ in my religion, saying what I say, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And glory be to Allah; I am not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ [Yusuf: 108].

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, commanding His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to call to His way and religion, and to enter into His law and what Allah sent him with, the People of the Book from the two communities [i.e., Jews and Christians] and the unlettered (ummiyyin) among the polytheists. He said: ﴿And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered: Have you submitted? If they submit, then they have been guided; but if they turn away, then your duty is only to convey the message﴾. That is, Allah will reckon with them, and to Him is their return and their final place. He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, and to Him belongs wisdom in that and the conclusive proof. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾. That is, He is Knowing of who deserves guidance and who deserves misguidance, and He is the One ﴿who is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 23]. And that is only because of His wisdom and His mercy.

This verse and similar ones are among the clearest indications of the universality of his mission (ﷺ), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to all of creation, as is known necessarily from his religion, and as the Book and the Sunnah indicate in more than one verse and hadith. Among that is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [Al-A'raf: 158], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [Al-Furqan: 1]. In the two Sahihs and others, what is established by mass transmission through numerous incidents is that he (ﷺ) sent his letters calling the kings of the regions and groups of the children of Adam, from their Arabs and non-Arabs, their People of the Book and their unlettered, in compliance with Allah's command to him in that. Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one of this nation hears of me, Jew or Christian, and dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the people of the Fire." Narrated by Muslim. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 153.]]

He (ﷺ) also said: "I have been sent to the red and the black." [[In manuscripts J, R, A and W: "al-aswad wa al-ahmar".]] And he said: "A prophet used to be sent only to his own people, but I have been sent to all people." Imam Ahmad said: Mu'ammal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: that a Jewish boy used to serve the Prophet (ﷺ) by preparing his ablution water and handing him his sandals. He fell ill, and the Prophet (ﷺ) came to visit him and entered upon him, while his father was sitting at his head. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O so-and-so, say: There is no god but Allah." The boy looked at his father, and his father remained silent. The Prophet (ﷺ) repeated it to him, and he looked at his father again. His father said: Obey Abu al-Qasim. So the boy said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) went out saying: "Praise be to Allah, who has rescued him from the Fire through me." Al-Bukhari narrated it in the Sahih. [[Musnad (3/175) and al-Bukhari, no. 1356.]] And there are other verses and hadiths besides these.

Ibn Jarir reported that Ibn Abbas recited: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice; there is no god except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise. Indeed [innahu] the religion with Allah is Islam﴾, with the "inna" of "innahu" in the kasra [i.e., "innahu"] and the "inna" of "inna al-din" in the fatha [i.e., "anna al-din"], meaning: He bears witness, and His angels and those of knowledge among mankind bear witness, that the religion with Allah is Islam. The majority read it with a kasra as an informative statement, and both meanings are sound. However, this is more apparent according to the view of the majority, and Allah knows best.

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed that those given the Scripture before differed only after the proof had been established against them, through the sending of messengers to them and the sending down of books to them. He said: ﴿And those given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾. That is, some of them transgressed against others, so they differed about the truth due to their jealousy, hatred and enmity toward one another, so that the hatred of some of them toward others led them to oppose them in all their statements and actions, even if those were true. Then He said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, then indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. That is, whoever denies what Allah has sent down in His Book, Allah will requite him for that, will call him to account for his denial, and will punish him for opposing His Book. [[In manuscripts A and W: "anzalahu" and "bi-kitabihi".]]

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they argue with you﴾, that is, they dispute with you about monotheism, ﴿then say: I have submitted myself entirely to Allah, and so have those who follow me﴾. That is, say: I have sincerely devoted my worship to Allah alone, with no partner, no equal, no son and no consort for Him. ﴿And those who follow me﴾ in my religion, saying what I say, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And glory be to Allah; I am not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ [Yusuf: 108].

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, commanding His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to call to His way and religion, and to enter into His law and what Allah sent him with, the People of the Book from the two communities [i.e., Jews and Christians] and the unlettered (ummiyyin) among the polytheists. He said: ﴿And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered: Have you submitted? If they submit, then they have been guided; but if they turn away, then your duty is only to convey the message﴾. That is, Allah will reckon with them, and to Him is their return and their final place. He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, and to Him belongs wisdom in that and the conclusive proof. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of the servants﴾. That is, He is Knowing of who deserves guidance and who deserves misguidance, and He is the One ﴿who is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 23]. And that is only because of His wisdom and His mercy.

This verse and similar ones are among the clearest indications of the universality of his mission (ﷺ), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to all of creation, as is known necessarily from his religion, and as the Book and the Sunnah indicate in more than one verse and hadith. Among that is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [Al-A'raf: 158], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [Al-Furqan: 1]. In the two Sahihs and others, what is established by mass transmission through numerous incidents is that he (ﷺ) sent his letters calling the kings of the regions and groups of the children of Adam, from their Arabs and non-Arabs, their People of the Book and their unlettered, in compliance with Allah's command to him in that. Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one of this nation hears of me, Jew or Christian, and dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the people of the Fire." Narrated by Muslim. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 153.]]

He (ﷺ) also said: "I have been sent to the red and the black." [[In manuscripts J, R, A and W: "al-aswad wa al-ahmar".]] And he said: "A prophet used to be sent only to his own people, but I have been sent to all people." Imam Ahmad said: Mu'ammal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: that a Jewish boy used to serve the Prophet (ﷺ) by preparing his ablution water and handing him his sandals. He fell ill, and the Prophet (ﷺ) came to visit him and entered upon him, while his father was sitting at his head. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O so-and-so, say: There is no god but Allah." The boy looked at his father, and his father remained silent. The Prophet (ﷺ) repeated it to him, and he looked at his father again. His father said: Obey Abu al-Qasim. So the boy said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) went out saying: "Praise be to Allah, who has rescued him from the Fire through me." Al-Bukhari narrated it in the Sahih. [[Musnad (3/175) and al-Bukhari, no. 1356.]] And there are other verses and hadiths besides these.

He (Allah) bears witness, and sufficient is He as a witness. He is the most truthful of witnesses, the most just of them, and the most truthful of speakers, [[In manuscript wa: "yashhadu".]] that there is no god except Him. That is, He alone is singled out for divinity over all creation, all of creation are His servants and creatures, all are in need of Him, and He is free of need of anything other than Him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ [An-Nisa: 166]. [[In manuscripts J and R: "bihi", which is an error.]]

Then He joined the witness of His angels and of those possessed of knowledge to His own witness, saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge [bear witness]﴾. This is a great distinction for the scholars in this position.

﴿Standing in justice﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), and He is so in all circumstances.

﴿There is no god except Him﴾ is an emphasis of what came before. ﴿The Almighty, the All-Wise﴾: The Almighty is the One whose sanctuary cannot be violated, in greatness and majesty. The All-Wise is wise in His statements, His actions, His legislation and His decree.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Jubayr ibn Amr al-Qurashi narrated to me, Abu Sa'id [[In manuscripts A and W: "Abu Sa'd".]] al-Ansari narrated to us, from Abu Yahya, mawla of the family of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, from al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was at Arafah reciting this verse: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice; there is no god except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾, and [he added]: "And I am among those who bear witness to that, O Lord." [[Musnad (1/166). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6/325): "In its chain are unknown narrators."]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it by another route, saying: Ali ibn Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Mutawakkil al-Asqalani narrated to us, Umar ibn Hafs ibn Thabit Abu Sa'id al-Ansari narrated to us, Abd al-Malik ibn Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Zubayr, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited this verse: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels﴾, and he said: "And I bear witness, O Lord." [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/146). In its chain are unknown narrators.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Abdan ibn Ahmad and Ali ibn Sa'id al-Razi narrated to us, both saying: Ammar ibn Umar ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Ghalib al-Qattan narrated to me, saying: I came to Kufah on business and stayed near al-A'mash. One night I wanted to set out, and he got up and prayed the night prayer. He passed by this verse: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice; there is no god except Him, the Almighty, the All-Wise. Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾. Then al-A'mash said: "And I bear witness to what Allah has borne witness to, and I entrust Allah with this testimony, which is a deposit with Him for me: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾," repeating it several times. I said: He has surely heard something in it. So I went to him in the morning and bid him farewell. Then I said: O Abu Muhammad, I heard you repeating this verse. He said: Has it not reached you what is in it? I said: I have been with you for a month and you have not told me. He said: By Allah, I will not tell you of it for a year. So I stayed for a year, sitting at his door. When the year had passed, I said: O Abu Muhammad, the year has passed. He said: Abu Wa'il narrated to me, from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection its companion will be brought, and Allah, mighty and majestic, will say: My servant made a covenant with Me, and I am most worthy to fulfil the covenant. Admit My servant to Paradise." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/245). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/326): "In it is Umar ibn al-Mukhtar, who is weak." Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (5/36) by way of Ammar ibn Umar al-Mukhtar, and said: "None narrates it except Umar al-Mukhtar, and the extent of what he narrates is questionable."]]

* *

Whoever meets Allah after His sending of Muhammad (ﷺ) with a religion other than his law, it will not be accepted. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 85]. In this verse, informing that the religion accepted with Him is confined to Islam, He said: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾.

This is a condemnation from Allah, the Exalted, of the People of the Book for the sins and prohibited acts they committed in denying the signs of Allah, both in the past and in the present, which the messengers conveyed to them, out of arrogance towards them, obstinacy against them, self-magnification against the truth, and refusal to follow it. This is the utmost of arrogance, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu al-Zubayr al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muslim al-Naysaburi, resident of Makkah, narrated to us: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Hafs (meaning Ibn Thabit ibn Zurarah al-Ansari) told me, narrating to us: Muhammad ibn Hamzah told me, narrating: Abu al-Hasan, a client of the Banu Asad, from Makhul, from Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb al-Khuza'i, from Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which of the people will suffer the most severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "A man who kills a prophet, or one who enjoins what is good and forbids what is evil." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [up to His saying: ﴿and they will have no helpers﴾] - the verse. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Ubaydah, the Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets at the beginning of the day in a single hour, then a hundred and seventy men from the Children of Israel stood up and commanded those who had killed them to do good and forbade them from evil, and they were all killed by the end of that same day. They are the ones whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned."

Likewise, Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Ubayd al-Wassabi Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Ibn Humayr, from Abu al-Hasan, client of Banu Asad, from Makhul, with the same chain. [Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir (1/161) and al-Tabari in his Tafsir (6/285). Abu Ubayd al-Wassabi did not meet Muhammad ibn Humayr, as mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil. Abu Ubayd has been corroborated: Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah followed him, and al-Bazzar narrated it through the route of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah from Muhammad ibn Humayr with the same. Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know of any route for it from Abu Ubaydah other than this one, and we have not heard anyone name this Abu al-Hasan from whom Muhammad ibn Humayr narrated. And the hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "In it is Abu al-Hasan, client of Banu Asad, and he is unknown."]

And from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Children of Israel killed three hundred prophets at the beginning of the day, and then they set up their vegetable market at its end." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Almighty Allah says, rebuking the Jews and Christians who, in their claim, hold fast to their two books that are in their hands, namely the Torah and the Gospel. When they are called to submit their disputes to what is in them of obedience to Allah in what He commanded them therein, namely following Muhammad (ﷺ), they turn away, being averse to them. This is at the furthest extent of censure for them and of highlighting their opposition and obstinacy.

Then He said: ﴿That is because they say, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days."﴾ That is, what drove them and emboldened them to oppose the truth was their fabrication against Allah concerning what they claimed for themselves, that they would be punished in the Fire only seven days, one day for every thousand years of the worldly life. The explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Baqarah. Then He said: ﴿And what they used to fabricate deceived them regarding their religion.﴾ [That is, it deceived them regarding their religion] [[Addition from manuscript w.]] That is: what they deceived themselves with, through their claim that the Fire would not touch them for their sins except for a few numbered days, has kept them firm in their false religion. They are the ones who invented this from their own selves and fabricated it, and Allah has not sent down any authority for it. Allah the Exalted said, threatening and warning them: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt?﴾ That is: how will their condition be, when they have fabricated against Allah, denied His messengers, and killed His prophets and the scholars of their people who enjoined what is good and forbade what is evil? Allah the Exalted will question them about all of that, hold them to account for it, and recompense them for it. Therefore He said: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt?﴾ — there is no doubt in its occurrence and its coming to pass — ﴿and every soul will be paid in full for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾

Allah the Exalted said, threatening and warning them: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt?﴾ That is: how will their condition be, when they have fabricated against Allah, denied His messengers, and killed His prophets and the scholars of their people who enjoined what is good and forbade what is evil? Allah the Exalted will question them about all of that, hold them to account for it, and recompense them for it. Therefore He said: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt?﴾ — there is no doubt in its occurrence and its coming to pass — ﴿and every soul will be paid in full for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verse 26–27:

Allah the Exalted says: "Say," O Muhammad, magnifying your Lord, relying upon Him, thanking Him, and entrusting yourself to Him: "O Allah, Master of the Kingdom," meaning: to You belongs all the dominion. "You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You exalt whom You will, and You abase whom You will." Meaning: You are the Giver, You are the Withholder, and You are the One whose will, whatever You wish, comes to be, and whatever You do not wish, does not come to be.

In this verse there is a reminder and guidance to thank Allah the Exalted for His blessing upon His Messenger ﷺ and upon this Ummah, because Allah transferred prophethood from the Children of Israel to the Arab Prophet, the Qurashi, Meccan, unlettered one, the Seal of the Prophets absolutely, and the Messenger of Allah to all of mankind and the jinn, the two weighty creations. In him Allah gathered the excellences of all who came before him, and He singled him out with qualities not given to any prophet or messenger: in knowledge of Allah and His law, in his being informed of the unseen, past and future, in his unveiling the realities of the Hereafter, and in the spreading of his Ummah throughout the horizons, in the east and west of the earth, and in the manifestation of his religion and law over all other religions and laws. So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Judgment, as long as the night and day alternate. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: "Say, O Allah, Master of the Kingdom, You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty away from whom You will, and You exalt whom You will, and You abase whom You will; in Your hand is all good; indeed You are over all things competent." Meaning: You are the one who disposes of His creation, the one who does what He wills, just as Allah, blessed and exalted, refuted those who presumed to dictate to Him concerning His affair, when He said: "And they said, 'Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?'" [Az-Zukhruf: 31].

Allah said in refutation of them: "Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the worldly life and raised some of them above others in degrees..." [Az-Zukhruf: 32] to the end of the verse. Meaning: We dispose of Our creation as We wish, without any preventer or repeller, and to Us belongs wisdom and proof in that. Likewise We give prophethood to whom We wish, as He said: "Allah knows best where to place His message" [Al-An'am: 124], and He said: "See how We have preferred some of them over others, and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference" [Al-Isra: 21]. The hafiz Ibn 'Asakir related in the biography of "Ishaq ibn Ahmad" from his History, from the Caliph al-Ma'mun, that he saw in a palace in the lands of the Romans an inscription written in Himyaritic script, which was translated for him, and it read: "In the name of Allah, the night and day do not alternate, nor do the stars of the sky revolve in their orbits, except by the transfer of blessing from a king whose rule has ended to another king. The dominion of the Lord of the Throne is everlasting forever, neither perishing nor shared." [[Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn 'Asakir (2/706 manuscript) and Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (4/264).]]

* *

His saying: "You cause the night to enter into the day and You cause the day to enter into the night" means: You take from the length of this and add it to the shortness of that, so that they become equal; then You take from this and put it into that, so that they differ, then they become equal again. Likewise in the seasons of the year: spring, summer, autumn and winter.

* *

His saying: "You bring the living out of the dead and You bring the dead out of the living" means: You bring the grain out of the crop and the crop out of the grain, the palm tree out of the date-stone and the date-stone out of the palm tree, the believer out of the disbeliever and the disbeliever out of the believer, the chicken out of the egg and the egg out of the chicken, and whatever is of this kind among all things. "And You provide for whom You will without reckoning" means: You give whom You wish of wealth in an amount that he cannot count or measure, and You restrict it for others, due to the wisdom, will, desire and justice that are Yours. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Ghallabi related to us, Ja'far ibn Jisr ibn Farqad related to us, my father related to us, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "The Greatest Name of Allah is that by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and it is in this verse of Al 'Imran: 'Say, O Allah, Master of the Kingdom, You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty away from whom You will, and You exalt whom You will, and You abase whom You will; in Your hand is all good; indeed You are over all things competent.'" [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/172); in its chain is Jisr ibn Farqad, who is weak.]]

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, forbade His believing servants from taking the disbelievers as allies (awliya'), taking them as intimate friends (awliya') to whom they secretly convey affection in preference to the believers. Then He warned against that, saying: ﴿And whoever does that has nothing with Allah at all⦆. That is, whoever commits what Allah has forbidden in this matter has disassociated himself from Allah, as He said: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear authority against yourselves?﴾ [an-Nisa': 144]. And He said [Exalted is He]: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them is indeed one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 51]. 

[And He, Exalted, said]: ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And whoever does that among you has certainly strayed from the sound way﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1]. And He, Exalted, said, after mentioning the allegiance of the believers to one another among the Emigrants, the Helpers and the Bedouins: ﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do likewise, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾ [al-Anfal: 73].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except when you fear a danger from them⦆ (illa an tattaqu minhum taqatan). That is, except for one who fears their harm in some lands or at some times; he is permitted to show them outward caution (taqiyyah) but not in his inner self and intention. This is as al-Bukhari related from Abu ad-Darda', who said: "We smile in the faces of some people while our hearts curse them."

ath-Thawri said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "Taqiyyah is not by action; taqiyyah is only by the tongue." Similarly al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "Taqiyyah is only by the tongue." Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu ash-Sha'tha', ad-Dahhak and ar-Rabi' ibn Anas. What they said is supported by Allah's saying: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his faith, except one who is compelled while his heart is at peace with faith—but whoever opens his breast to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment﴾ [an-Nahl: 106].

Al-Bukhari said: al-Hasan said: "Taqiyyah is until the Day of Resurrection."

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾. That is, He warns you of His vengeance, meaning opposing Him and His severe punishment for whoever allies with His enemies and opposes His allies.

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾. That is, to Him is the return and the final destination, and He will recompense every doer for his deeds.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Husayn, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sabit, from 'Amr ibn Maymun [ibn Mihran] who said: Mu'adh ibn Jabal stood among us and said: "O Banu Awd, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you. You know that the return to Allah is either to Paradise or to the Fire."

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 29–30:

He, may He be blessed and exalted, informs His servants that He knows the secrets (sara'ir), the inner thoughts (dama'ir), and the outward appearances (zawahir), and that nothing among them is hidden from Him. Rather, His knowledge encompasses them in all states, moments, breaths and every time, and with everything in the heavens and the earth. Not even the weight of an atom escapes Him, nor anything smaller than that, in all the regions of the earth, the seas and the mountains. ﴿And He is Able over all things﴾, meaning: His power is executed in all of that.

This is a warning from Him to His servants to fear Him and to be wary, and not to commit what He has forbidden or what He dislikes of them, for He is Knowing of all their affairs and He is Able to hasten their punishment, even if He grants respite to whoever is granted respite among them. He gives respite, then He seizes with the seizing of the Mighty, the Able. Therefore He said after this: ﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present [and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that were a great distance]﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, all of the servant's deeds, good and evil, will be presented to him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he put forward and what he left behind﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13]. So whatever good deeds he sees will gladden and delight him, and whatever evil he sees will grieve and enrage him, and he will wish that he were free of it, and that there were a vast distance between them, just as he will say to his devil, who was his companion in this world and the one who emboldened him to do evil: ﴿Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts, for wretched is the companion﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 38].

Then He, exalted is He, said, emphasizing, threatening and warning: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾, meaning: He makes you fear His punishment. Then He said, giving hope to His servants so that they do not despair of His mercy and do not lose hope in His kindness: ﴿And Allah is Kind to the servants﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri (rahimahu Allah) said: From His kindness to them, He warned them of Himself. Others said: That is, He is Merciful to His creation, He loves for them that they remain upright upon His straight path and His upright religion, and that they follow His noble Messenger (ﷺ).

This noble verse judges everyone who claims to love Allah but does not follow the Muhammadan way. Such a person is lying in his claim in reality, unless he follows the Muhammadan Shari'ah and the Prophetic religion in all his statements and conditions. This is as established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected." For this reason Allah says: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾. That is: you will attain, beyond what you sought of your love for Him, His love for you, which is greater than the first. As one of the wise scholars said: "The matter is not that you love, but that you are loved."

Al-Hasan al-Basri and others among the early generations (al-Salaf) said: "A people claimed that they love Allah, so Allah tested them with this verse: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Is religion anything other than love and hatred? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾." Abu Zur'ah said: "This 'Abd al-A'la is munkar al-hadith" (a narrator whose narrations are rejected) [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (1/202). It was also narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (8/368) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/291), through 'Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir.

Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to their (Bukhari and Muslim's) conditions." Al-Dhahabi criticised him, saying: "In it is 'Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan. Al-Daraqutni said: He is not trustworthy."

Ibn Hibban said: "He narrates from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir what is not from his narrations; it is not permissible to argue with him in any case."

Al-'Uqayli said: "He brought munkar hadiths, none of which is preserved."]].

Then He said: ﴿and He will forgive you your sins; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is: by following the Messenger (ﷺ) you will obtain all of this through the blessing of his mission.

Then He said, commanding everyone, special and general: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger; but if they turn away﴾, that is, they oppose his command, ﴿then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾. He (may He be exalted) informs that He chose these houses over all the other people on earth. He chose Adam, peace be upon him, whom He created with His own hand, into whom He breathed of His spirit, to whom He made His angels prostrate, whom He taught the names of all things, and whom He settled in the Garden and then sent down from it, for the wisdom He had in that.
