And He chose the family of Abraham, and among them the master of mankind and the seal of the prophets absolutely, Muhammad (ﷺ), and the family of Imran. By Imran here is meant the father of Mary, daughter of Imran, the mother of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon them. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar [[In manuscript A: "Bashshar".]], may Allah have mercy on him, said: He is Imran ibn Yashm ibn Amun ibn Maisha ibn Hizqiya ibn Ahrioq ibn Yuthum ibn Azariya [[In manuscript W: "Azaziya".]] ibn Amsiya ibn Yawash ibn Ajrihu ibn Yazim ibn Yahfashat ibn Insha ibn Abiyan [[In manuscripts R and A: "Athan"; in manuscript W: "Ayyan".]] ibn Rukhay'am ibn Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both. Thus Jesus, peace be upon him, is from the offspring of Abraham, as its explanation will come in Surah al-An'am, God willing, and in Him is trust.

The wife of 'Imran, this one, is the mother of Maryam [daughter of 'Imran] [[Addition from ج, ر, أ, و.]] peace be upon her [[In و: "سم".]]. She was Hannah daughter of Faqudh. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: She was a woman who could not conceive. One day she saw a bird feeding its young, and she longed for a child. She called upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to grant her a child, and Allah answered her supplication. Her husband lay with her, and she conceived by him. When she was certain of the pregnancy, she vowed that the child would be ﴿dedicated﴾, meaning purely devoted to worship and to serving the Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House in Jerusalem). She said: ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering, so accept it from me. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ That is, the All-Hearing of my supplication, the All-Knowing of my intention. She did not know whether what was in her womb was male or female. ﴿So when she gave birth to her, she said, "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," and Allah knew best what she had delivered.﴾ It is recited with a raised taa' (ت) as the taa' of the speaker, meaning that this is part of her own words. It is also recited with a sukun on the taa', meaning that it is a statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And the male is not like the female.﴾ That is, in strength and vigour in worship and in serving the Masjid al-Aqsa. ﴿And I have named her Maryam.﴾ In this there is evidence for the permissibility of naming a child on the day of birth, as is apparent from the context, because it is a law from before us, and it is related as an affirmed practice. The Sunnah is established on this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), where he said: "A son has been born to me tonight, and I have named him after my father Ibrahim." Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim. [[Related by al-Bukhari as a suspended narration (mu'allaq), no. (1303), and by Muslim, no. (2315), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] Likewise, it is established in both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) that Anas ibn Malik took his brother, when his mother had given birth to him, to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he (ﷺ) rubbed his palate with a date (tahnik) and named him 'Abdullah. [[Related by al-Bukhari, no. (5470), and by Muslim, no. (2144).]] In Sahih al-Bukhari: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, a son has been born to me; what shall I name him?" He said, "Name your son 'Abd al-Rahman." [[In ج، ر: "ابنك".]] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6186), from the hadith of Jabir.]] It is also established in the Sahih that when Abu Usayd brought his son to him so that he might rub his palate, he (ﷺ) became distracted from him, so his father ordered him returned to their house. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was mentioned in the gathering, he named him al-Mundhir. [[Related by al-Bukhari, no. (6191), and by Muslim, no. (2149), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi.]]

As for the hadith of Qatadah, from al-Hasan al-Basri, from Samurah ibn Jundub, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every boy is held in pledge by his 'aqiqah; a sacrifice is made for him on his seventh day, he is named, and his head is shaved." It was related by Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan, and al-Tirmidhi declared it sound with this wording. It is also narrated as "and he is smeared with blood (yudamma)", and that is more firmly established and more accurately preserved. [[Al-Musnad (5/12), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2838), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1522), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/166), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3165). Al-Hasan has explicitly stated that he heard this hadith from Samurah; therefore al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (a good and sound hadith).]] And Allah knows best. Similarly, what al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar related in the Book of Genealogies: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) offered an 'aqiqah for his son Ibrahim on his seventh day and named him Ibrahim. Its chain does not establish it, and it contradicts what is in the Sahih. [[Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book "Tuhfat al-Mawdud fi Ahkam al-Mawlud", p. 67, after citing the statement of al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar from his teachers: "Thus said al-Zubayr, and that he named him on his seventh day; but the raised (marfu') hadith is more authentic than his statement and more deserving."]] Even if it were sound, it would be interpreted as meaning that he became known by that name on that day. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His statement, reporting about the mother of Maryam that she said: ﴿And I seek refuge for her with You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Shaytan.﴾ That is, I sought Allah's protection for her from the evil of Shaytan, and she sought protection for her offspring, who was her son 'Isa, peace be upon him. Allah answered her in this, as 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No child is born except that Shaytan touches him at the moment of his birth, so he cries out loudly from the touch of him, except Maryam and her son." Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿And I seek refuge for her with You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Shaytan.﴾" Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim [[Sahih al-Bukhari (4548) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2366).]] from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq. Ibn Jarir also related it from Ahmad ibn al-Faraj, from Baqiyyah, [from al-Zubaydi] [[Addition from أ، و.]] from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar terms. He also related a narration from the hadith of Qays, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No child is born except that Shaytan has squeezed him once or twice, except 'Isa son of Maryam and Maryam." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And I seek refuge for her with You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Shaytan.﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/339).]]

And from the hadith of al-'Ala' from his father, from Abu Hurayrah. Muslim related it from Abu al-Tahir, from Ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Abu Yunus, from Abu Hurayrah. Wahb also related it from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from 'Ajlan, mawla of al-Mishma'all, from Abu Hurayrah. Muhammad ibn Ishaq related it from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the essence of the hadith. Likewise, al-Layth ibn Sa'd related it from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, al-A'raj, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child of Adam is pricked by Shaytan in his side at the moment his mother gives birth to him, except 'Isa son of Maryam; he went to prick him but pricked the veil instead." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/342). Ahmad also related it in his Musnad (2/523) by way of Abu al-Zinad from al-A'raj, with the same wording.]]

The wife of 'Imran, this one, is the mother of Maryam [daughter of 'Imran] [[Addition from ج, ر, أ, و.]] peace be upon her [[In و: "سم".]]. She was Hannah daughter of Faqudh. The Sunnah is established on this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), where he said: "A son has been born to me tonight, and I have named him after my father Ibrahim." Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim. [[Related by al-Bukhari as a suspended narration (mu'allaq), no. (1303), and by Muslim, no. (2315), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] Likewise, it is established in both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) that Anas ibn Malik took his brother, when his mother had given birth to him, to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he (ﷺ) rubbed his palate with a date (tahnik) and named him 'Abdullah. [[Related by al-Bukhari, no. (5470), and by Muslim, no. (2144).]] In Sahih al-Bukhari: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, a son has been born to me; what shall I name him?" He said, "Name your son 'Abd al-Rahman." [[In ج، ر: "ابنك".]] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6186), from the hadith of Jabir.]] It is also established in the Sahih that when Abu Usayd brought his son to him so that he might rub his palate, he (ﷺ) became distracted from him, so his father ordered him returned to their house. (2838), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1522), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/166), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3165). Al-Hasan has explicitly stated that he heard this hadith from Samurah; therefore al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (a good and sound hadith).]] And Allah knows best. [[Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book "Tuhfat al-Mawdud fi Ahkam al-Mawlud", p. 67, after citing the statement of al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar from his teachers: "Thus said al-Zubayr, and that he named him on his seventh day; but the raised (marfu') hadith is more authentic than his statement and more deserving."]] Even if it were sound, it would be interpreted as meaning that he became known by that name on that day. * *

As for His statement, reporting about the mother of Maryam that she said: ﴿And I seek refuge for her with You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Shaytan.﴾ That is, I sought Allah's protection for her from the evil of Shaytan, and she sought protection for her offspring, who was her son 'Isa, peace be upon him. Allah answered her in this, as 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No child is born except that Shaytan touches him at the moment of his birth, so he cries out loudly from the touch of him, except Maryam and her son." Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿And I seek refuge for her with You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Shaytan.﴾" Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim [[Sahih al-Bukhari (4548) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2366).]] from the hadith of 'Abd al-Razzaq. Ibn Jarir also related it from Ahmad ibn al-Faraj, from Baqiyyah, [from al-Zubaydi] [[Addition from أ، و.]] from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in similar terms. He also related a narration from the hadith of Qays, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No child is born except that Shaytan has squeezed him once or twice, except 'Isa son of Maryam and Maryam." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And I seek refuge for her with You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Shaytan.﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/339).]]

And from the hadith of al-'Ala' from his father, from Abu Hurayrah. Muslim related it from Abu al-Tahir, from Ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Abu Yunus, from Abu Hurayrah. Wahb also related it from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from 'Ajlan, mawla of al-Mishma'all, from Abu Hurayrah. Muhammad ibn Ishaq related it from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the essence of the hadith. Likewise, al-Layth ibn Sa'd related it from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, al-A'raj, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child of Adam is pricked by Shaytan in his side at the moment his mother gives birth to him, except 'Isa son of Maryam; he went to prick him but pricked the veil instead." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/342). Ahmad also related it in his Musnad (2/523) by way of Abu al-Zinad from al-A'raj, with the same wording.]]

Our Lord informs us [in ج, ر, أ, و: "exalted is He"] that He accepted her from her mother, the vow, and that He ﴿made her grow in a goodly growth﴾, meaning He made her of a comely form and a delightful appearance, facilitated for her the means of acceptance, and joined her with the righteous among His servants, that she might learn from them goodness, knowledge, and religion. And for this reason He said: ﴿and Zechariah took charge of her﴾. In another reading: ﴿and he made Zechariah her guardian﴾, with the fa' doubled and Zechariah in the accusative as the object, meaning He made him her guardian (kafil).

Ibn Ishaq said: "This was only because she was an orphan." Others mentioned that the Children of Israel were struck by a year of drought, so Zechariah took charge of Maryam for this reason. There is no contradiction between the two statements. And Allah knows best.

Allah decreed that Zechariah be her guardian for her happiness, so that she might acquire from him abundant beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds; and because he was the husband of her maternal aunt, as Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Jarir [and others] [addition from و] mentioned. It was also said: he was the husband of her sister, as occurs in the Sahih: "Then I found Yahya and Isa, who are cousins (ibn al-khala)." This may also be applied, by extension, to what Ibn Ishaq mentioned. On this view, she was in the custody of her maternal aunt. It is firmly established in the Two Sahihs that the Prophet (ﷺ) ruled concerning Amara bint Hamza that she should be in the custody of her maternal aunt, the wife of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and said: "The maternal aunt is in the position of a mother."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2699) and Sahih Muslim no. (1783).]]

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed us of her nobility and eminence in the place of her worship, saying: ﴿Whenever Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary (mihrab), he found provision with her﴾. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Sha'tha', Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Atiyah al-Awfi, and al-Suddi [and al-Sha'bi] [addition from ج، أ] said: meaning he found with her summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer. From Mujahid: ﴿he found provision with her﴾ means knowledge, or he said: scrolls containing knowledge. Ibn Abi Hatim related it, but the first view is more sound. This indicates the miracles (karamat) of the friends of Allah, and there are many similar instances in the Sunnah.

When Zechariah saw this with her, ﴿he said: O Maryam, from where is this for you?﴾, meaning: from where does this come to you? ﴿She said: It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Sahl ibn Zanjalah narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went for days without eating any food, until it grieved him. He went around the houses of his wives, but found nothing with any of them. Then he came to Fatimah and said: "My daughter, do you have anything I may eat, for I am hungry?" She said: "No, by Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you." When he left her, a neighbour of hers sent her two loaves and a piece of meat. She took them and placed them in a bowl of hers, and said: "By Allah, I will prefer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over myself and those with me." They were all in need of a full meal. So she sent Hasan or Husayn to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he returned to her. She said to him: "May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, Allah has sent something, and I have kept it aside for you." He said: "Bring it, my daughter." She said: "So I brought him the bowl. She uncovered the bowl, and behold, it was full of bread and meat. When she looked at it she was amazed, and knew that it was a blessing from Allah, so she praised Allah and sent blessings upon His Prophet, and presented it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he saw it, he praised Allah and said: "From where is this for you, my daughter?" She said: "O father, ﴿It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾" He praised Allah and said: "Praise be to Allah who has made you, my daughter, resemble the mistress of the women of the Children of Israel, for whenever Allah provided her with something and she was asked about it, she would say: ﴿It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for 'Ali [and they carried it]. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ate, and 'Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, Husayn, all the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), and his entire household ate until they were satisfied. She said: The bowl remained as it was, so she distributed its remainder among all the neighbours, and Allah placed in it blessing and abundant good.[[Musnad Abi Ya'la as cited in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah by Ibn Hajar (4/74). Its chain includes 'Abdullah ibn Salih, who is criticised, and Ibn Lahi'ah, whom the majority deemed weak.]]

When Zakariyya (upon him peace) saw that Allah, exalted is He, provides Maryam (upon her peace) with winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter, he then longed for offspring. Although he was an elderly man whose bones had weakened and whose head had turned white with grey hair, and although his wife was also old and barren, nevertheless, in spite of all this, he asked his Lord and called upon Him in a low voice, saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring﴾, i.e., from Your presence, ﴿good offspring﴾, i.e., a righteous child, ﴿Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication﴾.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the chamber﴾, i.e., the angels addressed him directly, speaking to him so that he heard it, while he was standing in prayer in the chamber of his worship, the place of his solitude, the place of his private communion and prayer. Then He informed of what the angels gave him good news of: ﴿That Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya﴾, i.e., of a son who will be born to you from your loins, whose name is Yahya. Qatadah and others said: he was named Yahya only because Allah gave him life (ahyahu) through faith.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾, al-Awfi and others narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu al-Sha'tha', al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Dahhak and others said regarding this verse, ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾: i.e., confirming 'Isa ibn Maryam. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: he was the first to confirm 'Isa ibn Maryam. Qatadah said: and he followed his way and his method. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying, ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾: Yahya and 'Isa were cousins, and the mother of Yahya used to say to Maryam: "I find that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb." That is his confirmation of him: his confirmation of him while in his mother's womb. He was the first to confirm 'Isa, and "a word of Allah" is 'Isa, and he (Yahya) is older than 'Isa (upon them both peace). Al-Suddi also said likewise.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and noble (sayyidan)﴾, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said: it means the forbearing (al-halim). Qatadah said: a sayyid in knowledge and worship. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Thawri and al-Dahhak said: the sayyid is the forbearing, the God-fearing. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: he is the jurist, the scholar. 'Atiyyah said: a sayyid in his character and his religion. 'Ikrimah said: he is the one whom anger does not overcome. Ibn Zayd said: he is the noble. Mujahid and others said: he is honored by Allah, mighty and majestic.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and chaste (hasuran)﴾, it was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Sha'tha' and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi that they said: it is one who does not approach women. From Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas: it is one who cannot father children. Al-Dahhak said: it is one who has no child and no semen.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Jarir informed us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding "hasur": the one who does not emit semen. Ibn Abi Hatim has narrated in this matter a very strange hadith. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ghalib al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to me, 'Ubadah (i.e., Ibn al-'Awwam) narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Ibn al-'As (Abdullah or 'Amr is uncertain), from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying: ﴿and noble and chaste﴾. He said: Then he took up something from the earth and said: "His male organ was like this." [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/241); Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (11/561) narrated it through Yahya ibn Sa'id with this chain.]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib narrate from Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: "There is no one among the creation of Allah whom He will meet with a sin except Yahya ibn Zakariyya." Then Sa'id recited: ﴿and noble and chaste﴾. Then he took up something from the earth and said: "The hasur is one whose male organ is like this," and Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan pointed with the tip of his index finger. This is a mawquf report, and it is stronger in chain than the marfu' report; indeed, the soundness of the marfu' report is open to question. And Allah, glory be to Him, knows best.

Qadi 'Iyad said in his book al-Shifa': Know that Allah, exalted is He, praised Yahya by describing him as hasur, and it is not as some have said: that he was a hayyub (one who avoids women), or that he had no male organ. Rather, the expert exegetes and the critical scholars denied this, and said: this is a deficiency and a defect, and it is not fitting for the prophets, upon them peace. Its meaning is rather that he was protected from sins, i.e., he did not commit them, as if he were restrained from them. It was also said: restraining himself from desires. And it was said: he had no desire for women.

From this it has become clear to you that the inability to marry is a deficiency, and that the excellence lies in the desire being present and then his suppressing it, either through striving, as with 'Isa, or through sufficiency from Allah, mighty and majestic, as with Yahya, upon him peace. Then it is a right for one who is capable of it, who fulfills what is obligatory regarding it, and whom it does not distract from his Lord, to a lofty rank, and that is the rank of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, whose many wives did not distract him from the worship of his Lord; rather, that increased him in worship, through their protection, his provision for them, his acquiring for them, and his guiding them. Indeed, he stated that they were not among the portions of his worldly life, though they were among the worldly portions of others, saying: "Beloved to me of your world are..."

That is his wording. The intent is that He praised Yahya by describing him as hasur, not that he does not approach women. Rather its meaning, as he and others said, is that he was protected from indecencies and filth, and that this does not prevent his marrying lawful women, having relations with them and fathering children by them. Indeed, the existence of offspring for him may be understood from the earlier supplication of Zakariyya, where he said: ﴿so grant me from Yourself good offspring﴾, as if he said: a son who has descendants, progeny and lineage. And Allah, glory be to Him, knows best.

Then the Prophet ﷺ bent down to a speck of dust from the earth, took it and said: "His male organ was like this speck."]

His saying: ﴿and a prophet from among the righteous﴾. This is a second glad tiding of Yahya's prophethood after the glad tiding of his birth, and it is higher than the first, like His saying, exalted is He, to the mother of Musa: ﴿Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾ [al-Qasas: 7]. When Zakariyya, upon him peace, became certain of this glad tiding, he began to wonder at the existence of a child from him after old age: ﴿He said: My Lord, how will I have a boy when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?﴾ He (the angel) said: ﴿Thus Allah does what He wills﴾, i.e., such is the great command of Allah; nothing can overpower Him, and no matter is too great for Him.

﴿He said: My Lord, make for me a sign﴾, i.e., a sign by which I may know the existence of the child from me. ﴿He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture﴾, i.e., by signs, you being unable to speak while you are sound and healthy, as in His saying: ﴿for three nights, sound﴾ [Maryam: 10]. Then he was commanded to increase in remembrance, gratitude and glorification in this state, so He said: ﴿And remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning﴾. Another part on expanding this topic will come at the beginning of Surah Maryam, if Allah, exalted is He, wills.

This is an announcement from Allah, the Exalted, of what the angels said to Maryam, peace be upon her, by Allah's command to them: that Allah has chosen her (iṣṭafāhā), meaning He selected her for her great worship, her asceticism, her nobility, and her purity from impurities and whisperings [[In A: "al-Wasawis."]]. He chose her a second time, again and again, for her greatness above the women of the worlds.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾. He said: Abu Hurayrah used to narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "The best of women who ride camels are the women of Quraysh: they are the most tender toward a child in its infancy and the most attentive to a husband in what is in his hand. Yet Maryam, daughter of 'Imran, never rode a camel." They did not narrate it through this chain except Muslim, for he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd, both from 'Abd al-Razzaq, with this chain [[Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (1/128), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (200). Al-Bukhari also narrated it in his Sahih, no. (5082), by another chain: he narrated it from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, with it.]].

Hisham ibn 'Urwah said, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The best of its women is Maryam daughter of 'Imran, and the best of its women is Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid." They both narrated it in the two Sahihs, through the hadith of Hisham, with the like of it [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3815), (3432), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2430).]].

al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Bakr ibn Zanjawayh informed us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us [[In A: "from."]], Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Enough for you from the women of the worlds are Maryam daughter of 'Imran, Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid, Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, and Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh." al-Tirmidhi alone narrated it and graded it sahih [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3878).]].

'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far al-Razi said, from his father, who said: Thabit al-Bunani used to narrate from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The best of the women of the worlds are four: Maryam daughter of 'Imran, Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatimah daughter of the Messenger of Allah [ﷺ]" [[Addition from J and A.]]. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (4/217) through 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, who said: Thabit al-Bunani... and mentioned it. Ibn 'Adi said after citing this hadith: "He is not followed in some of his narrations."

It has been followed: al-Khatib narrated it in Tarikh Baghdad (9/404) through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Thabit, with it. Abu Ja'far al-Razi, 'Isa ibn Mahan, is spoken of, but it is narrated from Anas by another chain: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas, with it. Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq (11/430), and from his route Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. (2222), "Mawarid."]].

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, through the route of Shu'bah, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women only three have reached perfection: Maryam daughter of 'Imran, Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, and Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid. And the excellence of 'A'ishah over women is like the excellence of tharid over the rest of food" [[The Hafiz Ibn Kathir also mentioned it in his book al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah (2/56).]].

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Adam al-'Asqalani narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us, I heard Murrah al-Hamdani with a hadith from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women none has reached perfection except Maryam daughter of 'Imran and Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh." The group [of compilers] narrated it, except Abu Dawud, through several routes from Shu'bah with it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/397). Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih, nos. (3411), (3433); Muslim, no. (2431); al-Tirmidhi, no. (1834); al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra, no. (8356); and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (3280).]]. The wording of al-Bukhari is: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women none has reached perfection except Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh and Maryam daughter of 'Imran. And indeed the excellence of 'A'ishah over women is like the excellence of tharid over the rest of food."

I have exhaustively traced the routes and wordings of this hadith in the story of 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon them both, in my book "al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah," and to Allah belongs all praise and grace [[al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah (2/55-57).]].

Then He, the Exalted, informed about the angels: that they commanded her to increase in worship, humility, submission, prostration, bowing, and diligence in works for her, because of the matter Allah willed concerning her, which He had decreed and decided: a trial for her and an elevation in both abodes, through the great power of Allah that He manifested in her, when He created from her a child without a father. So He said, the Exalted: ﴿O Maryam, be devout to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾. As for qunut, it is obedience with humility, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿Rather, to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 116] [[In A and W: (And to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him) [al-Rum: 26].]].

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the route of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, with it, and in it there is a strangeness [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/261) and Tafsir al-Tabari (6/403). Mujahid said: Maryam, peace be upon her, would stand until her ankles swelled. Al-Hasan said rather: it means worship your Lord. ﴿And prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾, meaning: be among them.

al-Awza'i said: She remained in her sanctuary bowing, prostrating, and standing, until the yellow water came down onto her feet. May Allah be pleased with her.

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned in her biography, through the route of Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Kudaymi, about whom there is criticism: 'Ali ibn Bahr ibn Barri narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, regarding His words: ﴿O Maryam, be devout to your Lord and prostrate﴾: he said: She prostrated until the yellow water came down into her eyes [[Ta'rikh Dimashq by Ibn 'Asakir (p. 369), Taraajim al-Nisa' ed. al-Majma' al-'Ilmi bi-Dimashq, and Mukhtasar Ta'rikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (26/78).]].

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned: al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Damrah narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Maryam, peace be upon her, used to bathe every night.

Then He, the Exalted, said to His Messenger [peace and blessings be upon him] [[Addition from W.]], after having informed him of the clear reality of the matter: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you﴾, meaning: We relate it to you. ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would be the guardian of Maryam, nor were you with them when they disputed﴾, meaning: You were not with them, O Muhammad, so that you could inform them through direct observation of what occurred. Rather, Allah informed you of it as if you had been present and witnessing what took place when they drew lots over who would take charge of Maryam, out of their desire for the reward.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn [In A: "Abi."] Jurayj, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, that he informed him from 'Ikrimah, and Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Then Maryam's mother set out with her, meaning Maryam's mother with Maryam, carrying her in her cloths, to the sons of al-Kahin ibn Harun, brother of Musa, peace be upon them both. He said: At that time they were in charge in Bayt al-Maqdis, in what is near the Ka'bah's keepers. She said to them: Take this consecrated one, for I have dedicated her and she is my daughter, and a menstruating woman does not enter the church. Shall I not return her to my house? They said: This is the daughter of our imam, [for 'Imran used to lead them in prayer] and the keeper of our offerings. Zakariyya said: Hand her to me, for her aunt is under me. They said: Our hearts will not be content; she is the daughter of our imam. So that is when they drew lots with their pens, those with which they write the Torah, and Zakariyya's lot came up, so he took charge of her [[I did not find it in the printed Tafsir al-Tabari.]].

'Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others besides them, also mentioned, with some of their narrations merging into others, that they went to the River Jordan and drew lots there, casting their pens into it. Whoever's pen remained in the flow of the water would be her guardian. They cast their pens, and the water carried them all away except the pen of Zakariyya, which remained. It is said that it went upstream, cutting against the current of the water. And he was, along with that, their eldest and their chief, their scholar, their imam, and their prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, above all the prophets [[In J and A: "the prophets."]] [and the messengers] [[Addition from A.]].

It has been followed: al-Khatib narrated it in Tarikh Baghdad (9/404) through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd, who said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Thabit, with it. Abu Ja'far al-Razi, 'Isa ibn Mahan, is spoken of, but it is narrated from Anas by another chain: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas, with it. Musannaf 'Abd al-Razzaq (11/430), and from his route Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. (2222), "Mawarid."]].

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, through the route of Shu'bah, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women only three have reached perfection: Maryam daughter of 'Imran, Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, and Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid. And the excellence of 'A'ishah over women is like the excellence of tharid over the rest of food" [[The Hafiz Ibn Kathir also mentioned it in his book al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah (2/56).]].

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Adam al-'Asqalani narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us, I heard Murrah al-Hamdani with a hadith from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women none has reached perfection except Maryam daughter of 'Imran and Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh." The group [of compilers] narrated it, except Abu Dawud, through several routes from Shu'bah with it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (6/397). Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih, nos. (3411), (3433); Muslim, no. (2431); al-Tirmidhi, no. (1834); al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra, no. (8356); and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (3280).]]. The wording of al-Bukhari is: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women none has reached perfection except Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh and Maryam daughter of 'Imran. And indeed the excellence of 'A'ishah over women is like the excellence of tharid over the rest of food."

I have exhaustively traced the routes and wordings of this hadith in the story of 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon them both, in my book "al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah," and to Allah belongs all praise and grace [[al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah (2/55-57).]].

Then He, the Exalted, informed about the angels: that they commanded her to increase in worship, humility, submission, prostration, bowing, and diligence in works for her, because of the matter Allah willed concerning her, which He had decreed and decided: a trial for her and an elevation in both abodes, through the great power of Allah that He manifested in her, when He created from her a child without a father. So He said, the Exalted: ﴿O Maryam, be devout to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾. As for qunut, it is obedience with humility, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿Rather, to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 116] [[In A and W: (And to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him) [al-Rum: 26].]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me: that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Every letter in the Qur'an in which qunut is mentioned means obedience." Ibn Jarir narrated it from the route of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, with it, and in it there is a strangeness [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/261) and Tafsir al-Tabari (6/403). Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (3/75). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/320): "Its chain includes Ibn Lahi'ah, who is weak." Also in it is Darraj, of whom Ahmad said: "His hadiths are munkar (rejected)." al-Nasa'i and Abu Hatim declared him weak. Abu Dawud said: "His hadiths are sound except what is from Abu al-Haytham from Abu Sa'id."]].

Mujahid said: Maryam, peace be upon her, would stand until her ankles swelled. Qunut is: prolonging the bowing in prayer, meaning complying with His words, the Exalted: ﴿O Maryam, be devout to your Lord﴾. Al-Hasan said rather: it means worship your Lord. ﴿And prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾, meaning: be among them.

al-Awza'i said: She remained in her sanctuary bowing, prostrating, and standing, until the yellow water came down onto her feet. May Allah be pleased with her.

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned in her biography, through the route of Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Kudaymi, about whom there is criticism: 'Ali ibn Bahr ibn Barri narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, regarding His words: ﴿O Maryam, be devout to your Lord and prostrate﴾: he said: She prostrated until the yellow water came down into her eyes [[Ta'rikh Dimashq by Ibn 'Asakir (p. 369), Taraajim al-Nisa' ed. al-Majma' al-'Ilmi bi-Dimashq, and Mukhtasar Ta'rikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (26/78).]].

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned: al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Damrah narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Maryam, peace be upon her, used to bathe every night.

Then He, the Exalted, said to His Messenger [peace and blessings be upon him] [[Addition from W.]], after having informed him of the clear reality of the matter: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you﴾, meaning: We relate it to you. ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would be the guardian of Maryam, nor were you with them when they disputed﴾, meaning: You were not with them, O Muhammad, so that you could inform them through direct observation of what occurred. Rather, Allah informed you of it as if you had been present and witnessing what took place when they drew lots over who would take charge of Maryam, out of their desire for the reward.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn [In A: "Abi."] Jurayj, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, that he informed him from 'Ikrimah, and Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Then Maryam's mother set out with her, meaning Maryam's mother with Maryam, carrying her in her cloths, to the sons of al-Kahin ibn Harun, brother of Musa, peace be upon them both. He said: At that time they were in charge in Bayt al-Maqdis, in what is near the Ka'bah's keepers. She said to them: Take this consecrated one, for I have dedicated her and she is my daughter, and a menstruating woman does not enter the church. Shall I not return her to my house? They said: This is the daughter of our imam, [for 'Imran used to lead them in prayer] and the keeper of our offerings. Zakariyya said: Hand her to me, for her aunt is under me. They said: Our hearts will not be content; she is the daughter of our imam. So that is when they drew lots with their pens, those with which they write the Torah, and Zakariyya's lot came up, so he took charge of her [[I did not find it in the printed Tafsir al-Tabari.]].

'Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others besides them, also mentioned, with some of their narrations merging into others, that they went to the River Jordan and drew lots there, casting their pens into it. Whoever's pen remained in the flow of the water would be her guardian. They cast their pens, and the water carried them all away except the pen of Zakariyya, which remained. It is said that it went upstream, cutting against the current of the water. And he was, along with that, their eldest and their chief, their scholar, their imam, and their prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, above all the prophets [[In J and A: "the prophets."]] [and the messengers] [[Addition from A.]].

This is a message from the angels to Maryam, peace be upon her, giving her the good news that a great son will be born to her, one of high standing.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When the angels said: "O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good news of a Word from Him"﴾. That is, [a son] whose existence will be by a word from Allah, that is, by His saying to him "Be!" and he is. This is the explanation of His saying: ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 39], as the majority of scholars (al-Jumhur) have stated, as has already been explained. ﴿His name will be the Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam﴾, meaning that he will be known by this in this world, and the believers will recognise him by it.

The Messiah (al-Masih) was so named. Some of the early generations (al-Salaf) said: because of his frequent wandering (siyaha). It was also said: because he had smooth feet (masih al-qadamayn), meaning they had no arch (akhmas). It was also said: because whenever he wiped (masaha) one of those afflicted with defects, he would be healed by Allah's permission, the Exalted.

* *

His saying ﴿'Isa son of Maryam﴾ attributes him to his mother, since he had no father. ﴿Honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and one of those brought near﴾ means that he has honour and standing with Allah in this world, through the law (al-shari'a) that Allah reveals to him and the Scripture that He sends down to him, and other things with which He grants him favour. In the Hereafter he will intercede with Allah for whomever He permits him to intercede for, and his intercession will be accepted, following the example of his brothers among the Resolute Messengers (Ulu al-'Azm), may the blessings of Allah be upon them all.

* *

His saying ﴿and he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity﴾ means that he will call to the worship of Allah alone, with no partner, while still a child, as a miracle and a sign, and in his maturity, when Allah reveals to him that. ﴿And [he is] among the righteous﴾ means that in his speech and his action he has sound knowledge and righteous deeds.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn Qusayt, from Muhammad ibn Shurahbil, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No infant has spoken in the cradle except 'Isa and the companion of Juraij."[[Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his Tafsir (2/272, 273) through his father, from Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq with this chain.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu al-Saqr Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Qaza'a narrated to us; al-Husayn, meaning al-Marwazi, narrated to us; Jarir, meaning Ibn Hazim, narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Only three have spoken in the cradle: 'Isa, a child at the time of Juraij, and another child."[[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/272). It is also narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (3436) (2482), and by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2550), through Jarir ibn Hazim, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah with this chain.]]

When Maryam heard the angels' good news to her from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, she said in her private supplication: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a son when no man has touched me?﴾ She means: how can this child come into being from me, when I am not a married woman, I have no intention of marrying, and I am not unchaste? Far be it from Allah! Then the angel, speaking from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, answered this question: ﴿Thus Allah creates what He wills﴾, meaning that this is the way of Allah's great command, and nothing can overpower Him. Here He used the word "creates" (yakhluqu) and did not say "does" (yaf'alu), as in the story of Zakariya. Rather, He stated here explicitly that He creates, so that no doubt would remain, and He confirmed this by His saying: ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it "Be," and it is﴾, meaning that it is not delayed at all, but comes into being immediately after the command without any interval, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [Al-Qamar: 50], meaning: We command only once, with no repetition (mathnawiyya) in it, and so that thing comes swiftly, like a glance of the eye.

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the completion of the angels' glad tidings to Maryam (Mary) concerning her son 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him: that Allah will teach him ﴿the Book and the Wisdom﴾. Apparently, what is meant by "the Book" here is writing. As for "wisdom" (hikmah), its explanation has already been discussed in Surah al-Baqarah, verse 129.

﴿And the Torah and the Gospel﴾. The Torah (Tawrat) is the Book that Allah revealed to Musa (Moses) ibn 'Imran. The Gospel (Injil) is that which Allah revealed to 'Isa, peace be upon them both. 'Isa, peace be upon him, used to memorise this and that.

His saying: ﴿and a messenger to the Children of Israel﴾, meaning that He will make him a messenger to the Children of Israel, saying to them: ﴿Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: that I create for you from clay the likeness of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission﴾. This is what he would do: he would shape from clay the form of a bird, then blow into it, and it would fly before their eyes by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who made this a miracle indicating that Allah had sent him.

﴿And I heal the one born blind (al-akmah)﴾. It was said: he is one who sees by day but not by night. It was said the reverse. It was said: he is the one with weak eyesight (al-a'sha). It was said: he is the one with watery eyes (al-a'mash). It was said: he is the one who was born blind. The last of these is closer to the truth, because it is more eloquent as a miracle and stronger as a challenge. ﴿And the leper﴾ is well known.

﴿And I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission﴾. Many scholars said: Allah sent every prophet with a miracle suited to the people of his time. The dominant feature of the time of Musa, peace be upon him, was magic and the veneration of magicians, so Allah sent him with a miracle that dazzled the eyes and bewildered every magician. When they were certain that it came from the Mighty, the Compeller, they submitted to Islam and became among the righteous. As for 'Isa, peace be upon him, he was sent in a time of physicians and people of natural science, so he brought them signs that no one could match unless he were supported by the One who ordained the Shari'ah (law). How could a physician have the power to give life to inanimate matter, or to cure the blind and the leper, or to raise one who is in his grave until the Day of Calling Out? Likewise, Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent in a time of eloquent speakers, rhetoricians and masters of poetry. He brought them a Book from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, such that if mankind and the jinn gathered to produce its like, or ten surahs like it, or one surah like it, they would never be able to, even if they helped one another. That is only because the speech of the Lord is never resembled by the speech of creation.

﴿And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses﴾, meaning: I inform you of what one of you has eaten now, and what he has stored in his house for tomorrow. ﴿Indeed in that﴾, meaning in all of that, ﴿is a sign for you﴾, meaning as proof of my truthfulness in what I have brought you, ﴿if you are believers﴾.

﴿And confirming that which is before me of the Torah﴾, meaning: affirming and establishing it for them. ﴿And to make lawful for you some of that which was forbidden to you﴾. In this is an indication that 'Isa, peace be upon him, abrogated some of the Shari'ah of the Torah. This is the correct of the two opinions. Among the scholars, some said he abrogated nothing from it; rather, he made lawful for them some of what they had disputed and erred about, so he uncovered for them what was hidden in that matter, as He said in another verse: ﴿and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ﴾ (Az-Zukhruf: 63). And Allah knows best.

Then he said: ﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾, meaning with a proof and an indication of my truthfulness in what I say to you. ﴿So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him﴾, meaning: I and you are equal in servitude to Him, in submission and humility before Him. ﴿This is a straight path﴾.

This is what he would do: he would shape from clay the form of a bird, then blow into it, and it would fly before their eyes by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who made this a miracle indicating that Allah had sent him.

It was said: he is the one with watery eyes (al-a'mash). It was said: he is the one who was born blind. The last of these is closer to the truth, because it is more eloquent as a miracle and stronger as a challenge. ﴿And the leper﴾ is well known.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verse 55–58:

The commentators differed concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, I will take you in death and raise you to Me﴾. Qatadah and others said: This is of the (grammatical) "front and back" (al-muqaddam wa'l-mu'akhkhar, inversion of order). Its meaning is: "Indeed, I will raise you to Me and cause you to die (mutawaffika) afterward," meaning after that.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿I will take you in death﴾ means: I will cause you to die (mumītuka).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from one who is not accused (of falsehood), from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Allah caused him to die for three hours of the day, when Allah raised him to Himself.

Ibn Ishaq said: The Christians claim that Allah caused him to die for seven hours, then brought him back to life.

Ishaq ibn Bishr [in A: "Bashir"] related from Idris, from Wahb: Allah caused him to die for three days, then resurrected him, then raised him.

Mattar al-Warraq said: "Mutawaffika" means: taking you from the world, and it is not a death of dying. Similarly Ibn Jarir said: His taking him (tawaffi) is His raising him.

Most of the scholars said: What is meant by "wafah" (taking in death) here is sleep, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And it is He who takes you in the night [and knows what you have committed by day]﴾ [al-An'am: 60], and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others until a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought﴾ [az-Zumar: 42]. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say, when he rose from sleep: "All praise is for Allah, who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection." And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander, and for their saying: "Indeed, we killed the Messiah, ʿIsa son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah"﴾, up to His saying [the Exalted] ﴿And they did not kill him, with certainty. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise. And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness﴾ [an-Nisa: 156–159]. The pronoun in His saying ﴿before his death﴾ refers back to ʿIsa, peace be upon him; that is: there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in ʿIsa before the death of ʿIsa, and that is when he descends to the earth before the Day of Resurrection, as will be explained later. At that time all the People of the Scripture will believe in him, for he will abolish the jizyah and will accept nothing but Islam.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas related to us, from al-Hasan, that he said concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, I will take you in death﴾, meaning the death of sleep: He raised him in his sleep. Al-Hasan said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Jews: "Indeed ʿIsa did not die, and indeed he will return to you before the Day of Resurrection." [Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/296); and al-Tabari in his Tafsir (6/455) narrated it through ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, from al-Hasan, as a mursal report.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And purify you from those who disbelieve﴾, that is, by My raising you up to the heaven. ﴿And I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾. And so it came to pass: when Allah raised the Messiah, peace be upon him, to the heaven, his companions split into sects after him. Among them were those who believed in what Allah sent him with, that he is the servant of Allah, His Messenger, and the son of His handmaiden. Among them were those who exaggerated concerning him and made him the son of Allah. Others said: He is Allah. Others said: He is the third of three. Allah related their sayings in the Qur'an and refuted each group. They remained thus for about three hundred years. Then there emerged for them a king from the kings of the Greeks called Constantine, who entered the religion of Christianity. It was said: (he did so as) a trick to corrupt it, for he was a philosopher; and it was said: (it was) out of ignorance on his part. Yet he altered for them the religion of the Messiah and distorted it, adding to it and subtracting from it. Laws were laid down for them, and "the great trust" (al-amanah al-kabirah), which is the lowly betrayal, was instituted. In his time the flesh of swine was made lawful; they prayed toward the East; they fashioned images of the churches for him; and they increased their fasting by ten days on account of a sin he had committed, so they claim. The religion of the Messiah became the religion of Constantine, except that he built for them churches, sanctuaries, monasteries and hermitages exceeding twelve thousand places of worship, and he built the city named after him, and the royal sect among them followed him. In all of this they dominated the Jews, and Allah supported them over them because they were nearer to the truth than they, although all of them are disbelievers, upon whom be the curses of Allah.

When Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, those who believed in him, believing in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers in the true manner, were the followers of every prophet upon the face of the earth, since they affirmed the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, the Seal of the Messengers and the master of the children of Adam, who called them to affirm all of the truth. Thus they were more entitled to every prophet than his own community, who claim that they follow his creed and way, despite having altered and changed (it).

Moreover, even if none of that had been the case, Allah would have abrogated, by His law (shari'ah) brought by Muhammad ﷺ, the law of all the messengers, with the true religion which is not changed nor altered until the Hour arrives, and which remains established, victorious and manifest over every religion. For this reason Allah granted His companions the eastern and western parts of the earth, they acquired all the kingdoms, all the states submitted to them, they broke Chosroes and subdued Caesar, and they seized their treasures and spent them in the way of Allah, as their Prophet informed them from their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, in His saying: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, as He made successors those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely change their state after their fear into security﴾ [an-Nur: 65], and so on. For this reason, when they were the true believers in the Messiah, they took the land of Syria from the Christians and expelled them to the Romans, who sought refuge in their city of Constantinople. Islam and its people remain above them until the Day of Resurrection. The Truthful, the Believed (al-Sadiq al-Masduq) has informed his community that their last ones will conquer Constantinople, and will seize the wealth in it, and will slay the Romans with a very great slaughter, the like of which people have not seen and will not see its equal afterward. It is not befitting for Allah to take a son; Glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Maryam: 34–35]. And here He, the Exalted, said.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah﴾ in terms of Allah's power, since He created him without a father, ﴿is like the likeness of Adam﴾, for Allah created him without a father or a mother. Rather, ﴿He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ The One who created Adam is able to create Jesus all the more so and more fittingly. If claiming sonship for Jesus is permissible because he was created without a father, then it is all the more permissible for Adam. It is known by consensus that this is false, so the claim regarding Jesus is even more false and its corruption even more evident. But the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, willed to show His power to His creation when He created Adam neither from a male nor from a female, created Eve from a male without a female, and created Jesus from a female without a male, just as He created the rest of creation from a male and a female. For this reason God said in Surah Maryam: ﴿And that We may make him a sign for the people﴾ [Maryam: 21].

Here He also said: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾ That is, this statement is the truth concerning Jesus, from which there is no turning away and no correct position other than it. What lies beyond the truth but error?

Then God, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), commanded him to invoke a curse (mubahalah) upon whoever opposed the truth concerning the matter of Jesus after the clear proof had appeared: ﴿Then whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves,﴾ that is, let us present them in the state of mubahalah ﴿then let us earnestly pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars﴾ that is, let us call down a curse upon one another ﴿so let the curse of Allah be upon the liars﴾ that is, from us or from you.

The occasion of revelation of this mubahalah, and of what precedes it from the beginning of the surah up to this point, concerned the delegation of Najran. When the Christians arrived, they began to dispute about Jesus and to assert about him what they asserted of sonship and divinity. So Allah revealed the opening of this surah in refutation of them, as Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and others have mentioned.

Ibn Ishaq said in his well-known Sirah and others said: A delegation of the Christians of Najran, sixty riders, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among them were fourteen men of their nobles to whom their affairs returned: al-Aqib, whose name was Abd al-Masih; al-Sayyid, who was al-Ayham; Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, brother of Bakr ibn Wa'il; Uways (or Aws) ibn al-Harith; Zayd; Qays; Yazid; Nabih; Khuwaylid; Amr; Khalid; Abd Allah; and Yuhannis.

The affairs of these men returned to three of them: al-Aqib, who was the leader of the people, their counsellor and the one whose opinion they never departed from; al-Sayyid, who was their scholar, the owner of their caravan and their gathering; and Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, who was their bishop, their rabbi, their imam and the master of their schools. He was an Arab from the Bakr ibn Wa'il, but he had become a Christian. The Romans and their kings held him in high esteem, honoured him, built churches for him, provided for him and gave him servants, because of the firmness they knew of him in their religion. He had known well the matter, the qualities and the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the earlier scriptures he knew, but his ignorance led him to persist in Christianity, because of the honour and high standing he enjoyed among its adherents.

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, saying: They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah and entered upon him in his mosque after he had prayed the afternoon prayer. They wore striped garments: robes and cloaks, in the splendour of the men of Bani al-Harith ibn Ka'b. He said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who saw them said: We have not seen a delegation like them after them. Their prayer time came, so they stood in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and prayed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave them." So they prayed facing the east.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them, and among them Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah and al-Aqib Abd al-Masih, or al-Sayyid al-Ayham, who were upon the religion of the king regarding Christianity, despite their differing positions. They said: He is Allah; they said: He is the son of Allah; and they said: He is the third of three. Exalted is Allah far above that by a great exaltation. And this is also the position of Christianity. They argued for their saying "He is Allah" that he used to give life to the dead, heal the sick, inform of the unseen, and create from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathe into it so that it became a bird, all of this by the command of Allah, "and that He may make him a sign for the people."

They argued for their saying that he is the son of Allah, saying: He had no known father, and he spoke in the cradle with something no one of the children of Adam had done before him.

They argued for their saying that he is the third of three by the words of Allah, "We have done," "We have commanded," "We have created," and "We have decreed." They said: If He were one, He would have said only "I have done, I have decreed, I have commanded and I have created." But rather He is Himself, and Jesus, and Mary, and all of this in their saying has been revealed in the Qur'an.

When the two rabbis (ḥabrān) spoke with him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Submit." They said: We have submitted. He said: "You have not submitted, so submit." They said: Indeed, we submitted before you. He said: "You have lied. What prevents you from Islam is your claim that Allah has a son, your worship of the cross, and your eating of pork." They said: Then who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent regarding them and did not answer them. So Allah revealed concerning that, from their saying and their disagreement, the beginning of Surah Al 'Imran up to some eighty-odd verses of it.

Then Ibn Ishaq discussed the tafsir up to where he said: When the news from Allah reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the decisive judgement between him and them, and he was commanded with what he was commanded regarding invoking a curse upon them if they rejected that, he invited them to it. They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, leave us to consider our affair, then we will come to you with what we want to do regarding what you have invited us to." So they departed from him, then they withdrew with al-Aqib, who was their counsellor, and they said: "O Abd al-Masih, what do you see?" He said: "By Allah, O assembly of Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a sent prophet, and he has brought you the decisive account concerning your companion. You know that no people ever invoked a curse upon a prophet and then their elder remained, nor did their young grow up. If you do it, it will be the destruction of you. If you insist on the familiar practice of your religion and on remaining on what you hold regarding your companion, then make peace with the man and return to your lands."

They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to invoke a curse upon you, and to leave you upon your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your Companions whom you approve for us, to judge between us in matters over which we have differed concerning our wealth, for you are trustworthy to us."

Muhammad ibn Ja'far said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Come to me this evening, and I will send with you the strong and trustworthy one." Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "I never loved leadership as I loved it that day, hoping that I would be the one. So I went to the noon prayer early. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the noon prayer and gave the salam, he looked to his right and his left, and I began stretching up so that he would see me. He kept searching with his gaze until he saw Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and he called him: 'Go out with them and judge between them with truth concerning what they differ about.'" Umar said: "Abu Ubaydah took it, may Allah be pleased with him."

[Sirat Ibn Hisham (1/573-575); al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (6/151) through Salamah ibn al-Fadl from Ibn Ishaq.]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, that the delegation of the people of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar, except that he said regarding the nobles that they were twelve. He mentioned the rest with a longer wording and additional elements.

Al-Bukhari said: Abbas ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, who said: al-Aqib and al-Sayyid, the two leaders of Najran, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wishing to invoke a curse upon him. He said: One of them said to his companion: "Do not do it, for by Allah, if he is a prophet and we invoke a curse upon him, neither we nor our descendants after us will prosper." They said: "We will give you what you asked of us, and send with us a trustworthy man, and send with us only a trustworthy one." He said: "I will surely send with you a man who is trustworthy, truly trustworthy." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) aspired to it, and he said: "Stand up, O Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah." When he stood, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is the trustworthy one of this Ummah."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through several routes from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Silah, from Hudhayfah, similarly.

Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Israil from Abu Ishaq, from Silah, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Every nation has a trustworthy one, and the trustworthy one of this Ummah is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah."

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Raqqi Abu Yazid narrated to us, Furat narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying at the Ka'bah, I will surely come to him and step on his neck." He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If he had done so, the angels would have seized him openly. And if the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and they would have seen their seats in the Fire. And if those who were invited to mubahalah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had come out, they would have returned without finding wealth or family."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i through the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Abd al-Karim, with the same. Al-Tirmidhi said: a hasan sahih hadith.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah the story of the delegation of Najran in a very lengthy form. We will mention it, for in it are many benefits, some strangeness, and relevance to this context. Al-Bayhaqi said:

حدثنا أبو عبد الله الحافظ وأبو سعيد محمد بن موسى بن الفضل، قالا: حدثنا أبو العباس محمد بن يعقوب، حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الجبار، حدثنا يونس بن بُكَير، عن سلمة بن عبد يسوع، عن أبيه، عن جده. قال يونس، وكان نصرانيًا فأسلم: إن رسول الله ﷺ كتب إلى أهل نجران قبل أن ينزل عليه ﴿طس سليمان﴾: "بسم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب، من محمد النبي رسول الله إلى أسقف نجران وأهل نجران، سلم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أسلم".]] أنتم، فإني أحمد إليكم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب. أما بعد، فإني أدعوكم إلى عبادة الله من عبادة العباد، وأدعوكم إلى ولاية الله من ولاية العباد، فإن أبيتم فالجزية، فإن أبيتم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أبيتم فقد".]] آذنتكم بحرب والسلام".

فلما أتى الأسقف الكتاب فقرأه فظع به، وذعره ذعرًا شديدًا، وبعث إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: شُرحبيل بن وداعة، وكان من همدان، ولم يكن أحد يُدعى إذا نزلت معضلة قبله، لا الأيهم ولا السيد ولا العاقب، فدفع الأسقف كتاب رسول الله ﷺ إلى شرحبيل فقرأه، فقال الأسقف: يا أبا مريم، ما رأيك [[في جـ: "ما رأيك يا أبا مريم".]]؟ فقال شرحبيل: قد علمتَ ما وعد الله إبراهيم في ذرية إسماعيل من النبوة، فما يؤمن أن يكون هذا هو ذاك الرجل، ليس لي في النبوة رأي، ولو كان أمرٌ من أمور الدنيا لأشرتُ عليك فيه برأيي، وجهدتُ لك. فقال له الأسقف: تنحَّ فاجلس. فتنحى شرحبيل فجلس ناحية. فبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: عبد الله بن شُرحبيل، وهو من ذي أصبح من حِمير، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل، فقال له الأسقف: فاجلس، فتنحى فجلس ناحية. وبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: جبار بن فيض، من بني الحارث بن كعب، أحد بني الحَماس، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل وعبد الله، فأمره الأسقف فتنحى فجلس ناحية.

فلما اجتمع الرأي منهم على تلك المقالة جميعًا، أمر الأسقف بالناقوس فضُرب به، ورُفعت النيران والمسوح في الصوامع، وكذلك كانوا يفعلون إذا فزعوا بالنهار، وإذا كان فزعهم ليلًا ضربوا بالناقوس، ورُفعت النيران في الصوامع، فاجتمعوا [[في جـ، ر: "فاجتمع".]] حين ضُرب بالناقوس ورُفعت المسوح، أهلَ الوادي أعلاه وأسفله -وطول الوادي مسيرة يوم للراكب السريع، وفيه ثلاث وسبعون قرية، وعشرون ومائة ألف مقاتل. فقرأ عليهم كتاب رسول الله ﷺ، وسألهم عن الرأي فيه، فاجتمع رأي أهل الرأي منهم على أن يبعثوا شرحبيل بن وداعة الهمداني، وعبد الله بن شرحبيل الأصبحي، وجبار بن فيض الحارثي، فيأتونهم [[في أ: "فيأتوهم".]] بخبر رسول الله ﷺ. فانطلق الوفد، حتى إذا كانوا بالمدينة وضعوا ثياب السفر عنهم، ولبسوا حُللًا لهم يجرُّونها من حِبرة، وخواتيم الذهب، ثم انطلقوا حتى أتوا رسول الله ﷺ، فسلموا عليه، فلم يرد عليهم [[في جـ: "عليه السلام" وفي أ: "عليهم السلام".]]، وتصدَّوْا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فلم يكلمهم، وعليهم تلك الحُلل وخواتيم الذهب. فانطلقوا يتبعون عثمان بن عفان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف، وكانا معرفة لهم، فوجدوهما في ناس من المهاجرين والأنصار في مجلس، فقالوا: يا عثمان ويا عبد الرحمن، إن نبيكم كتب إلينا بكتاب، فأقبلنا مجيبين له، فأتيناه فسلمنا عليه فلم يرد سلامنا، وتصدينا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فأعيانا أن يكلمنا، فما الرأي منكما، أترَوْن أن نرجع؟ فقالا لعلي بن أبي طالب -وهو في القوم-: ما ترى يا أبا الحسن في هؤلاء القوم؟ فقال علي لعثمان ولعبد الرحمن: أرى أن يضعوا حُللهم هذه وخواتيمهم، ويلبسوا ثياب سفرهم، ثم يعودا إليه. ففعلوا، فسلموا، فرد سلامهم، ثم قال: "والذي بعثني بالحق لقد أتَوْني المرةَ الأولى، وإن إبليس لَمعهم". ثم ساءلهم وساءلوه، فلم تزل به وبهم المسألة حتى قالوا: ما تقول في عيسى، فإنا نرجع إلى قومنا ونحن نصارى، يسرنا إن كنتَ نبيًّا أن نسمع ما تقول فيه [[في جـ: "فيه ما تقول".]]؟ قال رسول الله ﷺ: "ما عندي فيه شيء يومي هذا، فأقيموا حتى أخبركم بما [[في أ: "ما".]] يقول لي ربي في عيسى". فأصبح الغد وقد أنزل الله، عز وجل، هذه الآية: ﴿إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون. الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين. فمن حاجّك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنة الله على﴾ [[زيادة من جـ، ر، أ، و، وفي هـ: "إلى قوله".]] ﴿الكاذبين﴾. فأبَوْا أن يُقِرُّوا بذلك. فلما أصبح رسول الله ﷺ الغدَ بعد ما أخبرهم الخبرَ، أقبل مشتملًا على الحسن والحسين في خميل له، وفاطمة تمشي عند ظهره للمُلاعنة، وله يومئذٍ عدةُ نسوة. فقال شرحبيل لصاحبيه: قد علمتما أن الوادي إذا اجتمع أعلاه وأسفله لم يَرِدوا ولم يَصدروا إلا عن رأيي [[في ر: "رأي".]]، وإني والله أرى أمرًا ثقيلًا، والله لئن كان هذا الرجل ملكًا مبعوثًا، فكنا أول العرب طعن في عينيه [[في جـ، ر: "عينه".]] وردّ عليه أمره، لا يذهب لنا من صدره ولا من صدور أصحابه حتى يصيبونا بجائحة، وإنا لأدنى العرب منهم جوارًا، ولئن كان هذا الرجل نبيًّا مرسلًا فلاعنّاه لا يبقى على وجه الأرض منا شعر ولا ظفر إلا هلك. فقال [[في أ: "فقالا".]] له صاحباه: يا أبا مريم، فما الرأي؟ فقال: أرى [[في ر: "رأيي".]] أن أحكّمه، فإني أرى رجلًا لا يحكم شططًا أبدًا. فقالا له: أنت وذاك. قال: فلقي [[في جـ: "فتلقى"، وفي ر: "فيلقى".]] شرحبيلُ رسولَ الله ﷺ، فقال له: إني قد رأيت خيرًا من مُلاعنتك. فقال: "وما هو؟" فقال: حُكمك اليوم إلى الليل، وليلتُك إلى الصباح، فمهما حكّمتَ فينا فهو جائز. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: "لعل وراءك أحدًا يثرِّب عليك؟" فقال شرحبيل: سل صاحبيّ. فسألهما، فقالا: ما يرد الوادي ولا يصدر إلا عن رأي شرحبيل. فرجع رسول الله ﷺ فلم يلاعنهم، حتى إذا كان الغد أتَوْه فكتب لهم هذا الكتاب: "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، هذا ما كتب محمد النبي رسول الله لنجران -إن كان عليهم حكمُه- في كل ثمرة، وكل صفراء وبيضاء وسوداء ورقيق فاضلٍ [[في و: "فافضل".]] عليهم، وترك ذلك كله لهم، على ألفي حُلّة، في كل رجب ألف حلة، وفي كل صفر ألف حلة" وذكر تمام الشروط وبقية السياق [[دلائل النبوة للبيهقي (٥/٣٨٥).]].

والغرض أن وفودهم كان في سنة تسع؛ لأن الزهري قال: كان أهل نجران أول من أدى الجزية إلى رسول الله ﷺ، وآية الجزية إنما أُنزلت بعد الفتح، وهي قوله تعالى: ﴿قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر [ولا يحرّمون ما حرّم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون] ﴾ [التوبة: ٢٩] [[زيادة من جـ، أ، ر، و، وفي هـ: "الآية".]].

وقال أبو بكر بن مردويه: حدثنا سليمان بن أحمد، حدثنا أحمد بن داود المكي، حدثنا بشر بن مهران، أخبرنا محمد بن دينار، عن داود بن أبي هند، عن الشعبي، عن جابر قال: قدم على النبي ﷺ العاقب والطيب، فدعاهما إلى المُلاعنة، فواعداه على أن يلاعناه [[في جـ، أ، و: "يعاوداه". وفي ر: "يعاديه".]] الغداة. قال: فغدا رسول الله ﷺ، فأخذ بيد علي وفاطمة والحسن والحسين، ثم أرسل إليهما فأبيا أن يجيئا [[في أ: "يجيبا".]] وأقرّا بالخراج. قال: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "والذي بعثني بالحق لو قالا لا، لأمطر عليهم الوادي [[في جـ: "الوادي عليهم".]] نارًا". قال جابر: فيهم نزلت ﴿ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾. قال جابر: ﴿وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾ رسولُ الله ﷺ وعليَّ بن أبي طالب، ﴿وأبناءنا﴾ الحسنَ والحسين، ﴿ونساءنا﴾ فاطمةَ.

وهكذا رواه الحاكم في مستدركه، عن علي بن عيسى، عن أحمد بن محمد الأزهري [[في ر: "الأزهر" وفي أ، و: "الزهري".]] عن علي بن حُجر، عن علي بن مُسهر، عن داود بن أبي هند، به بمعناه. ثم قال: صحيح على شرط مسلم، ولم يخرجاه [[المستدرك (٢/٥٩٣، ٥٩٤)، ورواه أبو نعيم في دلائل النبوة (٢/٥٩٣) من طريق داود بن أبي هند عن الشعبي عن جابر به.]].

هكذا قال، وقد رواه أبو داود الطيالسي، عن شعبة، عن المغيرة [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "مغيرة".]] عن الشعبي مرسلًا، وهذا أصح [[رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره (٢/٣١٠) من طريق شعبة به، ورواه ابن أبي شيبة في المصنف (١٤/٥٤٩)، والطبري في تفسيره (٦/٤٦٨) من طريق جرير عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا، ورواه سعيد بن منصور في السنن برقم (٥٠٠) من طريق هشيم عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا.]]. وقد رُوي عن ابن عباس والبراء نحو ذلك.

ثم قال الله تعالى: ﴿إن هذا لهو القصص الحق﴾ أي: هذا الذي قصصناه عليك يا محمد في شأن عيسى هو الحق الذي لا معدل عنه ولا محيد. ﴿وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم. فإن تولّوا﴾ أي: عن هذا إلى غيره. ﴿فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين﴾ أي: من عدل عن الحق إلى الباطل فهو المفسد، والله عليم به، وسيجزيه على ذلك شر الجزاء، وهو القادر الذي لا يفوته شيء [سبحانه وبحمده، ونعوذ به من حلول نقمه] [[زيادة من و.]].

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah﴾ in terms of Allah's power, since He created him without a father, ﴿is like the likeness of Adam﴾, for Allah created him without a father or a mother. Rather, ﴿He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ The One who created Adam is able to create Jesus all the more so and more fittingly. If claiming sonship for Jesus is permissible because he was created without a father, then it is all the more permissible for Adam. It is known by consensus that this is false, so the claim regarding Jesus is even more false and its corruption even more evident. But the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, willed to show His power to His creation when He created Adam neither from a male nor from a female, created Eve from a male without a female, and created Jesus from a female without a male, just as He created the rest of creation from a male and a female. For this reason God said in Surah Maryam: ﴿And that We may make him a sign for the people﴾ [Maryam: 21].

Here He also said: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾ That is, this statement is the truth concerning Jesus, from which there is no turning away and no correct position other than it. What lies beyond the truth but error?

Then God, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), commanded him to invoke a curse (mubahalah) upon whoever opposed the truth concerning the matter of Jesus after the clear proof had appeared: ﴿Then whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves,﴾ that is, let us present them in the state of mubahalah ﴿then let us earnestly pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars﴾ that is, let us call down a curse upon one another ﴿so let the curse of Allah be upon the liars﴾ that is, from us or from you.
