The occasion of revelation of this mubahalah, and of what precedes it from the beginning of the surah up to this point, concerned the delegation of Najran. When the Christians arrived, they began to dispute about Jesus and to assert about him what they asserted of sonship and divinity. So Allah revealed the opening of this surah in refutation of them, as Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and others have mentioned.

Ibn Ishaq said in his well-known Sirah and others said: A delegation of the Christians of Najran, sixty riders, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among them were fourteen men of their nobles to whom their affairs returned: al-Aqib, whose name was Abd al-Masih; al-Sayyid, who was al-Ayham; Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, brother of Bakr ibn Wa'il; Uways (or Aws) ibn al-Harith; Zayd; Qays; Yazid; Nabih; Khuwaylid; Amr; Khalid; Abd Allah; and Yuhannis.

The affairs of these men returned to three of them: al-Aqib, who was the leader of the people, their counsellor and the one whose opinion they never departed from; al-Sayyid, who was their scholar, the owner of their caravan and their gathering; and Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, who was their bishop, their rabbi, their imam and the master of their schools. He was an Arab from the Bakr ibn Wa'il, but he had become a Christian. The Romans and their kings held him in high esteem, honoured him, built churches for him, provided for him and gave him servants, because of the firmness they knew of him in their religion. He had known well the matter, the qualities and the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the earlier scriptures he knew, but his ignorance led him to persist in Christianity, because of the honour and high standing he enjoyed among its adherents.

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, saying: They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah and entered upon him in his mosque after he had prayed the afternoon prayer. They wore striped garments: robes and cloaks, in the splendour of the men of Bani al-Harith ibn Ka'b. He said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who saw them said: We have not seen a delegation like them after them. Their prayer time came, so they stood in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and prayed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave them." So they prayed facing the east.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them, and among them Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah and al-Aqib Abd al-Masih, or al-Sayyid al-Ayham, who were upon the religion of the king regarding Christianity, despite their differing positions. They said: He is Allah; they said: He is the son of Allah; and they said: He is the third of three. Exalted is Allah far above that by a great exaltation. And this is also the position of Christianity. They argued for their saying "He is Allah" that he used to give life to the dead, heal the sick, inform of the unseen, and create from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathe into it so that it became a bird, all of this by the command of Allah, "and that He may make him a sign for the people."

They argued for their saying that he is the son of Allah, saying: He had no known father, and he spoke in the cradle with something no one of the children of Adam had done before him.

They argued for their saying that he is the third of three by the words of Allah, "We have done," "We have commanded," "We have created," and "We have decreed." They said: If He were one, He would have said only "I have done, I have decreed, I have commanded and I have created." But rather He is Himself, and Jesus, and Mary, and all of this in their saying has been revealed in the Qur'an.

When the two rabbis (ḥabrān) spoke with him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Submit." They said: We have submitted. He said: "You have not submitted, so submit." They said: Indeed, we submitted before you. He said: "You have lied. What prevents you from Islam is your claim that Allah has a son, your worship of the cross, and your eating of pork." They said: Then who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent regarding them and did not answer them. So Allah revealed concerning that, from their saying and their disagreement, the beginning of Surah Al 'Imran up to some eighty-odd verses of it.

Then Ibn Ishaq discussed the tafsir up to where he said: When the news from Allah reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the decisive judgement between him and them, and he was commanded with what he was commanded regarding invoking a curse upon them if they rejected that, he invited them to it. They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, leave us to consider our affair, then we will come to you with what we want to do regarding what you have invited us to." So they departed from him, then they withdrew with al-Aqib, who was their counsellor, and they said: "O Abd al-Masih, what do you see?" He said: "By Allah, O assembly of Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a sent prophet, and he has brought you the decisive account concerning your companion. You know that no people ever invoked a curse upon a prophet and then their elder remained, nor did their young grow up. If you do it, it will be the destruction of you. If you insist on the familiar practice of your religion and on remaining on what you hold regarding your companion, then make peace with the man and return to your lands."

They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to invoke a curse upon you, and to leave you upon your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your Companions whom you approve for us, to judge between us in matters over which we have differed concerning our wealth, for you are trustworthy to us."

Muhammad ibn Ja'far said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Come to me this evening, and I will send with you the strong and trustworthy one." Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "I never loved leadership as I loved it that day, hoping that I would be the one. So I went to the noon prayer early. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the noon prayer and gave the salam, he looked to his right and his left, and I began stretching up so that he would see me. He kept searching with his gaze until he saw Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and he called him: 'Go out with them and judge between them with truth concerning what they differ about.'" Umar said: "Abu Ubaydah took it, may Allah be pleased with him."

[Sirat Ibn Hisham (1/573-575); al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (6/151) through Salamah ibn al-Fadl from Ibn Ishaq.]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, that the delegation of the people of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar, except that he said regarding the nobles that they were twelve. He mentioned the rest with a longer wording and additional elements.

Al-Bukhari said: Abbas ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, who said: al-Aqib and al-Sayyid, the two leaders of Najran, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wishing to invoke a curse upon him. He said: One of them said to his companion: "Do not do it, for by Allah, if he is a prophet and we invoke a curse upon him, neither we nor our descendants after us will prosper." They said: "We will give you what you asked of us, and send with us a trustworthy man, and send with us only a trustworthy one." He said: "I will surely send with you a man who is trustworthy, truly trustworthy." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) aspired to it, and he said: "Stand up, O Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah." When he stood, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is the trustworthy one of this Ummah."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through several routes from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Silah, from Hudhayfah, similarly.

Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Israil from Abu Ishaq, from Silah, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Every nation has a trustworthy one, and the trustworthy one of this Ummah is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah."

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Raqqi Abu Yazid narrated to us, Furat narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying at the Ka'bah, I will surely come to him and step on his neck." He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If he had done so, the angels would have seized him openly. And if the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and they would have seen their seats in the Fire. And if those who were invited to mubahalah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had come out, they would have returned without finding wealth or family."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i through the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Abd al-Karim, with the same. Al-Tirmidhi said: a hasan sahih hadith.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah the story of the delegation of Najran in a very lengthy form. We will mention it, for in it are many benefits, some strangeness, and relevance to this context. Al-Bayhaqi said:

حدثنا أبو عبد الله الحافظ وأبو سعيد محمد بن موسى بن الفضل، قالا: حدثنا أبو العباس محمد بن يعقوب، حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الجبار، حدثنا يونس بن بُكَير، عن سلمة بن عبد يسوع، عن أبيه، عن جده. قال يونس، وكان نصرانيًا فأسلم: إن رسول الله ﷺ كتب إلى أهل نجران قبل أن ينزل عليه ﴿طس سليمان﴾: "بسم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب، من محمد النبي رسول الله إلى أسقف نجران وأهل نجران، سلم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أسلم".]] أنتم، فإني أحمد إليكم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب. أما بعد، فإني أدعوكم إلى عبادة الله من عبادة العباد، وأدعوكم إلى ولاية الله من ولاية العباد، فإن أبيتم فالجزية، فإن أبيتم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أبيتم فقد".]] آذنتكم بحرب والسلام".

فلما أتى الأسقف الكتاب فقرأه فظع به، وذعره ذعرًا شديدًا، وبعث إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: شُرحبيل بن وداعة، وكان من همدان، ولم يكن أحد يُدعى إذا نزلت معضلة قبله، لا الأيهم ولا السيد ولا العاقب، فدفع الأسقف كتاب رسول الله ﷺ إلى شرحبيل فقرأه، فقال الأسقف: يا أبا مريم، ما رأيك [[في جـ: "ما رأيك يا أبا مريم".]]؟ فقال شرحبيل: قد علمتَ ما وعد الله إبراهيم في ذرية إسماعيل من النبوة، فما يؤمن أن يكون هذا هو ذاك الرجل، ليس لي في النبوة رأي، ولو كان أمرٌ من أمور الدنيا لأشرتُ عليك فيه برأيي، وجهدتُ لك. فقال له الأسقف: تنحَّ فاجلس. فتنحى شرحبيل فجلس ناحية. فبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: عبد الله بن شُرحبيل، وهو من ذي أصبح من حِمير، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل، فقال له الأسقف: فاجلس، فتنحى فجلس ناحية. وبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: جبار بن فيض، من بني الحارث بن كعب، أحد بني الحَماس، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل وعبد الله، فأمره الأسقف فتنحى فجلس ناحية.

فلما اجتمع الرأي منهم على تلك المقالة جميعًا، أمر الأسقف بالناقوس فضُرب به، ورُفعت النيران والمسوح في الصوامع، وكذلك كانوا يفعلون إذا فزعوا بالنهار، وإذا كان فزعهم ليلًا ضربوا بالناقوس، ورُفعت النيران في الصوامع، فاجتمعوا [[في جـ، ر: "فاجتمع".]] حين ضُرب بالناقوس ورُفعت المسوح، أهلَ الوادي أعلاه وأسفله -وطول الوادي مسيرة يوم للراكب السريع، وفيه ثلاث وسبعون قرية، وعشرون ومائة ألف مقاتل. فقرأ عليهم كتاب رسول الله ﷺ، وسألهم عن الرأي فيه، فاجتمع رأي أهل الرأي منهم على أن يبعثوا شرحبيل بن وداعة الهمداني، وعبد الله بن شرحبيل الأصبحي، وجبار بن فيض الحارثي، فيأتونهم [[في أ: "فيأتوهم".]] بخبر رسول الله ﷺ. فانطلق الوفد، حتى إذا كانوا بالمدينة وضعوا ثياب السفر عنهم، ولبسوا حُللًا لهم يجرُّونها من حِبرة، وخواتيم الذهب، ثم انطلقوا حتى أتوا رسول الله ﷺ، فسلموا عليه، فلم يرد عليهم [[في جـ: "عليه السلام" وفي أ: "عليهم السلام".]]، وتصدَّوْا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فلم يكلمهم، وعليهم تلك الحُلل وخواتيم الذهب. فانطلقوا يتبعون عثمان بن عفان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف، وكانا معرفة لهم، فوجدوهما في ناس من المهاجرين والأنصار في مجلس، فقالوا: يا عثمان ويا عبد الرحمن، إن نبيكم كتب إلينا بكتاب، فأقبلنا مجيبين له، فأتيناه فسلمنا عليه فلم يرد سلامنا، وتصدينا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فأعيانا أن يكلمنا، فما الرأي منكما، أترَوْن أن نرجع؟ فقالا لعلي بن أبي طالب -وهو في القوم-: ما ترى يا أبا الحسن في هؤلاء القوم؟ فقال علي لعثمان ولعبد الرحمن: أرى أن يضعوا حُللهم هذه وخواتيمهم، ويلبسوا ثياب سفرهم، ثم يعودا إليه. ففعلوا، فسلموا، فرد سلامهم، ثم قال: "والذي بعثني بالحق لقد أتَوْني المرةَ الأولى، وإن إبليس لَمعهم". ثم ساءلهم وساءلوه، فلم تزل به وبهم المسألة حتى قالوا: ما تقول في عيسى، فإنا نرجع إلى قومنا ونحن نصارى، يسرنا إن كنتَ نبيًّا أن نسمع ما تقول فيه [[في جـ: "فيه ما تقول".]]؟ قال رسول الله ﷺ: "ما عندي فيه شيء يومي هذا، فأقيموا حتى أخبركم بما [[في أ: "ما".]] يقول لي ربي في عيسى". فأصبح الغد وقد أنزل الله، عز وجل، هذه الآية: ﴿إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون. الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين. فمن حاجّك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنة الله على﴾ [[زيادة من جـ، ر، أ، و، وفي هـ: "إلى قوله".]] ﴿الكاذبين﴾. فأبَوْا أن يُقِرُّوا بذلك. فلما أصبح رسول الله ﷺ الغدَ بعد ما أخبرهم الخبرَ، أقبل مشتملًا على الحسن والحسين في خميل له، وفاطمة تمشي عند ظهره للمُلاعنة، وله يومئذٍ عدةُ نسوة. فقال شرحبيل لصاحبيه: قد علمتما أن الوادي إذا اجتمع أعلاه وأسفله لم يَرِدوا ولم يَصدروا إلا عن رأيي [[في ر: "رأي".]]، وإني والله أرى أمرًا ثقيلًا، والله لئن كان هذا الرجل ملكًا مبعوثًا، فكنا أول العرب طعن في عينيه [[في جـ، ر: "عينه".]] وردّ عليه أمره، لا يذهب لنا من صدره ولا من صدور أصحابه حتى يصيبونا بجائحة، وإنا لأدنى العرب منهم جوارًا، ولئن كان هذا الرجل نبيًّا مرسلًا فلاعنّاه لا يبقى على وجه الأرض منا شعر ولا ظفر إلا هلك. فقال [[في أ: "فقالا".]] له صاحباه: يا أبا مريم، فما الرأي؟ فقال: أرى [[في ر: "رأيي".]] أن أحكّمه، فإني أرى رجلًا لا يحكم شططًا أبدًا. فقالا له: أنت وذاك. قال: فلقي [[في جـ: "فتلقى"، وفي ر: "فيلقى".]] شرحبيلُ رسولَ الله ﷺ، فقال له: إني قد رأيت خيرًا من مُلاعنتك. فقال: "وما هو؟" فقال: حُكمك اليوم إلى الليل، وليلتُك إلى الصباح، فمهما حكّمتَ فينا فهو جائز. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: "لعل وراءك أحدًا يثرِّب عليك؟" فقال شرحبيل: سل صاحبيّ. فسألهما، فقالا: ما يرد الوادي ولا يصدر إلا عن رأي شرحبيل. فرجع رسول الله ﷺ فلم يلاعنهم، حتى إذا كان الغد أتَوْه فكتب لهم هذا الكتاب: "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، هذا ما كتب محمد النبي رسول الله لنجران -إن كان عليهم حكمُه- في كل ثمرة، وكل صفراء وبيضاء وسوداء ورقيق فاضلٍ [[في و: "فافضل".]] عليهم، وترك ذلك كله لهم، على ألفي حُلّة، في كل رجب ألف حلة، وفي كل صفر ألف حلة" وذكر تمام الشروط وبقية السياق [[دلائل النبوة للبيهقي (٥/٣٨٥).]].

والغرض أن وفودهم كان في سنة تسع؛ لأن الزهري قال: كان أهل نجران أول من أدى الجزية إلى رسول الله ﷺ، وآية الجزية إنما أُنزلت بعد الفتح، وهي قوله تعالى: ﴿قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر [ولا يحرّمون ما حرّم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون] ﴾ [التوبة: ٢٩] [[زيادة من جـ، أ، ر، و، وفي هـ: "الآية".]].

وقال أبو بكر بن مردويه: حدثنا سليمان بن أحمد، حدثنا أحمد بن داود المكي، حدثنا بشر بن مهران، أخبرنا محمد بن دينار، عن داود بن أبي هند، عن الشعبي، عن جابر قال: قدم على النبي ﷺ العاقب والطيب، فدعاهما إلى المُلاعنة، فواعداه على أن يلاعناه [[في جـ، أ، و: "يعاوداه". وفي ر: "يعاديه".]] الغداة. قال: فغدا رسول الله ﷺ، فأخذ بيد علي وفاطمة والحسن والحسين، ثم أرسل إليهما فأبيا أن يجيئا [[في أ: "يجيبا".]] وأقرّا بالخراج. قال: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "والذي بعثني بالحق لو قالا لا، لأمطر عليهم الوادي [[في جـ: "الوادي عليهم".]] نارًا". قال جابر: فيهم نزلت ﴿ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾. قال جابر: ﴿وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾ رسولُ الله ﷺ وعليَّ بن أبي طالب، ﴿وأبناءنا﴾ الحسنَ والحسين، ﴿ونساءنا﴾ فاطمةَ.

وهكذا رواه الحاكم في مستدركه، عن علي بن عيسى، عن أحمد بن محمد الأزهري [[في ر: "الأزهر" وفي أ، و: "الزهري".]] عن علي بن حُجر، عن علي بن مُسهر، عن داود بن أبي هند، به بمعناه. ثم قال: صحيح على شرط مسلم، ولم يخرجاه [[المستدرك (٢/٥٩٣، ٥٩٤)، ورواه أبو نعيم في دلائل النبوة (٢/٥٩٣) من طريق داود بن أبي هند عن الشعبي عن جابر به.]].

هكذا قال، وقد رواه أبو داود الطيالسي، عن شعبة، عن المغيرة [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "مغيرة".]] عن الشعبي مرسلًا، وهذا أصح [[رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره (٢/٣١٠) من طريق شعبة به، ورواه ابن أبي شيبة في المصنف (١٤/٥٤٩)، والطبري في تفسيره (٦/٤٦٨) من طريق جرير عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا، ورواه سعيد بن منصور في السنن برقم (٥٠٠) من طريق هشيم عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا.]]. وقد رُوي عن ابن عباس والبراء نحو ذلك.

ثم قال الله تعالى: ﴿إن هذا لهو القصص الحق﴾ أي: هذا الذي قصصناه عليك يا محمد في شأن عيسى هو الحق الذي لا معدل عنه ولا محيد. ﴿وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم. فإن تولّوا﴾ أي: عن هذا إلى غيره. ﴿فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين﴾ أي: من عدل عن الحق إلى الباطل فهو المفسد، والله عليم به، وسيجزيه على ذلك شر الجزاء، وهو القادر الذي لا يفوته شيء [سبحانه وبحمده، ونعوذ به من حلول نقمه] [[زيادة من و.]].

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah﴾ in terms of Allah's power, since He created him without a father, ﴿is like the likeness of Adam﴾, for Allah created him without a father or a mother. Rather, ﴿He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ The One who created Adam is able to create Jesus all the more so and more fittingly. If claiming sonship for Jesus is permissible because he was created without a father, then it is all the more permissible for Adam. It is known by consensus that this is false, so the claim regarding Jesus is even more false and its corruption even more evident. But the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, willed to show His power to His creation when He created Adam neither from a male nor from a female, created Eve from a male without a female, and created Jesus from a female without a male, just as He created the rest of creation from a male and a female. For this reason God said in Surah Maryam: ﴿And that We may make him a sign for the people﴾ [Maryam: 21].

Here He also said: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾ That is, this statement is the truth concerning Jesus, from which there is no turning away and no correct position other than it. What lies beyond the truth but error?

Then God, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), commanded him to invoke a curse (mubahalah) upon whoever opposed the truth concerning the matter of Jesus after the clear proof had appeared: ﴿Then whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves,﴾ that is, let us present them in the state of mubahalah ﴿then let us earnestly pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars﴾ that is, let us call down a curse upon one another ﴿so let the curse of Allah be upon the liars﴾ that is, from us or from you.

The occasion of revelation of this mubahalah, and of what precedes it from the beginning of the surah up to this point, concerned the delegation of Najran. When the Christians arrived, they began to dispute about Jesus and to assert about him what they asserted of sonship and divinity. So Allah revealed the opening of this surah in refutation of them, as Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and others have mentioned.

Ibn Ishaq said in his well-known Sirah and others said: A delegation of the Christians of Najran, sixty riders, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among them were fourteen men of their nobles to whom their affairs returned: al-Aqib, whose name was Abd al-Masih; al-Sayyid, who was al-Ayham; Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, brother of Bakr ibn Wa'il; Uways (or Aws) ibn al-Harith; Zayd; Qays; Yazid; Nabih; Khuwaylid; Amr; Khalid; Abd Allah; and Yuhannis.

The affairs of these men returned to three of them: al-Aqib, who was the leader of the people, their counsellor and the one whose opinion they never departed from; al-Sayyid, who was their scholar, the owner of their caravan and their gathering; and Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, who was their bishop, their rabbi, their imam and the master of their schools. He was an Arab from the Bakr ibn Wa'il, but he had become a Christian. The Romans and their kings held him in high esteem, honoured him, built churches for him, provided for him and gave him servants, because of the firmness they knew of him in their religion. He had known well the matter, the qualities and the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the earlier scriptures he knew, but his ignorance led him to persist in Christianity, because of the honour and high standing he enjoyed among its adherents.

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, saying: They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah and entered upon him in his mosque after he had prayed the afternoon prayer. They wore striped garments: robes and cloaks, in the splendour of the men of Bani al-Harith ibn Ka'b. He said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who saw them said: We have not seen a delegation like them after them. Their prayer time came, so they stood in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and prayed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave them." So they prayed facing the east.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them, and among them Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah and al-Aqib Abd al-Masih, or al-Sayyid al-Ayham, who were upon the religion of the king regarding Christianity, despite their differing positions. They said: He is Allah; they said: He is the son of Allah; and they said: He is the third of three. Exalted is Allah far above that by a great exaltation. And this is also the position of Christianity. They argued for their saying "He is Allah" that he used to give life to the dead, heal the sick, inform of the unseen, and create from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathe into it so that it became a bird, all of this by the command of Allah, "and that He may make him a sign for the people."

They argued for their saying that he is the son of Allah, saying: He had no known father, and he spoke in the cradle with something no one of the children of Adam had done before him.

They argued for their saying that he is the third of three by the words of Allah, "We have done," "We have commanded," "We have created," and "We have decreed." They said: If He were one, He would have said only "I have done, I have decreed, I have commanded and I have created." But rather He is Himself, and Jesus, and Mary, and all of this in their saying has been revealed in the Qur'an.

When the two rabbis (ḥabrān) spoke with him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Submit." They said: We have submitted. He said: "You have not submitted, so submit." They said: Indeed, we submitted before you. He said: "You have lied. What prevents you from Islam is your claim that Allah has a son, your worship of the cross, and your eating of pork." They said: Then who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent regarding them and did not answer them. So Allah revealed concerning that, from their saying and their disagreement, the beginning of Surah Al 'Imran up to some eighty-odd verses of it.

Then Ibn Ishaq discussed the tafsir up to where he said: When the news from Allah reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the decisive judgement between him and them, and he was commanded with what he was commanded regarding invoking a curse upon them if they rejected that, he invited them to it. They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, leave us to consider our affair, then we will come to you with what we want to do regarding what you have invited us to." So they departed from him, then they withdrew with al-Aqib, who was their counsellor, and they said: "O Abd al-Masih, what do you see?" He said: "By Allah, O assembly of Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a sent prophet, and he has brought you the decisive account concerning your companion. You know that no people ever invoked a curse upon a prophet and then their elder remained, nor did their young grow up. If you do it, it will be the destruction of you. If you insist on the familiar practice of your religion and on remaining on what you hold regarding your companion, then make peace with the man and return to your lands."

They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to invoke a curse upon you, and to leave you upon your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your Companions whom you approve for us, to judge between us in matters over which we have differed concerning our wealth, for you are trustworthy to us."

Muhammad ibn Ja'far said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Come to me this evening, and I will send with you the strong and trustworthy one." Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "I never loved leadership as I loved it that day, hoping that I would be the one. So I went to the noon prayer early. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the noon prayer and gave the salam, he looked to his right and his left, and I began stretching up so that he would see me. He kept searching with his gaze until he saw Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and he called him: 'Go out with them and judge between them with truth concerning what they differ about.'" Umar said: "Abu Ubaydah took it, may Allah be pleased with him."

[Sirat Ibn Hisham (1/573-575); al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (6/151) through Salamah ibn al-Fadl from Ibn Ishaq.]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, that the delegation of the people of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar, except that he said regarding the nobles that they were twelve. He mentioned the rest with a longer wording and additional elements.

Al-Bukhari said: Abbas ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, who said: al-Aqib and al-Sayyid, the two leaders of Najran, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wishing to invoke a curse upon him. He said: One of them said to his companion: "Do not do it, for by Allah, if he is a prophet and we invoke a curse upon him, neither we nor our descendants after us will prosper." They said: "We will give you what you asked of us, and send with us a trustworthy man, and send with us only a trustworthy one." He said: "I will surely send with you a man who is trustworthy, truly trustworthy." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) aspired to it, and he said: "Stand up, O Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah." When he stood, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is the trustworthy one of this Ummah."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through several routes from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Silah, from Hudhayfah, similarly.

Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Israil from Abu Ishaq, from Silah, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Every nation has a trustworthy one, and the trustworthy one of this Ummah is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah."

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Raqqi Abu Yazid narrated to us, Furat narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying at the Ka'bah, I will surely come to him and step on his neck." He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If he had done so, the angels would have seized him openly. And if the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and they would have seen their seats in the Fire. And if those who were invited to mubahalah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had come out, they would have returned without finding wealth or family."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i through the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Abd al-Karim, with the same. Al-Tirmidhi said: a hasan sahih hadith.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah the story of the delegation of Najran in a very lengthy form. We will mention it, for in it are many benefits, some strangeness, and relevance to this context. Al-Bayhaqi said:

حدثنا أبو عبد الله الحافظ وأبو سعيد محمد بن موسى بن الفضل، قالا: حدثنا أبو العباس محمد بن يعقوب، حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الجبار، حدثنا يونس بن بُكَير، عن سلمة بن عبد يسوع، عن أبيه، عن جده. قال يونس، وكان نصرانيًا فأسلم: إن رسول الله ﷺ كتب إلى أهل نجران قبل أن ينزل عليه ﴿طس سليمان﴾: "بسم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب، من محمد النبي رسول الله إلى أسقف نجران وأهل نجران، سلم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أسلم".]] أنتم، فإني أحمد إليكم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب. أما بعد، فإني أدعوكم إلى عبادة الله من عبادة العباد، وأدعوكم إلى ولاية الله من ولاية العباد، فإن أبيتم فالجزية، فإن أبيتم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أبيتم فقد".]] آذنتكم بحرب والسلام".

فلما أتى الأسقف الكتاب فقرأه فظع به، وذعره ذعرًا شديدًا، وبعث إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: شُرحبيل بن وداعة، وكان من همدان، ولم يكن أحد يُدعى إذا نزلت معضلة قبله، لا الأيهم ولا السيد ولا العاقب، فدفع الأسقف كتاب رسول الله ﷺ إلى شرحبيل فقرأه، فقال الأسقف: يا أبا مريم، ما رأيك [[في جـ: "ما رأيك يا أبا مريم".]]؟ فقال شرحبيل: قد علمتَ ما وعد الله إبراهيم في ذرية إسماعيل من النبوة، فما يؤمن أن يكون هذا هو ذاك الرجل، ليس لي في النبوة رأي، ولو كان أمرٌ من أمور الدنيا لأشرتُ عليك فيه برأيي، وجهدتُ لك. فقال له الأسقف: تنحَّ فاجلس. فتنحى شرحبيل فجلس ناحية. فبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: عبد الله بن شُرحبيل، وهو من ذي أصبح من حِمير، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل، فقال له الأسقف: فاجلس، فتنحى فجلس ناحية. وبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: جبار بن فيض، من بني الحارث بن كعب، أحد بني الحَماس، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل وعبد الله، فأمره الأسقف فتنحى فجلس ناحية.

فلما اجتمع الرأي منهم على تلك المقالة جميعًا، أمر الأسقف بالناقوس فضُرب به، ورُفعت النيران والمسوح في الصوامع، وكذلك كانوا يفعلون إذا فزعوا بالنهار، وإذا كان فزعهم ليلًا ضربوا بالناقوس، ورُفعت النيران في الصوامع، فاجتمعوا [[في جـ، ر: "فاجتمع".]] حين ضُرب بالناقوس ورُفعت المسوح، أهلَ الوادي أعلاه وأسفله -وطول الوادي مسيرة يوم للراكب السريع، وفيه ثلاث وسبعون قرية، وعشرون ومائة ألف مقاتل. فقرأ عليهم كتاب رسول الله ﷺ، وسألهم عن الرأي فيه، فاجتمع رأي أهل الرأي منهم على أن يبعثوا شرحبيل بن وداعة الهمداني، وعبد الله بن شرحبيل الأصبحي، وجبار بن فيض الحارثي، فيأتونهم [[في أ: "فيأتوهم".]] بخبر رسول الله ﷺ. فانطلق الوفد، حتى إذا كانوا بالمدينة وضعوا ثياب السفر عنهم، ولبسوا حُللًا لهم يجرُّونها من حِبرة، وخواتيم الذهب، ثم انطلقوا حتى أتوا رسول الله ﷺ، فسلموا عليه، فلم يرد عليهم [[في جـ: "عليه السلام" وفي أ: "عليهم السلام".]]، وتصدَّوْا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فلم يكلمهم، وعليهم تلك الحُلل وخواتيم الذهب. فانطلقوا يتبعون عثمان بن عفان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف، وكانا معرفة لهم، فوجدوهما في ناس من المهاجرين والأنصار في مجلس، فقالوا: يا عثمان ويا عبد الرحمن، إن نبيكم كتب إلينا بكتاب، فأقبلنا مجيبين له، فأتيناه فسلمنا عليه فلم يرد سلامنا، وتصدينا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فأعيانا أن يكلمنا، فما الرأي منكما، أترَوْن أن نرجع؟ فقالا لعلي بن أبي طالب -وهو في القوم-: ما ترى يا أبا الحسن في هؤلاء القوم؟ فقال علي لعثمان ولعبد الرحمن: أرى أن يضعوا حُللهم هذه وخواتيمهم، ويلبسوا ثياب سفرهم، ثم يعودا إليه. ففعلوا، فسلموا، فرد سلامهم، ثم قال: "والذي بعثني بالحق لقد أتَوْني المرةَ الأولى، وإن إبليس لَمعهم". ثم ساءلهم وساءلوه، فلم تزل به وبهم المسألة حتى قالوا: ما تقول في عيسى، فإنا نرجع إلى قومنا ونحن نصارى، يسرنا إن كنتَ نبيًّا أن نسمع ما تقول فيه [[في جـ: "فيه ما تقول".]]؟ قال رسول الله ﷺ: "ما عندي فيه شيء يومي هذا، فأقيموا حتى أخبركم بما [[في أ: "ما".]] يقول لي ربي في عيسى". فأصبح الغد وقد أنزل الله، عز وجل، هذه الآية: ﴿إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون. الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين. فمن حاجّك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنة الله على﴾ [[زيادة من جـ، ر، أ، و، وفي هـ: "إلى قوله".]] ﴿الكاذبين﴾. فأبَوْا أن يُقِرُّوا بذلك. فلما أصبح رسول الله ﷺ الغدَ بعد ما أخبرهم الخبرَ، أقبل مشتملًا على الحسن والحسين في خميل له، وفاطمة تمشي عند ظهره للمُلاعنة، وله يومئذٍ عدةُ نسوة. فقال شرحبيل لصاحبيه: قد علمتما أن الوادي إذا اجتمع أعلاه وأسفله لم يَرِدوا ولم يَصدروا إلا عن رأيي [[في ر: "رأي".]]، وإني والله أرى أمرًا ثقيلًا، والله لئن كان هذا الرجل ملكًا مبعوثًا، فكنا أول العرب طعن في عينيه [[في جـ، ر: "عينه".]] وردّ عليه أمره، لا يذهب لنا من صدره ولا من صدور أصحابه حتى يصيبونا بجائحة، وإنا لأدنى العرب منهم جوارًا، ولئن كان هذا الرجل نبيًّا مرسلًا فلاعنّاه لا يبقى على وجه الأرض منا شعر ولا ظفر إلا هلك. فقال [[في أ: "فقالا".]] له صاحباه: يا أبا مريم، فما الرأي؟ فقال: أرى [[في ر: "رأيي".]] أن أحكّمه، فإني أرى رجلًا لا يحكم شططًا أبدًا. فقالا له: أنت وذاك. قال: فلقي [[في جـ: "فتلقى"، وفي ر: "فيلقى".]] شرحبيلُ رسولَ الله ﷺ، فقال له: إني قد رأيت خيرًا من مُلاعنتك. فقال: "وما هو؟" فقال: حُكمك اليوم إلى الليل، وليلتُك إلى الصباح، فمهما حكّمتَ فينا فهو جائز. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: "لعل وراءك أحدًا يثرِّب عليك؟" فقال شرحبيل: سل صاحبيّ. فسألهما، فقالا: ما يرد الوادي ولا يصدر إلا عن رأي شرحبيل. فرجع رسول الله ﷺ فلم يلاعنهم، حتى إذا كان الغد أتَوْه فكتب لهم هذا الكتاب: "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، هذا ما كتب محمد النبي رسول الله لنجران -إن كان عليهم حكمُه- في كل ثمرة، وكل صفراء وبيضاء وسوداء ورقيق فاضلٍ [[في و: "فافضل".]] عليهم، وترك ذلك كله لهم، على ألفي حُلّة، في كل رجب ألف حلة، وفي كل صفر ألف حلة" وذكر تمام الشروط وبقية السياق [[دلائل النبوة للبيهقي (٥/٣٨٥).]].

والغرض أن وفودهم كان في سنة تسع؛ لأن الزهري قال: كان أهل نجران أول من أدى الجزية إلى رسول الله ﷺ، وآية الجزية إنما أُنزلت بعد الفتح، وهي قوله تعالى: ﴿قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر [ولا يحرّمون ما حرّم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون] ﴾ [التوبة: ٢٩] [[زيادة من جـ، أ، ر، و، وفي هـ: "الآية".]].

وقال أبو بكر بن مردويه: حدثنا سليمان بن أحمد، حدثنا أحمد بن داود المكي، حدثنا بشر بن مهران، أخبرنا محمد بن دينار، عن داود بن أبي هند، عن الشعبي، عن جابر قال: قدم على النبي ﷺ العاقب والطيب، فدعاهما إلى المُلاعنة، فواعداه على أن يلاعناه [[في جـ، أ، و: "يعاوداه". وفي ر: "يعاديه".]] الغداة. قال: فغدا رسول الله ﷺ، فأخذ بيد علي وفاطمة والحسن والحسين، ثم أرسل إليهما فأبيا أن يجيئا [[في أ: "يجيبا".]] وأقرّا بالخراج. قال: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "والذي بعثني بالحق لو قالا لا، لأمطر عليهم الوادي [[في جـ: "الوادي عليهم".]] نارًا". قال جابر: فيهم نزلت ﴿ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾. قال جابر: ﴿وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾ رسولُ الله ﷺ وعليَّ بن أبي طالب، ﴿وأبناءنا﴾ الحسنَ والحسين، ﴿ونساءنا﴾ فاطمةَ.

وهكذا رواه الحاكم في مستدركه، عن علي بن عيسى، عن أحمد بن محمد الأزهري [[في ر: "الأزهر" وفي أ، و: "الزهري".]] عن علي بن حُجر، عن علي بن مُسهر، عن داود بن أبي هند، به بمعناه. ثم قال: صحيح على شرط مسلم، ولم يخرجاه [[المستدرك (٢/٥٩٣، ٥٩٤)، ورواه أبو نعيم في دلائل النبوة (٢/٥٩٣) من طريق داود بن أبي هند عن الشعبي عن جابر به.]].

هكذا قال، وقد رواه أبو داود الطيالسي، عن شعبة، عن المغيرة [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "مغيرة".]] عن الشعبي مرسلًا، وهذا أصح [[رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره (٢/٣١٠) من طريق شعبة به، ورواه ابن أبي شيبة في المصنف (١٤/٥٤٩)، والطبري في تفسيره (٦/٤٦٨) من طريق جرير عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا، ورواه سعيد بن منصور في السنن برقم (٥٠٠) من طريق هشيم عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا.]]. وقد رُوي عن ابن عباس والبراء نحو ذلك.

ثم قال الله تعالى: ﴿إن هذا لهو القصص الحق﴾ أي: هذا الذي قصصناه عليك يا محمد في شأن عيسى هو الحق الذي لا معدل عنه ولا محيد. ﴿وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم. فإن تولّوا﴾ أي: عن هذا إلى غيره. ﴿فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين﴾ أي: من عدل عن الحق إلى الباطل فهو المفسد، والله عليم به، وسيجزيه على ذلك شر الجزاء، وهو القادر الذي لا يفوته شيء [سبحانه وبحمده، ونعوذ به من حلول نقمه] [[زيادة من و.]].

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah﴾ in terms of Allah's power, since He created him without a father, ﴿is like the likeness of Adam﴾, for Allah created him without a father or a mother. Rather, ﴿He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ The One who created Adam is able to create Jesus all the more so and more fittingly. If claiming sonship for Jesus is permissible because he was created without a father, then it is all the more permissible for Adam. It is known by consensus that this is false, so the claim regarding Jesus is even more false and its corruption even more evident. But the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, willed to show His power to His creation when He created Adam neither from a male nor from a female, created Eve from a male without a female, and created Jesus from a female without a male, just as He created the rest of creation from a male and a female. For this reason God said in Surah Maryam: ﴿And that We may make him a sign for the people﴾ [Maryam: 21].

Here He also said: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾ That is, this statement is the truth concerning Jesus, from which there is no turning away and no correct position other than it. What lies beyond the truth but error?

Then God, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), commanded him to invoke a curse (mubahalah) upon whoever opposed the truth concerning the matter of Jesus after the clear proof had appeared: ﴿Then whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves,﴾ that is, let us present them in the state of mubahalah ﴿then let us earnestly pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars﴾ that is, let us call down a curse upon one another ﴿so let the curse of Allah be upon the liars﴾ that is, from us or from you.

The occasion of revelation of this mubahalah, and of what precedes it from the beginning of the surah up to this point, concerned the delegation of Najran. When the Christians arrived, they began to dispute about Jesus and to assert about him what they asserted of sonship and divinity. So Allah revealed the opening of this surah in refutation of them, as Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and others have mentioned.

Ibn Ishaq said in his well-known Sirah and others said: A delegation of the Christians of Najran, sixty riders, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among them were fourteen men of their nobles to whom their affairs returned: al-Aqib, whose name was Abd al-Masih; al-Sayyid, who was al-Ayham; Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, brother of Bakr ibn Wa'il; Uways (or Aws) ibn al-Harith; Zayd; Qays; Yazid; Nabih; Khuwaylid; Amr; Khalid; Abd Allah; and Yuhannis.

The affairs of these men returned to three of them: al-Aqib, who was the leader of the people, their counsellor and the one whose opinion they never departed from; al-Sayyid, who was their scholar, the owner of their caravan and their gathering; and Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, who was their bishop, their rabbi, their imam and the master of their schools. He was an Arab from the Bakr ibn Wa'il, but he had become a Christian. The Romans and their kings held him in high esteem, honoured him, built churches for him, provided for him and gave him servants, because of the firmness they knew of him in their religion. He had known well the matter, the qualities and the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the earlier scriptures he knew, but his ignorance led him to persist in Christianity, because of the honour and high standing he enjoyed among its adherents.

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, saying: They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah and entered upon him in his mosque after he had prayed the afternoon prayer. They wore striped garments: robes and cloaks, in the splendour of the men of Bani al-Harith ibn Ka'b. He said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who saw them said: We have not seen a delegation like them after them. Their prayer time came, so they stood in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and prayed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave them." So they prayed facing the east.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them, and among them Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah and al-Aqib Abd al-Masih, or al-Sayyid al-Ayham, who were upon the religion of the king regarding Christianity, despite their differing positions. They said: He is Allah; they said: He is the son of Allah; and they said: He is the third of three. Exalted is Allah far above that by a great exaltation. And this is also the position of Christianity. They argued for their saying "He is Allah" that he used to give life to the dead, heal the sick, inform of the unseen, and create from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathe into it so that it became a bird, all of this by the command of Allah, "and that He may make him a sign for the people."

They argued for their saying that he is the son of Allah, saying: He had no known father, and he spoke in the cradle with something no one of the children of Adam had done before him.

They argued for their saying that he is the third of three by the words of Allah, "We have done," "We have commanded," "We have created," and "We have decreed." They said: If He were one, He would have said only "I have done, I have decreed, I have commanded and I have created." But rather He is Himself, and Jesus, and Mary, and all of this in their saying has been revealed in the Qur'an.

When the two rabbis (ḥabrān) spoke with him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Submit." They said: We have submitted. He said: "You have not submitted, so submit." They said: Indeed, we submitted before you. He said: "You have lied. What prevents you from Islam is your claim that Allah has a son, your worship of the cross, and your eating of pork." They said: Then who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent regarding them and did not answer them. So Allah revealed concerning that, from their saying and their disagreement, the beginning of Surah Al 'Imran up to some eighty-odd verses of it.

Then Ibn Ishaq discussed the tafsir up to where he said: When the news from Allah reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the decisive judgement between him and them, and he was commanded with what he was commanded regarding invoking a curse upon them if they rejected that, he invited them to it. They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, leave us to consider our affair, then we will come to you with what we want to do regarding what you have invited us to." So they departed from him, then they withdrew with al-Aqib, who was their counsellor, and they said: "O Abd al-Masih, what do you see?" He said: "By Allah, O assembly of Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a sent prophet, and he has brought you the decisive account concerning your companion. You know that no people ever invoked a curse upon a prophet and then their elder remained, nor did their young grow up. If you do it, it will be the destruction of you. If you insist on the familiar practice of your religion and on remaining on what you hold regarding your companion, then make peace with the man and return to your lands."

They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to invoke a curse upon you, and to leave you upon your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your Companions whom you approve for us, to judge between us in matters over which we have differed concerning our wealth, for you are trustworthy to us."

Muhammad ibn Ja'far said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Come to me this evening, and I will send with you the strong and trustworthy one." Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "I never loved leadership as I loved it that day, hoping that I would be the one. So I went to the noon prayer early. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the noon prayer and gave the salam, he looked to his right and his left, and I began stretching up so that he would see me. He kept searching with his gaze until he saw Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and he called him: 'Go out with them and judge between them with truth concerning what they differ about.'" Umar said: "Abu Ubaydah took it, may Allah be pleased with him."

[Sirat Ibn Hisham (1/573-575); al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (6/151) through Salamah ibn al-Fadl from Ibn Ishaq.]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, that the delegation of the people of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar, except that he said regarding the nobles that they were twelve. He mentioned the rest with a longer wording and additional elements.

Al-Bukhari said: Abbas ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, who said: al-Aqib and al-Sayyid, the two leaders of Najran, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wishing to invoke a curse upon him. He said: One of them said to his companion: "Do not do it, for by Allah, if he is a prophet and we invoke a curse upon him, neither we nor our descendants after us will prosper." They said: "We will give you what you asked of us, and send with us a trustworthy man, and send with us only a trustworthy one." He said: "I will surely send with you a man who is trustworthy, truly trustworthy." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) aspired to it, and he said: "Stand up, O Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah." When he stood, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is the trustworthy one of this Ummah."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through several routes from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Silah, from Hudhayfah, similarly.

Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Israil from Abu Ishaq, from Silah, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Every nation has a trustworthy one, and the trustworthy one of this Ummah is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah."

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Raqqi Abu Yazid narrated to us, Furat narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying at the Ka'bah, I will surely come to him and step on his neck." He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If he had done so, the angels would have seized him openly. And if the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and they would have seen their seats in the Fire. And if those who were invited to mubahalah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had come out, they would have returned without finding wealth or family."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i through the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Abd al-Karim, with the same. Al-Tirmidhi said: a hasan sahih hadith.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah the story of the delegation of Najran in a very lengthy form. We will mention it, for in it are many benefits, some strangeness, and relevance to this context. Al-Bayhaqi said:

حدثنا أبو عبد الله الحافظ وأبو سعيد محمد بن موسى بن الفضل، قالا: حدثنا أبو العباس محمد بن يعقوب، حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الجبار، حدثنا يونس بن بُكَير، عن سلمة بن عبد يسوع، عن أبيه، عن جده. قال يونس، وكان نصرانيًا فأسلم: إن رسول الله ﷺ كتب إلى أهل نجران قبل أن ينزل عليه ﴿طس سليمان﴾: "بسم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب، من محمد النبي رسول الله إلى أسقف نجران وأهل نجران، سلم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أسلم".]] أنتم، فإني أحمد إليكم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب. أما بعد، فإني أدعوكم إلى عبادة الله من عبادة العباد، وأدعوكم إلى ولاية الله من ولاية العباد، فإن أبيتم فالجزية، فإن أبيتم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أبيتم فقد".]] آذنتكم بحرب والسلام".

فلما أتى الأسقف الكتاب فقرأه فظع به، وذعره ذعرًا شديدًا، وبعث إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: شُرحبيل بن وداعة، وكان من همدان، ولم يكن أحد يُدعى إذا نزلت معضلة قبله، لا الأيهم ولا السيد ولا العاقب، فدفع الأسقف كتاب رسول الله ﷺ إلى شرحبيل فقرأه، فقال الأسقف: يا أبا مريم، ما رأيك [[في جـ: "ما رأيك يا أبا مريم".]]؟ فقال شرحبيل: قد علمتَ ما وعد الله إبراهيم في ذرية إسماعيل من النبوة، فما يؤمن أن يكون هذا هو ذاك الرجل، ليس لي في النبوة رأي، ولو كان أمرٌ من أمور الدنيا لأشرتُ عليك فيه برأيي، وجهدتُ لك. فقال له الأسقف: تنحَّ فاجلس. فتنحى شرحبيل فجلس ناحية. فبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: عبد الله بن شُرحبيل، وهو من ذي أصبح من حِمير، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل، فقال له الأسقف: فاجلس، فتنحى فجلس ناحية. وبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: جبار بن فيض، من بني الحارث بن كعب، أحد بني الحَماس، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل وعبد الله، فأمره الأسقف فتنحى فجلس ناحية.

فلما اجتمع الرأي منهم على تلك المقالة جميعًا، أمر الأسقف بالناقوس فضُرب به، ورُفعت النيران والمسوح في الصوامع، وكذلك كانوا يفعلون إذا فزعوا بالنهار، وإذا كان فزعهم ليلًا ضربوا بالناقوس، ورُفعت النيران في الصوامع، فاجتمعوا [[في جـ، ر: "فاجتمع".]] حين ضُرب بالناقوس ورُفعت المسوح، أهلَ الوادي أعلاه وأسفله -وطول الوادي مسيرة يوم للراكب السريع، وفيه ثلاث وسبعون قرية، وعشرون ومائة ألف مقاتل. فقرأ عليهم كتاب رسول الله ﷺ، وسألهم عن الرأي فيه، فاجتمع رأي أهل الرأي منهم على أن يبعثوا شرحبيل بن وداعة الهمداني، وعبد الله بن شرحبيل الأصبحي، وجبار بن فيض الحارثي، فيأتونهم [[في أ: "فيأتوهم".]] بخبر رسول الله ﷺ. فانطلق الوفد، حتى إذا كانوا بالمدينة وضعوا ثياب السفر عنهم، ولبسوا حُللًا لهم يجرُّونها من حِبرة، وخواتيم الذهب، ثم انطلقوا حتى أتوا رسول الله ﷺ، فسلموا عليه، فلم يرد عليهم [[في جـ: "عليه السلام" وفي أ: "عليهم السلام".]]، وتصدَّوْا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فلم يكلمهم، وعليهم تلك الحُلل وخواتيم الذهب. فانطلقوا يتبعون عثمان بن عفان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف، وكانا معرفة لهم، فوجدوهما في ناس من المهاجرين والأنصار في مجلس، فقالوا: يا عثمان ويا عبد الرحمن، إن نبيكم كتب إلينا بكتاب، فأقبلنا مجيبين له، فأتيناه فسلمنا عليه فلم يرد سلامنا، وتصدينا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فأعيانا أن يكلمنا، فما الرأي منكما، أترَوْن أن نرجع؟ فقالا لعلي بن أبي طالب -وهو في القوم-: ما ترى يا أبا الحسن في هؤلاء القوم؟ فقال علي لعثمان ولعبد الرحمن: أرى أن يضعوا حُللهم هذه وخواتيمهم، ويلبسوا ثياب سفرهم، ثم يعودا إليه. ففعلوا، فسلموا، فرد سلامهم، ثم قال: "والذي بعثني بالحق لقد أتَوْني المرةَ الأولى، وإن إبليس لَمعهم". ثم ساءلهم وساءلوه، فلم تزل به وبهم المسألة حتى قالوا: ما تقول في عيسى، فإنا نرجع إلى قومنا ونحن نصارى، يسرنا إن كنتَ نبيًّا أن نسمع ما تقول فيه [[في جـ: "فيه ما تقول".]]؟ قال رسول الله ﷺ: "ما عندي فيه شيء يومي هذا، فأقيموا حتى أخبركم بما [[في أ: "ما".]] يقول لي ربي في عيسى". فأصبح الغد وقد أنزل الله، عز وجل، هذه الآية: ﴿إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون. الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين. فمن حاجّك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنة الله على﴾ [[زيادة من جـ، ر، أ، و، وفي هـ: "إلى قوله".]] ﴿الكاذبين﴾. فأبَوْا أن يُقِرُّوا بذلك. فلما أصبح رسول الله ﷺ الغدَ بعد ما أخبرهم الخبرَ، أقبل مشتملًا على الحسن والحسين في خميل له، وفاطمة تمشي عند ظهره للمُلاعنة، وله يومئذٍ عدةُ نسوة. فقال شرحبيل لصاحبيه: قد علمتما أن الوادي إذا اجتمع أعلاه وأسفله لم يَرِدوا ولم يَصدروا إلا عن رأيي [[في ر: "رأي".]]، وإني والله أرى أمرًا ثقيلًا، والله لئن كان هذا الرجل ملكًا مبعوثًا، فكنا أول العرب طعن في عينيه [[في جـ، ر: "عينه".]] وردّ عليه أمره، لا يذهب لنا من صدره ولا من صدور أصحابه حتى يصيبونا بجائحة، وإنا لأدنى العرب منهم جوارًا، ولئن كان هذا الرجل نبيًّا مرسلًا فلاعنّاه لا يبقى على وجه الأرض منا شعر ولا ظفر إلا هلك. فقال [[في أ: "فقالا".]] له صاحباه: يا أبا مريم، فما الرأي؟ فقال: أرى [[في ر: "رأيي".]] أن أحكّمه، فإني أرى رجلًا لا يحكم شططًا أبدًا. فقالا له: أنت وذاك. قال: فلقي [[في جـ: "فتلقى"، وفي ر: "فيلقى".]] شرحبيلُ رسولَ الله ﷺ، فقال له: إني قد رأيت خيرًا من مُلاعنتك. فقال: "وما هو؟" فقال: حُكمك اليوم إلى الليل، وليلتُك إلى الصباح، فمهما حكّمتَ فينا فهو جائز. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: "لعل وراءك أحدًا يثرِّب عليك؟" فقال شرحبيل: سل صاحبيّ. فسألهما، فقالا: ما يرد الوادي ولا يصدر إلا عن رأي شرحبيل. فرجع رسول الله ﷺ فلم يلاعنهم، حتى إذا كان الغد أتَوْه فكتب لهم هذا الكتاب: "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، هذا ما كتب محمد النبي رسول الله لنجران -إن كان عليهم حكمُه- في كل ثمرة، وكل صفراء وبيضاء وسوداء ورقيق فاضلٍ [[في و: "فافضل".]] عليهم، وترك ذلك كله لهم، على ألفي حُلّة، في كل رجب ألف حلة، وفي كل صفر ألف حلة" وذكر تمام الشروط وبقية السياق [[دلائل النبوة للبيهقي (٥/٣٨٥).]].

والغرض أن وفودهم كان في سنة تسع؛ لأن الزهري قال: كان أهل نجران أول من أدى الجزية إلى رسول الله ﷺ، وآية الجزية إنما أُنزلت بعد الفتح، وهي قوله تعالى: ﴿قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر [ولا يحرّمون ما حرّم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون] ﴾ [التوبة: ٢٩] [[زيادة من جـ، أ، ر، و، وفي هـ: "الآية".]].

وقال أبو بكر بن مردويه: حدثنا سليمان بن أحمد، حدثنا أحمد بن داود المكي، حدثنا بشر بن مهران، أخبرنا محمد بن دينار، عن داود بن أبي هند، عن الشعبي، عن جابر قال: قدم على النبي ﷺ العاقب والطيب، فدعاهما إلى المُلاعنة، فواعداه على أن يلاعناه [[في جـ، أ، و: "يعاوداه". وفي ر: "يعاديه".]] الغداة. قال: فغدا رسول الله ﷺ، فأخذ بيد علي وفاطمة والحسن والحسين، ثم أرسل إليهما فأبيا أن يجيئا [[في أ: "يجيبا".]] وأقرّا بالخراج. قال: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "والذي بعثني بالحق لو قالا لا، لأمطر عليهم الوادي [[في جـ: "الوادي عليهم".]] نارًا". قال جابر: فيهم نزلت ﴿ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾. قال جابر: ﴿وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾ رسولُ الله ﷺ وعليَّ بن أبي طالب، ﴿وأبناءنا﴾ الحسنَ والحسين، ﴿ونساءنا﴾ فاطمةَ.

وهكذا رواه الحاكم في مستدركه، عن علي بن عيسى، عن أحمد بن محمد الأزهري [[في ر: "الأزهر" وفي أ، و: "الزهري".]] عن علي بن حُجر، عن علي بن مُسهر، عن داود بن أبي هند، به بمعناه. ثم قال: صحيح على شرط مسلم، ولم يخرجاه [[المستدرك (٢/٥٩٣، ٥٩٤)، ورواه أبو نعيم في دلائل النبوة (٢/٥٩٣) من طريق داود بن أبي هند عن الشعبي عن جابر به.]].

هكذا قال، وقد رواه أبو داود الطيالسي، عن شعبة، عن المغيرة [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "مغيرة".]] عن الشعبي مرسلًا، وهذا أصح [[رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره (٢/٣١٠) من طريق شعبة به، ورواه ابن أبي شيبة في المصنف (١٤/٥٤٩)، والطبري في تفسيره (٦/٤٦٨) من طريق جرير عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا، ورواه سعيد بن منصور في السنن برقم (٥٠٠) من طريق هشيم عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا.]]. وقد رُوي عن ابن عباس والبراء نحو ذلك.

ثم قال الله تعالى: ﴿إن هذا لهو القصص الحق﴾ أي: هذا الذي قصصناه عليك يا محمد في شأن عيسى هو الحق الذي لا معدل عنه ولا محيد. ﴿وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم. فإن تولّوا﴾ أي: عن هذا إلى غيره. ﴿فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين﴾ أي: من عدل عن الحق إلى الباطل فهو المفسد، والله عليم به، وسيجزيه على ذلك شر الجزاء، وهو القادر الذي لا يفوته شيء [سبحانه وبحمده، ونعوذ به من حلول نقمه] [[زيادة من و.]].

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah﴾ in terms of Allah's power, since He created him without a father, ﴿is like the likeness of Adam﴾, for Allah created him without a father or a mother. Rather, ﴿He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ The One who created Adam is able to create Jesus all the more so and more fittingly. If claiming sonship for Jesus is permissible because he was created without a father, then it is all the more permissible for Adam. It is known by consensus that this is false, so the claim regarding Jesus is even more false and its corruption even more evident. But the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, willed to show His power to His creation when He created Adam neither from a male nor from a female, created Eve from a male without a female, and created Jesus from a female without a male, just as He created the rest of creation from a male and a female. For this reason God said in Surah Maryam: ﴿And that We may make him a sign for the people﴾ [Maryam: 21].

Here He also said: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾ That is, this statement is the truth concerning Jesus, from which there is no turning away and no correct position other than it. What lies beyond the truth but error?

Then God, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), commanded him to invoke a curse (mubahalah) upon whoever opposed the truth concerning the matter of Jesus after the clear proof had appeared: ﴿Then whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves,﴾ that is, let us present them in the state of mubahalah ﴿then let us earnestly pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars﴾ that is, let us call down a curse upon one another ﴿so let the curse of Allah be upon the liars﴾ that is, from us or from you.

The occasion of revelation of this mubahalah, and of what precedes it from the beginning of the surah up to this point, concerned the delegation of Najran. When the Christians arrived, they began to dispute about Jesus and to assert about him what they asserted of sonship and divinity. So Allah revealed the opening of this surah in refutation of them, as Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and others have mentioned.

Ibn Ishaq said in his well-known Sirah and others said: A delegation of the Christians of Najran, sixty riders, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among them were fourteen men of their nobles to whom their affairs returned: al-Aqib, whose name was Abd al-Masih; al-Sayyid, who was al-Ayham; Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, brother of Bakr ibn Wa'il; Uways (or Aws) ibn al-Harith; Zayd; Qays; Yazid; Nabih; Khuwaylid; Amr; Khalid; Abd Allah; and Yuhannis.

The affairs of these men returned to three of them: al-Aqib, who was the leader of the people, their counsellor and the one whose opinion they never departed from; al-Sayyid, who was their scholar, the owner of their caravan and their gathering; and Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah, who was their bishop, their rabbi, their imam and the master of their schools. He was an Arab from the Bakr ibn Wa'il, but he had become a Christian. The Romans and their kings held him in high esteem, honoured him, built churches for him, provided for him and gave him servants, because of the firmness they knew of him in their religion. He had known well the matter, the qualities and the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the earlier scriptures he knew, but his ignorance led him to persist in Christianity, because of the honour and high standing he enjoyed among its adherents.

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, saying: They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah and entered upon him in his mosque after he had prayed the afternoon prayer. They wore striped garments: robes and cloaks, in the splendour of the men of Bani al-Harith ibn Ka'b. He said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who saw them said: We have not seen a delegation like them after them. Their prayer time came, so they stood in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and prayed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave them." So they prayed facing the east.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke with them, and among them Abu Harithah ibn Alqamah and al-Aqib Abd al-Masih, or al-Sayyid al-Ayham, who were upon the religion of the king regarding Christianity, despite their differing positions. They said: He is Allah; they said: He is the son of Allah; and they said: He is the third of three. Exalted is Allah far above that by a great exaltation. And this is also the position of Christianity. They argued for their saying "He is Allah" that he used to give life to the dead, heal the sick, inform of the unseen, and create from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathe into it so that it became a bird, all of this by the command of Allah, "and that He may make him a sign for the people."

They argued for their saying that he is the son of Allah, saying: He had no known father, and he spoke in the cradle with something no one of the children of Adam had done before him.

They argued for their saying that he is the third of three by the words of Allah, "We have done," "We have commanded," "We have created," and "We have decreed." They said: If He were one, He would have said only "I have done, I have decreed, I have commanded and I have created." But rather He is Himself, and Jesus, and Mary, and all of this in their saying has been revealed in the Qur'an.

When the two rabbis (ḥabrān) spoke with him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Submit." They said: We have submitted. He said: "You have not submitted, so submit." They said: Indeed, we submitted before you. He said: "You have lied. What prevents you from Islam is your claim that Allah has a son, your worship of the cross, and your eating of pork." They said: Then who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent regarding them and did not answer them. So Allah revealed concerning that, from their saying and their disagreement, the beginning of Surah Al 'Imran up to some eighty-odd verses of it.

Then Ibn Ishaq discussed the tafsir up to where he said: When the news from Allah reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the decisive judgement between him and them, and he was commanded with what he was commanded regarding invoking a curse upon them if they rejected that, he invited them to it. They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, leave us to consider our affair, then we will come to you with what we want to do regarding what you have invited us to." So they departed from him, then they withdrew with al-Aqib, who was their counsellor, and they said: "O Abd al-Masih, what do you see?" He said: "By Allah, O assembly of Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a sent prophet, and he has brought you the decisive account concerning your companion. You know that no people ever invoked a curse upon a prophet and then their elder remained, nor did their young grow up. If you do it, it will be the destruction of you. If you insist on the familiar practice of your religion and on remaining on what you hold regarding your companion, then make peace with the man and return to your lands."

They came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to invoke a curse upon you, and to leave you upon your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your Companions whom you approve for us, to judge between us in matters over which we have differed concerning our wealth, for you are trustworthy to us."

Muhammad ibn Ja'far said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Come to me this evening, and I will send with you the strong and trustworthy one." Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "I never loved leadership as I loved it that day, hoping that I would be the one. So I went to the noon prayer early. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the noon prayer and gave the salam, he looked to his right and his left, and I began stretching up so that he would see me. He kept searching with his gaze until he saw Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, and he called him: 'Go out with them and judge between them with truth concerning what they differ about.'" Umar said: "Abu Ubaydah took it, may Allah be pleased with him."

[Sirat Ibn Hisham (1/573-575); al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (6/151) through Salamah ibn al-Fadl from Ibn Ishaq.]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, that the delegation of the people of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar, except that he said regarding the nobles that they were twelve. He mentioned the rest with a longer wording and additional elements.

Al-Bukhari said: Abbas ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, who said: al-Aqib and al-Sayyid, the two leaders of Najran, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wishing to invoke a curse upon him. He said: One of them said to his companion: "Do not do it, for by Allah, if he is a prophet and we invoke a curse upon him, neither we nor our descendants after us will prosper." They said: "We will give you what you asked of us, and send with us a trustworthy man, and send with us only a trustworthy one." He said: "I will surely send with you a man who is trustworthy, truly trustworthy." The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) aspired to it, and he said: "Stand up, O Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah." When he stood, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is the trustworthy one of this Ummah."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, through several routes from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Silah, from Hudhayfah, similarly.

Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Israil from Abu Ishaq, from Silah, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly.

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Every nation has a trustworthy one, and the trustworthy one of this Ummah is Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah."

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Raqqi Abu Yazid narrated to us, Furat narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying at the Ka'bah, I will surely come to him and step on his neck." He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If he had done so, the angels would have seized him openly. And if the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and they would have seen their seats in the Fire. And if those who were invited to mubahalah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had come out, they would have returned without finding wealth or family."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i through the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Abd al-Karim, with the same. Al-Tirmidhi said: a hasan sahih hadith.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah the story of the delegation of Najran in a very lengthy form. We will mention it, for in it are many benefits, some strangeness, and relevance to this context. Al-Bayhaqi said:

حدثنا أبو عبد الله الحافظ وأبو سعيد محمد بن موسى بن الفضل، قالا: حدثنا أبو العباس محمد بن يعقوب، حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الجبار، حدثنا يونس بن بُكَير، عن سلمة بن عبد يسوع، عن أبيه، عن جده. قال يونس، وكان نصرانيًا فأسلم: إن رسول الله ﷺ كتب إلى أهل نجران قبل أن ينزل عليه ﴿طس سليمان﴾: "بسم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب، من محمد النبي رسول الله إلى أسقف نجران وأهل نجران، سلم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أسلم".]] أنتم، فإني أحمد إليكم إله إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب. أما بعد، فإني أدعوكم إلى عبادة الله من عبادة العباد، وأدعوكم إلى ولاية الله من ولاية العباد، فإن أبيتم فالجزية، فإن أبيتم [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "أبيتم فقد".]] آذنتكم بحرب والسلام".

فلما أتى الأسقف الكتاب فقرأه فظع به، وذعره ذعرًا شديدًا، وبعث إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: شُرحبيل بن وداعة، وكان من همدان، ولم يكن أحد يُدعى إذا نزلت معضلة قبله، لا الأيهم ولا السيد ولا العاقب، فدفع الأسقف كتاب رسول الله ﷺ إلى شرحبيل فقرأه، فقال الأسقف: يا أبا مريم، ما رأيك [[في جـ: "ما رأيك يا أبا مريم".]]؟ فقال شرحبيل: قد علمتَ ما وعد الله إبراهيم في ذرية إسماعيل من النبوة، فما يؤمن أن يكون هذا هو ذاك الرجل، ليس لي في النبوة رأي، ولو كان أمرٌ من أمور الدنيا لأشرتُ عليك فيه برأيي، وجهدتُ لك. فقال له الأسقف: تنحَّ فاجلس. فتنحى شرحبيل فجلس ناحية. فبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: عبد الله بن شُرحبيل، وهو من ذي أصبح من حِمير، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل، فقال له الأسقف: فاجلس، فتنحى فجلس ناحية. وبعث الأسقف إلى رجل من أهل نجران يقال له: جبار بن فيض، من بني الحارث بن كعب، أحد بني الحَماس، فأقرأه الكتاب، وسأله عن الرأي فيه، فقال له مثل قول شرحبيل وعبد الله، فأمره الأسقف فتنحى فجلس ناحية.

فلما اجتمع الرأي منهم على تلك المقالة جميعًا، أمر الأسقف بالناقوس فضُرب به، ورُفعت النيران والمسوح في الصوامع، وكذلك كانوا يفعلون إذا فزعوا بالنهار، وإذا كان فزعهم ليلًا ضربوا بالناقوس، ورُفعت النيران في الصوامع، فاجتمعوا [[في جـ، ر: "فاجتمع".]] حين ضُرب بالناقوس ورُفعت المسوح، أهلَ الوادي أعلاه وأسفله -وطول الوادي مسيرة يوم للراكب السريع، وفيه ثلاث وسبعون قرية، وعشرون ومائة ألف مقاتل. فقرأ عليهم كتاب رسول الله ﷺ، وسألهم عن الرأي فيه، فاجتمع رأي أهل الرأي منهم على أن يبعثوا شرحبيل بن وداعة الهمداني، وعبد الله بن شرحبيل الأصبحي، وجبار بن فيض الحارثي، فيأتونهم [[في أ: "فيأتوهم".]] بخبر رسول الله ﷺ. فانطلق الوفد، حتى إذا كانوا بالمدينة وضعوا ثياب السفر عنهم، ولبسوا حُللًا لهم يجرُّونها من حِبرة، وخواتيم الذهب، ثم انطلقوا حتى أتوا رسول الله ﷺ، فسلموا عليه، فلم يرد عليهم [[في جـ: "عليه السلام" وفي أ: "عليهم السلام".]]، وتصدَّوْا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فلم يكلمهم، وعليهم تلك الحُلل وخواتيم الذهب. فانطلقوا يتبعون عثمان بن عفان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف، وكانا معرفة لهم، فوجدوهما في ناس من المهاجرين والأنصار في مجلس، فقالوا: يا عثمان ويا عبد الرحمن، إن نبيكم كتب إلينا بكتاب، فأقبلنا مجيبين له، فأتيناه فسلمنا عليه فلم يرد سلامنا، وتصدينا لكلامه نهارًا طويلًا فأعيانا أن يكلمنا، فما الرأي منكما، أترَوْن أن نرجع؟ فقالا لعلي بن أبي طالب -وهو في القوم-: ما ترى يا أبا الحسن في هؤلاء القوم؟ فقال علي لعثمان ولعبد الرحمن: أرى أن يضعوا حُللهم هذه وخواتيمهم، ويلبسوا ثياب سفرهم، ثم يعودا إليه. ففعلوا، فسلموا، فرد سلامهم، ثم قال: "والذي بعثني بالحق لقد أتَوْني المرةَ الأولى، وإن إبليس لَمعهم". ثم ساءلهم وساءلوه، فلم تزل به وبهم المسألة حتى قالوا: ما تقول في عيسى، فإنا نرجع إلى قومنا ونحن نصارى، يسرنا إن كنتَ نبيًّا أن نسمع ما تقول فيه [[في جـ: "فيه ما تقول".]]؟ قال رسول الله ﷺ: "ما عندي فيه شيء يومي هذا، فأقيموا حتى أخبركم بما [[في أ: "ما".]] يقول لي ربي في عيسى". فأصبح الغد وقد أنزل الله، عز وجل، هذه الآية: ﴿إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون. الحق من ربك فلا تكن من الممترين. فمن حاجّك فيه من بعد ما جاءك من العلم فقل تعالوا ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم ثم نبتهل فنجعل لعنة الله على﴾ [[زيادة من جـ، ر، أ، و، وفي هـ: "إلى قوله".]] ﴿الكاذبين﴾. فأبَوْا أن يُقِرُّوا بذلك. فلما أصبح رسول الله ﷺ الغدَ بعد ما أخبرهم الخبرَ، أقبل مشتملًا على الحسن والحسين في خميل له، وفاطمة تمشي عند ظهره للمُلاعنة، وله يومئذٍ عدةُ نسوة. فقال شرحبيل لصاحبيه: قد علمتما أن الوادي إذا اجتمع أعلاه وأسفله لم يَرِدوا ولم يَصدروا إلا عن رأيي [[في ر: "رأي".]]، وإني والله أرى أمرًا ثقيلًا، والله لئن كان هذا الرجل ملكًا مبعوثًا، فكنا أول العرب طعن في عينيه [[في جـ، ر: "عينه".]] وردّ عليه أمره، لا يذهب لنا من صدره ولا من صدور أصحابه حتى يصيبونا بجائحة، وإنا لأدنى العرب منهم جوارًا، ولئن كان هذا الرجل نبيًّا مرسلًا فلاعنّاه لا يبقى على وجه الأرض منا شعر ولا ظفر إلا هلك. فقال [[في أ: "فقالا".]] له صاحباه: يا أبا مريم، فما الرأي؟ فقال: أرى [[في ر: "رأيي".]] أن أحكّمه، فإني أرى رجلًا لا يحكم شططًا أبدًا. فقالا له: أنت وذاك. قال: فلقي [[في جـ: "فتلقى"، وفي ر: "فيلقى".]] شرحبيلُ رسولَ الله ﷺ، فقال له: إني قد رأيت خيرًا من مُلاعنتك. فقال: "وما هو؟" فقال: حُكمك اليوم إلى الليل، وليلتُك إلى الصباح، فمهما حكّمتَ فينا فهو جائز. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: "لعل وراءك أحدًا يثرِّب عليك؟" فقال شرحبيل: سل صاحبيّ. فسألهما، فقالا: ما يرد الوادي ولا يصدر إلا عن رأي شرحبيل. فرجع رسول الله ﷺ فلم يلاعنهم، حتى إذا كان الغد أتَوْه فكتب لهم هذا الكتاب: "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، هذا ما كتب محمد النبي رسول الله لنجران -إن كان عليهم حكمُه- في كل ثمرة، وكل صفراء وبيضاء وسوداء ورقيق فاضلٍ [[في و: "فافضل".]] عليهم، وترك ذلك كله لهم، على ألفي حُلّة، في كل رجب ألف حلة، وفي كل صفر ألف حلة" وذكر تمام الشروط وبقية السياق [[دلائل النبوة للبيهقي (٥/٣٨٥).]].

والغرض أن وفودهم كان في سنة تسع؛ لأن الزهري قال: كان أهل نجران أول من أدى الجزية إلى رسول الله ﷺ، وآية الجزية إنما أُنزلت بعد الفتح، وهي قوله تعالى: ﴿قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر [ولا يحرّمون ما حرّم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون] ﴾ [التوبة: ٢٩] [[زيادة من جـ، أ، ر، و، وفي هـ: "الآية".]].

وقال أبو بكر بن مردويه: حدثنا سليمان بن أحمد، حدثنا أحمد بن داود المكي، حدثنا بشر بن مهران، أخبرنا محمد بن دينار، عن داود بن أبي هند، عن الشعبي، عن جابر قال: قدم على النبي ﷺ العاقب والطيب، فدعاهما إلى المُلاعنة، فواعداه على أن يلاعناه [[في جـ، أ، و: "يعاوداه". وفي ر: "يعاديه".]] الغداة. قال: فغدا رسول الله ﷺ، فأخذ بيد علي وفاطمة والحسن والحسين، ثم أرسل إليهما فأبيا أن يجيئا [[في أ: "يجيبا".]] وأقرّا بالخراج. قال: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "والذي بعثني بالحق لو قالا لا، لأمطر عليهم الوادي [[في جـ: "الوادي عليهم".]] نارًا". قال جابر: فيهم نزلت ﴿ندع أبناءنا وأبناءكم ونساءنا ونساءكم وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾. قال جابر: ﴿وأنفسنا وأنفسكم﴾ رسولُ الله ﷺ وعليَّ بن أبي طالب، ﴿وأبناءنا﴾ الحسنَ والحسين، ﴿ونساءنا﴾ فاطمةَ.

وهكذا رواه الحاكم في مستدركه، عن علي بن عيسى، عن أحمد بن محمد الأزهري [[في ر: "الأزهر" وفي أ، و: "الزهري".]] عن علي بن حُجر، عن علي بن مُسهر، عن داود بن أبي هند، به بمعناه. ثم قال: صحيح على شرط مسلم، ولم يخرجاه [[المستدرك (٢/٥٩٣، ٥٩٤)، ورواه أبو نعيم في دلائل النبوة (٢/٥٩٣) من طريق داود بن أبي هند عن الشعبي عن جابر به.]].

هكذا قال، وقد رواه أبو داود الطيالسي، عن شعبة، عن المغيرة [[في جـ، ر، أ، و: "مغيرة".]] عن الشعبي مرسلًا، وهذا أصح [[رواه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره (٢/٣١٠) من طريق شعبة به، ورواه ابن أبي شيبة في المصنف (١٤/٥٤٩)، والطبري في تفسيره (٦/٤٦٨) من طريق جرير عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا، ورواه سعيد بن منصور في السنن برقم (٥٠٠) من طريق هشيم عن مغيرة عن الشعبي به مرسلًا.]]. وقد رُوي عن ابن عباس والبراء نحو ذلك.

ثم قال الله تعالى: ﴿إن هذا لهو القصص الحق﴾ أي: هذا الذي قصصناه عليك يا محمد في شأن عيسى هو الحق الذي لا معدل عنه ولا محيد. ﴿وما من إله إلا الله وإن الله لهو العزيز الحكيم. فإن تولّوا﴾ أي: عن هذا إلى غيره. ﴿فإن الله عليم بالمفسدين﴾ أي: من عدل عن الحق إلى الباطل فهو المفسد، والله عليم به، وسيجزيه على ذلك شر الجزاء، وهو القادر الذي لا يفوته شيء [سبحانه وبحمده، ونعوذ به من حلول نقمه] [[زيادة من و.]].

This address includes the People of the Scripture, Jews and Christians, and whoever follows their way. ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word﴾. The word (kalimah) is used for a complete meaningful sentence, as is the case here. Then He described it by saying: ﴿that is equitable between us and you﴾, meaning just and fair, where we and you are on equal terms. Then He explained it by saying: ﴿that we worship none but Allah and associate nothing with Him﴾.

Not an idol, nor a statue, nor a cross, nor a false deity (taghut), nor fire, nor anything else. Rather, we single out worship for Allah alone, with no partner. This is the call of all the Messengers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We did not send any messenger before you except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 25]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid taghut"﴾ [An-Nahl: 36].

Then He said: ﴿and not take one another as lords besides Allah﴾. Ibn Juraij said: this means that some of us do not obey others in disobedience to Allah. 'Ikrimah said: this means that some of us do not prostrate to others.

﴿And if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾ That is: if they turn away from this equity and this call, then call them to witness your steadfastness upon Islam, which Allah has prescribed for you.

We have mentioned in the commentary on al-Bukhari, when narrating it through the chain of al-Zuhri, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Abu Sufyan, the story of his visit to Caesar (Qaysar), when Caesar asked them about the lineage of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his description and attributes, and what he called to. Abu Sufyan informed him of all of that clearly, even though Abu Sufyan was at that time a polytheist who had not yet embraced Islam. This was after the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah and before the Conquest, as is explicitly stated in the hadith. And when [Caesar] asked him, "Does he break his promises?" he said, "I said: No, and we are in a truce with him, and we do not know what he will do during it." He said: "I could not add a single word other than this." The point is that he said: "Then the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought and read, and in it was:

'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great one of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: Embrace Islam and you will be safe; embrace Islam and Allah will give you your reward twice. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the Arisiyyin (peasants). And, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we worship none but Allah and associate nothing with Him, and that some of us do not take others as lords besides Allah." But if they turn away, then say: "Bear witness that we are Muslims."'" [[The story of Heraclius with Abu Sufyan was narrated by al-Bukhari in full in his Sahih, no. (7).]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others have mentioned that the beginning of Surah Al 'Imran, up to about eighty-some verses of it, was revealed concerning the delegation of Najran. Al-Zuhri said: they were the first to offer the jizya (poll-tax). There is no disagreement that the verse of the jizya was revealed after the Conquest. So what is the reconciliation between the writing of this verse before the Conquest in the letter to Heraclius, as part of the letter, and what Muhammad ibn Ishaq and al-Zuhri mentioned? The answer has several aspects:

First: It is possible that this verse was revealed twice, once before al-Hudaybiyyah and once after the Conquest.

Second: It is possible that the beginning of Surah Al 'Imran was revealed concerning the delegation of Najran up to this verse, and this verse was revealed before that. Ibn Ishaq's statement "up to about eighty-some verses" would then not be accurate, given the indication of the hadith of Abu Sufyan.

Third: It is possible that the arrival of the delegation of Najran was before al-Hudaybiyyah, and what they offered was a reconciliation in place of mubahalah (mutual cursing), not in the form of the jizya, but rather within the category of truce and settlement. The later revelation of the verse of the jizya agreed with that arrangement, just as the ruling of the one-fifth (khumus) and the four-fifths came in accordance with what 'Abdullah ibn Jahsh did in that expedition (sariyyah) before Badr, and then the ordinance of distribution was revealed in accordance with that.

Fourth: It is possible that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to write this [statement] [[Added from ja, ra, a, w.]] in his letter to Heraclius, it had not yet been revealed; then the Qur'an was revealed in agreement with it, just as it was revealed in agreement with the opinion of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) regarding the veil, the captives, not praying over the hypocrites, the verse ﴿And take from the station of Abraham a place of prayer﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 125], and the verse ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for you wives better than you﴾ [At-Tahrim: 5], and so on.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verse 65–68:

He (Exalted is He) rebukes the Jews and the Christians for their disputation concerning Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), and for the claim of each group that he was one of them, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said:

Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Christians of Najran and the rabbis of the Jews gathered in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and disputed before him. The rabbis said: "Abraham was none but a Jew." The Christians said: "Abraham was none but a Christian." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham, when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Will you not reason?﴾ That is: how can you claim, O Jews, that he was a Jew, when his time was before Allah sent down the Torah to Moses? And how can you claim, O Christians, that he was a Christian, when Christianity arose long after his time? Therefore He said: ﴿Will you not reason?﴾

Then He said: ﴿Here you are, those who have argued about that of which you have knowledge; but why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? And Allah knows, while you know not.﴾

This is a denunciation of those who argue about matters of which they have no knowledge. The Jews and the Christians disputed about Abraham without knowledge. Had they argued about what they actually had knowledge of from their religions, which were prescribed for them until the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ), it would have been more fitting for them. Instead they spoke about what they did not know, so Allah rebuked them for that and commanded them to refer what they have no knowledge of to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, who knows affairs in their realities and manifest forms. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah knows, while you know not.﴾
