Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a hanif (inclining to truth), a Muslim﴾, that is, one who turned away from polytheism, intending faith ﴿and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [al-Baqarah: 135].

This verse is like the one that preceded it in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And they say, "Be Jews or Christians, you will be guided." Say, "Rather, the religion of Abraham, inclining to truth, and he was not of the polytheists."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 135].

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among the people are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe; and Allah is the Ally of the believers.﴾ He says: The most deserving of following Abraham the Friend are those who followed him in his religion, and this Prophet, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), and those who believed among his companions, the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them.

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Abu al-Ahwas informed us, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every Prophet has his allies from among the prophets, and my ally among them is my father and the Friend of my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, the most worthy of Abraham among the people are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe; and Allah is the Ally of the believers.﴾

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Bazzar through the narration of Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from his father, with the same chain. It is fitting to mention here the hadith that al-Bukhari cited in more than one place of his Sahih, and one of the best versions of it is his narration in the Book of Guarantee (Kafalah), where he said: Al-Layth said: Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he mentioned a man from the Children of Israel who asked some of the Children of Israel to lend him a thousand dinars. He said: "Bring me witnesses, I will have them witness it." He said: "Allah is sufficient as a witness." He said: "Bring me a guarantor." He said: "Allah is sufficient as a guarantor." He said: "You have spoken the truth." So he gave him the money for a specified term. The man went out to sea and attended to his need. Then he sought a ship to board so that he could arrive by the appointed time, but he did not find a ship. So he took a piece of wood, hollowed it out, put a thousand dinars into it along with a letter from him to his companion, then sealed its opening, brought it to the sea, and said: "O Allah, You know that I borrowed a thousand dinars from so-and-so, and he asked me for a guarantor, and I said: 'Allah is sufficient as a guarantor,' and he was content with You. He asked me for a witness, and I said: 'Allah is sufficient as a witness,' and he was content with You. I truly strove to find a ship to send to him what is his, but I could not, so I entrust it to You." Then he threw it into the sea until it drifted into it, and he departed while still seeking a ship to go to his land. Meanwhile, the man who had lent him went out looking, hoping that a ship would bring him his money, and behold, there was the piece of wood containing the money. He took it for his family as firewood, but when he broke it open he found the money and the letter. Allah, the Exalted, says: Indeed, those who sell for a small price (yashtaruna) the covenant of Allah and their oaths, [namely] the covenant which Allah took from them concerning following Muhammad ﷺ, and mentioning his description to the people and making clear his matter, and their false, sinful, wicked oaths for a paltry, insignificant price, which is the goods of this worldly life, which is transient and perishing: ﴿They will have no share in the Hereafter﴾. That is, they have no portion in it and no benefit from it. ﴿Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection﴾. That is, with mercy from Him toward them; meaning, He will not speak to them with words of kindness, nor look at them with an eye of mercy. ﴿Nor will He purify them﴾, that is, from sins and defilements, but He will command them to the Fire. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾

Hadiths related to this noble verse have been transmitted, and we will mention what is easily available of them:

The First Hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: 'Ali ibn Mudrik informed me, who said: I heard Abu Zur'ah, from Kharashah ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three whom Allah will not speak to, nor look at, on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they? They have failed and lost." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeated it three times. He said: "The one who lets his garment trail (al-musbil), the one who promotes his merchandise by a false oath (al-munfiq), and the one who reminds of his favours (al-mannan)." Muslim and the authors of the Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, with the same chain.

Another route: Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, from al-Hurayri, from Abu al-'Ala' ibn al-Shikhkhir, from Abu al-Ahmas, who said: I met Abu Dharr and said to him: "It has reached me that you narrate a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "Surely you do not think I would lie against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after I have heard it from him. What has reached you about me?" I said: "It has reached me that you say: Three whom Allah loves, and three whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, detests." He said: "I said it and I heard it." I said: "Who are those whom Allah loves?" He said: "A man who meets the enemy in a company and thrusts his chest toward them until he is killed or Allah grants victory to his companions; a people who travel and the journey lengthens for them until they wish the earth were folded up for them, so they halt and one of them withdraws to pray until he awakens them for their departure; and a man who has a neighbour who harms him, so he endures his harm until death or departure separates them." I said: "And who are those whom Allah detests?" He said: "The merchant who swears much (al-hallaf), or the seller who swears much, and the arrogant poor man, and the stingy man who reminds of favours (al-mannan)." Gharib from this route.

The Second Hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim, who said: 'Adi ibn 'Adi narrated to us, Raja' ibn Haywah and al-Urs ibn 'Amirah informed me, from his father 'Adi, namely Ibn 'Amirah al-Kindi, who said: A man from Kindah called Imru' al-Qays ibn 'Abis disputed with a man from Hadramawt over land before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He judged against the Hadrami by the evidence, but he had no evidence, so he judged against Imru' al-Qays by the oath. The Hadrami said: "If I let him take the oath, O Messenger of Allah, by the Lord of the Ka'bah, my land is gone." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever swears a false oath to seize by it the property of a person will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while He is angry with him." Raja' said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿Indeed, those who sell for a small price the covenant of Allah and their oaths﴾. Imru' al-Qays said: "What is for the one who leaves it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Paradise." He said: "Then I bear witness that I have left it for him entirely." An-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of 'Adi ibn 'Adi, with the same chain.

The Third Hadith: Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever swears an oath in which he is a wicked liar, to seize by it the property of a Muslim man, will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while He is angry with him."

Al-Ash'ath said: By Allah, this was revealed concerning me. There was land between me and a Jew, and he denied it, so I brought him before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Do you have evidence?" I said: "No." He said to the Jew: "Swear." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, he will swear and my property will be lost." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who sell for a small price the covenant of Allah and their oaths﴾ [to the end of] the verse. Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash.

Another route: Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever unjustly seizes the property of a Muslim man will meet Allah while He is angry with him." He said: Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays came and said: "What is Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrating to you?" We related it to him, and he said: "This hadith was about me. I brought a cousin of mine before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a well of mine which was in his possession, and he denied it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Your evidence that it is your well, or else his oath.'" He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have no evidence, and if you make it by his oath, my well will be taken; indeed my opponent is a wicked man." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever unjustly seizes the property of a Muslim man will meet Allah while He is angry with him." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who sell for a small price the covenant of Allah and their oaths, [those will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment]﴾.

The Fourth Hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rushdin narrated to us, from Zabban, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed, Allah the Exalted has servants whom He will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify, nor look at." It was said: "And who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "One who disowns his parents, turning away from them, and one who disowns his child, and a man on whom a people bestowed favour, but he denied their favour and disowned them."

The Fifth Hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, al-'Awwam informed us (meaning Ibn Hawshab), from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman (meaning al-Saksaki), from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa: that a man displayed his merchandise in the market and swore by Allah that he had been offered for it what he had not been offered, in order to deceive a Muslim man into it, and this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who sell for a small price the covenant of Allah and their oaths﴾. al-Bukhari narrated it through more than one route from al-'Awwam.

The Sixth Hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at, nor purify, and for them is a painful punishment: a man who withheld surplus water from the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil), a man who swore an oath upon merchandise after the 'Asr prayer, meaning falsely, and a man who pledged allegiance to a leader: if he gives him, he fulfils it for him, and if he does not give him, he does not fulfil it." Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Waki', and al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

Ibn Kathir said:

Allah, the Exalted, informs us about the Jews, upon whom be the curses of Allah, that among them is a group who distort the words from their places (yuharrifun al-kalim 'an mawadi'ihi) and alter the speech of Allah (yubaddilun kalama Allah), turning it away from its intended meaning, so that they may deceive the ignorant into thinking that it is in the Book of Allah in that form, and attribute it to Allah, when it is a lie against Allah, while they know within themselves that they have lied and fabricated in all of that. Therefore He said: ﴿And they speak falsehood against Allah while they know﴾.

Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿Twisting their tongues with the Book﴾ means they distort it.

Similarly, al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that they distort and add (to the Book), and no one among the creation of Allah removes a word of the books of Allah; rather, they distort it by interpreting it in other than its proper interpretation.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Indeed the Torah and the Gospel, as Allah sent them down, have not had a single letter changed in them, but they lead people astray through distortion and misinterpretation, and through books that they used to write from their own selves, ﴿and they say, "It is from Allah," and it is not from Allah﴾. As for the books of Allah, they are preserved and cannot be altered.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. If Wahb meant what is in their hands of that, then there is no doubt that alteration, distortion, addition and omission have entered it. As for the translation of that witnessed text into Arabic, there is a great error in it, many additions and omissions, and gross misunderstanding. It is of the category of interpreting a translated meaning, and most of their understanding, indeed nearly all of it, is corrupt. But if he meant the books of Allah which are His books from Him, then those, as he said, are preserved and nothing has entered them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 79–80:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to us, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Abu Rafi' al-Qurazi said, when the rabbis of the Jews and the Christians of the people of Najran gathered before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he invited them to Islam: "Do you want us to worship you, O Muhammad, as the Christians worship 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary)?" A man from the people of Najran, a Christian called al-Ra'is, said: "Is that what you want from us, O Muhammad, and is it to this that you call us?" Or as he said. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I seek refuge in Allah from worshipping other than Allah, or from commanding the worship of other than Him. It is not for this that He sent me, nor for this that He commanded me." Or as he said (ﷺ). Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning their words: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Scripture and authority and prophethood⦆ [the verse][[Added from manuscripts J, R, A, W.]] up to His words: ﴿after you have submitted [to Allah]﴾[[Ibn Hisham, al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/554), and al-Tabari in his Tafsir (6/539) narrated it through Ibn Ishaq.]].

So His words ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Scripture and authority and prophethood, and then he would say to the people, "Be worshippers of me rather than of Allah"﴾ mean: it is not fitting for a human to whom Allah has given the Scripture, authority and prophethood to say to the people, "Worship me instead of Allah," that is, besides Allah. And if this is not fitting for a prophet or a messenger, then it is all the more so, and by way of greater priority, that it is not fitting for anyone else among mankind. For this reason al-Hasan al-Basri said: "It is not appropriate for a believer to command the people to worship him." He said: "This is because the people (meaning the People of the Book) used to worship one another; they would worship their rabbis and monks, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Tawbah: 31][[Added from manuscripts J, R, A, W, and in H: "the verse".]]. In the Musnad and in al-Tirmidhi (as will come), it is related that 'Adi ibn Hatim said: "O Messenger of Allah, they did not worship them." He said: "Yes, indeed. They made lawful for them what was forbidden and forbade for them what was lawful, and they followed them. That is their worship of them."

So the ignorant among the rabbis and monks, and the leaders of misguidance, fall under this blame and reproach, unlike the messengers and their followers among the scholars who act upon their knowledge. They only command what Allah has commanded, which His noble messengers conveyed to them, and they only forbid what Allah has forbidden, which His noble messengers conveyed to them. The messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all, are the envoys between Allah and His creation in delivering what they were entrusted with of the message and conveying the trust. They fulfilled this in the most complete manner, advised the creation, and conveyed the truth to them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿But be distinguished worshippers of the Lord because of what you have been teaching of the Scripture and what you have been studying﴾, that is: rather, the messenger says to the people, "Be rabbanis (those devoted to the Lord)." Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Razin and others said: that is, wise, learned, and forbearing scholars. Al-Hasan and others said: jurists (fuqaha'). This was also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas. Also from al-Hasan: people of worship and people of piety.

Al-Dahhak said regarding His words ﴿because of what you have been teaching of the Scripture and what you have been studying﴾: It is incumbent upon whoever learns the Qur'an to be a jurist. "Tu'allimun" means: you make [its meaning] understood, i.e., you cause its meaning to be comprehended. It was also read as ﴿tu'allimun﴾ with a shaddah, from ta'lim (teaching). ﴿and what you have been studying﴾ means: you memorize its words.

Then He said: ﴿And He would not order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords﴾, that is: nor would He command you to worship anyone other than Allah, neither a sent prophet nor a near angel. ﴿Would He order you to disbelieve after you have submitted [to Allah]?﴾ That is: He would not do that. For whoever calls to the worship of other than Allah has called to disbelief, and the prophets only command faith, which is the worship of Allah alone, with no partner for Him, as He said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. And He said: ﴿And We had certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl: 36], the verse. And He said: ﴿And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We ever appoint, besides the Most Merciful, deities to be worshipped?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45]. And He said, informing about the angels: ﴿And whoever among them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," - We would recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 29].

For this reason, the Exalted and Most Holy said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must support him." He said: "Do you affirm and accept My burden on this condition?"﴾ That is: whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom.

﴿Then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you﴾, ﴿you must believe in him and you must support him.﴾ He said: ﴿Do you affirm...﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Rabi' and Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿Isri﴾ means My covenant.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿Isri﴾ means: heavy is what you have taken upon yourselves of My covenant, that is, My strong and emphatic pact.

﴿They said: "We affirm." He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses. Whoever turns away after that"﴾ that is, from this covenant and pact, ﴿those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

And He commanded him to take the covenant from his own nation: that if Muhammad (ﷺ) were sent while they were alive, they would surely believe in him and support him.

Tawus, al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah said: Allah took the covenant of the prophets that some of them would confirm one another.

This does not contradict what 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas said, nor negate it; rather it entails it and implies it. For this reason, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, in the same sense as the words of 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abdullah ibn Thabit, who said: 'Umar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I passed by a brother of mine from Quraiza, and he wrote for me some comprehensive passages (jawami' al-kalim) from the Torah. So 'Umar said: "We are pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved and said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if Musa (Moses), upon him be peace, were to appear among you and you followed him and abandoned me, you would surely go astray. He, exalted is He, rebukes those who desire a religion other than the religion of Allah, which He sent down through His Books and sent His messengers with, and which is worshipping Him alone with no partner, the One ﴿to Whom submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning that whoever is in them submits to Him, willingly or unwillingly, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows [prostrate] in the mornings and the evenings﴾ [al-Ra'd: 15]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created, how their shadows turn from the right and the left, prostrating to Allah while they are humbled? They fear their Lord above them and do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Nahl: 48–50].

The believer submits to Allah with his heart and his body, while the disbeliever submits to Allah unwillingly, for he is under subjugation, compulsion and the great authority, which cannot be opposed or resisted.

A hadith has been transmitted concerning the interpretation of this verse, with a different and strange meaning. The hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said:

Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-'Askari narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Hafs al-Nufayli narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Mihsan al-'Ukkashi narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly﴾. As for "whoever is in the heavens," they are the angels; as for "whoever is on the earth," they are those born upon Islam; and as for "unwillingly," they are those brought from the captive nations in chains and shackles, who are led to Paradise while they are unwilling.[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (11/194). The name of Ibn 'Abbas has dropped out here, so the isnad (chain of narration) in his work is: from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ, with this text. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6/326): "It contains Muhammad ibn Mihsan al-'Ukkashi, who is matruk (abandoned in narration)."]]

It is also reported in the Sahih: "Your Lord is amazed at a people who are led to Paradise in chains."[[Sahih al-Bukhari (3010).]] A supporting report will come from another route, but the first meaning of the verse is stronger.

Waki' said in his Tafsir: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly﴾: he said, "It is like His saying: ﴿And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah'﴾ [Luqman: 25]."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 86–89:

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' al-Basri narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man from the Ansar had embraced Islam, then apostatized and joined the polytheists. Then he regretted it, and sent to his people: "Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me: Is there any repentance for me?" He said: Then this was revealed: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had testified that the Messenger was true and clear proofs had come to them?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿except for those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

This was also related by al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim, through the route of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, with the same chain. Al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Humayd al-A'raj narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: al-Harith ibn Suwayd came and embraced Islam with the Prophet ﷺ, then al-Harith disbelieved and returned to his people, so Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿...except for those who repent after that and make amends, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. He said: A man from his people carried it to him and recited it to him. Al-Harith said: "By Allah, as far as I know, you are indeed truthful, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more truthful than you, and Allah is the most truthful of the three." He said: So al-Harith returned, embraced Islam, and his Islam was good.

As for the words of the Most High: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and had testified that the Messenger was true and clear proofs had come to them?﴾ That is: the proofs and evidences were established against them regarding the truth of what the Messenger brought them, and the matter became clear to them. Then they apostatized back into the darkness of polytheism. How, then, do such people deserve guidance after they have become entangled in blindness? Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

Then He said: ﴿Those—their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together.⦆ That is: Allah curses them, and His creation curses them. ﴿Abiding therein⦆ That is: in the curse. ﴿Their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be reprieved⦆ That is: the punishment will not be relaxed for them, nor will it be lightened for them for a single moment.

Then the Most High said: ﴿Except for those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful⦆ This is from His kindness, His goodness, His compassion, His mercy, and His benevolence toward His creation: that whoever turns to Him in repentance, He turns to him in forgiveness.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verse 92:

[Waki' narrated in his Tafsir from Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, regarding ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾ that he said: "Al-birr is Paradise."] [[Addition from w.]] And Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah was the wealthiest of the Ansar [[In j, a: "the wealthiest of the Ansar", and in r, w: "the greatest Ansari".]] in Madinah in property, and the dearest of his properties to him was Bayruha', which faced the Masjid, and the Prophet ﷺ would enter it and drink from its pure water. Anas said: When this was revealed: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾, Abu Talhah said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed Allah says: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾, and indeed the dearest of my properties to me is Bayruha', and indeed it is a charity for Allah, I hope for its righteousness and its reserve with Allah the Exalted, so place it, O Messenger of Allah, wherever Allah shows you [Ta'ala]." [[Addition from j.]] The Prophet ﷺ said: "Bakh! That is a profitable property, that is a profitable property. I have heard what you said, and I think that you should give it to your nearest relatives." Abu Talhah said: "I will do so, O Messenger of Allah." So Abu Talhah distributed it among his relatives and the sons of his paternal uncle. [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] [[Al-Musnad (3/141), Sahih al-Bukhari, numbers (1461, 2752, 2318, 2769, 5611, 4554), and Sahih Muslim, number (998).]]

And in the Two Sahihs, that Umar [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from w.]] said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have never acquired property more precious to me than my share at Khaybar. So what do you command me regarding it?" He said: "Keep the principal and give the fruit in charity." [[I did not find it in them, but al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Sunan (2/232) and al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan (4/193) through the chain of Sufyan, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar that Umar said, and he mentioned it.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abu al-Khattab Ziyad ibn Yahya al-Hassani narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, from Abu Amr ibn Hamas, from Hamzah ibn Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: Abdullah said: This verse came to my mind: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾, so I considered what Allah had given me, and I found nothing dearer to me than a Roman slave-girl. So I said: "She is free for the sake of Allah." Had I returned to something I had dedicated to Allah, I would have married her, meaning I would have wed her. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, number (2914), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/326): "Al-Bazzar narrated it, and in its chain is one whom I do not know."]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verse 93–95:

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, who said: Ibn 'Abbas [may Allah be pleased with him] said: A group of the Jews came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and said: "Tell us about some matters which we will ask you about, which none knows except a prophet." He said: "Ask me whatever you wish, but make for me a covenant (dhimmah) of Allah and what Ya'qub (Jacob) took from his sons: if I tell you something and you recognize it, you will follow me in Islam." They said: "That is for you." He said: "Then ask me whatever you wish." They said: "Tell us about four matters: Tell us, which food did Isra'il (Israel) forbid for himself? And how is the water of the woman and the water of the man? How does this unlettered Prophet [sleep]? And who is his guardian (wali) among the angels?" So he took from them the covenant that if he informed them, they would surely follow him. He said: "I adjure you by Him who sent down the Torah to Musa (Moses): Do you know that Isra'il became severely ill and his sickness lasted long, so he vowed to Allah that if Allah cured him of his sickness, he would forbid the most beloved drink and the most beloved food to him? The most beloved food to him was the meat of camels, and the most beloved drink to him was their milk?" They said: "Yes, by Allah." He said: "O Allah, bear witness against them." And he said: "I adjure you by Allah, than whom there is no god but He, who sent down the Torah to Musa: Do you know that the water of the man is white and thick, and the water of the woman is yellow and thin, and whichever of them prevails, the child and the resemblance belong to it by the leave of Allah; if the water of the man prevails over the water of the woman, it is male by the leave of Allah, and if the water of the woman prevails over the water of the man, it is female by the leave of Allah?" They said: "Yes." He said: "O Allah, bear witness against them." And he said: "I adjure you by Him who sent down the Torah to Musa: Do you know that this unlettered Prophet's eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep?" They said: "O Allah, yes." He said: "O Allah, bear witness." They said: "And you now, tell us who is your guardian among the angels? For then we will either unite with you or part from you." He said: "My guardian is Jibril (Gabriel), and Allah has never sent a prophet except that he was his guardian." They said: "Then at that point we part from you; if your guardian were other than him, we would have followed you (pledged allegiance to you)." At that point Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 97] to the end of the verse.

And Ahmad also narrated it from Husayn ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Hamid, with the same chain.

Another route: Ahmad said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-'Ijli narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Jews approached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we will ask you about five things; if you inform us of them, we will know that you are a prophet and follow you." So he took from them what Isra'il had taken from his sons when he said: ﴿Allah is Guardian over what we say﴾ [Yusuf: 66]. He said: "Speak." They said: "Tell us about the sign of a prophet." He said: "His eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep." They said: "Tell us how a woman becomes female and how she becomes male." He said: "The two waters meet; when the water of the man prevails over the water of the woman, she becomes male, and when the water of the woman prevails over the water of the man, she becomes female." They said: "Tell us what Isra'il forbade for himself." He said: "He used to suffer from sciatica (irq al-nasa), and he found nothing that suited him except the milk of such-and-such," - Ahmad said: some of them said: meaning the camels - "so he forbade their meat." They said: "You have spoken the truth." They said: "Tell us what this thunder is." He said: "An angel from the angels of Allah, appointed over the clouds, in his hand (or in his hands) is a whip of fire with which he drives the clouds, guiding them wherever Allah the Mighty and Majestic commands." They said: "Then what is this sound that is heard?" He said: "Its voice." They said: "You have spoken the truth. Only one remains, and it is the one by which we will follow you if you inform us of it, for there is no prophet except that he has an angel who brings him the news. So tell us, who is your companion?" He said: "Jibril, peace be upon him." They said: "Jibril is the one who brings war, fighting and punishment; he is our enemy. If you had said Mika'il, who brings mercy, plants and rain, it would have been (different)." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril - for he has brought it down upon your heart by the leave of Allah, confirming what came before it, and as guidance and good tidings for the believers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 97].

Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-'Ijli, similar to it. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan gharib.

Ibn Jurayj and al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: Isra'il - that is Ya'qub, peace be upon him - was afflicted by sciatica at night, which disturbed him and kept him from sleep, and the pain would subside during the day. So he vowed to Allah that if Allah granted him recovery, he would not eat any vein (irq) nor any animal that had a vein.

Similarly said al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. Thus it was related and narrated by Ibn Jarir in his tafsir. He said: His sons followed him in forbidding that, emulating him and following his way. He said: And His saying ﴿before the Torah was revealed﴾ means: he forbade that for himself before the Torah was revealed.

I say: This context, after what preceded, has two connections.

The first: Isra'il, peace be upon him, forbade the things most beloved to him and abandoned them for the sake of Allah, and this was permissible in their law. Thus it has a connection after His saying: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾. This is the prescribed (mashru') path for us: spending in obedience to Allah from what the servant loves and desires, as He said: ﴿And gives wealth despite love for it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177], and He said: ﴿And they give food despite love for it﴾ [al-Insan: 8].

The second connection: Since the discourse had proceeded in refutation of the Christians and their false belief concerning the Messiah, and the falsity of what they had gone to was made clear, and the truth and certainty concerning the matter of 'Isa and his mother was manifested, how Allah created him by His power and will, and sent him to the Children of Isra'il calling to the worship of his Lord, the Exalted - it began a refutation of the Jews, may Allah curse them, and clarification that the abrogation (naskh) which they denied the occurrence and permissibility of has indeed occurred. For Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has explicitly stated in their book, the Torah, that when Nuh, peace be upon him, came out of the ark, Allah permitted him all the beasts of the earth to eat from them. Then after this Isra'il forbade for himself the meat and milk of camels, and his sons followed him in that, and the Torah came with the prohibition of that and other things in addition to it. Allah had permitted Adam to marry his daughters to his sons, and later that was forbidden. Concubinage (tasarri) upon a wife was permissible in the law of Ibrahim, and al-Khalil Ibrahim did it with Hajar when he took her as a concubine over Sarah, and the Torah forbade the like of this to them. Likewise the union of two sisters was common, and Ya'qub, peace be upon him, did it, combining two sisters, and then that was forbidden to them in the Torah. All of this is explicitly stated in their Torah, so this is abrogation itself. Therefore, let what Allah legislated for the Messiah, peace be upon him, in permitting some of what was forbidden in the Torah be likewise; so what is the matter with them that they did not follow him, but rather denied and opposed him? Likewise what Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ with of the upright religion, the straight path, and the creed of his father Ibrahim - so what is the matter with them that they do not believe? For this reason He said: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Isra'il made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed﴾, meaning: all foods were lawful to them before the Torah was revealed except what Isra'il forbade. Then He said: ﴿Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾, for it speaks to what we have said. ﴿Then whoever fabricates lies against Allah after that - those are the wrongdoers.﴾

That is: whoever lies against Allah and claims that He legislated for them the Sabbath and perpetual adherence to the Torah, and that He did not send another prophet calling to Allah with proofs and evidences after what we have explained of the occurrence of abrogation and the manifestation of what we have mentioned - ﴿those are the wrongdoers.﴾

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Allah has spoken the truth.﴾ That is: Say, O Muhammad: He has spoken truthfully in what He informed and in what He legislated in the Qur'an. ﴿So follow the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists.﴾ That is: follow the religion of Ibrahim which Allah legislated in the Qur'an upon the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ, for it is the truth about which there is no doubt and no dispute, and it is the way than which no prophet has brought anything more complete, clearer, more manifest, or more perfect, as He the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 161], and He the Exalted said: ﴿Then We revealed to you: Follow the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [al-Nahl: 123].

Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-'Ijli, similar to it. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan gharib.

Ibn Jurayj and al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: Isra'il - that is Ya'qub, peace be upon him - was afflicted by sciatica at night, which disturbed him and kept him from sleep, and the pain would subside during the day. So he vowed to Allah that if Allah granted him recovery, he would not eat any vein (irq) nor any animal that had a vein.

Similarly said al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. Thus it was related and narrated by Ibn Jarir in his tafsir. He said: His sons followed him in forbidding that, emulating him and following his way. He said: And His saying ﴿before the Torah was revealed﴾ means: he forbade that for himself before the Torah was revealed.

I say: This context, after what preceded, has two connections.

The first: Isra'il, peace be upon him, forbade the things most beloved to him and abandoned them for the sake of Allah, and this was permissible in their law. Thus it has a connection after His saying: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾. This is the prescribed (mashru') path for us: spending in obedience to Allah from what the servant loves and desires, as He said: ﴿And gives wealth despite love for it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177], and He said: ﴿And they give food despite love for it﴾ [al-Insan: 8].

The second connection: Since the discourse had proceeded in refutation of the Christians and their false belief concerning the Messiah, and the falsity of what they had gone to was made clear, and the truth and certainty concerning the matter of 'Isa and his mother was manifested, how Allah created him by His power and will, and sent him to the Children of Isra'il calling to the worship of his Lord, the Exalted - it began a refutation of the Jews, may Allah curse them, and clarification that the abrogation (naskh) which they denied the occurrence and permissibility of has indeed occurred. For Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has explicitly stated in their book, the Torah, that when Nuh, peace be upon him, came out of the ark, Allah permitted him all the beasts of the earth to eat from them. Then after this Isra'il forbade for himself the meat and milk of camels, and his sons followed him in that, and the Torah came with the prohibition of that and other things in addition to it. Allah had permitted Adam to marry his daughters to his sons, and later that was forbidden. Concubinage (tasarri) upon a wife was permissible in the law of Ibrahim, and al-Khalil Ibrahim did it with Hajar when he took her as a concubine over Sarah, and the Torah forbade the like of this to them. Likewise the union of two sisters was common, and Ya'qub, peace be upon him, did it, combining two sisters, and then that was forbidden to them in the Torah. All of this is explicitly stated in their Torah, so this is abrogation itself. Therefore, let what Allah legislated for the Messiah, peace be upon him, in permitting some of what was forbidden in the Torah be likewise; so what is the matter with them that they did not follow him, but rather denied and opposed him? Likewise what Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ with of the upright religion, the straight path, and the creed of his father Ibrahim - so what is the matter with them that they do not believe? For this reason He said: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Isra'il made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed﴾, meaning: all foods were lawful to them before the Torah was revealed except what Isra'il forbade. Then He said: ﴿Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾, for it speaks to what we have said. ﴿Then whoever fabricates lies against Allah after that - those are the wrongdoers.﴾

That is: whoever lies against Allah and claims that He legislated for them the Sabbath and perpetual adherence to the Torah, and that He did not send another prophet calling to Allah with proofs and evidences after what we have explained of the occurrence of abrogation and the manifestation of what we have mentioned - ﴿those are the wrongdoers.﴾

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Allah has spoken the truth.﴾ That is: Say, O Muhammad: He has spoken truthfully in what He informed and in what He legislated in the Qur'an. ﴿So follow the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists.﴾ That is: follow the religion of Ibrahim which Allah legislated in the Qur'an upon the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ, for it is the truth about which there is no doubt and no dispute, and it is the way than which no prophet has brought anything more complete, clearer, more manifest, or more perfect, as He the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 161], and He the Exalted said: ﴿Then We revealed to you: Follow the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ [al-Nahl: 123].

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, who said: Ibn 'Abbas [may Allah be pleased with him] said: A group of the Jews came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and said: "Tell us about some matters which we will ask you about, which none knows except a prophet." He said: "Ask me whatever you wish, but make for me a covenant (dhimmah) of Allah and what Ya'qub (Jacob) took from his sons: if I tell you something and you recognize it, you will follow me in Islam." They said: "That is for you." He said: "Then ask me whatever you wish." They said: "Tell us about four matters: Tell us, which food did Isra'il (Israel) forbid for himself? So he took from them the covenant that if he informed them, they would surely follow him. He said: "I adjure you by Him who sent down the Torah to Musa (Moses): Do you know that Isra'il became severely ill and his sickness lasted long, so he vowed to Allah that if Allah cured him of his sickness, he would forbid the most beloved drink and the most beloved food to him? The most beloved food to him was the meat of camels, and the most beloved drink to him was their milk?" They said: "Yes, by Allah." He said: "O Allah, bear witness against them." And he said: "I adjure you by Allah, than whom there is no god but He, who sent down the Torah to Musa: Do you know that the water of the man is white and thick, and the water of the woman is yellow and thin, and whichever of them prevails, the child and the resemblance belong to it by the leave of Allah; if the water of the man prevails over the water of the woman, it is male by the leave of Allah, and if the water of the woman prevails over the water of the man, it is female by the leave of Allah?" They said: "Yes." He said: "O Allah, bear witness against them." And he said: "I adjure you by Him who sent down the Torah to Musa: Do you know that this unlettered Prophet's eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep?" They said: "O Allah, yes." He said: "O Allah, bear witness." They said: "And you now, tell us who is your guardian among the angels? For then we will either unite with you or part from you." He said: "My guardian is Jibril (Gabriel), and Allah has never sent a prophet except that he was his guardian." They said: "Then at that point we part from you; if your guardian were other than him, we would have followed you (pledged allegiance to you)." At that point Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 97] to the end of the verse.

And Ahmad also narrated it from Husayn ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Hamid, with the same chain.

Another route: Ahmad said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-'Ijli narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Jews approached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we will ask you about five things; if you inform us of them, we will know that you are a prophet and follow you." So he took from them what Isra'il had taken from his sons when he said: ﴿Allah is Guardian over what we say﴾ [Yusuf: 66]. He said: "Speak." They said: "Tell us about the sign of a prophet." He said: "His eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep." They said: "Tell us how a woman becomes female and how she becomes male." He said: "The two waters meet; when the water of the man prevails over the water of the woman, she becomes male, and when the water of the woman prevails over the water of the man, she becomes female." They said: "Tell us what Isra'il forbade for himself." He said: "He used to suffer from sciatica (irq al-nasa), and he found nothing that suited him except the milk of such-and-such," - Ahmad said: some of them said: meaning the camels - "so he forbade their meat." They said: "You have spoken the truth." They said: "Tell us what this thunder is." He said: "An angel from the angels of Allah, appointed over the clouds, in his hand (or in his hands) is a whip of fire with which he drives the clouds, guiding them wherever Allah the Mighty and Majestic commands." They said: "Then what is this sound that is heard?" He said: "Its voice." They said: "You have spoken the truth. Only one remains, and it is the one by which we will follow you if you inform us of it, for there is no prophet except that he has an angel who brings him the news. So tell us, who is your companion?" He said: "Jibril, peace be upon him." They said: "Jibril is the one who brings war, fighting and punishment; he is our enemy. If you had said Mika'il, who brings mercy, plants and rain, it would have been (different)."
