Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 3, verses 96–97 (part 1 of 3):

Allah, the Exalted, informs that the first House (bayt) established for mankind, meaning for all people, for their worship and their rites, where they circumambulate it, pray toward it, and seclude themselves at it, is ﴿the one at Bakkah﴾. This refers to the Ka'bah which was built by Ibrahim (Abraham), the Friend of Allah [peace be upon him], whom both groups, the Christians and the Jews, claim to follow in his religion and method. Yet they do not make pilgrimage to the House which he built by Allah's command, and to which he called people for Hajj (pilgrimage). Therefore He said: ﴿blessed﴾, meaning it was established as blessed, ﴿and a guidance for the worlds﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which mosque was established first on the earth?" He said: "The Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque)." I said, "Then which?" He said: "The Masjid al-Aqsa (the Farthest Mosque)." I said, "How much time was between them?" He said: "Forty years." I said, "Then which?" He said: "Then wherever the prayer overtakes you, pray there, for all of it is a mosque."

It was also related by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same chain.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Ali, regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed﴾. He said: "The houses were a qiblah (direction of prayer), but it was the first house established for the worship of Allah, the Exalted."

[He said:] And my father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, who said: A man stood up before Ali and said: "Will you not tell me about the House: is it the first house established on the earth?" He said: "No, but it is the first house in which blessing was placed, the Maqam Ibrahim (the Station of Ibrahim), and whoever enters it is safe." He mentioned the full report about how Ibrahim built the House. We have already explained this in detail in Surat al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it.

Al-Suddi claimed that it was the first house placed on the face of the earth absolutely. The correct view is the statement of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

As for the hadith which al-Bayhaqi narrated in his book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (Proofs of Prophethood) concerning the building of the Ka'bah, by way of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, traced to the Prophet (marfu'): "Allah sent Jibril (Gabriel) to Adam and Hawwa' (Eve), and commanded them to build the Ka'bah. Adam built it, then he was commanded to circumambulate it, and it was said to him: 'You are the first of mankind, and this is the first house established for mankind.'" Al-Bayhaqi said: "Ibn Lahi'ah alone narrated it in this form, traced to the Prophet." As you see, it is one of the odd narrations of Ibn Lahi'ah, and he is weak. The more likely view, and Allah knows best, is that this is a report traced to Abdullah ibn 'Amr only (mawquf), and it is from the two Zamilatan (two loaded books of the People of the Scripture) which were obtained by them on the Day of Yarmuk, from the speech of the People of the Book.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the one at Bakkah﴾. Bakkah is, according to the well-known view, one of the names of Makkah. It has been said that it was named so because it "bakka" (crushes) the necks of tyrants and oppressors, meaning they are humbled and submit there. It has also been said: because people crowd (yatabakka) therein, meaning they throng together.

Qatadah said: Allah crushed (bakka) people with it, so women pray in front of the men, and He does not do this in any other land.

The same was related from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Hammad ibn Salamah mentioned, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Makkah is from al-Fajj to al-Tan'im, and Bakkah is from the House to al-Batha'.

Shu'bah said, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim: Bakkah is the House and the Mosque. Al-Zuhri said the same.

'Ikrimah in one narration, and Maymun ibn Mihran, said: Bakkah is the House and what surrounds it, and what lies beyond that is Makkah.

Abu Salih, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Ata'iyyah al-'Awfi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Bakkah is the place of the House, and everything other than that is Makkah.

They have mentioned many names for Makkah: Makkah, Bakkah, al-Bayt al-'Atiq (the Ancient House), al-Bayt al-Haram (the Sacred House), al-Balad al-Amin (the Secure City), al-Ma'mun, Umm Ruhm, Umm al-Qura (Mother of Towns), Salah, al-'Arsh on the pattern of Badr, al-Qadis, because it purifies from sins, al-Muqaddasah (the Sanctified), al-Nasah (with a nun, and also with a ba'), al-Hatimah, al-Nassasah, al-Ra's, Kuwtha, al-Balda, al-Banniyyah, and al-Ka'bah.

* *

His saying: ﴿In it are clear signs﴾, meaning manifest proofs that it is from the building of Ibrahim, and that Allah exalted it and honored it.

Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿the Station of Ibrahim﴾, meaning: the stone on which, when the building rose, he stood to help raise the foundations and the walls, as he stood on it while his son Isma'il handed him the stones. It had been stuck to the wall of the House until 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, moved it during his caliphate to the east, so that the circumambulation could be done freely, and so that they would not disturb those praying at it after the tawaf (circumambulation). This is because Allah, the Exalted, has commanded us to pray at it when He said: ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125]. We have already presented the hadiths on this, so there is no need to repeat them here, and to Allah belongs all praise and favor.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿In it are clear signs, the Station of Ibrahim﴾, meaning: among them are the Station of Ibrahim and al-Mash'ar (the sacred site at Muzdalifah).

Mujahid said: The trace of his two feet on the Station is a clear sign. The same was related from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others.

Abu Talib said in his qasidah (ode):

"And the footprint of Ibrahim in the rock is moist,
upon his two feet, barefoot, not sandaled."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id and 'Amr al-Awdi narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿the Station of Ibrahim﴾. He said: "The whole Haram is the Station of Ibrahim." The wording of 'Amr is: "The whole rock is the Station of Ibrahim."

It was related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: "The Hajj is the Station of Ibrahim." Thus I saw it in the copy, and perhaps it is "the whole rock is the Station of Ibrahim," and Mujahid has explicitly stated this.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾, meaning: the Haram of Makkah, whoever enters it while afraid is secure from every harm. The matter was also like this in the time of Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance), as al-Hasan al-Basri and others said: a man would commit a murder, then put a woolen tuft around his neck and enter the Haram, and the son of the one he killed would meet him but would not harm him until he left.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Taymi narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾. He said: "Whoever seeks refuge in the House, the House protects him, but he is not sheltered, not fed, and not given drink; when he leaves, he is seized for his sin."

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they not see that We made a secure sanctuary while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 67]. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and gave them security against fear﴾ [Quraysh: 3–4]. Indeed, among its prohibitions is the prohibition of hunting its game and frightening it from its nests, and the prohibition of cutting its trees, plucking its fruits, and cutting its grass. The hadiths and reports on this are established from a group of the Companions, both marfu' and mawquf.

In the two Sahihs, and the wording is that of Muslim, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest, the Conquest of Makkah: "There is no hijrah (migration) now, but there is jihad and intention. And when you are called to go forth, then go forth." And he said on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "Indeed, this land (city), Allah made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by Allah's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not made lawful for anyone before me, and it was made lawful for me only for an hour of a day. So it is sacred by Allah's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorny plants are not to be cut, its game is not to be frightened, its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who announces it, and its grass is not to be cut." Al-'Abbas said: "O Messenger of Allah, except idhkhir (a fragrant grass), for it is for their smiths and for their houses." He said: "Except idhkhir."

Also in both (Sahihs), from Abu Hurayrah, something similar or close to it. And also in both, and the wording is that of Muslim, from Abu Shurayh al-'Adawi, that he said to 'Amr ibn Sa'id, while he was sending armies to Makkah: "Permit me, O Amir, to narrate to you a statement which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made on the day after the Conquest. My ears heard it, my heart retained it, and my eyes saw him when he spoke it. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'Indeed, Makkah was made sacred by Allah, and it was not made sacred by the people. So it is not lawful for a person who believes in Allah and the Last Day to shed blood in it, or to cut a tree in it. If anyone takes permission to fight in it based on the fighting of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then say to him: Indeed, Allah permitted His Messenger, but He did not permit you. He permitted me only for an hour of a day. Its sanctity has returned today as it was yesterday. So let the one present convey it to the absent.'" It was said to Abu Shurayh: "What did 'Amr say to you?" He said: "I know this better than you, O Abu Shurayh. Indeed, the Haram does not protect a disobedient person, nor a fugitive with blood, nor a fugitive with disgrace."

And from Jabir who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "It is not lawful for any of you to carry weapons in Makkah." Related by Muslim.

And from Abdullah ibn 'Adi ibn al-Hamra' al-Zuhri, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, while he was standing at al-Hazwarah in the market of Makkah: "By Allah, you (Makkah) are the best land of Allah, and the most beloved land of Allah to Allah. Had I not been driven out from you, I would not have left."

Related by Imam Ahmad, and this wording is his, and by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)." He also authenticated something similar from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas. And Ahmad narrated something similar from Abu Hurayrah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Bishr ibn Adam, son of the daughter of Azhar al-Sammān narrated to us, Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Zuraiq ibn Muslim al-A'ma, client of the Banu Makhzum, Ziyad ibn Abi 'Ayyash narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾. He said: "Safe from the Fire."

In the meaning of this statement is the hadith that al-Bayhaqi narrated: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abdan told us, Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd told us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Wasiti told us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman told us, Ibn al-Mu'ammal told us, from Ibn Muhsin, from 'Ata', from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever enters the House (the Ka'bah) enters into goodness and leaves from evil, and he leaves forgiven." Then he said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mu'ammal is alone in narrating it, and he is not strong.[[Al-Sunan al-Kubra (5/158). It is also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/201) and al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. 1161, through the route of 'Abdullah ibn al-Mu'ammal with the same chain.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾ is the verse that makes Hajj obligatory, according to the majority (al-jumhur). It was also said that the verse is His saying: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:196], but the first view is more apparent.

Numerous hadiths have come that Hajj is one of the pillars (arkan), supports, and foundations of Islam, and the Muslims have unanimously agreed upon this with a necessary consensus (ijma' darurRi). It is obligatory upon the accountable person (al-mukallaf) only once in his lifetime, by the text and by consensus.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun told us, al-Rabi' ibn Muslim al-Qurashi informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us and said: "O people, Hajj has been prescribed for you, so perform Hajj." A man said: "Every year, O Messenger of Allah?" He remained silent until the man had said it three times. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and you would not have been able to do it." Then he said: "Leave me as I have left you, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. When I command you to do something, do of it what you are able, and when I forbid you from something, leave it." Muslim also narrated it, from Zuhayr ibn Harb, from Yazid ibn Harun, with a similar wording.[[Al-Musnad (2/508) and Sahih Muslim, no. 1337.]]

Sufyan ibn Husayn, Sulayman ibn Kathir, 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd and Muhammad ibn Abi Hafsah narrated from al-Zuhri, from Abu Sinan al-Du'ali, whose name is Yazid ibn Umayyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us and said: "O people, indeed Allah has prescribed for you the Hajj." Al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it every year?" He said: "If I had said it, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory, you would not have acted upon it, and you would not have been able to act upon it. Hajj is once; whoever does more, it is voluntary (tatawwu')."

Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with the same wording. Shurayk narrated it from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, with a similar wording. It has also been narrated from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd.[[Al-Musnad (1/290), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1721, Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/111), Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2886, and al-Mustadrak (2/293).]]

[And] Imam Ahmad said: Mansur ibn Wardan told us, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from 'Ali, who said: When the verse was revealed, ﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, every year?" He remained silent. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, every year?" He said: "No, and if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:101].

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Mansur ibn Wardan, with the same chain. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib." But there is room to question this, because al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Bakhtari did not hear from 'Ali.[[Al-Musnad (1/113), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3055, Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2884, and al-Mustadrak (2/294).]]

Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Ubaydah told us, from his father, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is Hajj every year?" He said: "If I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory, you would not have carried it out, and if you had not carried it out, you would have been punished."[[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2885. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/4): "This chain is sound, and its narrators are trustworthy."]]

In the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', from Jabir, that Suraqah ibn Malik said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this our mut'ah (temporary combining of 'Umrah and Hajj) for this year of ours, or for ever?" He said: "No, rather for ever." In another narration: "Rather for ever and ever."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2505, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1216.]]

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad and the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Waqid ibn Abi Waqid al-Laythi, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his wives during his Hajj: "This one, then remain in your houses (zuhur al-husur)," meaning: remain in your homes and do not go out of the houses.[[Al-Musnad (5/218, 219) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1722.]]

As for istita'ah (ability), it has divisions: sometimes a person is able by himself, and sometimes by another, as is established in the books of rulings (fiqh).

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: 'Abd ibn Humayd told us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ibrahim ibn Yazid informed us, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far narrate from Ibn 'Umar, who said: A man stood up before the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Who is the pilgrim (al-hajj), O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who is disheveled and unkempt (al-sha'th al-tafil)." Another man stood up and said: "Which Hajj is best, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Al-'ajj wal-thajj" (the raising of the voice in talbiyah and the shedding of blood of sacrifice). Another man stood up and said: "What is the way (al-sabil), O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Provision and mount."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, nos. 813 and 2998, and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2896. In one copy: "Al-thiql" (the heavy one), which is an error; the correct reading is what we have recorded.]]

Thus Ibn Majah also narrated it through the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Yazid, who is al-Khuzi. Al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know it except from his narration, and some of the scholars have spoken against him because of his memorization." He said so here, and in the Book of Hajj he said: "This is a hasan hadith."

[And] there is no doubt that all the narrators of this chain are trustworthy except this al-Khuzi, and they have criticized him because of this hadith.

However, another has followed him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abdullah al-'Amiri told us, Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi told us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far, who said: I sat with 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, and he said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said to him: "What is the way?" He said: "Provision and mount." Likewise, Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the narration of Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, with the same chain.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Anas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Qatadah something similar.[[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/422).]]

This hadith has also been narrated through other routes, from the hadith of Anas, 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and 'A'ishah, all traced to the Prophet (marfu'), but there is criticism in their chains.[[Shaykh Nasir al-Din al-Albani gathered these routes and discussed them in his book Irwa' al-Ghalil (4/160) sufficiently, and concluded that the hadith is weak, and he benefited and excelled, may Allah reward him with good.]] This is as established in the Book of Rulings (Kitab al-Ahkam). And Allah knows best.

The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh took care to gather the routes of this hadith. Al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Qatadah, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah: ﴿for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾, and it was said: "What is the way?" He said: "Provision and mount." Then he said: "It is sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it."[[Al-Mustadrak (1/442).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub told me, Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the way?" He said: "Provision and mount."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/40), and its chain is mursal.]]

Waki' narrated it in his Tafsir, from Sufyan, from Yunus, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us, al-Thawri informed us, from Isma'il, who is Abu Isra'il al-Mala'i, from Fudayl, meaning Ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to Hajj, meaning the obligatory one, for none of you knows what may befall him."[[Al-Musnad (1/313).]]

Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, al-Hasan ibn 'Amr al-Fuqaymi told us, from Mihran ibn Abi Safwan, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to perform Hajj, let him hasten."

Abu Dawud narrated it from Musaddad, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Darir, with the same.[[Al-Musnad (1/225).]]

Ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾ that he said: "Whoever possesses three hundred dirhams has found a way to it."

From 'Ikrimah, his freed slave, that he said: "The way is health."

Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated, from Abu Janab, meaning al-Kalbi, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said concerning ﴿for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾: "Provision and camel."

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: That is, whoever denies the obligation of Hajj has disbelieved, and Allah is free of need from him.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When the verse was revealed, ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾, the Jews said: "We are Muslims." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Argue with them, and make them submit to the proof." That is, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Indeed Allah has enjoined upon the Muslims Hajj to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it." They said: "It was not prescribed for us," and they refused to perform Hajj. Allah said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾.[[Al-Tabari also narrated it in his Tafsir (7/50), through the route of 'Isa, from Sufyan, with the same chain.]]

Ibn Abi Najih also narrated similar from Mujahid.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far told us, Isma'il ibn 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud informed us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim and Shadh ibn Fayyad informed us, both saying: Hilal Abu Hashim al-Khurasani informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani informed us, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever possesses provision and a mount, and does not perform Hajj to the House of Allah, then it does not harm him whether he dies as a Jew or a Christian. That is because Allah said: ﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the hadith of Muslim ibn Ibrahim, with the same chain.

Likewise, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Zur'ah al-Razi: Hilal ibn Fayyad told us, Hilal Abu Hashim al-Khurasani told us, and he mentioned it with its chain like this. And al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qutta'i, from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Hilal ibn 'Abdullah, mawla of Rabi'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim al-Bahili, with the same, and he said: "[This is] a gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route, and there is criticism in its chain. Hilal is unknown (majhul), and al-Harith is weak in hadith."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/41), Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/421), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 812.]]

Al-Bukhari said: "Hilal (this narrator) is munkar al-hadith (weak in narration; his reports are rejected)." Ibn 'Adi said: "This hadith is not mahfuz (not preserved; it is an unreliable report)."

Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili, the hafiz (memorizer of hadith), related it from the hadith of Abu 'Amr al-Awza'i, who said: Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi al-Muhajir told me: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm told me that he heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say: "Whoever is able to perform Hajj but does not perform it, it is the same whether he dies a Jew or a Christian."

This chain is sahih (authentic) up to 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Sa'id ibn Mansur related in his Sunan, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I have certainly intended to send men to these regions to examine every person who has means (janda) but does not perform Hajj, and to impose the jizya on them; they are not Muslims. They are not Muslims."

[The author, Ibn Kathir, mentioned it in "Musnad 'Umar" and attributed it to Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Basri, and Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan, saying: "There is a break in the chain" (1/293).]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 3, verses 96–97 (part 1 of 3):

Allah, the Exalted, informs that the first House (bayt) established for mankind, meaning for all people, for their worship and their rites, where they circumambulate it, pray toward it, and seclude themselves at it, is ﴿the one at Bakkah﴾. This refers to the Ka'bah which was built by Ibrahim (Abraham), the Friend of Allah [peace be upon him], whom both groups, the Christians and the Jews, claim to follow in his religion and method. Yet they do not make pilgrimage to the House which he built by Allah's command, and to which he called people for Hajj (pilgrimage). Therefore He said: ﴿blessed﴾, meaning it was established as blessed, ﴿and a guidance for the worlds﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which mosque was established first on the earth?" He said: "The Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque)." I said, "Then which?" He said: "The Masjid al-Aqsa (the Farthest Mosque)." I said, "How much time was between them?" He said: "Forty years." I said, "Then which?" He said: "Then wherever the prayer overtakes you, pray there, for all of it is a mosque."

It was also related by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same chain.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Ali, regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed﴾. He said: "The houses were a qiblah (direction of prayer), but it was the first house established for the worship of Allah, the Exalted."

[He said:] And my father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, who said: A man stood up before Ali and said: "Will you not tell me about the House: is it the first house established on the earth?" He said: "No, but it is the first house in which blessing was placed, the Maqam Ibrahim (the Station of Ibrahim), and whoever enters it is safe." He mentioned the full report about how Ibrahim built the House. We have already explained this in detail in Surat al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it.

Al-Suddi claimed that it was the first house placed on the face of the earth absolutely. The correct view is the statement of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

As for the hadith which al-Bayhaqi narrated in his book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (Proofs of Prophethood) concerning the building of the Ka'bah, by way of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, traced to the Prophet (marfu'): "Allah sent Jibril (Gabriel) to Adam and Hawwa' (Eve), and commanded them to build the Ka'bah. Adam built it, then he was commanded to circumambulate it, and it was said to him: 'You are the first of mankind, and this is the first house established for mankind.'" Al-Bayhaqi said: "Ibn Lahi'ah alone narrated it in this form, traced to the Prophet." As you see, it is one of the odd narrations of Ibn Lahi'ah, and he is weak. The more likely view, and Allah knows best, is that this is a report traced to Abdullah ibn 'Amr only (mawquf), and it is from the two Zamilatan (two loaded books of the People of the Scripture) which were obtained by them on the Day of Yarmuk, from the speech of the People of the Book.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the one at Bakkah﴾. Bakkah is, according to the well-known view, one of the names of Makkah. It has been said that it was named so because it "bakka" (crushes) the necks of tyrants and oppressors, meaning they are humbled and submit there. It has also been said: because people crowd (yatabakka) therein, meaning they throng together.

Qatadah said: Allah crushed (bakka) people with it, so women pray in front of the men, and He does not do this in any other land.

The same was related from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Hammad ibn Salamah mentioned, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Makkah is from al-Fajj to al-Tan'im, and Bakkah is from the House to al-Batha'.

Shu'bah said, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim: Bakkah is the House and the Mosque. Al-Zuhri said the same.

'Ikrimah in one narration, and Maymun ibn Mihran, said: Bakkah is the House and what surrounds it, and what lies beyond that is Makkah.

Abu Salih, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Ata'iyyah al-'Awfi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Bakkah is the place of the House, and everything other than that is Makkah.

They have mentioned many names for Makkah: Makkah, Bakkah, al-Bayt al-'Atiq (the Ancient House), al-Bayt al-Haram (the Sacred House), al-Balad al-Amin (the Secure City), al-Ma'mun, Umm Ruhm, Umm al-Qura (Mother of Towns), Salah, al-'Arsh on the pattern of Badr, al-Qadis, because it purifies from sins, al-Muqaddasah (the Sanctified), al-Nasah (with a nun, and also with a ba'), al-Hatimah, al-Nassasah, al-Ra's, Kuwtha, al-Balda, al-Banniyyah, and al-Ka'bah.

* *

His saying: ﴿In it are clear signs﴾, meaning manifest proofs that it is from the building of Ibrahim, and that Allah exalted it and honored it.

Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿the Station of Ibrahim﴾, meaning: the stone on which, when the building rose, he stood to help raise the foundations and the walls, as he stood on it while his son Isma'il handed him the stones. It had been stuck to the wall of the House until 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, moved it during his caliphate to the east, so that the circumambulation could be done freely, and so that they would not disturb those praying at it after the tawaf (circumambulation). This is because Allah, the Exalted, has commanded us to pray at it when He said: ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125]. We have already presented the hadiths on this, so there is no need to repeat them here, and to Allah belongs all praise and favor.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿In it are clear signs, the Station of Ibrahim﴾, meaning: among them are the Station of Ibrahim and al-Mash'ar (the sacred site at Muzdalifah).

Mujahid said: The trace of his two feet on the Station is a clear sign. The same was related from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others.

Abu Talib said in his qasidah (ode):

"And the footprint of Ibrahim in the rock is moist,
upon his two feet, barefoot, not sandaled."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id and 'Amr al-Awdi narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿the Station of Ibrahim﴾. He said: "The whole Haram is the Station of Ibrahim." The wording of 'Amr is: "The whole rock is the Station of Ibrahim."

It was related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: "The Hajj is the Station of Ibrahim." Thus I saw it in the copy, and perhaps it is "the whole rock is the Station of Ibrahim," and Mujahid has explicitly stated this.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾, meaning: the Haram of Makkah, whoever enters it while afraid is secure from every harm. The matter was also like this in the time of Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance), as al-Hasan al-Basri and others said: a man would commit a murder, then put a woolen tuft around his neck and enter the Haram, and the son of the one he killed would meet him but would not harm him until he left.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Taymi narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾. He said: "Whoever seeks refuge in the House, the House protects him, but he is not sheltered, not fed, and not given drink; when he leaves, he is seized for his sin."

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they not see that We made a secure sanctuary while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 67]. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and gave them security against fear﴾ [Quraysh: 3–4]. Indeed, among its prohibitions is the prohibition of hunting its game and frightening it from its nests, and the prohibition of cutting its trees, plucking its fruits, and cutting its grass. The hadiths and reports on this are established from a group of the Companions, both marfu' and mawquf.

In the two Sahihs, and the wording is that of Muslim, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest, the Conquest of Makkah: "There is no hijrah (migration) now, but there is jihad and intention. And when you are called to go forth, then go forth." And he said on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "Indeed, this land (city), Allah made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by Allah's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not made lawful for anyone before me, and it was made lawful for me only for an hour of a day. So it is sacred by Allah's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorny plants are not to be cut, its game is not to be frightened, its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who announces it, and its grass is not to be cut." Al-'Abbas said: "O Messenger of Allah, except idhkhir (a fragrant grass), for it is for their smiths and for their houses." He said: "Except idhkhir."

Also in both (Sahihs), from Abu Hurayrah, something similar or close to it. And also in both, and the wording is that of Muslim, from Abu Shurayh al-'Adawi, that he said to 'Amr ibn Sa'id, while he was sending armies to Makkah: "Permit me, O Amir, to narrate to you a statement which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made on the day after the Conquest. My ears heard it, my heart retained it, and my eyes saw him when he spoke it. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'Indeed, Makkah was made sacred by Allah, and it was not made sacred by the people. So it is not lawful for a person who believes in Allah and the Last Day to shed blood in it, or to cut a tree in it. If anyone takes permission to fight in it based on the fighting of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then say to him: Indeed, Allah permitted His Messenger, but He did not permit you. He permitted me only for an hour of a day. Its sanctity has returned today as it was yesterday. So let the one present convey it to the absent.'" It was said to Abu Shurayh: "What did 'Amr say to you?" He said: "I know this better than you, O Abu Shurayh. Indeed, the Haram does not protect a disobedient person, nor a fugitive with blood, nor a fugitive with disgrace."

And from Jabir who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "It is not lawful for any of you to carry weapons in Makkah." Related by Muslim.

And from Abdullah ibn 'Adi ibn al-Hamra' al-Zuhri, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, while he was standing at al-Hazwarah in the market of Makkah: "By Allah, you (Makkah) are the best land of Allah, and the most beloved land of Allah to Allah. Had I not been driven out from you, I would not have left."

Related by Imam Ahmad, and this wording is his, and by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih (good and authentic)." He also authenticated something similar from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas. And Ahmad narrated something similar from Abu Hurayrah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Bishr ibn Adam, son of the daughter of Azhar al-Sammān narrated to us, Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Zuraiq ibn Muslim al-A'ma, client of the Banu Makhzum, Ziyad ibn Abi 'Ayyash narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾. He said: "Safe from the Fire."

In the meaning of this statement is the hadith that al-Bayhaqi narrated: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abdan told us, Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd told us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Wasiti told us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman told us, Ibn al-Mu'ammal told us, from Ibn Muhsin, from 'Ata', from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever enters the House (the Ka'bah) enters into goodness and leaves from evil, and he leaves forgiven." Then he said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mu'ammal is alone in narrating it, and he is not strong.[[Al-Sunan al-Kubra (5/158). It is also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/201) and al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. 1161, through the route of 'Abdullah ibn al-Mu'ammal with the same chain.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾ is the verse that makes Hajj obligatory, according to the majority (al-jumhur). It was also said that the verse is His saying: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:196], but the first view is more apparent.

Numerous hadiths have come that Hajj is one of the pillars (arkan), supports, and foundations of Islam, and the Muslims have unanimously agreed upon this with a necessary consensus (ijma' darurRi). It is obligatory upon the accountable person (al-mukallaf) only once in his lifetime, by the text and by consensus.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun told us, al-Rabi' ibn Muslim al-Qurashi informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us and said: "O people, Hajj has been prescribed for you, so perform Hajj." A man said: "Every year, O Messenger of Allah?" He remained silent until the man had said it three times. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and you would not have been able to do it." Then he said: "Leave me as I have left you, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. When I command you to do something, do of it what you are able, and when I forbid you from something, leave it." Muslim also narrated it, from Zuhayr ibn Harb, from Yazid ibn Harun, with a similar wording.[[Al-Musnad (2/508) and Sahih Muslim, no. 1337.]]

Sufyan ibn Husayn, Sulayman ibn Kathir, 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd and Muhammad ibn Abi Hafsah narrated from al-Zuhri, from Abu Sinan al-Du'ali, whose name is Yazid ibn Umayyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us and said: "O people, indeed Allah has prescribed for you the Hajj." Al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it every year?" He said: "If I had said it, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory, you would not have acted upon it, and you would not have been able to act upon it. Hajj is once; whoever does more, it is voluntary (tatawwu')."

Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with the same wording. Shurayk narrated it from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, with a similar wording. It has also been narrated from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd.[[Al-Musnad (1/290), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1721, Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/111), Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2886, and al-Mustadrak (2/293).]]

[And] Imam Ahmad said: Mansur ibn Wardan told us, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from 'Ali, who said: When the verse was revealed, ﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, every year?" He remained silent. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, every year?" He said: "No, and if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:101].

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Mansur ibn Wardan, with the same chain. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib." But there is room to question this, because al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Bakhtari did not hear from 'Ali.[[Al-Musnad (1/113), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3055, Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2884, and al-Mustadrak (2/294).]]

Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Ubaydah told us, from his father, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is Hajj every year?" He said: "If I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory, you would not have carried it out, and if you had not carried it out, you would have been punished."[[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2885. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/4): "This chain is sound, and its narrators are trustworthy."]]

In the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', from Jabir, that Suraqah ibn Malik said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this our mut'ah (temporary combining of 'Umrah and Hajj) for this year of ours, or for ever?" He said: "No, rather for ever." In another narration: "Rather for ever and ever."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2505, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1216.]]

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad and the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Waqid ibn Abi Waqid al-Laythi, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his wives during his Hajj: "This one, then remain in your houses (zuhur al-husur)," meaning: remain in your homes and do not go out of the houses.[[Al-Musnad (5/218, 219) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1722.]]

As for istita'ah (ability), it has divisions: sometimes a person is able by himself, and sometimes by another, as is established in the books of rulings (fiqh).

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: 'Abd ibn Humayd told us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ibrahim ibn Yazid informed us, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far narrate from Ibn 'Umar, who said: A man stood up before the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Who is the pilgrim (al-hajj), O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who is disheveled and unkempt (al-sha'th al-tafil)." Another man stood up and said: "Which Hajj is best, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Al-'ajj wal-thajj" (the raising of the voice in talbiyah and the shedding of blood of sacrifice). Another man stood up and said: "What is the way (al-sabil), O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Provision and mount."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, nos. 813 and 2998, and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2896. In one copy: "Al-thiql" (the heavy one), which is an error; the correct reading is what we have recorded.]]

Thus Ibn Majah also narrated it through the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Yazid, who is al-Khuzi. Al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know it except from his narration, and some of the scholars have spoken against him because of his memorization." He said so here, and in the Book of Hajj he said: "This is a hasan hadith."

[And] there is no doubt that all the narrators of this chain are trustworthy except this al-Khuzi, and they have criticized him because of this hadith.

However, another has followed him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abdullah al-'Amiri told us, Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi told us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far, who said: I sat with 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, and he said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said to him: "What is the way?" He said: "Provision and mount." Likewise, Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the narration of Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, with the same chain.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Anas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Qatadah something similar.[[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/422).]]

This hadith has also been narrated through other routes, from the hadith of Anas, 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and 'A'ishah, all traced to the Prophet (marfu'), but there is criticism in their chains.[[Shaykh Nasir al-Din al-Albani gathered these routes and discussed them in his book Irwa' al-Ghalil (4/160) sufficiently, and concluded that the hadith is weak, and he benefited and excelled, may Allah reward him with good.]] This is as established in the Book of Rulings (Kitab al-Ahkam). And Allah knows best.

The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh took care to gather the routes of this hadith. Al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Qatadah, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah: ﴿for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾, and it was said: "What is the way?" He said: "Provision and mount." Then he said: "It is sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it."[[Al-Mustadrak (1/442).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub told me, Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the way?" He said: "Provision and mount."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/40), and its chain is mursal.]]

Waki' narrated it in his Tafsir, from Sufyan, from Yunus, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us, al-Thawri informed us, from Isma'il, who is Abu Isra'il al-Mala'i, from Fudayl, meaning Ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to Hajj, meaning the obligatory one, for none of you knows what may befall him."[[Al-Musnad (1/313).]]

Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, al-Hasan ibn 'Amr al-Fuqaymi told us, from Mihran ibn Abi Safwan, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to perform Hajj, let him hasten."

Abu Dawud narrated it from Musaddad, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Darir, with the same.[[Al-Musnad (1/225).]]

Ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾ that he said: "Whoever possesses three hundred dirhams has found a way to it."

From 'Ikrimah, his freed slave, that he said: "The way is health."

Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated, from Abu Janab, meaning al-Kalbi, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said concerning ﴿for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾: "Provision and camel."

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: That is, whoever denies the obligation of Hajj has disbelieved, and Allah is free of need from him.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When the verse was revealed, ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾, the Jews said: "We are Muslims." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Argue with them, and make them submit to the proof." That is, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Indeed Allah has enjoined upon the Muslims Hajj to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it." They said: "It was not prescribed for us," and they refused to perform Hajj. Allah said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾.[[Al-Tabari also narrated it in his Tafsir (7/50), through the route of 'Isa, from Sufyan, with the same chain.]]

Ibn Abi Najih also narrated similar from Mujahid.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far told us, Isma'il ibn 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud informed us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim and Shadh ibn Fayyad informed us, both saying: Hilal Abu Hashim al-Khurasani informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani informed us, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever possesses provision and a mount, and does not perform Hajj to the House of Allah, then it does not harm him whether he dies as a Jew or a Christian. That is because Allah said: ﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by the people, for whoever is able to find a way to it. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the hadith of Muslim ibn Ibrahim, with the same chain.

Likewise, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Zur'ah al-Razi: Hilal ibn Fayyad told us, Hilal Abu Hashim al-Khurasani told us, and he mentioned it with its chain like this. And al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qutta'i, from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from Hilal ibn 'Abdullah, mawla of Rabi'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim al-Bahili, with the same, and he said: "[This is] a gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route, and there is criticism in its chain. Hilal is unknown (majhul), and al-Harith is weak in hadith."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/41), Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/421), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 812.]]

Al-Bukhari said: "Hilal (this narrator) is munkar al-hadith (weak in narration; his reports are rejected)." Ibn 'Adi said: "This hadith is not mahfuz (not preserved; it is an unreliable report)."

Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili, the hafiz (memorizer of hadith), related it from the hadith of Abu 'Amr al-Awza'i, who said: Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi al-Muhajir told me: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm told me that he heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say: "Whoever is able to perform Hajj but does not perform it, it is the same whether he dies a Jew or a Christian."

This chain is sahih (authentic) up to 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Sa'id ibn Mansur related in his Sunan, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I have certainly intended to send men to these regions to examine every person who has means (janda) but does not perform Hajj, and to impose the jizya on them; they are not Muslims. They are not Muslims."

[The author, Ibn Kathir, mentioned it in "Musnad 'Umar" and attributed it to Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Basri, and Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan, saying: "There is a break in the chain" (1/293).]

This is a rebuke from Allah, exalted is He, to the disbelievers among the People of the Book, for their obstinacy against the truth, their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their turning away from His path those among the believers who wish to follow it, with all their effort and capacity [[In manuscripts ج and أ: "obedience" (طاعتهم).]], while they know that what the Messenger brought is the truth from Allah, through the knowledge they possess from the earlier prophets and the noble messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all, and what they gave good news of and made known, concerning the mention of the unlettered (al-ummi) Prophet (ﷺ) [[Addition from manuscript أ.]], the Hashimite, Arab, Meccan, master of the descendants of Adam, seal of the prophets, and messenger of the Lord of the earth and the heavens. Allah, exalted is He, has threatened them for that, by informing that He is a witness over their conduct, by their opposing what is in their hands from the prophets, and their fighting against the Messenger who was given good news of, with denial, obstinate rejection and stubbornness. And Allah, exalted is He, informed that He is not unaware of what they do; that is, He will recompense them for that on a day when neither wealth nor children will benefit them.

This is a rebuke from Allah, exalted is He, to the disbelievers among the People of the Book, for their obstinacy against the truth, their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their turning away from His path those among the believers who wish to follow it, with all their effort and capacity [[In manuscripts ج and أ: "obedience" (طاعتهم).]], while they know that what the Messenger brought is the truth from Allah, through the knowledge they possess from the earlier prophets and the noble messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all, and what they gave good news of and made known, concerning the mention of the unlettered (al-ummi) Prophet (ﷺ) [[Addition from manuscript أ.]], the Hashimite, Arab, Meccan, master of the descendants of Adam, seal of the prophets, and messenger of the Lord of the earth and the heavens. Allah, exalted is He, has threatened them for that, by informing that He is a witness over their conduct, by their opposing what is in their hands from the prophets, and their fighting against the Messenger who was given good news of, with denial, obstinate rejection and stubbornness. And Allah, exalted is He, informed that He is not unaware of what they do; that is, He will recompense them for that on a day when neither wealth nor children will benefit them.

Almighty Allah warns His believing servants against obeying a group of those who were given the Scripture, who envy the believers for what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty, and for the favour He has granted them in sending His Messenger. As He said: ﴿Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 109]. Likewise, here He said: ﴿If you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelievers﴾. Then He said: ﴿And how could you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you and among you is His Messenger?﴾ That is, disbelief is far from you, and you are too exalted for it. For the verses of Allah descend upon His Messenger night and day, and he recites them to you and conveys them to you. This is like His saying: ﴿And why do you not believe in Allah, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are believers?﴾ [Al-Hadid: 8] and the verse after it.

And as has come in the hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said one day to his companions: "Which of the believers is most amazing to you in faith?" They said: "The angels." He said: "And how would they not believe, when they are in the presence of their Lord?!" They mentioned the prophets, and he said: "And how would they not believe, when revelation descends upon them?" They said: "Then us." He said: "And how would you not believe, when I am among you?!" They said: "Then which of the people is most amazing in faith?" He said: "A people who will come after you, who will find pages (ṣuḥuf) and will believe in what is in them." (Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/22, 23) from the hadith of Abu Jum'ah al-Ansari.) I have mentioned the chain of this hadith and the discussion of it at the beginning of my commentary on al-Bukhari, and all praise is due to Allah.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever holds fast to Allah has indeed been guided to a straight path﴾. That is: despite this, holding fast to Allah and relying upon Him is the foundation of guidance, the provision for keeping away from error, the means to rectitude, the path of soundness, and the attainment of the goal.

(Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/22, 23) from the hadith of Abu Jum'ah al-Ansari.) Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever holds fast to Allah has indeed been guided to a straight path﴾. That is: despite this, holding fast to Allah and relying upon Him is the foundation of guidance, the provision for keeping away from error, the means to rectitude, the path of soundness, and the attainment of the goal.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan and Shuʿbah, from Zubayd al-Yami, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah, that is Ibn Masʿud, regarding ﴿Be mindful of God with the mindfulness due to Him﴾, he said: "That He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not ungratefully denied." [Note: In another manuscript: "that He is thanked and not ungratefully denied, and remembered and not forgotten."]

This is a sound chain (isnad ṣaḥīḥ) that stops at Ibn Masʿud (mawqūf). ʿAmr ibn Maymun also narrated it from Ibn Masʿud in agreement with Murrah.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Ibn Wahb, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Zubayd, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿Be mindful of God with the mindfulness due to Him﴾ means that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, thanked and not ungratefully denied, and remembered and not forgotten."

Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Misʿar, from Zubayd, from Murrah, from Ibn Masʿud, as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet) report, and then he said: "It is ṣaḥīḥ according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." So he said. However, the more apparent view is that it is mawqūf (stopping at Ibn Masʿud). And God knows best.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Similar has been related from Murrah al-Hamdani, al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym, ʿAmr ibn Maymun, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Tawus, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Sinan, and al-Suddi, similar to this.

[It is also related from Anas that he said: "A servant does not truly fear God with the fear due to Him until his tongue is restrained."]

Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu al-ʿAliyah, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Suddi, and others held that this verse was abrogated (mansukh, meaning superseded by a later ruling, naskh) by the words of God Most High: ﴿So be mindful of God as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16].

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿Be mindful of God with the mindfulness due to Him﴾ that he said: "It was not abrogated. Rather, ﴿with the mindfulness due to Him﴾ means that they strive in His way with the striving due to Him, that they are not deterred by the blame of any blamer regarding God, and that they uphold justice even against themselves, their fathers, and their sons."

* *

As for His words ﴿And do not die except while you are Muslims﴾, meaning: maintain Islam in your health and safety so that you die upon it. For the Generous One has, by His generosity, established the custom that whoever lives upon something dies upon it, and whoever dies upon something is resurrected upon it. We seek refuge with God from the opposite of that.

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, who said: I heard Sulayman, from Mujahid, that people used to circumambulate the House (the Kaʿbah), while Ibn ʿAbbas was sitting with them holding a staff. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿O you who believe, be mindful of God with the mindfulness due to Him, and do not die except as Muslims﴾. And if a drop of al-Zaqqum were dripped, it would make the lives of the people of the earth bitter. So how about one who has no food except al-Zaqqum?"

Likewise, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasaʿi, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, related it through various routes from Shuʿbah, with the same wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." Al-Hakim said: "According to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it."

Imam Ahmad said: Waki narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Rabb al-Kaʿbah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever loves to be drawn away from the Fire and to enter Paradise, let his death come to him while he believes in God and the Last Day, and treats people as he loves to be treated."

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (may God's blessings and peace be upon him) say three days before his death: "None of you should die except while thinking well of God, the Mighty and Majestic."

Muslim related it through the route of al-Aʿmash, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, Abu Yunus narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "God said: I am according to My servant's thought of Me. If he thinks well of Me, it is for him; and if he thinks ill, it is for him."

The origin of this hadith is established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) through another route, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God [the Mighty and Majestic] says: I am according to My servant's thought of Me."

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Qurashi narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Thabit, and I think (from Anas): A man from the Ansar was ill, and the Prophet (ﷺ) came to visit him. He met him in the marketplace, greeted him, and said: "How are you, so-and-so?" He said: "Well, O Messenger of God. I hope in God, and I fear my sins." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Hope and fear do not come together in the heart of a servant at this time except that God gives him what he hopes for and secures him from what he fears."

Then he said: We do not know anyone who narrated it from Thabit except Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman. Likewise, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasaʿi, and Ibn Majah related it through his route. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (a single-route report)." Some have related it from Thabit as a mursal (a report missing its companion link).

[Note: Ibn Abi al-Dunya related it in "Husn al-Zann billah" (no. 31), and al-Mundhiri graded it hasan in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (4/268). As for the mursal form: Ibn Abi al-Dunya related it in "al-Marda wa al-Kaffarat" (no. 108), and from his route al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman, through Hammad from Thabit from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr as a mursal.]

As for the hadith that Imam Ahmad related: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that I would not fall (in battle) except while standing." al-Nasaʿi related it in his Sunan from Ismaʿil ibn Masʿud, from Khalid ibn al-Harith, from Shuʿbah, with the same wording, and he titled it: "Chapter: How one falls down for prostration." Then he related it similarly. It has been said that its meaning is: "On (the condition) that I not die except as a Muslim." It has also been said that its meaning is: "That I not be killed except while advancing, not turning back." This also returns to the first meaning.

* *

As for His words ﴿And hold firmly to the rope of God, all together, and do not be divided﴾: it has been said that ﴿the rope of God﴾ means the covenant of God, as He said in the verse after it: ﴿They are struck with humiliation wherever they are found, except by a rope from God and a rope from the people﴾ [Al ʿImran 3:112], meaning by a covenant and a guarantee. It has also been said that ﴿a rope from God﴾ means the Qur'an, as in the hadith of al-Harith al-Aʿwar, from ʿAli, traced to the Prophet, concerning the description of the Qur'an: "It is the firm rope of God and His straight path."

A specific hadith with this meaning has also been transmitted. Al-Imam al-Hafiz Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari said: Saʿid ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman al-ʿArzami, from ʿAtiyyah, from Abu Saʿid, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The Book of God is the rope of God extended from the heaven to the earth."

[Note: Tafsir al-Tabari (7/72). Its chain includes ʿAtiyyah al-ʿAwfi, who is weak.]

Ibn Mardawayh related through the route of Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, from Abu al-Ahwas, from ʿAbd Allah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "This Qur'an is the firm rope of God, it is the clear light, it is the beneficial cure, a protection for whoever holds to it, and a salvation for whoever follows it."

[Note: Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (1/555), Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (10/482), Ibn Hibban in al-Majruhin (1/99), and Ibn al-Jawzi in al-ʿIlal al-Mutanahiyah (1/101), and he said: "This hadith is not sound from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and it resembles being a statement of Ibn Masʿud."]

Similar has been related from the hadiths of Hudhayfah and Zayd ibn Arqam.

[Waki said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abu Wail, who said: ʿAbd Allah said: "This path is attended; the devils attend it. O servant of God, come along this way, and not to the (other) path. So hold firmly to the rope of God, for the rope of God is the Qur'an."]

* *

As for His words ﴿And do not be divided﴾: He commanded them to unity and forbade them from division. Numerous hadiths have been related forbidding division and commanding togetherness and harmony, as in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (may God's blessings and peace be upon him) said: "God is pleased with three things for you and is displeased with three things for you. He is pleased that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him; that you hold firmly to the rope of God all together and do not divide; and that you give sincere counsel to whom God has placed in charge of your affairs. And He is displeased with three things for you: gossip (qil wa qal), excessive questioning, and the squandering of wealth."

[Note: Sahih Muslim (1715).]

They were also promised protection from error when they agree (ʿismah), as numerous hadiths also related. And it was feared that they would split and differ. This did occur in this community, and they split into seventy-three sects, of which one sect is saved, destined for Paradise and safe from the punishment of the Fire. They are those who are upon what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions were upon.

* *

As for His words ﴿And remember the favor of God upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, so you became by His favor brothers, and you were on the brink of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it﴾, to the end of the verse. This context concerns the Aws and the Khazraj, for there had been many wars among them in the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period), intense enmity, grudges, rancor, and blood feuds, which led to long fighting and battles between them. When God brought Islam, those among them who entered it became brothers, loving one another for the majesty of God, connected for the sake of God, and cooperating in righteousness and piety. God Most High said: ﴿He it is who strengthened you with His help and with the believers, and brought their hearts together. Had you spent all that is on earth, you could not have brought their hearts together, but God brought them together. Indeed, He is Almighty, Wise﴾ [al-Anfal 8:62]. They had been on the brink of a pit of the Fire because of their disbelief, and God rescued them from it by guiding them to faith.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) also reminded them of this favor on the day he distributed the spoils of Hunayn. Some of them complained when he preferred others in the distribution, so he addressed them and said: "O assembly of the Ansar, did I not find you misguided and God guided you through me? And were you not divided and God united you through me? And were you not poor and God enriched you through me?" Whenever he said something, they replied: "God and His Messenger are most gracious."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and others have mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning the Aws and the Khazraj. The reason was that a man from the Jews passed by a gathering of the Aws and the Khazraj, and he was displeased by the unity and harmony they were enjoying. So he sent a man with him and instructed him to sit among them and remind them of what had happened between them in the wars, such as the Day of Bu'ath and those other battles. He did so, and he continued this practice until the hearts of the people were inflamed, some became angry with others, they grew agitated, called out with their battle-cries, took up their weapons, and arranged to meet at al-Harrah. When this reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he came to them and began to calm them, saying: "Will you call to the ways of the Jahiliyyah while I am among you?" Then he recited to them this verse, and they regretted what they had done, reconciled, embraced one another, and laid down their weapons. May Allah be pleased with them.

Ikrimah mentioned that it was revealed concerning them when they became agitated over the matter of the slander (al-ifk). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan and Shuʿbah, from Zubayd al-Yami, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah, that is Ibn Masʿud, regarding ﴿Be mindful of God with the mindfulness due to Him﴾, he said: "That He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not ungratefully denied." [Note: In another manuscript: "that He is thanked and not ungratefully denied, and remembered and not forgotten."]

This is a sound chain (isnad ṣaḥīḥ) that stops at Ibn Masʿud (mawqūf). ʿAmr ibn Maymun also narrated it from Ibn Masʿud in agreement with Murrah.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Ibn Wahb, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Zubayd, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿Be mindful of God with the mindfulness due to Him﴾ means that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, thanked and not ungratefully denied, and remembered and not forgotten."

Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Misʿar, from Zubayd, from Murrah, from Ibn Masʿud, as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet) report, and then he said: "It is ṣaḥīḥ according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." So he said. However, the more apparent view is that it is mawqūf (stopping at Ibn Masʿud). And God knows best.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Similar has been related from Murrah al-Hamdani, al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym, ʿAmr ibn Maymun, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Tawus, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Sinan, and al-Suddi, similar to this.

[It is also related from Anas that he said: "A servant does not truly fear God with the fear due to Him until his tongue is restrained."]

Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu al-ʿAliyah, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Suddi, and others held that this verse was abrogated (mansukh, meaning superseded by a later ruling, naskh) by the words of God Most High: ﴿So be mindful of God as much as you are able﴾ [al-Taghabun 64:16].

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words ﴿Be mindful of God with the mindfulness due to Him﴾ that he said: "It was not abrogated. Rather, ﴿with the mindfulness due to Him﴾ means that they strive in His way with the striving due to Him, that they are not deterred by the blame of any blamer regarding God, and that they uphold justice even against themselves, their fathers, and their sons."

* *

As for His words ﴿And do not die except while you are Muslims﴾, meaning: maintain Islam in your health and safety so that you die upon it. For the Generous One has, by His generosity, established the custom that whoever lives upon something dies upon it, and whoever dies upon something is resurrected upon it. We seek refuge with God from the opposite of that.

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, who said: I heard Sulayman, from Mujahid, that people used to circumambulate the House (the Kaʿbah), while Ibn ʿAbbas was sitting with them holding a staff. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "﴿O you who believe, be mindful of God with the mindfulness due to Him, and do not die except as Muslims﴾. And if a drop of al-Zaqqum were dripped, it would make the lives of the people of the earth bitter. So how about one who has no food except al-Zaqqum?"

Likewise, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasaʿi, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, related it through various routes from Shuʿbah, with the same wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." Al-Hakim said: "According to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it."

Imam Ahmad said: Waki narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Rabb al-Kaʿbah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever loves to be drawn away from the Fire and to enter Paradise, let his death come to him while he believes in God and the Last Day, and treats people as he loves to be treated."

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (may God's blessings and peace be upon him) say three days before his death: "None of you should die except while thinking well of God, the Mighty and Majestic."

Muslim related it through the route of al-Aʿmash, with the same wording.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And let there be among you a community who invite to good, enjoin what is right, and forbid what is wrong﴾. That is, let there be a group standing ready to carry out the command of Allah, calling to goodness, enjoining the right and forbidding the wrong. ﴿And those are the successful﴾. Ad-Dahhak said: they are the elite of the Companions and the elite of the transmitters, meaning the fighters (al-mujahidun, those who strive in the way of Allah) and the scholars (al-'ulama', the learned).

Abu Ja'far al-Baqir said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And let there be among you a community who invite to good﴾, then said: "The good is following the Qur'an and my Sunnah." Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh.

The purpose of this verse is that a group from the Ummah should be dedicated to this matter, although it is an obligation upon every individual of the Ummah according to his capacity, as is established in Sahih Muslim from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is unable, then with his tongue; and if he is unable, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith." And in another narration: "And there is not beyond that in faith even the weight of a mustard seed."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (49), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The Hafiz Ibn Kathir made a serious error here: the hadith 'Whoever among you sees an evil' is the hadith of Abu Musa."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman al-Hashimi narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, Amr ibn Abi Amr informed me, from Abdullah ibn Abdul-Rahman al-Ashhali, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, you will surely enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or else Allah will soon send upon you a punishment from Himself, then you will supplicate Him and He will not respond to you."

It was also narrated by at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Amr ibn Abi Amr, with it. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.[[Musnad (5/388) and Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (2169).]] The hadiths on this subject are numerous, along with the noble verses, as their explanation will come in their places.

Then Allah said: ﴿And do not be like those who divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them. And those will have a great punishment﴾. He forbids this Ummah from being like the previous nations in their division and differing, and in their abandonment of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong while the proof was established against them.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, Azhar ibn Abdullah al-Hawzani told me, from Abu Amir Abdullah ibn Luhay, who said: We performed Hajj with Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and when we arrived in Makkah he stood after praying Dhuhr and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The People of the Two Books split in their religion into seventy-two sects, and this Ummah will split into seventy-three sects — meaning the desires — all of them in the Fire except one, and it is the Jama'ah (community). Indeed, there will come out among my Ummah people into whom those desires will seep, just as rabies seeps into its owner; not a vein or joint remains without it entering it. By Allah — O assembly of Arabs — if you do not establish what your Prophet (ﷺ) brought, then others among the people are more deserving of not establishing it."

Abu Dawud narrated it likewise, from Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Muhammad ibn Yahya, both from Abu al-Mughirah — whose name is Abdul-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj al-Shami — with it. This hadith has been narrated through several chains.[[Musnad (4/102) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4597).]]

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection, when the faces of the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah will turn white, and the faces of the People of innovation and division will turn black. This was said by Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

﴿As for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve after your belief?"﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They are the hypocrites. ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.﴾ However, this description encompasses every disbeliever.

﴿As for those whose faces turn white, they will be in the mercy of Allah, wherein they will abide forever﴾ — that is, Paradise, remaining in it forever, never desiring to leave it.

Abu Isa at-Tirmidhi said, when explaining this verse: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Rabi' — and he is Ibn Subayh — and Hammad ibn Salamah, from Abu Ghalib, who said: Abu Umamah saw heads set up on the steps of Damascus, and Abu Umamah said: "The dogs of the Fire, the worst of the slain beneath the canopy of the sky, the best of the slain are those whom they killed." Then he recited: ﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black﴾ to the end of the verse. I said to Abu Umamah: "Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Had I not heard it except once, or twice, or thrice, or four times — until he counted seven — I would not have narrated it to you."

Then he said: This is a hasan hadith.
