Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The Hafiz Ibn Kathir made a serious error here: the hadith 'Whoever among you sees an evil' is the hadith of Abu Musa."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman al-Hashimi narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, Amr ibn Abi Amr informed me, from Abdullah ibn Abdul-Rahman al-Ashhali, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, you will surely enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or else Allah will soon send upon you a punishment from Himself, then you will supplicate Him and He will not respond to you."

It was also narrated by at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Amr ibn Abi Amr, with it. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.[[Musnad (5/388) and Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (2169).]] The hadiths on this subject are numerous, along with the noble verses, as their explanation will come in their places.

Then Allah said: ﴿And do not be like those who divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them. And those will have a great punishment﴾. He forbids this Ummah from being like the previous nations in their division and differing, and in their abandonment of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong while the proof was established against them.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Safwan narrated to us, Azhar ibn Abdullah al-Hawzani told me, from Abu Amir Abdullah ibn Luhay, who said: We performed Hajj with Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and when we arrived in Makkah he stood after praying Dhuhr and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The People of the Two Books split in their religion into seventy-two sects, and this Ummah will split into seventy-three sects — meaning the desires — all of them in the Fire except one, and it is the Jama'ah (community). Indeed, there will come out among my Ummah people into whom those desires will seep, just as rabies seeps into its owner; not a vein or joint remains without it entering it. By Allah — O assembly of Arabs — if you do not establish what your Prophet (ﷺ) brought, then others among the people are more deserving of not establishing it."

Abu Dawud narrated it likewise, from Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Muhammad ibn Yahya, both from Abu al-Mughirah — whose name is Abdul-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj al-Shami — with it. This hadith has been narrated through several chains.[[Musnad (4/102) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4597).]]

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection, when the faces of the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah will turn white, and the faces of the People of innovation and division will turn black. This was said by Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

﴿As for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve after your belief?"﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They are the hypocrites. ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.﴾ However, this description encompasses every disbeliever.

﴿As for those whose faces turn white, they will be in the mercy of Allah, wherein they will abide forever﴾ — that is, Paradise, remaining in it forever, never desiring to leave it.

Abu Isa at-Tirmidhi said, when explaining this verse: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Rabi' — and he is Ibn Subayh — and Hammad ibn Salamah, from Abu Ghalib, who said: Abu Umamah saw heads set up on the steps of Damascus, and Abu Umamah said: "The dogs of the Fire, the worst of the slain beneath the canopy of the sky, the best of the slain are those whom they killed." Then he recited: ﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black﴾ to the end of the verse. I said to Abu Umamah: "Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Had I not heard it except once, or twice, or thrice, or four times — until he counted seven — I would not have narrated it to you."

Then he said: This is a hasan hadith. It was narrated by Ibn Majah from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah from Abu Ghalib, and Ahmad recorded it in his Musnad, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ghalib, with similar wording.[[Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. (3000) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (176).]] Ibn Mardawayh narrated, when explaining this verse, from Abu Dharr, a lengthy hadith that is strange and extremely wondrous.

Then He said: ﴿These are the verses of Allah⁠ — that is, these are the verses of Allah, His proofs and His clear signs — ﴿We recite them to you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿in truth﴾, that is, We reveal what the matter is in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿And Allah does not intend any injustice to the worlds﴾ — that is, He is not unjust to them; rather He is the Just Judge who does not oppress. He is capable of everything and knows everything, so He has no need to wrong any of His creatures. Therefore He said: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning all of it is His dominion and His servants. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾, meaning He is the one who disposes of affairs in this world and the Hereafter, the Judge in this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 110–112 (part 1 of 4):

He, exalted is He, informs about this Muhammadan nation that they are the best of nations, so He said: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Maysara, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah regarding ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, that he said: "The best of people for people. You bring them in chains around their necks until they enter Islam." [[In ج, ر, أ, و: "يأتون" (ya'tun).]] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4557).]]

Likewise said Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, meaning: the best of people for people.

The meaning is that they are the best of nations and the most beneficial of people to people. For this reason He said: ﴿You enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah﴾. [[In ر: "يؤمنون" (yu'minun).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umayrah, from the wife of [Dhurrah] [[Addition from ج, ر, أ, and al-Musnad.]] the daughter of Abu Lahab, [from Durrah bint Abi Lahab] [[Addition from ج, ر, أ, and al-Musnad.]], who said: A man stood before the Prophet ﷺ while he was on the pulpit, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is the best of people?" He said: "The best of people are those who recite best, who are most God-fearing, who most enjoin what is right, who most forbid what is wrong, and who most maintain ties of kinship." [[al-Musnad (6/432).]]

Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, al-Nasa'i in his Sunan, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the narration of Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, that he said: "They are those who emigrated with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Makkah to Madinah." [[al-Musnad (1/319); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11072); al-Mustadrak (2/294). Al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound according to the condition of Muslim," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

The correct view is that this verse is general for the whole nation, each generation according to its share, and the best of its generations are those among whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, then those who follow them, then those who follow them, as He said in another verse: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾, meaning: the best, ﴿so that you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [[Addition from ج, ر, أ, و.]], and the verse continues.

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, the Sunan of Ibn Majah, and the Mustadrak of al-Hakim, from the narration of Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You complete seventy nations; you are the best of them, and you are the most honoured by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [[al-Musnad (4/447); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (3001); Sunan Ibn Majah (4287); al-Mustadrak (4/84).]]

This is a well-known hadith, and al-Tirmidhi graded it as hasan. It is also narrated from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Abu Sa'id [al-Khudri] [[Addition from ج.]], similar to it.

This nation has taken the lead in good deeds only through its Prophet Muhammad ﷺ [[In و: "may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]], for he is the noblest of Allah's creation, the most honoured of the Messengers before Allah. Allah sent him with a complete, great law that He had not given to any prophet before him or to any messenger among the Messengers. So the deed [according to] [[Addition from ج, ر.]] his method and path, a little of it stands in a place where the great deeds of others cannot stand in its place, as Imam Ahmad said:

'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah (i.e., Ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil), from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, who is Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, that he heard 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given what no one among the prophets has been given." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is it?" He said: "I was helped with terror, I was given the keys of the earth, I was named Ahmad, the earth was made pure and a place of prostration for me, and my nation was made the best of nations." Ahmad alone narrated it through this route, and its chain is hasan. [[al-Musnad (1/98). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/260): "In it is 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, who has poor memory." Al-Tirmidhi said: "Truthful, though some scholars spoke about him because of his memory. I heard Muhammad al-Bukhari say: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq, and al-Humaydi would use the hadith of Ibn 'Aqil as evidence." I say: The hadith is hasan.]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-'Ala' al-Hasan ibn Sawwar narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah, from Ibn Abi Hulays, from Yazid ibn Maysarah, who said: I heard Umm al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with her, say: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: I heard Abu al-Qasim ﷺ, and I never heard him call him by his kunyah before or after that, say: "Allah, the Exalted, says: 'O 'Isa, I am sending after you a nation: if what they love befalls them, they praise and thank [Allah]; and if what they dislike befalls them, they seek reward and are patient, though they have neither forbearance nor knowledge.'" He said: "O Lord, how can this be for them, when they have neither forbearance nor knowledge?" He said: "I will give them of My forbearance and My knowledge." [[al-Musnad (6/450).]]

Hadiths have come whose mention is appropriate here:

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, Bukayr [[In ج: "Bakr."]] ibn al-Akhnas narrated to us, from a man, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning, their faces like the full moon, their hearts upon the heart of one man. So I asked my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, for more, and He added for each one of them seventy thousand more." Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I thought that this would reach the people of the villages and what is near the edges of the deserts. [[al-Musnad (1/6). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/410): "In it is al-Mas'udi, who became confused, and the narrator from him is unnamed; the rest of Ahmad's narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated to us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Mihran, from Musa ibn 'Ubayd, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "My Lord has given me seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning." 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, why did you not ask Him for more?" He said: "I asked Him, and He gave me, with every man, seventy thousand." 'Umar said: "Why did you not ask Him for more?" He said: "I have asked Him, and He has given me like this." 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr [[In ج, ر, أ: "'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr."]] spread his hands apart, and 'Abd Allah said: He spread his two arms, and 'Abd Allah scooped with his hands. Hisham said: "And this is from Allah; its number is not known." [[al-Musnad (1/197). In its chain are al-Qasim ibn Mihran and Musa ibn 'Ubayd, who are both unknown; the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'ah, who said: Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd said: Thawban fell ill in Hims, and over it was 'Abd Allah ibn Qurt al-Azdi, and he did not visit him. A man from the Kala'iyyin entered upon Thawban to visit him, and Thawban said to him: [Do you write?] He said: Yes. He said: Write. So he wrote for the commander 'Abd Allah ibn Qurt: "From Thawban, [freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ] [[Addition from ج, ر, and al-Musnad.]], to proceed: If Musa and 'Isa, peace be upon them both, had a servant in your presence, you would have visited him." Then he folded the letter and said to him: Will you deliver it to him? He said: Yes. So the man set off with his letter and handed it to Ibn Qurt. When he saw it, he stood up in alarm. The people said: What is his matter? Has something new happened? So he came to Thawban until he entered upon him and visited him, and sat with him for a while, then stood up. Thawban took hold of his cloak and said: Sit until I tell you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I heard him say: "Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise, without reckoning or punishment upon them, with every thousand seventy thousand."

Ahmad alone narrated it through this route, and all of its narrators are trustworthy Syrians from Hims, so it is a sahih hadith. And to Allah belongs all praise.

Another route: al-Tabarani said: 'Amr ibn Ishaq ibn Zabriq al-Himsi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il [i.e., Ibn 'Ayyash] narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'ah, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu Asma' al-Rahabi, from Thawban, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "My Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, has promised me seventy thousand of my nation who will not be reckoned, with every thousand seventy thousand." This is perhaps the preserved version, with the addition of Abu Asma' al-Rahabi between Shurayh and Thawban. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/92). He also narrated it in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (1682).]] And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: We talked a great deal in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night, then in the morning we went to him, and he said: "The prophets were shown to me last night with their nations. A prophet would pass with three, and a prophet with a band, and a prophet with a small group, and a prophet with no one with him, until Musa, peace be upon him, passed by me with a great host of the Children of Israel, and they amazed me. I said: 'Who are these?' It was said to me: 'This is your brother Musa, with the Children of Israel.'" He said: "I said: 'Then where is my nation?' It was said: 'Look to your right.' I looked, and behold, the mountain-paths were filled with the faces of men. Then it was said to me: 'Look to your left.' I looked, and behold, the horizon was filled with the faces of men. Then it was said to me: 'Are you content?' I said: 'I am content, O Lord, I am content, O Lord.'" He said: "Then it was said to me: 'With these there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning.'" The Prophet ﷺ said: "May my father and mother be your ransom. If you are able to be among the seventy thousand, then do so; but if you fall short, then be among the people of the mountain-paths [[In ر: "الضراب" (al-dirab), which is an error; the correct reading is what we have recorded from al-Musnad (1/401).]]; and if you fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people there who are rushing about." 'Ukashah ibn Mihsan stood up and said: "Ask Allah, O Messenger of Allah, to make me one of them." That is, of the seventy thousand. He prayed for him. Then another man stood up and said: "Ask Allah, O Messenger of Allah, to make me one of them." He said: "'Ukashah has already preceded you with it." He said: Then we talked among ourselves and said: "Whom do you think these seventy thousand are?" They are a people who were born in Islam and never associated anything with Allah until they died. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "They are those who do not seek cauterization, nor incantation, nor divination, and upon their Lord they rely." [[al-Musnad (1/401).]]

Thus Ahmad narrated it with this chain and this context. He also narrated it from 'Abd al-Samad, from Hisham, from Qatadah, with its chain similar to it, and he added after his saying: "I am content, O Lord, I am content, O Lord," [he] said: "Are you content?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Look to your left." He said: "I looked, and behold, the horizon was filled with the faces of men." He said: "Are you content?" I said: "I am content." This is a sahih chain through this route, narrated by Ahmad alone, and they [the compilers of the six books] did not record it. [[al-Musnad (1/420).]]

A different hadith: Ahmad ibn Mani' said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, Hammad related to us, from Asim, from Zirr, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The nations were displayed before me at the season [of pilgrimage], and I saw my Ummah [[In ج, ر, أ: "I saw"]], and I was impressed by their large number and their appearance. They had filled the plain and the mountain." Then it was said: "Are you pleased, O Muhammad?" I said: "Yes." It was said: "With these there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning, and they are those who do not seek incantation (istirqa') or cauterization (ikhtiwa'), and upon their Lord they rely." Then 'Ukashah stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "You are one of them." Then another man stood and said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "'Ukashah has preceded you with it." [The addition in brackets is from ج.] Al-Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi narrated it and said: "This, in my view, is on the condition of Muslim." [Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, no. 2646 (Mawarid), and Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (9/233), and al-Bazzar in his Musnad (4/204), all through the route of Hammad from Asim.]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Judu'i al-Qadi related to us, 'Uqbah ibn Mukram related to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seventy thousand of my Ummah will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment." It was said: "Who are they?" He said: "They are those who do not cauterize, do not seek incantation, do not take omens, and upon their Lord they rely." [In ج: "Yadkhul" is "Yadkhulun".] Muslim narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Hassan, and in it is the mention of 'Ukashah. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (18/183) and Sahih Muslim no. 216.]

Another hadith: It is established in the two Sahihs, through the narration of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurayrah related to him, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A group of my Ummah will enter Paradise, and they are seventy thousand; their faces will shine like the brightness of the full moon." Abu Hurayrah said: 'Ukashah ibn Mihsan al-Asadi stood up, lifting his cloak, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "'Ukashah has preceded you with it." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6542 and Sahih Muslim no. 216.]

Another hadith: Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn 'Uthman related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Abu Ghassan related to us [In ج: "Ibn Ghassan"], from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed seventy thousand, or seven hundred thousand, of my Ummah will enter [Paradise], holding onto one another, until the first of them and the last of them enter Paradise, and their faces are in the likeness of the moon on the night of the full moon." [In أ and و: "their faces".] It was narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim together, from Qutaybah, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim, from his father, from Sahl, with it. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/142), Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6554 and Sahih Muslim no. 219.]

Another hadith: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Sa'id ibn Mansur related to us, Hushaym related to us, Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us, who said: I was with Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he said: "Which of you saw the star that shot across the sky last night?" I said: "I did." Then I said: "Indeed, I was not in prayer, but I had been stung." He said: "What did you do?" I said: "I sought incantation." He said: "What led you to that?" I said: "A hadith that al-Sha'bi related to us." He said: "And what did al-Sha'bi relate to you?" I said: "He related to us from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami that he said: 'There is no incantation except for the evil eye or a sting.'" He said: "He who stops at what he has heard has done well. But Ibn Abbas related to us from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'The nations were displayed before me. I saw a prophet with a small group, and a prophet with one or two men, and a prophet with no one with him. Then a great mass was raised for me, and I thought they were my Ummah. It was said to me: This is Musa and his people. But look at the horizon. I looked, and there was a great mass. It was said to me: Look at the other horizon. There was a great mass. It was said to me: These are your Ummah, and with them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment.'" Then he rose, entered his house, and the people debated about those who would enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment. Some of them said: "Perhaps they are those who accompanied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Others said: "Perhaps they are those who were born in Islam and did not associate anything with Allah," and they mentioned other things. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to them and said: "What is it that you are discussing?" They informed him, and he said: "They are those who do not seek incantation, do not ask for cauterization, do not take omens, and upon their Lord they rely." 'Ukashah ibn Mihsan stood and said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "You are one of them." Then another man stood and said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "'Ukashah has preceded you with it."

And al-Bukhari narrated it through Usayd ibn Zayd, from Hushaym, but in it is not "they do not seek incantation." [Sahih Muslim no. 220 and Sahih al-Bukhari nos. 5752, 3410, 5705, 6541, 6472.]

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah related to us, Ibn Juraij related to us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, and he mentioned a hadith, in which: "The first group will be saved, their faces like the full moon, seventy thousand, who will not be reckoned. Then those who follow them, like the brightest star in the sky. Then likewise." He mentioned the rest of it. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Rawh, except that he did not mention the Prophet (ﷺ). [Al-Musnad (3/283).]

Another hadith: Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Abi 'Asim said in his book al-Sunnah: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "My Lord promised me that He would admit seventy thousand of my Ummah into Paradise, with every thousand seventy thousand, without reckoning for them and without punishment. And three handfuls from the handfuls of my Lord, Mighty and Majestic."

Likewise al-Tabarani narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Ammar, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, with it, and this is a good chain (isnad). [Al-Sunnah of Ibn Abi 'Asim no. 589 and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/129).]

Another route from Abu Umamah: Ibn Abi 'Asim said: Duhaym related to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, Safwan ibn Amr related to us, from Sulaym ibn Amir, from Abu al-Yaman al-Hawzani [In ج, ر: "al-Hawdi"]—whose name is Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn Luhay—from Abu Umamah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah promised me that He would admit seventy thousand of my Ummah into Paradise without reckoning." Yazid ibn al-Akhnas said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, those in your Ummah are only like the reddish fly among flies." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah promised me seventy thousand, with every thousand seventy thousand, and He added to me three handfuls." [In ر: "the drones" for "flies".] This is also a good (hasan) chain. [Al-Sunnah of Ibn Abi 'Asim no. 588.]

Another hadith: Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Khulayd related to us, Abu Tawbah related to us, Mu'awiyah [In و: "Abu Mu'awiyah"] ibn Sallam related to us, from Zayd ibn Sallam, that he heard Abu Sallam say: Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali related to me that he heard 'Utbah ibn Abd al-Sulami, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, promised me that He would admit seventy thousand of my Ummah into Paradise without reckoning. Then each thousand will intercede for seventy thousand. Then my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will scoop with His two hands three handfuls." [In ر: "and he scooped"] Umar exclaimed Allahu akbar and said: "The first seventy thousand will be interceded for by Allah on behalf of their fathers, sons and kin, and I hope that Allah will make me one of the last handfuls."

Al-Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi said in his book Sifat al-Jannah: "I know of no defect (illah) in this chain. And Allah knows best." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/126, 127). Al-Tabarani also narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (1/254) with this chain. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/413): "In it is Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali, whom Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned without criticizing or authenticating him, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, Hisham—meaning al-Dastawai—related to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, from Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah, Ata' ibn Yasar related to us, that Rifa'ah al-Juhani related to him, who said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until when we were at al-Kudayd—or he said Qudayd—and he mentioned a hadith, in which: Then he said: "My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, promised me that He would admit seventy thousand of my Ummah into Paradise without reckoning. Indeed I hope that they will not enter it until you and those who are righteous among your wives and offspring have prepared dwellings in Paradise."

Al-Diya' [al-Maqdisi] [Addition from و] said: "This, in my view, is on the condition of Muslim." [Al-Musnad (4/16).]

Another hadith: Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah promised me that He would admit four hundred thousand of my Ummah into Paradise." Abu Bakr said: "Add to us, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "By Allah, like this"[In و: "He said: And like this, and he gathered his hands together. He said: Add to us, O Messenger of Allah. He said: And like this."] Umar said: "Enough, O Abu Bakr." Abu Bakr said: "Leave me. What harm is there if Allah admits us all into Paradise?" Umar said: "If Allah wills, He can admit His creation into Paradise with one handful [In أ: "all of them with one handful"]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Umar has spoken the truth."

This hadith with this chain is unique to 'Abd al-Razzaq, as stated by al-Diya'. Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani also narrated it:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Makhlad related to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Haytham al-Baladi related to us, Sulayman ibn Harb related to us, Abu Hilal related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "My Lord promised me that He would admit one hundred thousand of my Ummah into Paradise." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, add to us." He said: "And like this"—and Sulayman ibn Harb gestured with his hand likewise. I said [In أ: "Then he said"; in و: "He said"]: "O Messenger of Allah, add to us." Umar said: "Indeed Allah is able to admit people into Paradise with one handful." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Umar has spoken the truth." This is a strange (gharib) hadith from this route, and Abu Hilal's name is Muhammad ibn Sulaym al-Rasibi, from Basra. [Al-Hilyah of Abu Nu'aym (2/344). Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (3/193) through the route of Abu Hilal from Qatadah.]

Another route from Anas: Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr related to us, Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri al-Sulami related to us, Humayd related to us, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Seventy thousand of my Ummah will enter Paradise." They said: "Add to us, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "For every man seventy thousand." They said: "Add to us"—and he was on a sand dune [In ر: "they were"]—so he said: "Like this," and he scooped with his hand. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, may Allah remove from His mercy whoever enters the Fire after this." This chain is good (jayyid), its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat), except for Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri, about whom Ibn Ma'in was asked, and he said: "Salih." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/417).]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani narrated through Qatada, from Abu Bakr ibn Anas, from Abu Bakr ibn Umayr, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has promised me that He will admit three hundred thousand of my nation into Paradise." Umayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase it for us." He said, "Thus," gesturing with his hand. Umayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase it for us." Then Umar said: "Enough! Indeed Allah, if He wills, can admit the people into Paradise with one handful, or one scoop." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Umar has spoken the truth." [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (1/257). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/409): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Khulayd narrated to us, Abu Tawba narrated to us, Mu'awiya ibn Sallam narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Sallam, that he heard Abu Sallam say: Abdullah ibn Amir narrated to me that Qays al-Kindi narrated that Abu Sa'id [[In C: "Sa'd".]] al-Anmari narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my nation into Paradise without reckoning, and each thousand will intercede for seventy thousand [[In A and B: "for each thousand seventy".]], then my Lord will scoop three handfuls with His two palms." Qays said this, so I said to Abu Sa'id: "Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, with my ear, and my heart retained it." Abu Sa'id said: He (meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)) said: "That, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills, will encompass the emigrants of my nation, and Allah will complete the remainder from our Bedouins."

This hadith was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar, from Abu Tawba al-Rabi' ibn Nafi', with its chain, the same.

He added: Abu Sa'id said: "That was counted in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it reached four hundred million and ninety thousand million [[In A: "seven hundred", and in B: "nine hundred".]]."

Another hadith: Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Marthad al-Tabarani narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'a narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Verily, by He in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, from among you there will be raised on the Day of Resurrection to Paradise a group like the black night, all of them treading the earth. The angels will say: Why has there come with Muhammad more than came with the prophets?" And this is a good chain. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/297). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/404): "In it is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, who is weak."]]

Another type of hadith indicating the virtue and nobility of this nation and its honour before Allah, and that it is the best of nations in this world and the Hereafter.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me, from Jabir [[In B: "that he heard Jabir."]] that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed I hope that those who follow me from my nation on the Day of Resurrection will be a quarter of Paradise." He said: So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar." Then he said: "I hope that they will be a third of the people." He said: So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be half." This was narrated in the same way by Rawh, from Ibn Jurayj, with it. And it is according to the condition of Muslim. [[al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/402): "Ahmad, al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat narrated it, and the narrators of al-Bazzar are the narrators of the Sahih, and likewise one of Ahmad's chains."]]

It is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: "Are you not content to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?" So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar." Then he said: "Are you not content to be a third of the people of Paradise?" So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar." Then he said: "Indeed I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (6528, 6642) and Sahih Muslim, no. (221).]]

Another route from Ibn Mas'ud: al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Musawir narrated to us, Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, al-Harith ibn Hasira narrated to me, al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How will you be when a quarter of Paradise is for you and for the rest of the people three quarters of it?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "How will you be when a third of it is for you?" They said: "That is more." He said: "How will you be when half of it is for you?" They said: "That is more." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, and of them eighty rows are for you."

Al-Tabarani said: al-Harith ibn Hasira alone narrated it. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/208), and Ahmad in his Musnad (1/453) through the route of Affan from Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad with it. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/403): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except al-Harith ibn Hasira, who is deemed trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim narrated to us, Dirar ibn Murra Abu Sinan al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows; this nation is eighty rows of that."

Likewise he narrated it from Affan, from Abd al-Aziz, with it. al-Tirmidhi also recorded it from the hadith of Abu Sinan, with it, and said: "This is a good hadith." Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Alqama ibn Marthad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, with it. [[Musnad (5/355, 347), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2546), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4289).]]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi: Khalid ibn Yazid al-Bajali narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of them from my nation."

Khalid ibn Yazid al-Bajali alone narrated it, and Ibn Adi has spoken about him. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/348). Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (3/13) and said: "All his hadiths are not followed up on, neither in chain nor in text, and I have not seen any earlier scholar's statement about him; rather they neglected him, and in my view he is weak."]]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, Musa ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Hashim ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Amr, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: When the verses ﴿A company of the earlier generations, and a company of the later ones﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 38, 39] were revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are a quarter of the people of Paradise, you are a third of the people of Paradise, you are half of the people of Paradise, you are two-thirds of the people of Paradise." [[Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilya through the route of al-Tabarani (7/101), and quoted al-Tabarani's words: "Ibn al-Mubarak alone transmitted it in marfu' form from al-Thawri. Abu Amr is Muhammad, father of Asbat ibn Muhammad al-Kufi al-Qurashi."]]

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection; we are the first of the people to enter Paradise, except that they were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them. Allah guided us to the truth regarding what they differed about. This is the day about which they differed: the people follow us in it; tomorrow for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow for the Christians."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a marfu' report with similar wording. Muslim also narrated it through the route of al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, and we are the first to enter Paradise," and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (896, 3486, 3487) and Sahih Muslim, no. (855). Sahih Muslim, no. (855).]]

Another hadith: al-Daraqutni narrated in al-Afrad from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Paradise was forbidden to all the prophets until I enter it, and it was forbidden to the nations until my nation enters it."

He then said: Ibn Aqil alone narrated it from al-Zuhri, and none narrated from him other than him. Zuhayr ibn Muhammad alone narrated it from Ibn Aqil, and Amr ibn Abi Salama alone narrated it from Zuhayr.

Abu Ahmad ibn Adi al-Hafiz also narrated it, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-A'yan Muhammad ibn Abi Attab narrated to us, Abu Hafs al-Tinnisi, meaning Amr ibn Abi Salama, narrated to us, Sadaqa al-Dimashqi narrated to us, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Zuhri.

Al-Tha'labi also narrated it: Abu Abbas al-Makhladi narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad informed us, Ahmad ibn Isa al-Tinnisi informed us, Amr ibn Abi Salama narrated to us, Sadaqa ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Aqil, with it. [[Atraf al-Gharaib wa'l-Afrad (q21) of Ibn al-Qaysarani, al-Kamil of Ibn Adi (4/129). al-Baghawi narrated it in his tafsir (2/91) through the route of al-Tha'labi. Ibn Abi Hatim said in al-'Ilal (2/227), quoting Abu Zur'a: "This hadith is munkar; I do not know how it is."]]

These hadiths are in the sense of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and believing in Allah﴾. Whoever from this nation is characterized by these attributes enters with them into this praise and commendation of them, as Qatada said: "It reached us that Umar ibn al-Khattab [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Added from C, A.]], during a pilgrimage he performed, saw among the people haste, so he recited this verse: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, then said: Whoever is pleased to be of that nation, let him fulfil Allah's condition regarding it." Narrated by Ibn Jarir. [[In C, R: "tarala".]]

And whoever is not characterized by this resembles the People of the Book, whom Allah censured by His saying: ﴿They did not forbid one another from wrong that they committed. Evil was what they used to do﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 79]. Therefore, when Allah, Exalted is He, praised this nation for these attributes, He began to censure and rebuke the People of the Book, saying: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed﴾, meaning in what was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiant transgressors﴾, meaning: few of them believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, and most of them are upon misguidance, disbelief, deviation, and disobedience.

Then Allah the Exalted said, informing His believing servants and giving them good tidings that victory and triumph would be theirs over the People of the Book, the disbelieving, heretical ones: ﴿They will not harm you except for some insult. And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you; then they will not be helped.﴾ And so it happened. On the day of Khaybar, Allah humiliated them and rubbed their noses in the dust. Likewise, those before them among the Jews of Madinah, Banu Qaynuqa', Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayzah, were all humiliated by Allah. Likewise, the Christians in al-Sham were defeated by the Companions on many occasions, and they were stripped of the dominion of al-Sham forever and ever. The community of Islam will remain established in al-Sham until 'Isa ibn Maryam ('alayhi al-salam) descends while they are in that state, and he will rule by the religion of Islam, ('alayhi al-salam), according to the Shari'ah of Muhammad (ﷺ), the best of prayers and peace be upon him. He will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah, and accept nothing but Islam.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Humiliation will be imposed upon them wherever they are found, except under a rope from Allah and a rope from the people.﴾ That is: Allah has obligated upon them humiliation and abasement wherever they are, so they will not be safe, ﴿except under a rope from Allah﴾, that is, under a covenant (dhimmah) from Allah, which is the contract of protection (ʿaqd al-dhimmah) for them, the imposition of the jizyah upon them, and obligating them to the rulings of the religion. ﴿And a rope from the people﴾, that is, a safe-conduct from them and for them, as in the case of the truce-holder, the one under treaty, and the captive whom one of the Muslims grants safe-conduct, even if it is a woman, and likewise a slave, according to one of the two opinions of the scholars.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿except under a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾ means: under a covenant from Allah and a covenant from the people. This was also said by Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they incurred wrath from Allah﴾, that is, they were bound and they accepted a wrath from Allah, and they deserved it. ﴿And humiliation was imposed upon them﴾, that is, they were made to bear it, by decree and by law. For this reason He said: ﴿That is because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right﴾, that is, what drove them to that was arrogance, transgression and envy. So this resulted for them in humiliation, abasement and neediness forever, continuing into the humiliation of the Hereafter. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress﴾, that is, what drove them to disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the messengers of Allah, and what made them susceptible to that, was that they used to greatly disobey the commands of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and commit His prohibitions, and exceed the bounds in the law of Allah. We seek refuge in Allah from that, and Allah is the One whose help is sought.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib narrated to us, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sulayman al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ma'mar al-Azdi, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Children of Israel used to kill three hundred prophets in a single day, and then the market of their vegetable sellers would be set up at the end of the day.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 110–112 (part 1 of 4):

He, exalted is He, informs about this Muhammadan nation that they are the best of nations, so He said: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Maysara, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah regarding ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, that he said: "The best of people for people. You bring them in chains around their necks until they enter Islam." [[In ج, ر, أ, و: "يأتون" (ya'tun).]] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4557).]]

Likewise said Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, meaning: the best of people for people.

The meaning is that they are the best of nations and the most beneficial of people to people. For this reason He said: ﴿You enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah﴾. [[In ر: "يؤمنون" (yu'minun).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umayrah, from the wife of [Dhurrah] [[Addition from ج, ر, أ, and al-Musnad.]] the daughter of Abu Lahab, [from Durrah bint Abi Lahab] [[Addition from ج, ر, أ, and al-Musnad.]], who said: A man stood before the Prophet ﷺ while he was on the pulpit, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is the best of people?" He said: "The best of people are those who recite best, who are most God-fearing, who most enjoin what is right, who most forbid what is wrong, and who most maintain ties of kinship." [[al-Musnad (6/432).]]

Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, al-Nasa'i in his Sunan, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the narration of Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾, that he said: "They are those who emigrated with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Makkah to Madinah." [[al-Musnad (1/319); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11072); al-Mustadrak (2/294). Al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound according to the condition of Muslim," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

The correct view is that this verse is general for the whole nation, each generation according to its share, and the best of its generations are those among whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, then those who follow them, then those who follow them, as He said in another verse: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation﴾, meaning: the best, ﴿so that you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [[Addition from ج, ر, أ, و.]], and the verse continues.

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, the Sunan of Ibn Majah, and the Mustadrak of al-Hakim, from the narration of Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You complete seventy nations; you are the best of them, and you are the most honoured by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [[al-Musnad (4/447); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (3001); Sunan Ibn Majah (4287); al-Mustadrak (4/84).]]

This is a well-known hadith, and al-Tirmidhi graded it as hasan. It is also narrated from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Abu Sa'id [al-Khudri] [[Addition from ج.]], similar to it.

This nation has taken the lead in good deeds only through its Prophet Muhammad ﷺ [[In و: "may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]], for he is the noblest of Allah's creation, the most honoured of the Messengers before Allah. Allah sent him with a complete, great law that He had not given to any prophet before him or to any messenger among the Messengers. So the deed [according to] [[Addition from ج, ر.]] his method and path, a little of it stands in a place where the great deeds of others cannot stand in its place, as Imam Ahmad said:

'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah (i.e., Ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil), from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, who is Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, that he heard 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given what no one among the prophets has been given." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is it?" He said: "I was helped with terror, I was given the keys of the earth, I was named Ahmad, the earth was made pure and a place of prostration for me, and my nation was made the best of nations." Ahmad alone narrated it through this route, and its chain is hasan. [[al-Musnad (1/98). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/260): "In it is 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, who has poor memory." Al-Tirmidhi said: "Truthful, though some scholars spoke about him because of his memory. I heard Muhammad al-Bukhari say: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq, and al-Humaydi would use the hadith of Ibn 'Aqil as evidence." I say: The hadith is hasan.]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-'Ala' al-Hasan ibn Sawwar narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah, from Ibn Abi Hulays, from Yazid ibn Maysarah, who said: I heard Umm al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with her, say: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: I heard Abu al-Qasim ﷺ, and I never heard him call him by his kunyah before or after that, say: "Allah, the Exalted, says: 'O 'Isa, I am sending after you a nation: if what they love befalls them, they praise and thank [Allah]; and if what they dislike befalls them, they seek reward and are patient, though they have neither forbearance nor knowledge.'" He said: "O Lord, how can this be for them, when they have neither forbearance nor knowledge?" He said: "I will give them of My forbearance and My knowledge." [[al-Musnad (6/450).]]

Hadiths have come whose mention is appropriate here:

Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, Bukayr [[In ج: "Bakr."]] ibn al-Akhnas narrated to us, from a man, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning, their faces like the full moon, their hearts upon the heart of one man. So I asked my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, for more, and He added for each one of them seventy thousand more." Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I thought that this would reach the people of the villages and what is near the edges of the deserts. [[al-Musnad (1/6). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/410): "In it is al-Mas'udi, who became confused, and the narrator from him is unnamed; the rest of Ahmad's narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated to us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Mihran, from Musa ibn 'Ubayd, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "My Lord has given me seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning." 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, why did you not ask Him for more?" He said: "I asked Him, and He gave me, with every man, seventy thousand." 'Umar said: "Why did you not ask Him for more?" He said: "I have asked Him, and He has given me like this." 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr [[In ج, ر, أ: "'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr."]] spread his hands apart, and 'Abd Allah said: He spread his two arms, and 'Abd Allah scooped with his hands. Hisham said: "And this is from Allah; its number is not known." [[al-Musnad (1/197). In its chain are al-Qasim ibn Mihran and Musa ibn 'Ubayd, who are both unknown; the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'ah, who said: Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd said: Thawban fell ill in Hims, and over it was 'Abd Allah ibn Qurt al-Azdi, and he did not visit him. A man from the Kala'iyyin entered upon Thawban to visit him, and Thawban said to him: [Do you write?] He said: Yes. He said: Write. So he wrote for the commander 'Abd Allah ibn Qurt: "From Thawban, [freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ] [[Addition from ج, ر, and al-Musnad.]], to proceed: If Musa and 'Isa, peace be upon them both, had a servant in your presence, you would have visited him." Then he folded the letter and said to him: Will you deliver it to him? He said: Yes. So the man set off with his letter and handed it to Ibn Qurt. When he saw it, he stood up in alarm. The people said: What is his matter? Has something new happened? So he came to Thawban until he entered upon him and visited him, and sat with him for a while, then stood up. Thawban took hold of his cloak and said: Sit until I tell you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I heard him say: "Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise, without reckoning or punishment upon them, with every thousand seventy thousand."

Ahmad alone narrated it through this route, and all of its narrators are trustworthy Syrians from Hims, so it is a sahih hadith. And to Allah belongs all praise.

Another route: al-Tabarani said: 'Amr ibn Ishaq ibn Zabriq al-Himsi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il [i.e., Ibn 'Ayyash] narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'ah, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu Asma' al-Rahabi, from Thawban, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "My Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, has promised me seventy thousand of my nation who will not be reckoned, with every thousand seventy thousand." This is perhaps the preserved version, with the addition of Abu Asma' al-Rahabi between Shurayh and Thawban. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/92). He also narrated it in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (1682).]] And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from 'Imran ibn Husayn, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: We talked a great deal in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night, then in the morning we went to him, and he said: "The prophets were shown to me last night with their nations. A prophet would pass with three, and a prophet with a band, and a prophet with a small group, and a prophet with no one with him, until Musa, peace be upon him, passed by me with a great host of the Children of Israel, and they amazed me. I said: 'Who are these?' It was said to me: 'This is your brother Musa, with the Children of Israel.'" He said: "I said: 'Then where is my nation?' It was said: 'Look to your right.' I looked, and behold, the mountain-paths were filled with the faces of men. Then it was said to me: 'Look to your left.' I looked, and behold, the horizon was filled with the faces of men. Then it was said to me: 'Are you content?' I said: 'I am content, O Lord, I am content, O Lord.'" He said: "Then it was said to me: 'With these there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning.'" The Prophet ﷺ said: "May my father and mother be your ransom. If you are able to be among the seventy thousand, then do so; but if you fall short, then be among the people of the mountain-paths [[In ر: "الضراب" (al-dirab), which is an error; the correct reading is what we have recorded from al-Musnad (1/401).]]; and if you fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people there who are rushing about." 'Ukashah ibn Mihsan stood up and said: "Ask Allah, O Messenger of Allah, to make me one of them." That is, of the seventy thousand. He prayed for him. Then another man stood up and said: "Ask Allah, O Messenger of Allah, to make me one of them." He said: "'Ukashah has already preceded you with it." He said: Then we talked among ourselves and said: "Whom do you think these seventy thousand are?" They are a people who were born in Islam and never associated anything with Allah until they died. This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "They are those who do not seek cauterization, nor incantation, nor divination, and upon their Lord they rely." [[al-Musnad (1/401).]]

Thus Ahmad narrated it with this chain and this context. He also narrated it from 'Abd al-Samad, from Hisham, from Qatadah, with its chain similar to it, and he added after his saying: "I am content, O Lord, I am content, O Lord," [he] said: "Are you content?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Look to your left." He said: "I looked, and behold, the horizon was filled with the faces of men." He said: "Are you content?" I said: "I am content." This is a sahih chain through this route, narrated by Ahmad alone, and they [the compilers of the six books] did not record it. [[al-Musnad (1/420).]]

A different hadith: Ahmad ibn Mani' said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, Hammad related to us, from Asim, from Zirr, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The nations were displayed before me at the season [of pilgrimage], and I saw my Ummah [[In ج, ر, أ: "I saw"]], and I was impressed by their large number and their appearance. They had filled the plain and the mountain." Then it was said: "Are you pleased, O Muhammad?" I said: "Yes." It was said: "With these there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning, and they are those who do not seek incantation (istirqa') or cauterization (ikhtiwa'), and upon their Lord they rely." Then 'Ukashah stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "You are one of them." Then another man stood and said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "'Ukashah has preceded you with it." [The addition in brackets is from ج.] Al-Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi narrated it and said: "This, in my view, is on the condition of Muslim." [Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, no. 2646 (Mawarid), and Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (9/233), and al-Bazzar in his Musnad (4/204), all through the route of Hammad from Asim.]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Judu'i al-Qadi related to us, 'Uqbah ibn Mukram related to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seventy thousand of my Ummah will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment." It was said: "Who are they?" He said: "They are those who do not cauterize, do not seek incantation, do not take omens, and upon their Lord they rely." [In ج: "Yadkhul" is "Yadkhulun".] Muslim narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Hassan, and in it is the mention of 'Ukashah. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (18/183) and Sahih Muslim no. 216.]

Another hadith: It is established in the two Sahihs, through the narration of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurayrah related to him, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A group of my Ummah will enter Paradise, and they are seventy thousand; their faces will shine like the brightness of the full moon." Abu Hurayrah said: 'Ukashah ibn Mihsan al-Asadi stood up, lifting his cloak, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, make him one of them." Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "'Ukashah has preceded you with it." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6542 and Sahih Muslim no. 216.]

Another hadith: Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn 'Uthman related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related to us, Abu Ghassan related to us [In ج: "Ibn Ghassan"], from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed seventy thousand, or seven hundred thousand, of my Ummah will enter [Paradise], holding onto one another, until the first of them and the last of them enter Paradise, and their faces are in the likeness of the moon on the night of the full moon." [In أ and و: "their faces".] It was narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim together, from Qutaybah, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim, from his father, from Sahl, with it. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/142), Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6554 and Sahih Muslim no. 219.]

Another hadith: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Sa'id ibn Mansur related to us, Hushaym related to us, Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us, who said: I was with Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he said: "Which of you saw the star that shot across the sky last night?" I said: "I did." Then I said: "Indeed, I was not in prayer, but I had been stung." He said: "What did you do?" I said: "I sought incantation." He said: "What led you to that?" I said: "A hadith that al-Sha'bi related to us." He said: "And what did al-Sha'bi relate to you?" I said: "He related to us from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami that he said: 'There is no incantation except for the evil eye or a sting.'" He said: "He who stops at what he has heard has done well. But Ibn Abbas related to us from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'The nations were displayed before me. I saw a prophet with a small group, and a prophet with one or two men, and a prophet with no one with him. Then a great mass was raised for me, and I thought they were my Ummah. It was said to me: This is Musa and his people. But look at the horizon. I looked, and there was a great mass. It was said to me: Look at the other horizon. There was a great mass. It was said to me: These are your Ummah, and with them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment.'" Then he rose, entered his house, and the people debated about those who would enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment. Some of them said: "Perhaps they are those who accompanied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Others said: "Perhaps they are those who were born in Islam and did not associate anything with Allah," and they mentioned other things. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to them and said: "What is it that you are discussing?" They informed him, and he said: "They are those who do not seek incantation, do not ask for cauterization, do not take omens, and upon their Lord they rely." 'Ukashah ibn Mihsan stood and said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "You are one of them." Then another man stood and said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me one of them." He said: "'Ukashah has preceded you with it."

And al-Bukhari narrated it through Usayd ibn Zayd, from Hushaym, but in it is not "they do not seek incantation." [Sahih Muslim no. 220 and Sahih al-Bukhari nos. 5752, 3410, 5705, 6541, 6472.]

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah related to us, Ibn Juraij related to us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, and he mentioned a hadith, in which: "The first group will be saved, their faces like the full moon, seventy thousand, who will not be reckoned. Then those who follow them, like the brightest star in the sky. Then likewise." He mentioned the rest of it. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Rawh, except that he did not mention the Prophet (ﷺ). [Al-Musnad (3/283).]

Another hadith: Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Abi 'Asim said in his book al-Sunnah: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "My Lord promised me that He would admit seventy thousand of my Ummah into Paradise, with every thousand seventy thousand, without reckoning for them and without punishment. And three handfuls from the handfuls of my Lord, Mighty and Majestic."

Likewise al-Tabarani narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Ammar, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, with it, and this is a good chain (isnad). [Al-Sunnah of Ibn Abi 'Asim no. 589 and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/129).]

Another route from Abu Umamah: Ibn Abi 'Asim said: Duhaym related to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, Safwan ibn Amr related to us, from Sulaym ibn Amir, from Abu al-Yaman al-Hawzani [In ج, ر: "al-Hawdi"]—whose name is Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn Luhay—from Abu Umamah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah promised me that He would admit seventy thousand of my Ummah into Paradise without reckoning." Yazid ibn al-Akhnas said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, those in your Ummah are only like the reddish fly among flies." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah promised me seventy thousand, with every thousand seventy thousand, and He added to me three handfuls." [In ر: "the drones" for "flies".] This is also a good (hasan) chain. [Al-Sunnah of Ibn Abi 'Asim no. 588.]

Another hadith: Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Khulayd related to us, Abu Tawbah related to us, Mu'awiyah [In و: "Abu Mu'awiyah"] ibn Sallam related to us, from Zayd ibn Sallam, that he heard Abu Sallam say: Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali related to me that he heard 'Utbah ibn Abd al-Sulami, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, promised me that He would admit seventy thousand of my Ummah into Paradise without reckoning. Then each thousand will intercede for seventy thousand. Then my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will scoop with His two hands three handfuls." [In ر: "and he scooped"] Umar exclaimed Allahu akbar and said: "The first seventy thousand will be interceded for by Allah on behalf of their fathers, sons and kin, and I hope that Allah will make me one of the last handfuls."

Al-Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi said in his book Sifat al-Jannah: "I know of no defect (illah) in this chain. And Allah knows best." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/126, 127). Al-Tabarani also narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (1/254) with this chain. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/413): "In it is Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali, whom Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned without criticizing or authenticating him, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, Hisham—meaning al-Dastawai—related to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, from Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah, Ata' ibn Yasar related to us, that Rifa'ah al-Juhani related to him, who said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until when we were at al-Kudayd—or he said Qudayd—and he mentioned a hadith, in which: Then he said: "My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, promised me that He would admit seventy thousand of my Ummah into Paradise without reckoning. Indeed I hope that they will not enter it until you and those who are righteous among your wives and offspring have prepared dwellings in Paradise."

Al-Diya' [al-Maqdisi] [Addition from و] said: "This, in my view, is on the condition of Muslim." [Al-Musnad (4/16).]

Another hadith: Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah promised me that He would admit four hundred thousand of my Ummah into Paradise." Abu Bakr said: "Add to us, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "By Allah, like this"[In و: "He said: And like this, and he gathered his hands together. He said: Add to us, O Messenger of Allah. He said: And like this."] Umar said: "Enough, O Abu Bakr." Abu Bakr said: "Leave me. What harm is there if Allah admits us all into Paradise?" Umar said: "If Allah wills, He can admit His creation into Paradise with one handful [In أ: "all of them with one handful"]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Umar has spoken the truth."

This hadith with this chain is unique to 'Abd al-Razzaq, as stated by al-Diya'. Abu Nu'aym al-Isfahani also narrated it:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Makhlad related to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Haytham al-Baladi related to us, Sulayman ibn Harb related to us, Abu Hilal related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "My Lord promised me that He would admit one hundred thousand of my Ummah into Paradise." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, add to us." He said: "And like this"—and Sulayman ibn Harb gestured with his hand likewise. I said [In أ: "Then he said"; in و: "He said"]: "O Messenger of Allah, add to us." Umar said: "Indeed Allah is able to admit people into Paradise with one handful." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Umar has spoken the truth." This is a strange (gharib) hadith from this route, and Abu Hilal's name is Muhammad ibn Sulaym al-Rasibi, from Basra. [Al-Hilyah of Abu Nu'aym (2/344). Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (3/193) through the route of Abu Hilal from Qatadah.]

Another route from Anas: Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr related to us, Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri al-Sulami related to us, Humayd related to us, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Seventy thousand of my Ummah will enter Paradise." They said: "Add to us, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "For every man seventy thousand." They said: "Add to us"—and he was on a sand dune [In ر: "they were"]—so he said: "Like this," and he scooped with his hand. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, may Allah remove from His mercy whoever enters the Fire after this." This chain is good (jayyid), its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat), except for Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri, about whom Ibn Ma'in was asked, and he said: "Salih." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/417).]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani narrated through Qatada, from Abu Bakr ibn Anas, from Abu Bakr ibn Umayr, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has promised me that He will admit three hundred thousand of my nation into Paradise." Umayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase it for us." He said, "Thus," gesturing with his hand. Umayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase it for us." Then Umar said: "Enough! Indeed Allah, if He wills, can admit the people into Paradise with one handful, or one scoop." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Umar has spoken the truth." [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (1/257). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/409): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Khulayd narrated to us, Abu Tawba narrated to us, Mu'awiya ibn Sallam narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Sallam, that he heard Abu Sallam say: Abdullah ibn Amir narrated to me that Qays al-Kindi narrated that Abu Sa'id [[In C: "Sa'd".]] al-Anmari narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my nation into Paradise without reckoning, and each thousand will intercede for seventy thousand [[In A and B: "for each thousand seventy".]], then my Lord will scoop three handfuls with His two palms." Qays said this, so I said to Abu Sa'id: "Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes, with my ear, and my heart retained it." Abu Sa'id said: He (meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)) said: "That, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills, will encompass the emigrants of my nation, and Allah will complete the remainder from our Bedouins."

This hadith was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar, from Abu Tawba al-Rabi' ibn Nafi', with its chain, the same.

He added: Abu Sa'id said: "That was counted in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it reached four hundred million and ninety thousand million [[In A: "seven hundred", and in B: "nine hundred".]]."

Another hadith: Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Marthad al-Tabarani narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'a narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Verily, by He in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, from among you there will be raised on the Day of Resurrection to Paradise a group like the black night, all of them treading the earth. The angels will say: Why has there come with Muhammad more than came with the prophets?" And this is a good chain. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/297). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/404): "In it is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, who is weak."]]

Another type of hadith indicating the virtue and nobility of this nation and its honour before Allah, and that it is the best of nations in this world and the Hereafter.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me, from Jabir [[In B: "that he heard Jabir."]] that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed I hope that those who follow me from my nation on the Day of Resurrection will be a quarter of Paradise." He said: So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar." Then he said: "I hope that they will be a third of the people." He said: So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar." Then he said: "I hope that you will be half." This was narrated in the same way by Rawh, from Ibn Jurayj, with it. And it is according to the condition of Muslim. [[al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/402): "Ahmad, al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat narrated it, and the narrators of al-Bazzar are the narrators of the Sahih, and likewise one of Ahmad's chains."]]

It is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: "Are you not content to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?" So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar." Then he said: "Are you not content to be a third of the people of Paradise?" So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar." Then he said: "Indeed I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (6528, 6642) and Sahih Muslim, no. (221).]]

Another route from Ibn Mas'ud: al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Musawir narrated to us, Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, al-Harith ibn Hasira narrated to me, al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How will you be when a quarter of Paradise is for you and for the rest of the people three quarters of it?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "How will you be when a third of it is for you?" They said: "That is more." He said: "How will you be when half of it is for you?" They said: "That is more." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, and of them eighty rows are for you."

Al-Tabarani said: al-Harith ibn Hasira alone narrated it. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/208), and Ahmad in his Musnad (1/453) through the route of Affan from Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad with it. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/403): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except al-Harith ibn Hasira, who is deemed trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim narrated to us, Dirar ibn Murra Abu Sinan al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows; this nation is eighty rows of that."

Likewise he narrated it from Affan, from Abd al-Aziz, with it. al-Tirmidhi also recorded it from the hadith of Abu Sinan, with it, and said: "This is a good hadith." Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Alqama ibn Marthad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, with it. [[Musnad (5/355, 347), Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2546), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4289).]]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi: Khalid ibn Yazid al-Bajali narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of them from my nation."

Khalid ibn Yazid al-Bajali alone narrated it, and Ibn Adi has spoken about him. [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/348). Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (3/13) and said: "All his hadiths are not followed up on, neither in chain nor in text, and I have not seen any earlier scholar's statement about him; rather they neglected him, and in my view he is weak."]]

Another hadith: al-Tabarani said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, Musa ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Hashim ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Amr, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: When the verses ﴿A company of the earlier generations, and a company of the later ones﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 38, 39] were revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are a quarter of the people of Paradise, you are a third of the people of Paradise, you are half of the people of Paradise, you are two-thirds of the people of Paradise." [[Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilya through the route of al-Tabarani (7/101), and quoted al-Tabarani's words: "Ibn al-Mubarak alone transmitted it in marfu' form from al-Thawri. Abu Amr is Muhammad, father of Asbat ibn Muhammad al-Kufi al-Qurashi."]]

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection; we are the first of the people to enter Paradise, except that they were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them. Allah guided us to the truth regarding what they differed about. This is the day about which they differed: the people follow us in it; tomorrow for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow for the Christians."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a marfu' report with similar wording. Muslim also narrated it through the route of al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, and we are the first to enter Paradise," and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (896, 3486, 3487) and Sahih Muslim, no. (855). Sahih Muslim, no. (855).]]

Another hadith: al-Daraqutni narrated in al-Afrad from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Paradise was forbidden to all the prophets until I enter it, and it was forbidden to the nations until my nation enters it."

He then said: Ibn Aqil alone narrated it from al-Zuhri, and none narrated from him other than him. Zuhayr ibn Muhammad alone narrated it from Ibn Aqil, and Amr ibn Abi Salama alone narrated it from Zuhayr.
