He and his companions said: "If we knew there would be fighting today, we would follow you. But we do not think you will fight today."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued marching until he halted at the gorge of Uhud, on the side of the valley. He placed his back and his camp toward Uhud and said: "None of you shall fight until we order him to fight."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prepared for battle with seven hundred of his Companions. He appointed 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr, brother of the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, over the archers, and the archers that day numbered fifty men. He said to them: "Repel the cavalry from us, and let them not attack us from your side. Stay in your place whether the victory is ours or theirs. If you see us being snatched by birds, do not leave your place."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wore two coats of armour, and gave the banner to Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, brother of the Banu 'Abd al-Dar. On that day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away some of the young men and postponed others, until he permitted them at the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq), which took place nearly two years after this day.

The Quraysh arrayed themselves, numbering three thousand, with two hundred horses, which they had made to stand in line. They placed Khalid ibn al-Walid over the right wing of the cavalry, and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl over the left wing, and they gave the banner to the Banu 'Abd al-Dar. Then there occurred between the two groups what will come in detail in its proper place, at these verses, if Allah the Exalted wills.

Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And [remember] when you set out from your family in the morning to station the believers at their positions for battle﴾. That is: He showed them their stations and made them (or placed them) on the right wing and the left wing, and where You commanded them. ﴿And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾, that is: Hearing of what you say, and Knowing of your inner intentions.

Ibn Jarir raised here a question, the gist of which is: How can they say that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to Uhud on Friday after the prayer, when Allah said ﴿And [remember] when you set out from your family in the morning to station the believers at their positions for battle﴾? His answer was that his going out to station them in their positions was only on Saturday at the beginning of the day.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿When two parties among you were about to lose heart, while Allah was their ally. And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾. Al-Bukhari said: 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, he said: 'Amr said: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: "It was about us that this was revealed: ﴿When two parties among you were about to lose heart, while Allah was their ally. And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾." He said: "We were the two parties, the Banu Harithah and the Banu Salamah, and we would not like" — Sufyan said once: "it would not please me" — "that it had not been revealed, because of Allah's saying: ﴿while Allah was their ally﴾."

Muslim also narrated it through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah with the same chain. Likewise, more than one of the early scholars said that they were the Banu Harithah and the Banu Salamah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were humiliated. So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾. That is, on the day of Badr, which fell on a Friday, coinciding with the seventeenth of Ramadan in the second year after the Hijrah. It is the Day of Criterion (Yawm al-Furqan), on which Allah exalted Islam and its people, and humbled polytheism and destroyed its place, even though the Muslims were few on that day. They were three hundred and thirteen men, among whom were two horses and seventy camels, and the rest were on foot, having with them none of the equipment they needed. The enemy on that day numbered between nine hundred and a thousand, in full coats of mail and helmets, with complete equipment, proud cavalry horses, and abundant ornaments. Allah honoured His Messenger, made His revelation and His scripture manifest, whitened the face of the Prophet and his people, and disgraced Satan and his host. Therefore Allah the Exalted said, bestowing favour upon His believing servants and the party of the God-fearing: ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were humiliated﴾, that is: your number was small, so that they would know that victory is only from Allah, not by abundance of numbers or equipment. For this reason He said in another verse: ﴿And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you but it did not avail you at all, and the earth was constricted for you in spite of its vastness, and you turned back in retreat. Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers. Then Allah turns in forgiveness after that to whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [At-Tawbah: 25–27].

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, who said: I heard 'Iyad al-Ash'ari say: "I witnessed al-Yarmuk, and over us were five commanders: Abu 'Ubaydah, Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan, Ibn Hasanah, Khalid ibn al-Walid, and 'Iyad." — and this 'Iyad is not the one who narrated to Simak. He said: "'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, had said: 'When there is fighting, Abu 'Ubaydah is over you.'" He said: "We wrote to him that death had surged upon us, and we asked him for reinforcement. He wrote to us: 'Your letter has reached me asking me for reinforcement, and I direct you to One who is mightier in victory and stronger in soldiers: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So seek His help, for Muhammad (ﷺ) was given victory at Badr with fewer than your number. When my letter reaches you, fight them and do not refer back to me.'" He said: "We fought them and defeated them for four farsakhs. We also captured wealth, and we consulted together. 'Iyad advised us to give ten to every person." He said: "Abu 'Ubaydah said: 'Who will race me?' A young man said: 'I will, if you do not get angry.' So he outran him, and I saw the two braids of Abu 'Ubaydah swinging as he rode behind him on a purebred horse."

This is a sound chain (isnad). Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih through the hadith of Bundar, from Ghundar, similarly, and the hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi chose it in his book.

Badr is a place between Makkah and Madinah, known by its well, named after a man who dug it called "Badr ibn al-Narayn." Al-Sha'bi said: Badr is a well belonging to a man named Badr.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾, that is: that you may perform His obedience.

The reference of this event is the Battle of Uhud according to the majority of scholars. This is what Ibn 'Abbas said, along with al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and others. From al-Hasan al-Basri it is reported that the reference is the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated this, but it is a strange report (gharib) and cannot be relied upon.

The Battle of Uhud took place on Saturday in Shawwal in the third year after the Hijrah (migration). Qatadah said it was eleven nights into Shawwal. 'Ikrimah said it was Saturday, the middle of Shawwal. Allah knows best.

The cause was that when the polytheists lost those of their nobles who were killed at Badr, and the caravan with its trade goods that was with Abu Sufyan escaped, their caravan returned to Makkah. The sons of those who had been killed and the leaders of those who remained said to Abu Sufyan: "Set these funds aside for fighting Muhammad." They spent them on that, gathered the armies and the Ahabish (allied tribes), and marched with about three thousand men until they camped near Uhud, facing Madinah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the Friday prayer, and when he finished, he prayed over a man from the Banu al-Najjar called Malik ibn 'Amr. He consulted the people: "Should he go out to them, or remain in Madinah?" 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy advised remaining in Madinah: "If they stay, they will stay in a wretched place of confinement. If they enter it, the men will fight them in the streets, and the women and children will pelt them with stones from above. If they return, they will return defeated." Others among the Companions who had not witnessed Badr advised going out to them. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered, put on his armour, and went out to them. Some of them regretted and said: "Perhaps we forced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you wish, we will remain." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet, once he has put on his armour, to take it off until Allah judges between him and his enemy."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾, that is: that you may perform His obedience.

The mufassirun differed concerning this promise: was it on the Day of Badr or the Day of Uhud? There are two opinions:

The first: His saying ﴿When you said to the believers﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr﴾. This was narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, 'Amir al-Sha'bi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also chose this view.

'Abbad ibn Mansur narrated from al-Hasan regarding His saying ﴿When you said to the believers, "Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ that he said: "This is the Day of Badr." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said:

My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us from Dawud, from 'Amir (i.e., al-Sha'bi), that the Muslims were informed on the Day of Badr that Kurz ibn Jabir was reinforcing the polytheists, so that grieved them, and Allah revealed: ﴿Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?﴾ up to His saying ﴿marked﴾. He said: "Then news of the defeat reached Kurz, so he did not reinforce the polytheists, and Allah did not reinforce the Muslims with the five thousand."

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Allah reinforced the Muslims with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand."

If it is said: What is the reconciliation between this verse, according to this view, and His saying in the account of Badr: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand from the angels, following one another"﴾ [and Allah did not make it except as good tidings and so that your hearts may be assured thereby. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise] [al-Anfal 8:9–10]?

The answer: The specification of the thousand here does not contradict the three thousand or more beyond that, because of His saying ﴿following one another (murdifin)﴾, meaning that others follow them, and thousands of others like them follow them. This context is similar to this context in Surat Al 'Imran. The apparent meaning is that this occurred on the Day of Badr, as is well known, since the fighting of the angels was only on the Day of Badr, and Allah knows best. Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah: "Allah reinforced the believers on the Day of Badr with five thousand."

The second opinion: This promise is connected to His saying ﴿And when you left your family in the morning to position the believers at their stations for the battle﴾, and that was the Day of Uhud. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, Musa ibn 'Uqbah, and others. However, they said: the reinforcement with the five thousand did not occur, because the Muslims fled that day. 'Ikrimah added: nor with the three thousand, because of His saying ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾, and they were not patient, rather they fled, so they were not reinforced with a single angel.

* *

His saying ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾ means: if you are patient in confronting your enemy, and fear Me and obey My command.

* *

His saying ﴿and they come at you in this, their rage﴾ — al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: that is, from this direction of theirs. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Abu Salih said: that is, from this anger of theirs. al-Dahhak said: from their anger and their direction. al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: from this journey of theirs. It is also said: from this anger of theirs.

* *

His saying ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked﴾ means: distinguished by their markings (sima).

Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i narrated from Haritha ibn Mudarrib, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was white wool, and their marking was also on the forelocks of their horses."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Hadbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah regarding this verse ﴿marked﴾, he said: "With red wool."

Mujahid said: ﴿marked﴾ means: their manes were trimmed, and their forelocks were marked with white wool, on the tails of the horses.

al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The angels came to Muhammad (ﷺ) marked with wool, so Muhammad and his companions marked themselves and their horses by their markings with wool."

'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: ﴿marked﴾ means: with the marking of battle. Makhul said: ﴿marked﴾ means: with turbans.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from a hadith of 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Habib, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding His saying ﴿marked﴾: "Distinguished." And the marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was black turbans, and on the Day of Hunayn red turbans."

He also narrated from a hadith of Husayn ibn Mukhariq, from Sa'id, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The angels did not fight except on the Day of Badr."

Ibn Ishaq said: "Someone I do not suspect told me, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was white turbans which they let hang down their backs, and on the Day of Hunayn red turbans. The angels did not strike on any day other than the Day of Badr; on other days they were a number and a reinforcement, not striking."

Then he narrated it from al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, and mentioned something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Abbad: that al-Zubayr [ibn al-'Awwam] [addition from another manuscript], may Allah be pleased with him, had on him on the Day of Badr a yellow turban, wrapping it around himself, so the angels descended upon them with yellow turbans.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, and he mentioned it.

* *

His saying ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you, and so that your hearts may be assured by it﴾ means: Allah did not send down the angels and inform you of their descent except as good news for you, and a consolation for your hearts and a reassurance. Otherwise, ﴿victory is only from Allah﴾, who, if He willed, would have triumphed over His enemies without you, and without any need for your fighting them, as He said after commanding the believers to fight: ﴿That, and had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He ordered fighting] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah — never will He waste their deeds. He will guide them and amend their condition. And admit them to Paradise which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad 47:4–6]. Therefore He said here: ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you, and so that your hearts may be assured by it. And victory is not except from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾, meaning: He is the One of might that cannot be overcome, and of wisdom in His decree and its perfection.

Then He said: ﴿That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: He commanded you to strive and to fight, for He has wisdom in that in every case. Therefore He mentioned all the possible outcomes concerning the disbelievers and the fighters: He said ﴿that He may cut off a portion﴾, meaning: to destroy a group ﴿of those who disbelieved, or subdue them﴾, meaning: to humiliate them and turn them back in their rage, since they did not attain from you what they wanted. Therefore He said: ﴿or subdue them, so they turn back﴾, meaning: return ﴿defeated﴾, meaning: they did not obtain what they hoped for.

Then He inserted a sentence indicating that the judgment in this world and the Hereafter belongs to Him alone, with no partner, and He said: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, meaning: rather the whole matter is up to Me, as He said: ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:40], and He said ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:272], and He said ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas 28:56].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding His saying ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾: meaning, you have no part in the judgment concerning My servants except what I have commanded you regarding them.

Then He mentioned the rest of the outcomes, saying: ﴿or He turns to them in forgiveness﴾, meaning: from the disbelief they are in, and guides them after misguidance, ﴿or punishes them﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter, for their disbelief and their sins. Therefore He said: ﴿for indeed, they are wrongdoers﴾, meaning: they deserve that.

al-Bukhari said: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, 'Abd Allah informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, Salim narrated to me, from his father: that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, when he raised his head from bowing in the second rak'ah of the dawn prayer: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," after saying: "Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You is the praise." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed ﴿You have no part in the matter [or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾.

This was also narrated by al-Nasa'i, from a hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and 'Abd al-Razzaq, both from Ma'mar, with it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4069, 4559, 7346; and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11075.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Abu 'Aqil narrated to us — Ahmad said: he is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Aqil, a hadith transmitter of good standing and trustworthy — he said: 'Umar ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from Salim, from his father who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "O Allah, curse so-and-so. O Allah, curse al-Harith ibn Hisham. O Allah, curse Suhayl ibn 'Amr. O Allah, curse Safwan ibn Umayyah." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter, or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾, and so they were all forgiven. [al-Musnad, 2/93.]

Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah al-Ghallabi narrated to us, Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan narrated to us, from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate against four people. He said: So Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter [or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾ — and he said: "And Allah guided them to Islam." [al-Musnad, 2/104.]

Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan said, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate against men among the polytheists, naming them by their names, until Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, the verse.

al-Bukhari also said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whenever he wished to supplicate against someone — or to supplicate for someone — would perform the qunut after bowing. And perhaps he said, when he said "Allah hears whoever praises Him, our Lord, and to You is the praise": "O Allah, deliver al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, and the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them as years like the years of Yusuf." He would say it aloud. And he used to say, in some of his prayers in the dawn prayer: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," concerning some tribes of the Arabs, until Allah revealed ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, the verse. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4560.]

al-Bukhari said: Qatadah... [Humayd and Thabit narrated from Anas ibn Malik: The Prophet (ﷺ) was wounded on the Day of Uhud, and he said: "How will a people prosper who wounded their prophet?" So this was revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾. He (al-Bukhari) suspended this hadith, and Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, has linked its isnad (chain of narration) ...]

Al-Bukhari said, regarding the Battle of Uhud: "Yahya ibn Abdullah al-Sulami narrated to us, ʿAbdullah narrated to us—[he said]: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ʿAbdullah narrated to me, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say—when he raised his head from bowing, in the last rak'ah of the Fajr prayer—: 'O Allah, curse So-and-so, and So-and-so, and So-and-so,' after he would say: 'Allah hears those who praise Him; our Lord, and to You belongs all praise.' Then Allah revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision [whether He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾ [up to His words: ﴿indeed they are wrongdoers﴾]."

And from Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan, who said: I heard Salim ibn ʿAbdullah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to invoke curses upon Safwan ibn Umayyah, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, and al-Harith ibn Hisham, so the verse was revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision [or He accepts their repentance or punishes them] [[in the other manuscripts: "up to His words"]] for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4069.]].

This addition was narrated by al-Bukhari in a suspended, mursal form, while it is connected (muttasil) in Musnad Ahmad, as mentioned above.

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) had his incisor broken on the day of Uhud, and his forehead was wounded until blood flowed over his face. He said: "How will a people prosper who did this to their Prophet, while he calls them to their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic?" Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision, whether He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾.

Muslim alone narrated it. He related it from al-Qa'nabi, from Hammad, from Thabit, from Anas, and mentioned it [[Al-Musnad (3/99) and Sahih Muslim, no. 1791.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Matar, from Qatadah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was struck on the day of Uhud, his incisor was broken and his brow was split, so he fell with two coats of mail on him while blood flowed. Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, passed by him, sat him up and wiped the blood from his face, and he regained consciousness saying: "How (can) a people who did this to their Prophet, while he calls them to Allah?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision [or He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾.

Similarly, ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, in similar wording, but he did not say: "he regained consciousness" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/197, 198) and Tafsir ʿAbd al-Razzaq (2/135).]].

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning: all of it is His dominion, and its inhabitants are servants before Him. ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾, meaning: He is the One who disposes (of affairs), so none can repel His judgment, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [[In A: "Nothing overcomes Him."]].

The mufassirun differed concerning this promise: was it on the Day of Badr or the Day of Uhud? There are two opinions:

The first: His saying ﴿When you said to the believers﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr﴾. This was narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, 'Amir al-Sha'bi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also chose this view.

'Abbad ibn Mansur narrated from al-Hasan regarding His saying ﴿When you said to the believers, "Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ that he said: "This is the Day of Badr." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said:

My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us from Dawud, from 'Amir (i.e., al-Sha'bi), that the Muslims were informed on the Day of Badr that Kurz ibn Jabir was reinforcing the polytheists, so that grieved them, and Allah revealed: ﴿Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?﴾ up to His saying ﴿marked﴾. He said: "Then news of the defeat reached Kurz, so he did not reinforce the polytheists, and Allah did not reinforce the Muslims with the five thousand."

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Allah reinforced the Muslims with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand."

If it is said: What is the reconciliation between this verse, according to this view, and His saying in the account of Badr: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand from the angels, following one another"﴾ [and Allah did not make it except as good tidings and so that your hearts may be assured thereby. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise] [al-Anfal 8:9–10]?

The answer: The specification of the thousand here does not contradict the three thousand or more beyond that, because of His saying ﴿following one another (murdifin)﴾, meaning that others follow them, and thousands of others like them follow them. This context is similar to this context in Surat Al 'Imran. The apparent meaning is that this occurred on the Day of Badr, as is well known, since the fighting of the angels was only on the Day of Badr, and Allah knows best. Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah: "Allah reinforced the believers on the Day of Badr with five thousand."

The second opinion: This promise is connected to His saying ﴿And when you left your family in the morning to position the believers at their stations for the battle﴾, and that was the Day of Uhud. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, Musa ibn 'Uqbah, and others. However, they said: the reinforcement with the five thousand did not occur, because the Muslims fled that day. 'Ikrimah added: nor with the three thousand, because of His saying ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾, and they were not patient, rather they fled, so they were not reinforced with a single angel.

* *

His saying ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾ means: if you are patient in confronting your enemy, and fear Me and obey My command.

* *

His saying ﴿and they come at you in this, their rage﴾ — al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: that is, from this direction of theirs. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Abu Salih said: that is, from this anger of theirs. al-Dahhak said: from their anger and their direction. al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: from this journey of theirs. It is also said: from this anger of theirs.

* *

His saying ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked﴾ means: distinguished by their markings (sima).

Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i narrated from Haritha ibn Mudarrib, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was white wool, and their marking was also on the forelocks of their horses."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Hadbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah regarding this verse ﴿marked﴾, he said: "With red wool."

Mujahid said: ﴿marked﴾ means: their manes were trimmed, and their forelocks were marked with white wool, on the tails of the horses.

al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The angels came to Muhammad (ﷺ) marked with wool, so Muhammad and his companions marked themselves and their horses by their markings with wool."

'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: ﴿marked﴾ means: with the marking of battle. Makhul said: ﴿marked﴾ means: with turbans.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from a hadith of 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Habib, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding His saying ﴿marked﴾: "Distinguished." And the marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was black turbans, and on the Day of Hunayn red turbans."

He also narrated from a hadith of Husayn ibn Mukhariq, from Sa'id, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The angels did not fight except on the Day of Badr."

Ibn Ishaq said: "Someone I do not suspect told me, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was white turbans which they let hang down their backs, and on the Day of Hunayn red turbans. The angels did not strike on any day other than the Day of Badr; on other days they were a number and a reinforcement, not striking."

Then he narrated it from al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, and mentioned something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Abbad: that al-Zubayr [ibn al-'Awwam] [addition from another manuscript], may Allah be pleased with him, had on him on the Day of Badr a yellow turban, wrapping it around himself, so the angels descended upon them with yellow turbans.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, and he mentioned it.

* *

His saying ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you, and so that your hearts may be assured by it﴾ means: Allah did not send down the angels and inform you of their descent except as good news for you, and a consolation for your hearts and a reassurance. Otherwise, ﴿victory is only from Allah﴾, who, if He willed, would have triumphed over His enemies without you, and without any need for your fighting them, as He said after commanding the believers to fight: ﴿That, and had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He ordered fighting] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah — never will He waste their deeds. He will guide them and amend their condition. And admit them to Paradise which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad 47:4–6]. Therefore He said here: ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you, and so that your hearts may be assured by it. And victory is not except from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾, meaning: He is the One of might that cannot be overcome, and of wisdom in His decree and its perfection.

Then He said: ﴿That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: He commanded you to strive and to fight, for He has wisdom in that in every case. Therefore He mentioned all the possible outcomes concerning the disbelievers and the fighters: He said ﴿that He may cut off a portion﴾, meaning: to destroy a group ﴿of those who disbelieved, or subdue them﴾, meaning: to humiliate them and turn them back in their rage, since they did not attain from you what they wanted. Therefore He said: ﴿or subdue them, so they turn back﴾, meaning: return ﴿defeated﴾, meaning: they did not obtain what they hoped for.

Then He inserted a sentence indicating that the judgment in this world and the Hereafter belongs to Him alone, with no partner, and He said: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, meaning: rather the whole matter is up to Me, as He said: ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:40], and He said ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:272], and He said ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas 28:56].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding His saying ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾: meaning, you have no part in the judgment concerning My servants except what I have commanded you regarding them.

Then He mentioned the rest of the outcomes, saying: ﴿or He turns to them in forgiveness﴾, meaning: from the disbelief they are in, and guides them after misguidance, ﴿or punishes them﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter, for their disbelief and their sins. Therefore He said: ﴿for indeed, they are wrongdoers﴾, meaning: they deserve that.

al-Bukhari said: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, 'Abd Allah informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, Salim narrated to me, from his father: that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, when he raised his head from bowing in the second rak'ah of the dawn prayer: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," after saying: "Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You is the praise." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed ﴿You have no part in the matter [or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Abu 'Aqil narrated to us — Ahmad said: he is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Aqil, a hadith transmitter of good standing and trustworthy — he said: 'Umar ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from Salim, from his father who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "O Allah, curse so-and-so. O Allah, curse al-Harith ibn Hisham. O Allah, curse Suhayl ibn 'Amr. O Allah, curse Safwan ibn Umayyah." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter, or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾, and so they were all forgiven. [al-Musnad, 2/93.]

Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah al-Ghallabi narrated to us, Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan narrated to us, from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate against four people. He said: So Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter [or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾ — and he said: "And Allah guided them to Islam." [al-Musnad, 2/104.]

Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan said, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate against men among the polytheists, naming them by their names, until Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, the verse.

al-Bukhari also said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whenever he wished to supplicate against someone — or to supplicate for someone — would perform the qunut after bowing. And perhaps he said, when he said "Allah hears whoever praises Him, our Lord, and to You is the praise": "O Allah, deliver al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, and the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them as years like the years of Yusuf." He would say it aloud. And he used to say, in some of his prayers in the dawn prayer: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," concerning some tribes of the Arabs, until Allah revealed ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, the verse. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4560.]

Therefore He mentioned all the possible outcomes concerning the disbelievers and the fighters: He said ﴿that He may cut off a portion﴾, meaning: to destroy a group ﴿of those who disbelieved, or subdue them﴾, meaning: to humiliate them and turn them back in their rage, since they did not attain from you what they wanted. Therefore He said: ﴿or subdue them, so they turn back﴾, meaning: return ﴿defeated﴾, meaning: they did not obtain what they hoped for.

Then He inserted a sentence indicating that the judgment in this world and the Hereafter belongs to Him alone, with no partner, and He said: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, meaning: rather the whole matter is up to Me, as He said: ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:40], and He said ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:272], and He said ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas 28:56].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding His saying ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾: meaning, you have no part in the judgment concerning My servants except what I have commanded you regarding them.

Then He mentioned the rest of the outcomes, saying: ﴿or He turns to them in forgiveness﴾, meaning: from the disbelief they are in, and guides them after misguidance, ﴿or punishes them﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter, for their disbelief and their sins. Therefore He said: ﴿for indeed, they are wrongdoers﴾, meaning: they deserve that.

al-Bukhari said: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, 'Abd Allah informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, Salim narrated to me, from his father: that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, when he raised his head from bowing in the second rak'ah of the dawn prayer: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," after saying: "Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You is the praise." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed ﴿You have no part in the matter [or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾.

This was also narrated by al-Nasa'i, from a hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and 'Abd al-Razzaq, both from Ma'mar, with it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4069, 4559, 7346; and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11075.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Abu 'Aqil narrated to us — Ahmad said: he is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Aqil, a hadith transmitter of good standing and trustworthy — he said: 'Umar ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from Salim, from his father who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "O Allah, curse so-and-so. O Allah, curse al-Harith ibn Hisham. O Allah, curse Suhayl ibn 'Amr. O Allah, curse Safwan ibn Umayyah." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter, or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾, and so they were all forgiven. [al-Musnad, 2/93.]

Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah al-Ghallabi narrated to us, Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan narrated to us, from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate against four people. He said: So Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter [or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾ — and he said: "And Allah guided them to Islam." [al-Musnad, 2/104.]

Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan said, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate against men among the polytheists, naming them by their names, until Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, the verse.

al-Bukhari also said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whenever he wished to supplicate against someone — or to supplicate for someone — would perform the qunut after bowing. And perhaps he said, when he said "Allah hears whoever praises Him, our Lord, and to You is the praise": "O Allah, deliver al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, and the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them as years like the years of Yusuf." He would say it aloud. And he used to say, in some of his prayers in the dawn prayer: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," concerning some tribes of the Arabs, until Allah revealed ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, the verse. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4560.]

al-Bukhari said: Qatadah... [Humayd and Thabit narrated from Anas ibn Malik: The Prophet (ﷺ) was wounded on the Day of Uhud, and he said: "How will a people prosper who wounded their prophet?" So this was revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾. He (al-Bukhari) suspended this hadith, and Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, has linked its isnad (chain of narration) ...]

Al-Bukhari said, regarding the Battle of Uhud: "Yahya ibn Abdullah al-Sulami narrated to us, ʿAbdullah narrated to us—[he said]: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ʿAbdullah narrated to me, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say—when he raised his head from bowing, in the last rak'ah of the Fajr prayer—: 'O Allah, curse So-and-so, and So-and-so, and So-and-so,' after he would say: 'Allah hears those who praise Him; our Lord, and to You belongs all praise.' Then Allah revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision [whether He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾ [up to His words: ﴿indeed they are wrongdoers﴾]."

And from Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan, who said: I heard Salim ibn ʿAbdullah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to invoke curses upon Safwan ibn Umayyah, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, and al-Harith ibn Hisham, so the verse was revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision [or He accepts their repentance or punishes them] [[in the other manuscripts: "up to His words"]] for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4069.]].

This addition was narrated by al-Bukhari in a suspended, mursal form, while it is connected (muttasil) in Musnad Ahmad, as mentioned above.

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) had his incisor broken on the day of Uhud, and his forehead was wounded until blood flowed over his face. He said: "How will a people prosper who did this to their Prophet, while he calls them to their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic?" Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision, whether He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾.

Muslim alone narrated it. He related it from al-Qa'nabi, from Hammad, from Thabit, from Anas, and mentioned it [[Al-Musnad (3/99) and Sahih Muslim, no. 1791.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Matar, from Qatadah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was struck on the day of Uhud, his incisor was broken and his brow was split, so he fell with two coats of mail on him while blood flowed. Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, passed by him, sat him up and wiped the blood from his face, and he regained consciousness saying: "How (can) a people who did this to their Prophet, while he calls them to Allah?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision [or He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾.

Similarly, ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, in similar wording, but he did not say: "he regained consciousness" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/197, 198) and Tafsir ʿAbd al-Razzaq (2/135).]].

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning: all of it is His dominion, and its inhabitants are servants before Him. ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾, meaning: He is the One who disposes (of affairs), so none can repel His judgment, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [[In A: "Nothing overcomes Him."]].

The mufassirun differed concerning this promise: was it on the Day of Badr or the Day of Uhud? There are two opinions:

The first: His saying ﴿When you said to the believers﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr﴾. This was narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, 'Amir al-Sha'bi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also chose this view.

'Abbad ibn Mansur narrated from al-Hasan regarding His saying ﴿When you said to the believers, "Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ that he said: "This is the Day of Badr." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said:

My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us from Dawud, from 'Amir (i.e., al-Sha'bi), that the Muslims were informed on the Day of Badr that Kurz ibn Jabir was reinforcing the polytheists, so that grieved them, and Allah revealed: ﴿Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?﴾ up to His saying ﴿marked﴾. He said: "Then news of the defeat reached Kurz, so he did not reinforce the polytheists, and Allah did not reinforce the Muslims with the five thousand."

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Allah reinforced the Muslims with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand."

If it is said: What is the reconciliation between this verse, according to this view, and His saying in the account of Badr: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand from the angels, following one another"﴾ [and Allah did not make it except as good tidings and so that your hearts may be assured thereby. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise] [al-Anfal 8:9–10]?

The answer: The specification of the thousand here does not contradict the three thousand or more beyond that, because of His saying ﴿following one another (murdifin)﴾, meaning that others follow them, and thousands of others like them follow them. This context is similar to this context in Surat Al 'Imran. The apparent meaning is that this occurred on the Day of Badr, as is well known, since the fighting of the angels was only on the Day of Badr, and Allah knows best. Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah: "Allah reinforced the believers on the Day of Badr with five thousand."

The second opinion: This promise is connected to His saying ﴿And when you left your family in the morning to position the believers at their stations for the battle﴾, and that was the Day of Uhud. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, Musa ibn 'Uqbah, and others. However, they said: the reinforcement with the five thousand did not occur, because the Muslims fled that day. 'Ikrimah added: nor with the three thousand, because of His saying ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾, and they were not patient, rather they fled, so they were not reinforced with a single angel.

* *

His saying ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾ means: if you are patient in confronting your enemy, and fear Me and obey My command.

* *

His saying ﴿and they come at you in this, their rage﴾ — al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: that is, from this direction of theirs. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Abu Salih said: that is, from this anger of theirs. al-Dahhak said: from their anger and their direction. al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: from this journey of theirs. It is also said: from this anger of theirs.

* *

His saying ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked﴾ means: distinguished by their markings (sima).

Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i narrated from Haritha ibn Mudarrib, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was white wool, and their marking was also on the forelocks of their horses."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Hadbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah regarding this verse ﴿marked﴾, he said: "With red wool."

Mujahid said: ﴿marked﴾ means: their manes were trimmed, and their forelocks were marked with white wool, on the tails of the horses.

al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The angels came to Muhammad (ﷺ) marked with wool, so Muhammad and his companions marked themselves and their horses by their markings with wool."

'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: ﴿marked﴾ means: with the marking of battle. Makhul said: ﴿marked﴾ means: with turbans.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from a hadith of 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Habib, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding His saying ﴿marked﴾: "Distinguished." And the marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was black turbans, and on the Day of Hunayn red turbans."

He also narrated from a hadith of Husayn ibn Mukhariq, from Sa'id, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The angels did not fight except on the Day of Badr."

Ibn Ishaq said: "Someone I do not suspect told me, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was white turbans which they let hang down their backs, and on the Day of Hunayn red turbans. The angels did not strike on any day other than the Day of Badr; on other days they were a number and a reinforcement, not striking."

Then he narrated it from al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, and mentioned something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Abbad: that al-Zubayr [ibn al-'Awwam] [addition from another manuscript], may Allah be pleased with him, had on him on the Day of Badr a yellow turban, wrapping it around himself, so the angels descended upon them with yellow turbans.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, and he mentioned it.

* *

His saying ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you, and so that your hearts may be assured by it﴾ means: Allah did not send down the angels and inform you of their descent except as good news for you, and a consolation for your hearts and a reassurance. Otherwise, ﴿victory is only from Allah﴾, who, if He willed, would have triumphed over His enemies without you, and without any need for your fighting them, as He said after commanding the believers to fight: ﴿That, and had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He ordered fighting] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah — never will He waste their deeds. He will guide them and amend their condition. And admit them to Paradise which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad 47:4–6]. Therefore He said here: ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you, and so that your hearts may be assured by it. And victory is not except from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾, meaning: He is the One of might that cannot be overcome, and of wisdom in His decree and its perfection.

Then He said: ﴿That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: He commanded you to strive and to fight, for He has wisdom in that in every case. Therefore He said: ﴿for indeed, they are wrongdoers﴾, meaning: they deserve that.

'Ikrimah added: nor with the three thousand, because of His saying ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾, and they were not patient, rather they fled, so they were not reinforced with a single angel.

* *

His saying ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾ means: if you are patient in confronting your enemy, and fear Me and obey My command.

* *

His saying ﴿and they come at you in this, their rage﴾ — al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' and al-Suddi said: that is, from this direction of theirs. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Abu Salih said: that is, from this anger of theirs. al-Dahhak said: from their anger and their direction. al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: from this journey of theirs. It is also said: from this anger of theirs.

* *

His saying ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked﴾ means: distinguished by their markings (sima).

Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i narrated from Haritha ibn Mudarrib, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was white wool, and their marking was also on the forelocks of their horses."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Hadbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah regarding this verse ﴿marked﴾, he said: "With red wool."

Mujahid said: ﴿marked﴾ means: their manes were trimmed, and their forelocks were marked with white wool, on the tails of the horses.

al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The angels came to Muhammad (ﷺ) marked with wool, so Muhammad and his companions marked themselves and their horses by their markings with wool."

'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: ﴿marked﴾ means: with the marking of battle. Makhul said: ﴿marked﴾ means: with turbans.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from a hadith of 'Abd al-Quddus ibn Habib, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding His saying ﴿marked﴾: "Distinguished." And the marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was black turbans, and on the Day of Hunayn red turbans."

He also narrated from a hadith of Husayn ibn Mukhariq, from Sa'id, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The angels did not fight except on the Day of Badr."

Ibn Ishaq said: "Someone I do not suspect told me, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The marking of the angels on the Day of Badr was white turbans which they let hang down their backs, and on the Day of Hunayn red turbans. The angels did not strike on any day other than the Day of Badr; on other days they were a number and a reinforcement, not striking."

Then he narrated it from al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, and mentioned something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Abbad: that al-Zubayr [ibn al-'Awwam] [addition from another manuscript], may Allah be pleased with him, had on him on the Day of Badr a yellow turban, wrapping it around himself, so the angels descended upon them with yellow turbans.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, and he mentioned it.

* *

His saying ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you, and so that your hearts may be assured by it﴾ means: Allah did not send down the angels and inform you of their descent except as good news for you, and a consolation for your hearts and a reassurance. Otherwise, ﴿victory is only from Allah﴾, who, if He willed, would have triumphed over His enemies without you, and without any need for your fighting them, as He said after commanding the believers to fight: ﴿That, and had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He ordered fighting] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah — never will He waste their deeds. He will guide them and amend their condition. And admit them to Paradise which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad 47:4–6]. Therefore He said here: ﴿And Allah did not make it except as good tidings for you, and so that your hearts may be assured by it. And victory is not except from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾, meaning: He is the One of might that cannot be overcome, and of wisdom in His decree and its perfection.

Then He said: ﴿That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: He commanded you to strive and to fight, for He has wisdom in that in every case. Therefore He mentioned all the possible outcomes concerning the disbelievers and the fighters: He said ﴿that He may cut off a portion﴾, meaning: to destroy a group ﴿of those who disbelieved, or subdue them﴾, meaning: to humiliate them and turn them back in their rage, since they did not attain from you what they wanted. Therefore He said: ﴿or subdue them, so they turn back﴾, meaning: return ﴿defeated﴾, meaning: they did not obtain what they hoped for.

Then He inserted a sentence indicating that the judgment in this world and the Hereafter belongs to Him alone, with no partner, and He said: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, meaning: rather the whole matter is up to Me, as He said: ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:40], and He said ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:272], and He said ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas 28:56].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding His saying ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾: meaning, you have no part in the judgment concerning My servants except what I have commanded you regarding them.

Then He mentioned the rest of the outcomes, saying: ﴿or He turns to them in forgiveness﴾, meaning: from the disbelief they are in, and guides them after misguidance, ﴿or punishes them﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter, for their disbelief and their sins. Therefore He said: ﴿for indeed, they are wrongdoers﴾, meaning: they deserve that.

al-Bukhari said: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, 'Abd Allah informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, Salim narrated to me, from his father: that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, when he raised his head from bowing in the second rak'ah of the dawn prayer: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," after saying: "Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You is the praise." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed ﴿You have no part in the matter [or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾.

This was also narrated by al-Nasa'i, from a hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and 'Abd al-Razzaq, both from Ma'mar, with it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4069, 4559, 7346; and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11075.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Abu 'Aqil narrated to us — Ahmad said: he is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Aqil, a hadith transmitter of good standing and trustworthy — he said: 'Umar ibn Hamzah narrated to us, from Salim, from his father who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "O Allah, curse so-and-so. O Allah, curse al-Harith ibn Hisham. O Allah, curse Suhayl ibn 'Amr. O Allah, curse Safwan ibn Umayyah." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter, or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾, and so they were all forgiven. [al-Musnad, 2/93.]

Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah al-Ghallabi narrated to us, Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan narrated to us, from Nafi', from 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate against four people. He said: So Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter [or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾ — and he said: "And Allah guided them to Islam." [al-Musnad, 2/104.]

Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan said, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate against men among the polytheists, naming them by their names, until Allah revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, the verse.

al-Bukhari also said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whenever he wished to supplicate against someone — or to supplicate for someone — would perform the qunut after bowing. And perhaps he said, when he said "Allah hears whoever praises Him, our Lord, and to You is the praise": "O Allah, deliver al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, and the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them as years like the years of Yusuf." He would say it aloud. And he used to say, in some of his prayers in the dawn prayer: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so," concerning some tribes of the Arabs, until Allah revealed ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾, the verse. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4560.]

al-Bukhari said: Qatadah... [Humayd and Thabit narrated from Anas ibn Malik: The Prophet (ﷺ) was wounded on the Day of Uhud, and he said: "How will a people prosper who wounded their prophet?" So this was revealed: ﴿You have no part in the matter﴾. He (al-Bukhari) suspended this hadith, and Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, has linked its isnad (chain of narration) ...]

Al-Bukhari said, regarding the Battle of Uhud: "Yahya ibn Abdullah al-Sulami narrated to us, ʿAbdullah narrated to us—[he said]: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ʿAbdullah narrated to me, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say—when he raised his head from bowing, in the last rak'ah of the Fajr prayer—: 'O Allah, curse So-and-so, and So-and-so, and So-and-so,' after he would say: 'Allah hears those who praise Him; our Lord, and to You belongs all praise.' Then Allah revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision [whether He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾ [up to His words: ﴿indeed they are wrongdoers﴾]."

And from Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan, who said: I heard Salim ibn ʿAbdullah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to invoke curses upon Safwan ibn Umayyah, Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, and al-Harith ibn Hisham, so the verse was revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision [or He accepts their repentance or punishes them] [[in the other manuscripts: "up to His words"]] for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4069.]].

This addition was narrated by al-Bukhari in a suspended, mursal form, while it is connected (muttasil) in Musnad Ahmad, as mentioned above.

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) had his incisor broken on the day of Uhud, and his forehead was wounded until blood flowed over his face. He said: "How will a people prosper who did this to their Prophet, while he calls them to their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic?" Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision, whether He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾.

Muslim alone narrated it. He related it from al-Qa'nabi, from Hammad, from Thabit, from Anas, and mentioned it [[Al-Musnad (3/99) and Sahih Muslim, no. 1791.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Matar, from Qatadah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was struck on the day of Uhud, his incisor was broken and his brow was split, so he fell with two coats of mail on him while blood flowed. Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, passed by him, sat him up and wiped the blood from his face, and he regained consciousness saying: "How (can) a people who did this to their Prophet, while he calls them to Allah?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿Not for you is any decision [or He accepts their repentance or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers]﴾.

Similarly, ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, in similar wording, but he did not say: "he regained consciousness" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/197, 198) and Tafsir ʿAbd al-Razzaq (2/135).]].

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning: all of it is His dominion, and its inhabitants are servants before Him. ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾, meaning: He is the One who disposes (of affairs), so none can repel His judgment, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ [[In A: "Nothing overcomes Him."]].

The mufassirun differed concerning this promise: was it on the Day of Badr or the Day of Uhud? There are two opinions:

The first: His saying ﴿When you said to the believers﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr﴾. This was narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, 'Amir al-Sha'bi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also chose this view.

'Abbad ibn Mansur narrated from al-Hasan regarding His saying ﴿When you said to the believers, "Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ that he said: "This is the Day of Badr." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, then said:

My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us from Dawud, from 'Amir (i.e., al-Sha'bi), that the Muslims were informed on the Day of Badr that Kurz ibn Jabir was reinforcing the polytheists, so that grieved them, and Allah revealed: ﴿Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?﴾ up to His saying ﴿marked﴾. He said: "Then news of the defeat reached Kurz, so he did not reinforce the polytheists, and Allah did not reinforce the Muslims with the five thousand."

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "Allah reinforced the Muslims with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand."

If it is said: What is the reconciliation between this verse, according to this view, and His saying in the account of Badr: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand from the angels, following one another"﴾ [and Allah did not make it except as good tidings and so that your hearts may be assured thereby. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise] [al-Anfal 8:9–10]?

The answer: The specification of the thousand here does not contradict the three thousand or more beyond that, because of His saying ﴿following one another (murdifin)﴾, meaning that others follow them, and thousands of others like them follow them. This context is similar to this context in Surat Al 'Imran. The apparent meaning is that this occurred on the Day of Badr, as is well known, since the fighting of the angels was only on the Day of Badr, and Allah knows best. Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah: "Allah reinforced the believers on the Day of Badr with five thousand."

The second opinion: This promise is connected to His saying ﴿And when you left your family in the morning to position the believers at their stations for the battle﴾, and that was the Day of Uhud. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, Musa ibn 'Uqbah, and others. However, they said: the reinforcement with the five thousand did not occur, because the Muslims fled that day. 'Ikrimah added: nor with the three thousand, because of His saying ﴿Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah﴾, and they were not patient, rather they fled, so they were not reinforced with a single angel.
