Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 130–136 (part 1 of 3):

He, exalted is He, says, forbidding His believing servants from engaging in *riba* (usury) and consuming it "multiplied manifold," as they used to say in the *Jahiliyyah* (the pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance) when the term of a debt fell due: "Either you pay, or you increase it." If he paid, well and good; otherwise he would extend the term and the other would increase the amount. This would happen every year, so a small sum would often multiply until it became a great multiplied amount.

Allah commanded His servants to have *taqwa* (God-consciousness), "so that you may prosper" in this world and the Hereafter. Then He warned them of the Fire and cautioned them against it, saying: ﴿And beware of the Fire, which has been prepared for the disbelievers. And obey Allah and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy﴾.

Then He urged them to hasten to good deeds and to race toward gaining nearness to Him, saying: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous﴾. That is, just as the Fire was prepared for the disbelievers. It has been said that the meaning of His words ﴿whose width is the heavens and the earth﴾ is to indicate the vastness of its length, as He said describing the lining of the Garden's couches: ﴿Its linings are of brocade﴾ [al-Rahman: 54], meaning: then what do you think of the outer surface? It has also been said: rather, its width is like its length, because it is a dome beneath the Throne, and a domed or circular thing has a width equal to its length. This is indicated by what is established in the Sahih (the authentic collection): "When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for al-Firdaws (the highest garden), for it is the highest and the middle of Paradise, the rivers of Paradise gush forth from it, and its ceiling is the Throne of the Most Merciful." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2790, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

This verse is like His words in Surah al-Hadid: ﴿Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth﴾ [no. 21].

It has been related to us in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad that Heraclius (Hiraql) wrote to the Prophet ﷺ: "You have invited me to a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth; then where is the Fire?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Subhan Allah! Then where is the night when the day comes?" [al-Musnad (3/442), from al-Tanukhi. Ibn Kathir said in al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah (5/15): "This is a strange hadith, related solely by Ahmad, and its isnad is acceptable."]

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) also related it, saying: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Muslim ibn Khalid informed me, from Abu Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid, from Ya'la ibn Murrah [in qaf: "Abi Murrah," which is an error], who said: I met al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Hims, an elderly man who had become senile. He said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with Heraclius's letter. He handed the scroll to a man on his left. I asked: Who is your companion who is reading? They said: Mu'awiyah. Then there was my companion's letter: "You wrote inviting me to a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous; then where is the Fire?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Subhan Allah! Then where is the night when the day comes?" [Tafsir al-Tabari (7/211, 212).]

Al-A'mash, Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'bah also related, from Qays ibn Muslim [in alif: "Salamah," an error], from Tariq ibn Shihab, that some Jews asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth: "Then where is the Fire?" Umar, may Allah be pleased with him [addition from alif], said: "Do you see, when the night comes, where is the day? And when the day comes, where is the night?" They said: "You have indeed drawn a similar answer from the Torah."

Ibn Jarir related it through the three chains. [In jim and ra: "chains."] [Tafsir al-Tabari (7/211, 212).] Then he said: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Abu Nu'aym told us, Ja'far ibn Burqan told us, Yazid ibn al-Asamm informed us: that a man from the People of the Book said: They say ﴿a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth﴾, then where is the Fire? Ibn Abbas said: "Where does the night go when the day comes, and where does the day go when the night comes?" [In jim, ra, alif, waw: "Ibn Abbas said: Do you see, when the night comes, where the day is, and when the day comes, where the night is."]

This has also been related with a *marfu'* (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) chain. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar told us, al-Mughirah ibn Salamah Abu Hisham told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Asamm, from his paternal uncle Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Do you see the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth﴾? Then where is the Fire?" He said: "Do you see the night when it comes and covers everything, then where is the day?" He said: "Wherever Allah wills." He said: "And likewise the Fire is wherever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills." [In alif: "So" instead of "And likewise"; in waw: "Then likewise."] [Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (1/36) through Muhammad ibn Ma'mar from al-Mughirah with the same wording, and said: "It meets the conditions of both (Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it, and I know of no defect in it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]

This may have two meanings:

The first: that the meaning is that our not witnessing the night when the day comes does not necessitate that it has no place, even though we do not know where it is. Likewise the Fire is wherever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills. This is the more apparent meaning, as already mentioned in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah from al-Bazzar. [In alif: "Then this" and "from" instead of "on."]

The second: that the meaning is that when the day covers the face of the world from one side, the night is on the other side. Likewise the Garden is in the highest 'Illiyyin, above the heavens, beneath the Throne, and its width is as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿like the width of the heaven and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 21], while the Fire is in the lowest of the low. There is therefore no contradiction between its being like the width of the heavens and the earth and the existence of the Fire. And Allah knows best.

Then He mentioned the description of the people of Paradise, saying: ﴿Who spend in ease and in hardship﴾, that is, in hardship and ease, in what is pleasant and what is disliked, in health and in sickness, and in all circumstances, as He said: ﴿Who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly﴾ [al-Baqarah: 274]. The meaning is that nothing preoccupies them from obeying Allah, exalted is He, and spending in what pleases Him, and doing good to His creation, including their relatives and others, with all kinds of righteousness.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And those who restrain anger and pardon the people﴾, that is, when anger rises in them they suppress it, meaning they conceal it and do not act upon it, and they pardon, despite that, the one who wronged them. It has been mentioned in some reports: "Allah, exalted is He, says: O son of Adam, remember Me when you are angry, and I will remember you when I am angry, and I will not destroy you among those I destroy." [Ibn Abi Hatim related it; I have not found it in his Tafsir.]

Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Zamin told us, Isa ibn Shu'ayb al-Darir Abu'l-Fadl told us, al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Juyzi [in alif and waw: "al-Numayri," which is an error; the correct form is what we have written, from al-Jarh wa'l-Ta'dil 3/464] told me, from Abu Amr ibn Anas ibn Malik, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever restrains his anger, Allah will restrain His punishment from him; whoever guards his tongue, Allah will conceal his faults; and whoever seeks Allah's pardon, He will accept his excuse." [In waw: "wa" added from alif and waw.] This is a strange hadith, and its isnad is questionable. [Related by al-Khara'iti in Masawi' al-Akhlaq (329) and Ibn Abi Asim in al-Zuhd (47) through al-Rabi' from Abu Amr, mawla of Anas, from Anas. In al-Khara'iti it appears as "al-Rabi' ibn Muslim," perhaps a scribal error. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/298): "It contains al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Azdi, who is weak." The hadith has another route from Anas, related by al-Fadl ibn al-'Ala from Sufyan from Humayd from Anas, which al-Diya' al-Maqdisi recorded in al-Mukhtarah (2066, 2067) and said: "Al-Fadl is mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim without any criticism of him." I say: Ibn Abi Hatim related from his father (7/65): "A shaykh whose hadith is written down," and Ibn Ma'in and Ibn al-Madini declared him trustworthy.]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Malik told us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The strong man is not the one who overpowers others, but the strong man is the one who controls himself at the time of anger." Al-Shaykhan (Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it from the hadith of Malik. [al-Musnad (2/236); Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6114; Sahih Muslim no. 2609.]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, al-A'mash told us, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Abd Allah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Which of you values his heir's wealth more than his own wealth?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, none of us, but each values his own wealth more than his heir's wealth." He said: "Know that none of you values his heir's wealth more than his own wealth. Your wealth is only what you have sent forward, and your heir's wealth is what you have left behind." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said: "What do you count as a *sur'ah* (one who is overpowering) among you?" We said: "The one whom men cannot overpower." He said: "No, but the one who controls himself at the time of anger." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What do you count as a *raqub* (one who has lost children) among you?" We said: "The one who has no child." He said: "No, but the *raqub* is the one who has not sent forward any of his children [in jim and ra: 'not' instead of 'no']."

Al-Bukhari recorded the first part of it, and Muslim recorded the original of this hadith from the narration of al-Al-A'mash. [al-Musnad (1/382); Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6442.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, Shu'bah told us, I heard Urwah ibn Abd Allah al-Ja'fi narrating from Abu Hasbah, or Ibn Hasbah, from a man who witnessed the Prophet ﷺ delivering a sermon, who said: "Do you know what the *raqub* is?" They said: "The one who has no child." He said: "The *raqub* is the one who has lost many, who had a child but it died, and he sent none of them forward." He said: "Do you know what the *su'luk* (pauper) is?" They said: "The one who has no wealth." The Prophet ﷺ said: "The *su'luk* is the one who has wealth, but dies and sends none of it forward." He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "What is the *sur'ah*?" They said: "The one who is overpowered." He said: So the Prophet ﷺ said: "The *sur'ah* is the one who is entirely *sur'ah*, who becomes angry, his anger intensifies, his face reddens, his hair stands on end, and he overpowers his anger." [al-Musnad (5/367). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/69): "It contains Abu Hasbah or Ibn 'Usbah, whom I do not know, but the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hisham, that is Ibn Urwah, told us, from his father, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from a paternal uncle of his called Jariyah ibn Qudamah al-Sa'di, that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me a saying that will benefit me, and keep it brief, so that I may understand it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not become angry." He repeated the request several times, and each time he said: "Do not become angry."

It was also related in the same way from Abu Mu'awiyah, from Hisham. [Also] it was related from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Hisham, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me a saying and keep it brief, so that I may comprehend it." He said: "Do not become angry."

This hadith is related solely by Ahmad. [al-Musnad (5/34). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/69): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, from a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "Do not become angry." The man said: "I reflected on what the Prophet ﷺ had said, and I found that anger gathers all evil." [In jim, ra, alif, waw: "the Prophet said" instead of "he said."]

This is related solely by Ahmad. [al-Musnad (5/373). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/69): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ibn Abi Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abu al-Aswad, from Abu Dharr, who said: He was watering on a pool of his. A group of people came and said: "Which of you will bring (his animals) to Abu Dharr's pool and seek reward for some hairs from his head?" A man said: "I will." So the man came and brought (his animals) to the pool and broke it. Abu Dharr had been standing, so he sat down, then lay down. He was asked: "O Abu Dharr, why did you sit and then lie down?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: "If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit; if the anger leaves him, well and good, otherwise let him lie down."

Abu Dawud related it, from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, with its isnad, except that in his narration it occurred as: "from Abu Harb, from Abu Dharr." The correct reading is: Ibn Abi Harb, from his father, from Abu Dharr, as narrated by Abdullah ibn Ahmad from his father. (Al-Musnad 5/152 and Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. 4782, 4783.)

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Khalid narrated to us: Abu Wa'il al-San'ani narrated to us, saying: We were sitting with Urwah ibn Muhammad when a man entered upon him and said something that angered him. When he became angry, he got up, then returned to us having performed ablution, and said: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather Atiyyah, who is Ibn Sa'd al-Sa'di, and he had companionship (with the Prophet): He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed anger is from Satan, and Satan was created from fire, and fire is only extinguished by water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution."

Abu Dawud related it in the same way from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Khalid al-San'ani, from Abu Wa'il al-Qass al-Muradi al-San'ani. Abu Dawud said: I think he is Abdullah ibn Bahir. (Al-Musnad 4/226 and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4784.)

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us: Nuh ibn Ja'wanah al-Sulami narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever grants respite to one in difficulty or remits (his debt), Allah will protect him from the heat of Hell. Verily, the work of Paradise is hard and uphill (lit. a hill), (he said this three times). Verily, the work of the Fire is easy and smooth. The one who is happy is he who is protected from trials. There is no sip more beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than a sip of anger that a servant swallows; no servant swallows it for the sake of Allah except that Allah fills his inner being with faith."

Ahmad alone narrated it. Its isnad is good (hasan), with no impugned narrator in it, and its text is good. (Al-Musnad 1/327.)

Another hadith with the same meaning: Abu Dawud said: 'Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman, that is Ibn Mahdi, narrated to us, from Bishr, that is Ibn Mansur, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Suwayd ibn Wahb, from a man from among the sons of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever restrains anger while he is able to act upon it, Allah will fill him with security and faith. Whoever leaves off wearing a beautiful garment while he is able to wear it (Bishr said: I think he said: 'out of humility'), Allah will clothe him with the robe of honour. And whoever marries for the sake of Allah, Allah will crown him with the crown of sovereignty." (Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4778.)

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us: Abu Marhum narrated to me, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever restrains anger while he is able to act upon it, Allah will call him before the heads of all creation until He gives him the choice of whichever of the Houris he wishes."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also related it from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, with the same wording. al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib. (Al-Musnad 3/440; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4777; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, nos. 2021, 2493; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4186.)

Another hadith: 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Dawud ibn Qays informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from a man from the people of Syria, called 'Abd al-Jalil, from a paternal uncle of his, from Abu Hurayrah, regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who restrain anger﴾, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever restrains anger while he is able to act upon it, Allah will fill him with security and faith." Ibn Jarir related it. (Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq 1/136; Tafsir al-Tabari 7/216. Al-Bukhari related it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir 5/123 and said: "'Abd al-Jalil is not followed in this.")

Another hadith: Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib informed us, 'Ali ibn 'Asim informed us, Yunus ibn 'Ubayd informed me, from al-Hasan, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No servant has swallowed a sip better in reward than a sip of anger that he restrains seeking the Face of Allah."

Likewise Ibn Majah related it from Bishr ibn 'Umar, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, with the same wording. (Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4189; Ahmad in his Musnad 2/128 from the route of 'Ali ibn 'Asim from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, with the same wording.)

So His saying: ﴿And those who restrain anger﴾ means: they do not act upon their anger against people, but rather they withhold their evil from them and seek that reward from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then He said: ﴿And those who pardon people﴾, meaning: along with withholding evil, they pardon those who wrong them personally, so no resentment toward anyone remains in their souls. This is the most perfect of states, and for this reason He said: ﴿And Allah loves the doers of good﴾. So this is among the stations of ihsan (excellence in faith and conduct).

It is also in a hadith: "Three things I swear by: wealth is not diminished by charity; Allah does not increase a servant in anything through pardon except in honour; and whoever is humble for the sake of Allah, Allah will raise him." (Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 2325, from the hadith of Abu Kabshah al-Anmari.)

al-Hakim related in his al-Mustadrak, from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah al-Qurashi, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever would be pleased that buildings be raised high for him and that his ranks be elevated, let him pardon the one who wronged him, give to the one who denied him, and maintain ties with the one who severed them."

Then he said: "Sahih according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." (Al-Mustadrak 2/295. al-Dhahabi criticized it, saying: "In it is Abu Umayyah ibn Ya'la, whom al-Daraqutni declared weak, and Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah from 'Ubadah from Ubayy, and Ishaq did not meet 'Ubadah." al-Tabarani related it in al-Kabir 1/167 from the route of Abu Umayyah ibn Ya'la from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, with the same wording.)

Ibn Mardawayh also related similar wording from the hadiths of 'Ali, Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, Abu Hurayrah and Umm Salamah.

It is also related through al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: 'Where are those who pardon people? Come to your Lord and take your rewards!' And it becomes binding upon every Muslim man who pardons that he will enter Paradise."

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾, meaning: when a sin proceeds from them, they follow it with repentance and seeking forgiveness.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A man committed a sin and said: 'My Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'My servant has committed a sin, and he knows that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes account for it. I have forgiven My servant.' Then he committed another sin and said: 'My Lord, I have committed another sin, so forgive it.' He, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes account for it. I have forgiven My servant.' Then he committed another sin and said: 'My Lord, I have committed another sin, so forgive it.' He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives sin and takes account for it. I call you to witness that I have forgiven My servant. Let him do whatever he wishes.'"

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs, from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, with similar wording. (Al-Musnad 2/296; Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5707; Sahih Muslim, no. 2758, from the route of Ishaq ibn Abdullah.)

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr and Abu 'Amir narrated to us, both saying: Zuhayr narrated to us: Sa'd al-Ta'i narrated to us: Abu al-Mudillah, the freedman of the Mother of the Believers, narrated to us, having heard Abu Hurayrah, who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we see you our hearts soften, and we become people of the Hereafter. But when we part from you, the world pleases us, and we become attracted to women and children." He said: "If you were always in the state you are in with me, the angels would shake hands with you and visit you in your homes. And if you did not sin, Allah would bring a people who sin, so that He might forgive them." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us about Paradise, what is its construction?" He said: "A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is the strongest musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will enjoy bliss and will not despair, will live forever and will not die, his garments will not wear out and his youth will not fade. Three whose supplication is not rejected: the just ruler, the one fasting until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the oppressed, which is carried upon the clouds, the gates of heaven are opened for it, and the Lord says: 'By My might, I will surely help you, even if after a time.'"

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related it from another route, from Sa'd, with the same wording. (Al-Musnad 2/304, 305; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3598; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1752.)

Ablution and performing two rak'ahs (units of prayer) are especially recommended at the time of repentance, based on what Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal related:

Waki' narrated to us, Mis'ar narrated to us, and Sufyan, that is al-Thawri, from 'Uthman ibn al-Mughirah al-Thaqafi, from 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah, from Asma' ibn al-Hakam al-Fazari, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah benefited me from it as He willed. And when someone else narrated it to me, I made him swear an oath, and when he swore to me, I believed him. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me, and Abu Bakr spoke the truth, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No man commits a sin, then performs ablution and does it well" (Mis'ar said: "then prays"; and Sufyan said: "then prays two rak'ahs") "then seeks forgiveness from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that He forgives him."

Thus it was narrated by Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Humaydi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, the authors of the Sunan (collections of hadith), Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar, and al-Daraqutni, through several chains, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, with it. At-Tirmidhi said: "It is a hasan hadith (a good hadith)."[^1] We have mentioned its chains and the discussion of it at length in the Musnad (a collection arranged by companion) of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.[^2] In sum, it is a hasan hadith, and it is narrated by the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Caliph of the Prophet, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them both.[^3]

Among what supports the authenticity of this hadith is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the Commander of the Faithful Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "None of you performs wudu' (ablution) and completes (or: perfects) the wudu', then says: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' except that the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he enters by whichever of them he wishes."[^4]

And in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from the Commander of the Faithful Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, that he performed wudu' for them in the manner of the wudu' of the Prophet (ﷺ), then said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever performs wudu' like this wudu' of mine, then prays two rak'ahs (units of prayer) without speaking to himself during them, his previous sins will be forgiven."[^5]

Thus this hadith has been established through the narration of the four rightly-guided Caliphs, from the master of the first and the last and the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, as the Clear Book indicates, that seeking forgiveness for a sin benefits the sinners.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman informed us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "It reached me that Iblis, when the verse was revealed: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ and so on, wept."[^6]

Al-Hafiz Abu Yala said: Muhriz ibn Awn narrated to us, Uthman ibn Matar narrated to us, Abd al-Ghafur narrated to us, from Abu Nudrah, from Abu Raja', from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Hold fast to 'There is no god but Allah' and seeking forgiveness, so increase in both of them, for Iblis said: 'I destroyed the people with sins, and they destroyed me with 'There is no god but Allah' and seeking forgiveness. When I saw that, I destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.'"

Uthman ibn Matar and his shaykh are both weak.[^7]

Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, through the route of Amr ibn Abi Amr and Abu al-Haytham al-Utwari, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Iblis said: 'O Lord, by Your might, I will not cease to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies.' Allah said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness.'"[^8]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Umar ibn Abi Khalifah narrated to us, I heard Abu Badr narrate from Thabit, from Anas, who said: A man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have committed a sin," and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you commit a sin, seek forgiveness from your Lord." He said: "Indeed I seek forgiveness, then I return and commit (it again)." He said: "When you commit (it), then return and seek forgiveness from your Lord." He said it a fourth time, and he said: "Seek forgiveness from your Lord until Satan is the one who is exhausted."[^9]

This is a gharib hadith (a hadith narrated through a single or unusual chain) from this route.[^10]

* *

His saying: ﴿And who forgives sins except Allah﴾ means: none forgives them but Him, as Imam Ahmad said:

Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, Sallam ibn Miskin and al-Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from al-Aswad ibn Sari': that the Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a captive, and he said: "O Allah, I repent to You, and I do not repent to Muhammad." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He recognized the truth for its people."[^11]

* *

His saying: ﴿And they do not persist in what they have done while they know﴾ means: they repented from their sins and returned to Allah promptly, and they did not continue in disobedience and persist in it without giving it up. And if the sin was repeated from them, they repented from it, as al-Hafiz Abu Yala al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Musnad:

Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il and others narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, from Uthman ibn Waqid, from Abu Nudayrah, from a mawla (freed slave or client) of Abu Bakr, from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One who seeks forgiveness does not persist in sin, even if he returns to it seventy times in a day."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Bazzar in his Musnad also narrated it, from the hadith of Uthman ibn Waqid, whom Yahya ibn Ma'in declared trustworthy, with it. His shaykh Abu Nudayrah (in one copy: "Abu Basirah"; in another: "Abu Nasr") al-Wasiti, whose name is Muslim ibn Ubayd, was declared trustworthy by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. But the saying of Ali ibn al-Madini and al-Tirmidhi: "The isnad of this hadith is not strong," the apparent reason is the unknown identity of the mawla of Abu Bakr. However, the anonymity of one like him does no harm, because he is a senior Tabi'i (Successor), and his attribution to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq suffices for him. So it is a hasan hadith. And Allah knows best.[^12]

* *

His saying: ﴿while they know﴾. Mujahid and Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr said: ﴿while they know﴾ that whoever repents, Allah accepts his repentance.

This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants?﴾ [At-Tawbah: 104], and like His saying: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa': 110]. Similar examples of this are very numerous.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid informed us, Jarir narrated to us, Hibban, that is Ibn Zayd al-Shar'abi, narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said while on the minbar (pulpit): "Show mercy and you will be shown mercy, forgive and you will be forgiven. Woe to the crumbs of speech! Woe to those who persist, who persist in what they have done while they know."

Ahmad alone narrated it.[^13]

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, after describing them with what He described them with: ﴿Those – their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens﴾, meaning: their reward for these qualities is forgiveness from Allah and gardens ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning: of various kinds of drinks, ﴿wherein they will abide eternally﴾, meaning: remaining in them forever, ﴿And excellent is the reward of the workers﴾. The Exalted praises Paradise.

Ibn Kathir said, addressing His believing servants who were struck on the day of Uhud, when seventy of them were killed:

﴿Indeed, there have passed before you precedents (sunan)﴾. That is: something similar has already befallen the nations before you, the followers of the prophets. Then the final outcome was theirs, and the reversal of fortune was against the disbelievers. For this reason He said: ﴿So travel through the earth and observe what was the end of those who denied﴾.

Then He said: ﴿This is a clarification for mankind﴾, meaning the Qur'an contains a clear explanation of matters and of how the earlier nations fared with their enemies, ﴿and guidance and instruction﴾, meaning the Qur'an contains news of what came before you, ﴿guidance﴾ for your hearts, and ﴿instruction﴾, that is, a restraint from the prohibited things and sins.

Then, consoling the believers, He said: ﴿And do not weaken, nor grieve, for you will have the upper hand if you are believers﴾.

That is: the final outcome and victory are yours, O believers.

﴿If a wound has touched you, a wound has certainly touched the other people as well﴾. That is: if you have been struck with wounds and a group of you has been killed, then your enemies have likewise suffered something similar of killing and wounding. ﴿And those days We alternate among the people﴾, meaning We grant the enemies dominance over you at times, even though the final outcome is yours, because of the wisdoms We have in that. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "In such a case, that We may see" — that is, who will be patient in confronting the enemies. ﴿And that He may take from among you martyrs﴾, meaning they are killed in His cause and sacrifice their lives seeking His pleasure. ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers. And that Allah may purify those who believe﴾, that is, He expiates their sins if they have any; otherwise their ranks are raised according to what they were afflicted with. His saying ﴿and destroy the disbelievers﴾ means that when they are victorious they transgress and become arrogant, and that becomes the cause of their ruin, destruction, annihilation and extinction.

Then He said: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strove and made evident those who are patient?﴾ That is: did you suppose that you would enter Paradise without being tested by fighting and hardships, as Allah the Exalted said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while the example of those who passed away before you has not reached you? They were touched by misfortune and hardship and were shaken [until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near]﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:214]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We have believed," and they will not be tested? [And We did certainly test those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars]﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:1–3]. For this reason He said here: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strove and made evident those who are patient?﴾ That is: entering Paradise will not be attained by you until you are tested and Allah sees among you those who strive in His cause and those who are patient in confronting the enemies.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you encountered it. And now you have seen it while you were looking on﴾. That is: before this day, O believers, you used to wish to meet the enemy, burning for them and desiring to confront and endure them. Now there has come to you what you wished for and sought, so fight and endure.

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. But when you do meet them, be patient, and know that Paradise is under the shade of the swords." [Sahih al-Bukhari, mu'allaq, no. 3021; Sahih Muslim, no. 1741.]

For this reason He said: ﴿Then you have seen it﴾, meaning you witnessed death in the glitter of swords, the edges of spear-points, the interlacing of lances, and the rows of men arrayed for battle.

The theologians (al-mutakallimun) express this by takhyil (imaginative representation), which is the witnessing of what is not perceptible as though it were perceptible, just as a sheep imagines the friendship of the ram and the enmity of the wolf.

And that Allah may purify those who believe﴾, that is, He expiates their sins if they have any; otherwise their ranks are raised according to what they were afflicted with. His saying ﴿and destroy the disbelievers﴾ means that when they are victorious they transgress and become arrogant, and that becomes the cause of their ruin, destruction, annihilation and extinction.

Then He said: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strove and made evident those who are patient?﴾ That is: did you suppose that you would enter Paradise without being tested by fighting and hardships, as Allah the Exalted said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while the example of those who passed away before you has not reached you? They were touched by misfortune and hardship and were shaken [until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near]﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:214]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We have believed," and they will not be tested? [And We did certainly test those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars]﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:1–3]. For this reason He said here: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strove and made evident those who are patient?﴾ That is: entering Paradise will not be attained by you until you are tested and Allah sees among you those who strive in His cause and those who are patient in confronting the enemies.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you encountered it. And now you have seen it while you were looking on﴾. That is: before this day, O believers, you used to wish to meet the enemy, burning for them and desiring to confront and endure them. Now there has come to you what you wished for and sought, so fight and endure.

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. But when you do meet them, be patient, and know that Paradise is under the shade of the swords." [Sahih al-Bukhari, mu'allaq, no. 3021; Sahih Muslim, no. 1741.]

For this reason He said: ﴿Then you have seen it﴾, meaning you witnessed death in the glitter of swords, the edges of spear-points, the interlacing of lances, and the rows of men arrayed for battle.

The theologians (al-mutakallimun) express this by takhyil (imaginative representation), which is the witnessing of what is not perceptible as though it were perceptible, just as a sheep imagines the friendship of the ram and the enmity of the wolf.

When the Muslims who fled did flee on the Day of Uhud, and some of them were killed, Satan called out: "Surely Muhammad has been killed!" Ibn Qami'ah returned to the polytheists and said to them: "I have killed Muhammad." In fact, he had struck the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and wounded him on the head. This news fell into the hearts of many people, and they believed that the Messenger of Allah had been killed. They considered that this was possible for him, just as Allah has related about many of the Prophets, peace be upon them. Weakness and feebleness set in, and they held back from fighting. Concerning this, Allah [Mighty and Majestic] [[Addition from manuscript w.]] revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; the messengers have passed away before him.﴾ That is, he has an example among them in the prophethood and in the possibility of being killed.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from his father that a man from the Muhajirun passed by a man from the Ansar who was writhing in his blood. He said to him: "O so-and-so, did you know that Muhammad (ﷺ) has been killed?" The Ansari replied: "If Muhammad [(ﷺ)] [[Addition from manuscript r.]] has been killed, he has indeed conveyed the message. So fight for your religion." Then this was revealed: ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; the messengers have passed away before him.﴾ Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr [[Addition from manuscript w.]] al-Bayhaqi related it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah [[(2/248) through the route of Adam ibn Abi Iyas from Warqa' from Ibn Abi Najih, with the same chain.]].

Then Allah, Exalted, said, rebuking those who had become weak: ﴿So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ That is, will you retreat backwards? ﴿And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all; and Allah will reward the grateful.﴾ That is, those who obeyed Him, fought for His religion, and followed His Messenger, whether he was alive or dead.

It is likewise established in the Sahih (authentic) collections, the Masanid (hadith collections arranged by narrator), the Sunan and other books of Islam, through numerous routes that yield certainty. I have mentioned this in my Musnad of the two Shaykhs, Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both: that al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) recited this verse when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died. [[See: al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (5/213) and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (7/215-217).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Salamah informed me that 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, informed him that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came riding a horse from his dwelling in al-Sunh [[In manuscript r: "al-Sayh", which is an error; the vocalized form is from al-Bukhari (4452, 4453), and it is the correct one.]] until he dismounted, entered the mosque, and did not speak to the people until he entered upon 'A'ishah. He went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was covered with a striped Yemeni cloth. He uncovered his face [(ﷺ)] [[Addition from manuscript j.]], then bent over him, kissed him, and wept. Then he said: "May my father and mother be your ransom! By Allah, Allah will never make you taste two deaths. As for the death that was decreed for you, you have indeed died it."

Al-Zuhri said: Abu Salamah narrated to me from Ibn 'Abbas that Abu Bakr went out while Umar was speaking to the people. He said: "Sit down, O Umar," but Umar refused to sit. The people came to him and left Umar. Abu Bakr said: "Amma ba'du (to proceed). Whoever worshipped Muhammad, then Muhammad has died; and whoever worshipped Allah, then Allah is Living and never dies." Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; the messengers have passed away before him,﴾ up to His words: ﴿And Allah will reward the grateful.﴾ He said: "By Allah, it was as if the people had not known that Allah had revealed this verse until Abu Bakr recited it. The people took it from him, all of them, and no person among the people heard it without reciting it."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib informed me that Umar said: "By Allah, it was only that I heard Abu Bakr recite it that I was stunned, until my legs could not carry me, and until I fell to the ground." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, numbers (4452, 4453, 4454).]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah al-Qannad narrated to us, Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that 'Ali used to say during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah: ﴿So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ "By Allah, we will not turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us. And by Allah, if he dies or is killed, I will fight for what he fought for until I die. By Allah, I am his brother, his close friend, his cousin, and his heir; so who has more right to him than I?" [[Also related by Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir (2/581) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3/126) through the route of 'Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/134): "Its men are the men of the Sahih."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿No soul can die except by the permission of Allah, at a decreed term.﴾ That is: no one dies except by the decree of Allah, and only when he has completed the term that Allah has set for him. This verse contains encouragement for the cowardly and an incitement to them to fight, for advancing and holding back do not decrease one's lifespan nor increase it, as Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Al-'Abbas ibn Yazid al-'Abdi narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Suhban, who said: A man from the Muslims [[In manuscript j: "for the Muslims."]] — he was Hujr ibn 'Adi — said: "What prevents you from crossing to these enemies over this river?" — meaning the Tigris — ﴿and no soul can die except by the permission of Allah, at a decreed term.﴾ Then he drove his horse into the Tigris. When he drove it in, the people drove in after him. When the enemy saw them, they said: "Demons!" and they fled. [[In manuscript j: "and they fled."]] [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/584).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him of it; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him of it.﴾ That is: whoever's deed is for this world, he attains from it what Allah has decreed for him, and he will have no share in the Hereafter. Whoever intends by his deed the Hereafter, Allah gives him from it, along with what He has apportioned to him in this world. As He said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him from it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Shura: 20]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish. Then We have appointed for him Hell, which he will enter, blameworthy and rejected. So Allah rebuked them for their flight and their abandoning of the fighting, and said to them: ﴿So if he dies or is killed,﴾ O believers, will you apostatize from your religion and turn back on your heels?

The speech of Ibn Ishaq in the Sirah suggests another view. He said: That is, how many a prophet was struck by death, and with him were ribbiyyun, that is, groups; yet they did not weaken after their prophet, nor did they become feeble before their enemy, nor did they submit to what befell them in striving in the cause of Allah and of their religion. That is the patience, ﴿and Allah loves the patient.﴾

So he made His saying ﴿with him many devoted followers﴾ a circumstantial phrase [hal]. al-Suhayli supported this view and exaggerated in it, and it has a justification in His saying: ﴿so they did not weaken for what befell them﴾, and al-Umawi related it likewise in his Maghazi from the book of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, and no one else related it.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' and 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: al-ribbiyyun are the large multitudes.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿ribbiyyun kathir﴾ means: many scholars. And from him also: scholars who are patient, righteous, and pious.

Ibn Jarir related from some grammarians of Basra that the ribbiyyun are those who worship the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He said: Some of them responded to him, saying: "If it were so, it would be said rabbiyyun, with a fatha on the ra'."

Ibn Zayd said: "The ribbiyyun are the followers and the subjects, and the rabbaniyyun are the rulers."

﴿So they did not weaken for what befell them in the way of Allah, nor were they feeble, nor did they submit.﴾ Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿nor were they feeble﴾ by the killing of their Prophet; ﴿nor did they submit﴾ means: they did not apostatize from their support nor from their religion; rather they fought for what the Prophet of Allah had fought for, until they joined Allah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿nor did they submit﴾ means they humbled themselves. al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: they did not abase themselves before their enemy.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: that is, this befell them when their Prophet was killed.

﴿And Allah loves the patient. And their saying was only that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people."﴾ That is: their only practice was that.

﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world﴾ — that is, victory, triumph, and a good outcome — ﴿and the good reward of the Hereafter.﴾ That is: He combined those for them along with this. ﴿And Allah loves the doers of good.﴾

The people took it from him, all of them, and no person among the people heard it without reciting it."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib informed me that Umar said: "By Allah, it was only that I heard Abu Bakr recite it that I was stunned, until my legs could not carry me, and until I fell to the ground." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, numbers (4452, 4453, 4454).]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah al-Qannad narrated to us, Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that 'Ali used to say during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah: ﴿So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ "By Allah, we will not turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us. And by Allah, if he dies or is killed, I will fight for what he fought for until I die. By Allah, I am his brother, his close friend, his cousin, and his heir; so who has more right to him than I?" [[Also related by Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir (2/581) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3/126) through the route of 'Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/134): "Its men are the men of the Sahih."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿No soul can die except by the permission of Allah, at a decreed term.﴾ That is: no one dies except by the decree of Allah, and only when he has completed the term that Allah has set for him. For this reason He said: ﴿at a decreed term,﴾ like His saying: ﴿And no one is granted a long life, nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is in a Book﴾ [Fatir: 11], and like His saying: ﴿It is He who created you from clay, then decreed a term; and there is a specified term with Him﴾ [al-An'am: 2].

This verse contains encouragement for the cowardly and an incitement to them to fight, for advancing and holding back do not decrease one's lifespan nor increase it, as Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Al-'Abbas ibn Yazid al-'Abdi narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Suhban, who said: A man from the Muslims [[In manuscript j: "for the Muslims."]] — he was Hujr ibn 'Adi — said: "What prevents you from crossing to these enemies over this river?" — meaning the Tigris — ﴿and no soul can die except by the permission of Allah, at a decreed term.﴾ Then he drove his horse into the Tigris. When he drove it in, the people drove in after him. When the enemy saw them, they said: "Demons!" and they fled. [[In manuscript j: "and they fled."]] [[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (2/584).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him of it; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him of it.﴾ That is: whoever's deed is for this world, he attains from it what Allah has decreed for him, and he will have no share in the Hereafter. Whoever intends by his deed the Hereafter, Allah gives him from it, along with what He has apportioned to him in this world. As He said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him from it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Shura: 20]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish. Then We have appointed for him Hell, which he will enter, blameworthy and rejected. And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due effort while he is a believer — those are the ones whose effort is appreciated﴾ [al-Isra': 18-19]. Likewise He said here: ﴿And We will reward the grateful﴾: that is, We will give them from Our bounty and mercy in this world and the Hereafter according to their gratitude and their deeds.

Then Allah, Exalted, said — consoling the believers for what had entered their souls on the Day of Uhud: ﴿And how many a prophet has fought, with him many devoted followers.﴾ It was said: its meaning is: how many a prophet was killed, and with him were killed many of his companions, the rabbiyyun. This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, for he said: As for those who read ﴿qutila ma'ahu ribbiyyun kathir﴾ [was killed, with him many devoted followers], they said: "He only meant by the killing the Prophet and some of those with him among the rabbiyyun, not all of them, and He negated weakness and feebleness only from those among the rabbiyyun who remained and were not killed."

He said: As for whoever read ﴿qatala﴾ [fought], he chose that because He said: if they had been killed, there would be no sensible meaning to His saying: ﴿so they did not weaken﴾; for it is impossible to describe them as not having weakened and not having become feeble after they had been killed.

Then he chose the reading of whoever read ﴿qutila ma'ahu ribbiyyun kathir﴾, because Allah [Exalted] [[Addition from manuscript w.]] admonished, through these verses and those before them, those who fled on the Day of Uhud and abandoned the fighting, or who heard the crier shouting: "Indeed [[In manuscript r: "that."]] Muhammad has been killed." So Allah rebuked them for their flight and their abandoning of the fighting, and said to them: ﴿So if he dies or is killed,﴾ O believers, will you apostatize from your religion and turn back on your heels?

It was also said: "And how many a prophet was killed before him, with his companions, many devoted followers." [[In manuscript w: "And it was said: And how many a prophet was killed, with him many devoted followers."]]

The speech of Ibn Ishaq in the Sirah suggests another view. He said: That is, how many a prophet was struck by death, and with him were ribbiyyun, that is, groups; yet they did not weaken after their prophet, nor did they become feeble before their enemy, nor did they submit to what befell them in striving in the cause of Allah and of their religion. That is the patience, ﴿and Allah loves the patient.﴾

So he made His saying ﴿with him many devoted followers﴾ a circumstantial phrase [hal]. al-Suhayli supported this view and exaggerated in it, and it has a justification in His saying: ﴿so they did not weaken for what befell them﴾, and al-Umawi related it likewise in his Maghazi from the book of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, and no one else related it.

Some read: ﴿qatala ma'ahu ribbiyyun kathir﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri said, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿ribbiyyun kathir﴾ means: thousands.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Rabi' and 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: al-ribbiyyun are the large multitudes.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿ribbiyyun kathir﴾ means: many scholars. And from him also: scholars who are patient, righteous, and pious.

Ibn Jarir related from some grammarians of Basra that the ribbiyyun are those who worship the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He said: Some of them responded to him, saying: "If it were so, it would be said rabbiyyun, with a fatha on the ra'."

Ibn Zayd said: "The ribbiyyun are the followers and the subjects, and the rabbaniyyun are the rulers."

﴿So they did not weaken for what befell them in the way of Allah, nor were they feeble, nor did they submit.﴾ Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿nor were they feeble﴾ by the killing of their Prophet; ﴿nor did they submit﴾ means: they did not apostatize from their support nor from their religion; rather they fought for what the Prophet of Allah had fought for, until they joined Allah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿nor did they submit﴾ means they humbled themselves. al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: they did not abase themselves before their enemy.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: that is, this befell them when their Prophet was killed.

﴿And Allah loves the patient. And their saying was only that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people."﴾ That is: their only practice was that.

﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world﴾ — that is, victory, triumph, and a good outcome — ﴿and the good reward of the Hereafter.﴾ That is: He combined those for them along with this. ﴿And Allah loves the doers of good.﴾

Allah warns His believing servants against obeying the disbelievers and the hypocrites, for obeying them brings ruin in this world and in the Hereafter. Therefore He says: ﴿If you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about as losers.﴾

Then He commanded them to obey Him, to take Him as their Protector, to seek His help, and to rely upon Him. So He says: ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.﴾

Then He gave them good news that He will cast fear of them into the hearts of their enemies, and humiliation before them, because of their disbelief and their association of partners with Allah, along with what He has stored up for them in the Hereafter of punishment and retribution. So He says: ﴿We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾

It is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things that were not given to any prophet before me: I was helped with terror (cast into the hearts of the enemy) over a distance of one month's journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration (masjid) and a means of purification (tahur); spoils of war have been made lawful for me; I have been given intercession; and every prophet was sent only to his own people, whereas I have been sent to all mankind."

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us from Sulayman, that is al-Taymi, from Sayyar, from Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My Lord has favoured me over the prophets, or he said: over the nations, with four things: I have been sent to all people; the whole earth has been made for me and for my community a place of prostration and a means of purification, so wherever a man of my community is overtaken by the prayer, his place of prostration is there and his purification is there; I have been helped with terror, which He casts into the hearts of my enemies over a distance of one month's journey; and the spoils have been made lawful for me."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it through Sulayman al-Taymi, from Sayyar al-Qurashi al-Umawi, their client, the Damascene, who settled in Basra, from Abu Umamah Suday ibn 'Ajlan, may Allah be pleased with him, with the same wording. He said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Abu Yunus narrated to him, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been helped with terror against the enemy."

Muslim also narrated it through Ibn Wahb.

Imam Ahmad narrated: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from his father, Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things: I have been sent to the red and the black (people); the earth has been made for me a means of purification and a place of prostration; spoils have been made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; I have been helped with terror over a distance of one month's journey; and I have been given intercession. Every prophet has asked for his intercession, but I have kept my intercession hidden, and I have made it for those among my community who die without associating anything with Allah."

Ahmad alone narrated it.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve﴾ that he said: Allah cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan, so he returned to Makkah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abu Sufyan has taken from you a portion, but he has returned, and Allah has cast terror into his heart." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah had promised them victory.

This verse may be used as evidence for one of the two opinions mentioned earlier concerning His words: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord supports you with three thousand angels sent down?" Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will support you with five thousand angels marked for battle.﴾ That this (promise) was on the day of Uhud, because their enemy was three thousand fighters. When they met them, victory and triumph belonged to Islam at the beginning of the day. But when what happened occurred, namely the disobedience of the archers and the failure of some of the fighters, the promise that had been conditioned upon steadfastness and obedience was postponed. Therefore He says: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you﴾, that is, at the beginning of the day, ﴿when you were killing them﴾, that is, you were slaying them, ﴿by His permission﴾, that is, by His empowering you over them. ﴿Until, when you lost courage﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: al-fashal means cowardice. ﴿And you disputed about the matter and disobeyed﴾, as occurred with the archers, ﴿after He had shown you that which you love﴾, which is victory over them. ﴿Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾, that is, then He gave them power over you in order to try you and examine you. ﴿And certainly He has pardoned you﴾, that is, He forgave you that act. And that, Allah knows best, was due to the large number and equipment of the enemy and the small number and equipment of the Muslims.

Ibn Jurayj said concerning His words: ﴿And certainly He has pardoned you﴾: He did not annihilate you. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said likewise. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated both. ﴿And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad informed us, from his father, from 'Ubaydullah, (in some copies "Abi 'Ubaydullah," but the correct form is what we have recorded from the Musnad), from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: Allah has not given victory in any battle as He gave it on the day of Uhud. He said: We denied that, so Ibn 'Abbas said: Between me and whoever denies that is the Book of Allah. Indeed Allah says concerning the day of Uhud: ﴿And certainly Allah fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-hass means killing. ﴿Until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed, after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world and among you are some who desire the Hereafter﴾, to the end of the verse. He meant by this only the archers. That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) had stationed them in one place and said: "Protect our backs. If you see us being killed, do not come to our aid; and if you see us gaining spoils, do not share them with us." When the Prophet (ﷺ) gained spoils and they (the Muslims) had routed the camp of the polytheists, the archers all rushed in and entered the camp, plundering. The lines of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came together, they were thus (and he interlaced his fingers before him) and they engaged. When the archers abandoned that gap in which they had been stationed, the cavalry entered through that spot upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and some of them struck others and they became confused. Many of the Muslims were killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions had been (dominant) at the beginning of the day, until seven or nine of the standard-bearers of the polytheists were killed. The Muslims withdrew in a retreat toward the mountain, but they did not reach the cave, as people say; rather they were under al-Mihras. Satan shouted: "Muhammad has been killed!" It was not doubted that this was true, and we continued in that state, not doubting that it was true, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appeared between the two Sa'ds. We recognized him by his gait when he walked. He said: So we rejoiced until it was as if no harm had befallen us. He said: He climbed toward us saying: "The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah." And he said again: "O Allah, they have no right to prevail over us." Until he reached us, he remained for a while, and then Abu Sufyan was shouting at the foot of the mountain: "Exalt Hubal!" twice, meaning his idol. "Where is the son of Abu Kabshah? Where is the son of Abu Quhafah? Where is the son of al-Khattab?" 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not answer him?" He said: "Yes." So when he said: "Exalt Hubal!", 'Umar said: "Allah is higher and greater!" Abu Sufyan said: "Our idol has been gratified, so turn away from it," or: "Be silent!" Then he said: "Where is the son of Abu Kabshah? Where is the son of Abu Quhafah? Where is the son of al-Khattab?" 'Umar said: "This is the Messenger of Allah, this is Abu Bakr, and here I am, 'Umar." He said: Abu Sufyan said: "A day for a day of Badr! The days are alternating, and war is a matter of turns." He said: 'Umar said: "No, they are not equal: our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire." He said: Abu Sufyan said: "You claim that, but we have indeed then lost and failed." Then Abu Sufyan said: "You will find among your slain mutilation, and that was not by the opinion of our leaders." He said: Then the zeal of the Jahiliyyah overtook him, and he said: "Indeed, if that happened, we did not dislike it."

This is a strange (gharib) report with a remarkable chain and context, and it is a mursal narration from Ibn 'Abbas, for he did not witness Uhud, nor did his father.

Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak from Abu al-Nadr al-Faqih, from 'Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Sulayman ibn Dawud ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, with the same wording. Thus Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah narrated it from the report of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi, with the same wording. Some of it has supporting reports in the Sahih collections and elsewhere. Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The women were on the day of Uhud behind the Muslims, finishing off the wounded of the polytheists. Had I sworn on that day, I would have hoped to be truthful that none of us desired this world, until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾. When the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) opposed and disobeyed what they had been commanded, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone with nine men: seven from the Ansar and two from Quraysh, and he was the tenth of them. When they overtook him, he said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who turns them back from us." A man from the Ansar stood up and fought for a while until he was killed. When they overtook him again, he said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who turns them back from us." He kept saying this until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companion: "We have not been fair to our companions."

Then Abu Sufyan came and said: "Exalted is Hubal!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is most high and most majestic!" They said: "Allah is most high and most majestic!" Abu Sufyan said: "We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is our Protector, and the disbelievers have no protector." Then Abu Sufyan said: "A day for a day of Badr: a day for us and a day against us, and a day of distress and a day of victory. Hanzalah for Hanzalah, and so-and-so for so-and-so, and so-and-so for so-and-so." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Not equal. Our dead are alive, being provided for, and your dead are in the Fire, being tormented." Abu Sufyan said: "There was mutilation among the people, and though it was not by my command, nor did I forbid it, nor did I like it or dislike it, nor did it grieve me or please me." He said: They looked and saw that Hamzah's belly had been ripped open, and Hind had taken his liver and chewed it but could not swallow it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Did she eat anything?" They said: "No." He said: "Allah would not have allowed any part of Hamzah to enter the Fire."

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed Hamzah and prayed over him. A man from the Ansar was brought and placed beside him, and he prayed over him; then the Ansari was lifted and Hamzah was left, then another was brought and placed beside Hamzah, and he prayed over him; then he was lifted and Hamzah was left, until he prayed over him that day seventy times.

Ahmad alone narrated it also (al-Musnad 1/462).

Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "We met the polytheists that day, and the Prophet (ﷺ) seated a group of archers and appointed over them 'Abdullah (meaning Ibn Jubayr), and said: 'Do not leave your position if you see us gaining the upper hand over them, and do not leave it if you see them gaining the upper hand over us, so do not come to our aid.' When we met them, they fled, until we saw the women running up the mountain, lifting their skirts, and their anklets were visible, so they began to say: 'The spoils! The spoils!' 'Abdullah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined me not to leave. But they refused, and when they refused, he turned their faces, and seventy were killed. Abu Sufyan looked over and said: 'Is Muhammad among the people?' He said: 'Do not answer him.' He said: 'Is Ibn Abi Quhafa among the people?' He said: 'Do not answer him.' He said: 'Is Ibn al-Khattab among the people?' He said: 'These have been killed, and if they were alive they would have answered.' 'Umar could not contain himself and said: 'You lie, enemy of Allah! Allah has left for you what will grieve you.' Abu Sufyan said: 'Exalted is Hubal!' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Answer him.' They said: 'What should we say?' He said: 'Say: Allah is most high and most majestic.' Abu Sufyan said: 'We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Answer him.' They said: 'What should we say?' He said: 'Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector.' Abu Sufyan said: 'A day for a day of Badr, and war is in turns (sijal), and you will find mutilation that I did not order, and it did not displease me.'"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this chain, and he also narrated it from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', with similar wording (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4043 and 3986). It will come later in more detail.

Al-Bukhari also said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: When the day of Uhud came, the polytheists were defeated, and Iblis shouted: "O servants of Allah, behind you!" So their first ranks turned back and fought against their last ranks. Hudhayfah looked and saw his father al-Yaman, and said: "O servants of Allah, my father, my father!" She said: By Allah, they did not stop until they killed him. Hudhayfah said: "May Allah forgive you." 'Urwah said: By Allah, goodness remained in Hudhayfah until he met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4065).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam said: "By Allah, I saw myself looking at the female servants of Hind and her companions, lifting their skirts and fleeing; nothing was taken by them, neither much nor little. The archers turned toward the camp when we had driven the people away from it, desiring the plunder, and they left our backs open to the cavalry, which came at us from behind. A crier cried out: 'Beware, Muhammad has been killed!' So we turned back, and the people turned back upon us after we had struck the bearers of the banner, so that none of the people could come near it."

Ibn Ishaq said: The banner of the polytheists remained fallen until 'Amrah bint 'Alqamah al-Harithiyyah took it, and she gave it to Quraysh, and they rallied around it (Sirah Ibn Ishaq, Zahiriyyah MS, folio 170).

And al-Suddi narrated from 'Abd Khayr, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "I did not think that any of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) desired the world until there was revealed concerning us what was revealed on the day of Uhud: ﴿Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾."

It has been narrated through other chains from Ibn Mas'ud, and likewise from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and Abu Talhah, which Ibn Mardawayh recorded in his tafsir.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾. Ibn Ishaq said: al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi', one of the Banu 'Adi ibn al-Najjar, narrated to me, saying: Anas ibn al-Nadr, the uncle of Anas ibn Malik, passed by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah, among men of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, who had laid down their arms. He said: "What keeps you (here)?" They said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been killed." He said: "What is the point of life after him? Get up and die as he died." Then he faced the people and fought until he was killed.

Al-Bukhari said: Hassan ibn Hassan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Talhah narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik: that his uncle (meaning Anas ibn al-Nadr) was absent from Badr and said: "I was absent from the first battle the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought. If Allah lets me witness a battle with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah will see what I do." Then at Uhud the people fled, and he said: "O Allah, I apologize to You for what these people have done (meaning the Muslims), and I disown to You what the polytheists have brought." He advanced with his sword and met Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and said: "Where, O Sa'd? Indeed I smell the fragrance of Paradise beyond Uhud." He went on and was killed. He was not recognized until his sister recognized him by his fingertips, with a mark, and he had more than eighty wounds from stabbing, striking and arrow shots.

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Thabit from Anas, with similar wording (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4048; Sahih Muslim, no. 1903).

Al-Bukhari also said: 'Abdan narrated to us, Abu Hamzah informed us, from 'Uthman ibn Mawhab, who said: A man who had performed Hajj to the House saw a group sitting, and said: "Who are these sitters?" They said: "These are Quraysh." He said: "Who is the elder?" They said: "Ibn 'Umar." He came to him and said: "I will ask you about something, so tell me. I adjure you by the sanctity of this House: do you know that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan fled on the day of Uhud?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know that he was absent from Badr and did not witness it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know that he stayed away from the Pledge of al-Ridwan and did not witness it?" He said: "Yes." He said: Then he exclaimed Allahu akbar. Ibn 'Umar said: "Come, I will inform you and explain to you what you asked me about. As for his fleeing on the day of Uhud, I bear witness that Allah has pardoned him. As for his absence from Badr, he had under him the daughter of the Prophet (ﷺ), who was ill, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'You have the reward of a man who witnessed Badr, and his share.' As for his staying away from the Pledge of al-Ridwan, if anyone was more honored in the valley of Makkah than 'Uthman, he would have sent him instead of him. So he sent 'Uthman, and the Pledge of al-Ridwan took place after 'Uthman had gone to Makkah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said with his right hand: "This is the hand of 'Uthman," and struck it upon his other hand, and said: "This is the hand of 'Uthman; go with it now."

Then al-Bukhari narrated it through another chain, from Abu 'Awanah, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mawhab (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4066 and 3698).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿When you were going up and not turning back for anyone﴾, that is, He turned you away from them, ﴿when you were going up﴾, that is, up the mountain, fleeing from your enemies.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah read: ﴿When you were going up﴾, that is, up the mountain, ﴿and not turning back for anyone﴾, that is, while you did not turn back for anyone out of bewilderment, fear and terror, ﴿while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾, that is, while he was behind you, calling you to stop fleeing from the enemies, and to return, come back and charge again.

Al-Suddi said: When the polytheists attacked the Muslims at Uhud and routed them, some of them entered Madinah, and some of them went up the mountain to the rock and stood upon it, while the Messenger (ﷺ) was calling the people: "Come to me, servants of Allah! Come to me, servants of Allah!" So Allah mentioned their going up the mountain, then mentioned the Prophet's (ﷺ) calling to them, saying: ﴿When you were going up and not turning back for anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, al-Rabi' and Ibn Zayd said likewise.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari, who was still a polytheist and had not yet embraced Islam, composed a poem describing the defeat of the Muslims at Uhud, whose opening is:

O crow of separation, have you heard? Then say, for you speak only of what has already happened...
Indeed for good and for evil there is an end, and both are a direction and a turn...

Then he said:

Would that my elders had witnessed Badr, the Khazraj's dismay at the striking of spears,
When their camels knelt at Quba' and the slaughter raged among the 'Abd al-Ashhal;
Then they hurried away at that moment, dancing like the young camels dance, rising upon the hill.
We killed double of their nobles, and the scale of Badr was balanced.

Al-Hiffan: the young of camels.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 149–153 (part 3 of 4):
