The Prophet (ﷺ) had been left with only twelve men of his Companions, as al-Imam Ahmad related: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us that al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: On the day of Uhud, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr over the archers, who were fifty men, and he placed them in a position and said: "If you see us being snatched by the birds, do not leave your position until I send for you. And if you see us gaining the upper hand over the enemy and trampling them, do not leave your position until I send for you." He said: They routed them. He said: By Allah, I saw the women running up the mountain, their ankles and anklets showing, their garments raised. The companions of 'Abd Allah said: The spoils! O people, the spoils! Your companions have prevailed, so what are you waiting for? 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr said: Have you forgotten what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to you? They said: By Allah, we will go to the people and take a share of the spoils. When they reached them, their faces were turned away and they retreated in defeat. That is what the Messenger called them back to, from behind them. Only twelve men remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They inflicted seventy casualties upon us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions had inflicted on the polytheists at Badr one hundred and forty: seventy captives and seventy killed. Abu Sufyan said: Is Muhammad among the people? Is Muhammad among the people? Is Muhammad among the people? (three times). He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade them from answering him. Then he said: Is the son of Abu Quhafah among the people? Is the son of Abu Quhafah among the people? Is the son of al-Khattab among the people? Is the son of al-Khattab among the people? Then he turned to his companions and said: As for these, they have been killed; you have been spared them. 'Umar could not restrain himself and said: You lie, by Allah, O enemy of Allah! Those whom you named are all alive, and what will grieve you still remains. Abu Sufyan said: A day for a day of Badr, and war is a matter of turns (sijal). Indeed, you will find among the people mutilation which I did not order, and which did not displease me. Then he began to chant rhythmically, saying: "Exalt Hubal! Exalt Hubal!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Will you not answer him?" They said: O Messenger of Allah, what should we say? He said: "Say: Allah is higher and more majestic." He said: We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Will you not answer him?" They said: O Messenger of Allah, what should we say? He said: "Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector." (Al-Musnad, 4/293.)

Al-Bukhari related it from the hadith (prophetic report) of Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah in an abridged form, and he related it from the hadith of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, in a more detailed form, as has already passed. And Allah knows best.

Al-Bayhaqi related in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, from the hadith of 'Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The people fled from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, and there remained with him eleven men from the Ansar and Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah, while he was climbing the mountain. The polytheists came upon them, and he (ﷺ) said: "Is there anyone for these?" Talhah said: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Stay where you are, O Talhah." A man from the Ansar said: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He fought on his behalf and was killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those with him then ascended. Then the Ansari was killed, and they came upon him. He said: "Is there a man for these?" Talhah said the same as before, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same as before. A man from the Ansar said: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He fought on his behalf, and his companions went up. Then he was killed, and they came upon him. He kept saying the same as his first words, and Talhah would say: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He would hold him back, and a man from the Ansar would ask his permission to fight, and he would permit him, and he would fight as those before him had fought, until none remained with him except Talhah, and they were surrounded. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who will take care of these?" Talhah said: I am. He fought with the fighting of all who had been before him, and his fingertips were injured. He said: "Hiss!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you had said, 'In the name of Allah,' and mentioned the name of Allah, the angels would have lifted you up while the people looked at you, until you vanished into the air of the sky." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went up to his Companions, who were gathered together.

Al-Bukhari related from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Waki', from Isma'il, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: I saw the hand of Talhah paralysed, with which he shielded the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning on the day of Uhud.

In the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: On some of those days in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought, there remained with him none except Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah and Sa'd, according to their report.

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from 'Ali ibn Zayd and Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone on the day of Uhud with seven men from the Ansar and two men from Quraysh. When they overwhelmed him, he said: "Who will repel them from us, and he will have Paradise?" or "and he will be my companion in Paradise?" A man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. Then they overwhelmed him again, and he said: "Who will repel them from us, and he will have Paradise?" A man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. And so it continued until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his two companions: "We have not dealt justly with our companions."

Muslim related it from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same meaning.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: Ibn Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hashim ibn Hashim al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: I heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him) say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) emptied his quiver for me on the day of Uhud, and said: "Shoot, may my father and mother be your ransom."

(Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: nathala, meaning he shook out for me, i.e., the Messenger of Allah emptied out for me.)

Al-Bukhari related it from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah. (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4055.)

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to me, from some of the family of Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he shot on the day of Uhud in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Sa'd said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) handing me arrows and saying: "Shoot, may my father and mother be your ransom," until he would hand me an arrow with no head on it, and I would shoot with it.

It is firmly established in the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from his grandfather, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: On the day of Uhud I saw, to the right and left of the Prophet (ﷺ), two men in white garments, fighting on his behalf with the utmost fierceness. I had not seen them before that day or after it. He meant Jibril and Mika'il (peace be upon them). (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4054; Sahih Muslim, no. 2306.)

Abu al-Aswad said, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf, brother of Banu Jumah, had sworn while in Makkah that he would kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When his oath reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Rather, I will kill him, if Allah wills." When the day of Uhud came, Ubayy approached in his armour, his face covered, saying: "I shall not survive if Muhammad survives!" He charged at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), intending to kill him. Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, brother of Banu 'Abd al-Dar, confronted him, shielding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his own self, and Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr was killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the collarbone of Ubayy ibn Khalaf through a gap between the coat of mail and the helmet, and he struck him there with his spear. He fell from his horse to the ground, and no blood came out from his wound. His companions came to him and carried him, while he was bellowing like a bull. They said to him: Why are you so distressed? It is only a scratch! He mentioned to them the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I will kill Ubayy." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, if this which I have were distributed among the people of Dhu al-Majaz, they would all die." He died on the way to Hell, so far away be the companions of the Blaze.

Musa ibn 'Uqbah related it in his Maghazi (Military Campaigns), from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, in similar wording.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was propped up in the mountain pass, Ubayy ibn Khalaf reached him, saying: "I shall not survive if you survive!" The people said: O Messenger of Allah, shall one of us turn against him? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave him." When he drew near, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the spear from al-Harith ibn al-Simmah. One of the people said what was related to me: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it from him, he (Ubayy) shook violently, and we scattered away from him like hair scattering from the back of a camel when it shakes. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) approached him and struck him in the neck with a blow, from which he fell from his horse several times.

Al-Waqidi mentioned, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Amr ibn Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, something similar to this. (Sirat Ibn Ishaq, Zahiriyyah manuscript, folio 171, in the recension of Muhammad ibn Salamah.)

Al-Waqidi said: Ibn 'Umar used to say: Ubayy ibn Khalaf died at Batn Raghigh. I was traveling through Batn Raghigh after part of the night had passed, when I suddenly saw a fire blazing. I was frightened by it, and then a man came out of it, dragged by a chain, while thirst was tormenting him, and a man was saying: "Do not give him water, for this is the slain of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), this is Ubayy ibn Khalaf."

It is firmly established in the Sahihayn, from the narration of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who did this to the Messenger of Allah" (and at that time he was pointing to his molar tooth), "The anger of Allah has intensified against a man whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kills in the way of Allah." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4073; Sahih Muslim, no. 1793.)

Al-Bukhari also related it (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4074, 4076) from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The anger of Allah has intensified against the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed with his own hand in the way of Allah. The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The molar tooth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was struck, his cheek was split open, and his lip was wounded. The one who inflicted it was 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas.

Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to me, from one who had narrated to him, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: I never desired to kill anyone as much as I desired to kill 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas, though as far as I knew he was ill-tempered and hated among his people. The saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sufficed me concerning him: "The anger of Allah has intensified against the one who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." (Sirat Ibn Ishaq, Zahiriyyah manuscript, folio 172.)

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Uthman al-Jazari, from Miqsam, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invoked against 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas on the day of Uhud, when he broke his molar tooth and wounded his face, saying: "O Allah, let not the year pass over him until he dies a disbeliever." He had not completed a year before he died a disbeliever, bound for the Fire. (Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq, 1/136.)

Al-Waqidi reported from Ibn Abi Sabra, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Farwa, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard a man from the Muhajirun say: "I was present at Uhud, and I saw the arrows coming from every direction, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the middle of them, and every one of them was turned away from him. I also saw Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri saying that day: 'Show me Muhammad! I will not be saved if he is saved.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was beside him with no one else with him. Then he passed by him and was rebuked for this by Safwan, who said: 'By Allah, I did not see him. I swear by Allah that he is protected from us.' We set out four men, made a pact and agreed to kill him, but we did not get close to that."

Al-Waqidi said: "What is established according to us is that the one who struck the cheek of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was Ibn Qami'a, and the one who wounded his lip and struck his front tooth (ruba'iyyah) was Utba ibn Abi Waqqas."

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, who said: Isa ibn Talha informed me, from Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), whenever he mentioned the Day of Uhud, would say: 'That whole day belonged to Talha.' Then he began to narrate: 'I was the first to return on the Day of Uhud, and I saw a man fighting alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), defending him' - and I think he said 'out of zeal' - 'and I said: Be Talha! Since what I missed has escaped me, I said: a man from my own people would be dearer to me. Between me and the polytheists there was a man whom I did not recognize, and I was closer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than he was, and he was moving swiftly in a manner I cannot describe. Then it turned out to be Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah. We reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and his front tooth had been broken and his face was wounded, and two rings of the helmet had entered his cheek. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Attend to your companion," meaning Talha, who was bleeding profusely, but we did not pay attention to his words. He said: I went to pull that out of his face, but Abu Ubayda said: I adjure you by my right over you that you leave me. So I left him. He disliked to take hold of them with his hand lest he hurt the Prophet (ﷺ), so he clenched them with his teeth and pulled out one of the two rings, and his tooth fell out with the ring. I went to do what he had done, but he said: I adjure you by my right over you that you leave me. He did the same as he had done the first time, and his other front tooth fell out with the ring. Abu Ubayda (may Allah be pleased with him) was the most graceful of people in losing his teeth. Then we tended to the affairs of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then we came to Talha in one of those ditches, and he had more than seventy wounds, or fewer or more, from stabbing, shooting and striking, and his finger had been cut off, so we tended to his condition."

Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb and al-Tabarani also narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Yahya. In al-Haytham's version: Abu Ubayda said: "I beseech you, O Abu Bakr, by Allah, to leave me?" Then Abu Ubayda took the arrowhead with his mouth and began to move it gently, out of dislike that it would hurt the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he pulled the arrowhead out with his mouth, and Abu Ubayda's tooth was dislodged.

He mentioned its full text, and al-Hafiz Diya al-Maqdisi chose it in his book. (Musnad al-Tayalisi, p. 3, and al-Mukhtarah of Diya al-Maqdisi, no. 49, through the route of al-Haytham ibn Kulayb. al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. 63, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 4941 (al-Ihsan), narrated it through the route of Ishaq ibn Yahya. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6/112): "In it is Ishaq ibn Yahya, who is matruk (abandoned).")

Ali ibn al-Madini declared this hadith weak because of this Ishaq ibn Yahya, for Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, Ahmad, Yahya ibn Ma'in, al-Bukhari, Abu Zur'a, Abu Hatim, Muhammad ibn Sa'd, al-Nasa'i and others criticized him.

Ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Umar ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to him that it reached him that Malik, the father (Abi) of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was wounded on the Day of Uhud, sucked the wound until he cleaned it and it shone white. He was told: "Spit it out." He said: "No, by Allah, I will never spit it out." Then he turned back to fight. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to look at a man of the people of Paradise, let him look at this one." And he was martyred. (Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/266) through the route of Ibn Wahb.)

It is established in the two Sahihs, through the route of Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim, from his father, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that he was asked about the wound of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was wounded, his front tooth was broken, and the helmet was crushed on his head. Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was washing the blood, and Ali was pouring water on it with a shield. When Fatimah saw that the water only increased the blood, she took a piece of mat and burned it, and when it became ash, she pressed it onto the wound, and the blood stopped." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2911, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1790.)

* *

His saying: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾ means: He repaid you with grief for grief, as the Arabs say: "I stayed among the family of so-and-so" and "I stayed upon the family of so-and-so."

Ibn Jarir said: Likewise His saying: ﴿And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71], meaning upon the trunks of palm trees.

Ibn Abbas said: "The first grief was because of the defeat and when it was said: Muhammad (ﷺ) has been killed. The second was when the polytheists overcame them from above the mountain, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O Allah, they must not be allowed to prevail over us.'"

From Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: "The first grief was because of the defeat, and the second was when it was said: Muhammad (ﷺ) has been killed, and that was greater in their view than the defeat."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated both of these. Something similar was reported from Umar ibn al-Khattab. Ibn Abi Hatim also mentioned something similar from Qatadah.

Al-Suddi said: "The first grief was because of what they missed of the spoils and the victory, and the second was the enemy's looking down upon them."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾ means: one distress after another, the killing of those of your brothers who were killed, the enemy's rising over you, and what fell upon your hearts from the words of those who said: "Your Prophet has been killed." So that was successive upon you, grief upon grief.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: "The first grief was hearing of the killing of Muhammad, and the second was what befell them of killing and wounds." From Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, the reverse was reported.

From al-Suddi: "The first was what they missed of victory and spoils, and the second was the enemy's looking down upon them." This has already been mentioned from al-Suddi.

Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of these views is the view of the one who said: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾, meaning: He repaid you, O believers, with your grief at Allah's depriving you of the spoils of the polytheists, of victory over them and of triumph against them, and with what befell you of killing and wounds that day, after He had shown you in all that what you love, because of your disobedience to your Lord and your opposition to the command of the Prophet (ﷺ) - the grief of your thinking that your Prophet had been killed, and the enemy's advantage over you after your retreat from them.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that you would not grieve over what escaped you, nor over what befell you﴾ means: over what escaped you of the spoils from your enemy, ﴿nor over what befell you﴾ of killing and wounds. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi. ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾.

Allah warns His believing servants against obeying the disbelievers and the hypocrites, for obeying them brings ruin in this world and in the Hereafter. Therefore He says: ﴿If you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about as losers.﴾

Then He commanded them to obey Him, to take Him as their Protector, to seek His help, and to rely upon Him. So He says: ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.﴾

Then He gave them good news that He will cast fear of them into the hearts of their enemies, and humiliation before them, because of their disbelief and their association of partners with Allah, along with what He has stored up for them in the Hereafter of punishment and retribution. So He says: ﴿We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾

It is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things that were not given to any prophet before me: I was helped with terror (cast into the hearts of the enemy) over a distance of one month's journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration (masjid) and a means of purification (tahur); spoils of war have been made lawful for me; I have been given intercession; and every prophet was sent only to his own people, whereas I have been sent to all mankind."

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us from Sulayman, that is al-Taymi, from Sayyar, from Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My Lord has favoured me over the prophets, or he said: over the nations, with four things: I have been sent to all people; the whole earth has been made for me and for my community a place of prostration and a means of purification, so wherever a man of my community is overtaken by the prayer, his place of prostration is there and his purification is there; I have been helped with terror, which He casts into the hearts of my enemies over a distance of one month's journey; and the spoils have been made lawful for me."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it through Sulayman al-Taymi, from Sayyar al-Qurashi al-Umawi, their client, the Damascene, who settled in Basra, from Abu Umamah Suday ibn 'Ajlan, may Allah be pleased with him, with the same wording. He said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Abu Yunus narrated to him, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been helped with terror against the enemy."

Muslim also narrated it through Ibn Wahb.

Imam Ahmad narrated: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from his father, Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things: I have been sent to the red and the black (people); the earth has been made for me a means of purification and a place of prostration; spoils have been made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; I have been helped with terror over a distance of one month's journey; and I have been given intercession. Every prophet has asked for his intercession, but I have kept my intercession hidden, and I have made it for those among my community who die without associating anything with Allah."

Ahmad alone narrated it.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve﴾ that he said: Allah cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan, so he returned to Makkah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abu Sufyan has taken from you a portion, but he has returned, and Allah has cast terror into his heart." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah had promised them victory.

This verse may be used as evidence for one of the two opinions mentioned earlier concerning His words: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord supports you with three thousand angels sent down?" Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will support you with five thousand angels marked for battle.﴾ That this (promise) was on the day of Uhud, because their enemy was three thousand fighters. When they met them, victory and triumph belonged to Islam at the beginning of the day. But when what happened occurred, namely the disobedience of the archers and the failure of some of the fighters, the promise that had been conditioned upon steadfastness and obedience was postponed. Therefore He says: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you﴾, that is, at the beginning of the day, ﴿when you were killing them﴾, that is, you were slaying them, ﴿by His permission﴾, that is, by His empowering you over them. ﴿Until, when you lost courage﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: al-fashal means cowardice. ﴿And you disputed about the matter and disobeyed﴾, as occurred with the archers, ﴿after He had shown you that which you love﴾, which is victory over them. ﴿Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾, that is, then He gave them power over you in order to try you and examine you. ﴿And certainly He has pardoned you﴾, that is, He forgave you that act. And that, Allah knows best, was due to the large number and equipment of the enemy and the small number and equipment of the Muslims.

Ibn Jurayj said concerning His words: ﴿And certainly He has pardoned you﴾: He did not annihilate you. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said likewise. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated both. ﴿And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad informed us, from his father, from 'Ubaydullah, (in some copies "Abi 'Ubaydullah," but the correct form is what we have recorded from the Musnad), from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: Allah has not given victory in any battle as He gave it on the day of Uhud. He said: We denied that, so Ibn 'Abbas said: Between me and whoever denies that is the Book of Allah. Indeed Allah says concerning the day of Uhud: ﴿And certainly Allah fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-hass means killing. ﴿Until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed, after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world and among you are some who desire the Hereafter﴾, to the end of the verse. He meant by this only the archers. That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) had stationed them in one place and said: "Protect our backs. If you see us being killed, do not come to our aid; and if you see us gaining spoils, do not share them with us." When the Prophet (ﷺ) gained spoils and they (the Muslims) had routed the camp of the polytheists, the archers all rushed in and entered the camp, plundering. The lines of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came together, they were thus (and he interlaced his fingers before him) and they engaged. When the archers abandoned that gap in which they had been stationed, the cavalry entered through that spot upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and some of them struck others and they became confused. Many of the Muslims were killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions had been (dominant) at the beginning of the day, until seven or nine of the standard-bearers of the polytheists were killed. The Muslims withdrew in a retreat toward the mountain, but they did not reach the cave, as people say; rather they were under al-Mihras. Satan shouted: "Muhammad has been killed!" It was not doubted that this was true, and we continued in that state, not doubting that it was true, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appeared between the two Sa'ds. We recognized him by his gait when he walked. He said: So we rejoiced until it was as if no harm had befallen us. He said: He climbed toward us saying: "The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah." And he said again: "O Allah, they have no right to prevail over us." Until he reached us, he remained for a while, and then Abu Sufyan was shouting at the foot of the mountain: "Exalt Hubal!" twice, meaning his idol. "Where is the son of Abu Kabshah? Where is the son of Abu Quhafah? Where is the son of al-Khattab?" 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not answer him?" He said: "Yes." So when he said: "Exalt Hubal!", 'Umar said: "Allah is higher and greater!" Abu Sufyan said: "Our idol has been gratified, so turn away from it," or: "Be silent!" Then he said: "Where is the son of Abu Kabshah? Where is the son of Abu Quhafah? Where is the son of al-Khattab?" 'Umar said: "This is the Messenger of Allah, this is Abu Bakr, and here I am, 'Umar." He said: Abu Sufyan said: "A day for a day of Badr! The days are alternating, and war is a matter of turns." He said: 'Umar said: "No, they are not equal: our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire." He said: Abu Sufyan said: "You claim that, but we have indeed then lost and failed." Then Abu Sufyan said: "You will find among your slain mutilation, and that was not by the opinion of our leaders." He said: Then the zeal of the Jahiliyyah overtook him, and he said: "Indeed, if that happened, we did not dislike it."

This is a strange (gharib) report with a remarkable chain and context, and it is a mursal narration from Ibn 'Abbas, for he did not witness Uhud, nor did his father.

Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak from Abu al-Nadr al-Faqih, from 'Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Sulayman ibn Dawud ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, with the same wording. Thus Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah narrated it from the report of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi, with the same wording. Some of it has supporting reports in the Sahih collections and elsewhere. Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The women were on the day of Uhud behind the Muslims, finishing off the wounded of the polytheists. Had I sworn on that day, I would have hoped to be truthful that none of us desired this world, until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾. When the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) opposed and disobeyed what they had been commanded, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone with nine men: seven from the Ansar and two from Quraysh, and he was the tenth of them. When they overtook him, he said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who turns them back from us." A man from the Ansar stood up and fought for a while until he was killed. When they overtook him again, he said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who turns them back from us." He kept saying this until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companion: "We have not been fair to our companions."

Then Abu Sufyan came and said: "Exalted is Hubal!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is most high and most majestic!" They said: "Allah is most high and most majestic!" Abu Sufyan said: "We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is our Protector, and the disbelievers have no protector." Then Abu Sufyan said: "A day for a day of Badr: a day for us and a day against us, and a day of distress and a day of victory. Hanzalah for Hanzalah, and so-and-so for so-and-so, and so-and-so for so-and-so." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Not equal. Our dead are alive, being provided for, and your dead are in the Fire, being tormented." Abu Sufyan said: "There was mutilation among the people, and though it was not by my command, nor did I forbid it, nor did I like it or dislike it, nor did it grieve me or please me." He said: They looked and saw that Hamzah's belly had been ripped open, and Hind had taken his liver and chewed it but could not swallow it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Did she eat anything?" They said: "No." He said: "Allah would not have allowed any part of Hamzah to enter the Fire."

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed Hamzah and prayed over him. A man from the Ansar was brought and placed beside him, and he prayed over him; then the Ansari was lifted and Hamzah was left, then another was brought and placed beside Hamzah, and he prayed over him; then he was lifted and Hamzah was left, until he prayed over him that day seventy times.

Ahmad alone narrated it also (al-Musnad 1/462).

Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "We met the polytheists that day, and the Prophet (ﷺ) seated a group of archers and appointed over them 'Abdullah (meaning Ibn Jubayr), and said: 'Do not leave your position if you see us gaining the upper hand over them, and do not leave it if you see them gaining the upper hand over us, so do not come to our aid.' When we met them, they fled, until we saw the women running up the mountain, lifting their skirts, and their anklets were visible, so they began to say: 'The spoils! The spoils!' 'Abdullah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined me not to leave. But they refused, and when they refused, he turned their faces, and seventy were killed. Abu Sufyan looked over and said: 'Is Muhammad among the people?' He said: 'Do not answer him.' He said: 'Is Ibn Abi Quhafa among the people?' He said: 'Do not answer him.' He said: 'Is Ibn al-Khattab among the people?' He said: 'These have been killed, and if they were alive they would have answered.' 'Umar could not contain himself and said: 'You lie, enemy of Allah! Allah has left for you what will grieve you.' Abu Sufyan said: 'Exalted is Hubal!' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Answer him.' They said: 'What should we say?' He said: 'Say: Allah is most high and most majestic.' Abu Sufyan said: 'We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Answer him.' They said: 'What should we say?' He said: 'Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector.' Abu Sufyan said: 'A day for a day of Badr, and war is in turns (sijal), and you will find mutilation that I did not order, and it did not displease me.'"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this chain, and he also narrated it from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', with similar wording (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4043 and 3986). It will come later in more detail.

Al-Bukhari also said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: When the day of Uhud came, the polytheists were defeated, and Iblis shouted: "O servants of Allah, behind you!" So their first ranks turned back and fought against their last ranks. Hudhayfah looked and saw his father al-Yaman, and said: "O servants of Allah, my father, my father!" She said: By Allah, they did not stop until they killed him. Hudhayfah said: "May Allah forgive you." 'Urwah said: By Allah, goodness remained in Hudhayfah until he met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4065).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam said: "By Allah, I saw myself looking at the female servants of Hind and her companions, lifting their skirts and fleeing; nothing was taken by them, neither much nor little. The archers turned toward the camp when we had driven the people away from it, desiring the plunder, and they left our backs open to the cavalry, which came at us from behind. A crier cried out: 'Beware, Muhammad has been killed!' So we turned back, and the people turned back upon us after we had struck the bearers of the banner, so that none of the people could come near it."

Ibn Ishaq said: The banner of the polytheists remained fallen until 'Amrah bint 'Alqamah al-Harithiyyah took it, and she gave it to Quraysh, and they rallied around it (Sirah Ibn Ishaq, Zahiriyyah MS, folio 170).

And al-Suddi narrated from 'Abd Khayr, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "I did not think that any of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) desired the world until there was revealed concerning us what was revealed on the day of Uhud: ﴿Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾."

It has been narrated through other chains from Ibn Mas'ud, and likewise from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and Abu Talhah, which Ibn Mardawayh recorded in his tafsir.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾. Ibn Ishaq said: al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi', one of the Banu 'Adi ibn al-Najjar, narrated to me, saying: Anas ibn al-Nadr, the uncle of Anas ibn Malik, passed by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah, among men of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, who had laid down their arms. He said: "What keeps you (here)?" They said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been killed." He said: "What is the point of life after him? Get up and die as he died." Then he faced the people and fought until he was killed.

Al-Bukhari said: Hassan ibn Hassan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Talhah narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik: that his uncle (meaning Anas ibn al-Nadr) was absent from Badr and said: "I was absent from the first battle the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought. If Allah lets me witness a battle with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah will see what I do." Then at Uhud the people fled, and he said: "O Allah, I apologize to You for what these people have done (meaning the Muslims), and I disown to You what the polytheists have brought." He advanced with his sword and met Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and said: "Where, O Sa'd? Indeed I smell the fragrance of Paradise beyond Uhud." He went on and was killed. He was not recognized until his sister recognized him by his fingertips, with a mark, and he had more than eighty wounds from stabbing, striking and arrow shots.

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Thabit from Anas, with similar wording (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4048; Sahih Muslim, no. 1903).

Al-Bukhari also said: 'Abdan narrated to us, Abu Hamzah informed us, from 'Uthman ibn Mawhab, who said: A man who had performed Hajj to the House saw a group sitting, and said: "Who are these sitters?" They said: "These are Quraysh." He said: "Who is the elder?" They said: "Ibn 'Umar." He came to him and said: "I will ask you about something, so tell me. I adjure you by the sanctity of this House: do you know that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan fled on the day of Uhud?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know that he was absent from Badr and did not witness it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know that he stayed away from the Pledge of al-Ridwan and did not witness it?" He said: "Yes." He said: Then he exclaimed Allahu akbar. Ibn 'Umar said: "Come, I will inform you and explain to you what you asked me about. As for his fleeing on the day of Uhud, I bear witness that Allah has pardoned him. As for his absence from Badr, he had under him the daughter of the Prophet (ﷺ), who was ill, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'You have the reward of a man who witnessed Badr, and his share.' As for his staying away from the Pledge of al-Ridwan, if anyone was more honored in the valley of Makkah than 'Uthman, he would have sent him instead of him. So he sent 'Uthman, and the Pledge of al-Ridwan took place after 'Uthman had gone to Makkah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said with his right hand: "This is the hand of 'Uthman," and struck it upon his other hand, and said: "This is the hand of 'Uthman; go with it now."

Then al-Bukhari narrated it through another chain, from Abu 'Awanah, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mawhab (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4066 and 3698).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿When you were going up and not turning back for anyone﴾, that is, He turned you away from them, ﴿when you were going up﴾, that is, up the mountain, fleeing from your enemies.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah read: ﴿When you were going up﴾, that is, up the mountain, ﴿and not turning back for anyone﴾, that is, while you did not turn back for anyone out of bewilderment, fear and terror, ﴿while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾, that is, while he was behind you, calling you to stop fleeing from the enemies, and to return, come back and charge again.

Al-Suddi said: When the polytheists attacked the Muslims at Uhud and routed them, some of them entered Madinah, and some of them went up the mountain to the rock and stood upon it, while the Messenger (ﷺ) was calling the people: "Come to me, servants of Allah! Come to me, servants of Allah!" So Allah mentioned their going up the mountain, then mentioned the Prophet's (ﷺ) calling to them, saying: ﴿When you were going up and not turning back for anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, al-Rabi' and Ibn Zayd said likewise.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari, who was still a polytheist and had not yet embraced Islam, composed a poem describing the defeat of the Muslims at Uhud, whose opening is:

O crow of separation, have you heard? Then say, for you speak only of what has already happened...
Indeed for good and for evil there is an end, and both are a direction and a turn...

Then he said:

Would that my elders had witnessed Badr, the Khazraj's dismay at the striking of spears,
When their camels knelt at Quba' and the slaughter raged among the 'Abd al-Ashhal;
Then they hurried away at that moment, dancing like the young camels dance, rising upon the hill.
We killed double of their nobles, and the scale of Badr was balanced.

Al-Hiffan: the young of camels.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 149–153 (part 3 of 4):

The Prophet (ﷺ) had been left with only twelve men of his Companions, as al-Imam Ahmad related: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us that al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: On the day of Uhud, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr over the archers, who were fifty men, and he placed them in a position and said: "If you see us being snatched by the birds, do not leave your position until I send for you. And if you see us gaining the upper hand over the enemy and trampling them, do not leave your position until I send for you." He said: They routed them. He said: By Allah, I saw the women running up the mountain, their ankles and anklets showing, their garments raised. The companions of 'Abd Allah said: The spoils! O people, the spoils! Your companions have prevailed, so what are you waiting for? 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr said: Have you forgotten what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to you? They said: By Allah, we will go to the people and take a share of the spoils. When they reached them, their faces were turned away and they retreated in defeat. That is what the Messenger called them back to, from behind them. Only twelve men remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They inflicted seventy casualties upon us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions had inflicted on the polytheists at Badr one hundred and forty: seventy captives and seventy killed. Abu Sufyan said: Is Muhammad among the people? Is Muhammad among the people? Is Muhammad among the people? (three times). He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade them from answering him. Then he said: Is the son of Abu Quhafah among the people? Is the son of Abu Quhafah among the people? Is the son of al-Khattab among the people? Is the son of al-Khattab among the people? Then he turned to his companions and said: As for these, they have been killed; you have been spared them. 'Umar could not restrain himself and said: You lie, by Allah, O enemy of Allah! Those whom you named are all alive, and what will grieve you still remains. Abu Sufyan said: A day for a day of Badr, and war is a matter of turns (sijal). Indeed, you will find among the people mutilation which I did not order, and which did not displease me. Then he began to chant rhythmically, saying: "Exalt Hubal! Exalt Hubal!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Will you not answer him?" They said: O Messenger of Allah, what should we say? He said: "Say: Allah is higher and more majestic." He said: We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Will you not answer him?" They said: O Messenger of Allah, what should we say? He said: "Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector." (Al-Musnad, 4/293.)

Al-Bukhari related it from the hadith (prophetic report) of Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah in an abridged form, and he related it from the hadith of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, in a more detailed form, as has already passed. And Allah knows best.

Al-Bayhaqi related in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, from the hadith of 'Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The people fled from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, and there remained with him eleven men from the Ansar and Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah, while he was climbing the mountain. The polytheists came upon them, and he (ﷺ) said: "Is there anyone for these?" Talhah said: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Stay where you are, O Talhah." A man from the Ansar said: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He fought on his behalf and was killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those with him then ascended. Then the Ansari was killed, and they came upon him. He said: "Is there a man for these?" Talhah said the same as before, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same as before. A man from the Ansar said: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He fought on his behalf, and his companions went up. Then he was killed, and they came upon him. He kept saying the same as his first words, and Talhah would say: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He would hold him back, and a man from the Ansar would ask his permission to fight, and he would permit him, and he would fight as those before him had fought, until none remained with him except Talhah, and they were surrounded. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who will take care of these?" Talhah said: I am. He fought with the fighting of all who had been before him, and his fingertips were injured. He said: "Hiss!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you had said, 'In the name of Allah,' and mentioned the name of Allah, the angels would have lifted you up while the people looked at you, until you vanished into the air of the sky." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went up to his Companions, who were gathered together.

Al-Bukhari related from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Waki', from Isma'il, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: I saw the hand of Talhah paralysed, with which he shielded the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning on the day of Uhud.

In the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: On some of those days in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought, there remained with him none except Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah and Sa'd, according to their report.

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from 'Ali ibn Zayd and Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone on the day of Uhud with seven men from the Ansar and two men from Quraysh. When they overwhelmed him, he said: "Who will repel them from us, and he will have Paradise?" or "and he will be my companion in Paradise?" A man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. Then they overwhelmed him again, and he said: "Who will repel them from us, and he will have Paradise?" A man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. And so it continued until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his two companions: "We have not dealt justly with our companions."

Muslim related it from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same meaning.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: Ibn Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hashim ibn Hashim al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: I heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him) say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) emptied his quiver for me on the day of Uhud, and said: "Shoot, may my father and mother be your ransom."

(Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: nathala, meaning he shook out for me, i.e., the Messenger of Allah emptied out for me.)

Al-Bukhari related it from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah. (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4055.)

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to me, from some of the family of Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he shot on the day of Uhud in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Sa'd said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) handing me arrows and saying: "Shoot, may my father and mother be your ransom," until he would hand me an arrow with no head on it, and I would shoot with it.

It is firmly established in the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from his grandfather, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: On the day of Uhud I saw, to the right and left of the Prophet (ﷺ), two men in white garments, fighting on his behalf with the utmost fierceness. I had not seen them before that day or after it. He meant Jibril and Mika'il (peace be upon them). (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4054; Sahih Muslim, no. 2306.)

Abu al-Aswad said, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf, brother of Banu Jumah, had sworn while in Makkah that he would kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When his oath reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Rather, I will kill him, if Allah wills." When the day of Uhud came, Ubayy approached in his armour, his face covered, saying: "I shall not survive if Muhammad survives!" He charged at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), intending to kill him. Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, brother of Banu 'Abd al-Dar, confronted him, shielding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his own self, and Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr was killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the collarbone of Ubayy ibn Khalaf through a gap between the coat of mail and the helmet, and he struck him there with his spear. He fell from his horse to the ground, and no blood came out from his wound. His companions came to him and carried him, while he was bellowing like a bull. They said to him: Why are you so distressed? It is only a scratch! He mentioned to them the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I will kill Ubayy." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, if this which I have were distributed among the people of Dhu al-Majaz, they would all die." He died on the way to Hell, so far away be the companions of the Blaze.

Musa ibn 'Uqbah related it in his Maghazi (Military Campaigns), from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, in similar wording.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was propped up in the mountain pass, Ubayy ibn Khalaf reached him, saying: "I shall not survive if you survive!" The people said: O Messenger of Allah, shall one of us turn against him? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave him." When he drew near, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the spear from al-Harith ibn al-Simmah. One of the people said what was related to me: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it from him, he (Ubayy) shook violently, and we scattered away from him like hair scattering from the back of a camel when it shakes. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) approached him and struck him in the neck with a blow, from which he fell from his horse several times.

Al-Waqidi mentioned, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Amr ibn Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, something similar to this. (Sirat Ibn Ishaq, Zahiriyyah manuscript, folio 171, in the recension of Muhammad ibn Salamah.)

Al-Waqidi said: Ibn 'Umar used to say: Ubayy ibn Khalaf died at Batn Raghigh. I was traveling through Batn Raghigh after part of the night had passed, when I suddenly saw a fire blazing. I was frightened by it, and then a man came out of it, dragged by a chain, while thirst was tormenting him, and a man was saying: "Do not give him water, for this is the slain of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), this is Ubayy ibn Khalaf."

It is firmly established in the Sahihayn, from the narration of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who did this to the Messenger of Allah" (and at that time he was pointing to his molar tooth), "The anger of Allah has intensified against a man whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kills in the way of Allah." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4073; Sahih Muslim, no. 1793.)

Al-Bukhari also related it (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4074, 4076) from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The anger of Allah has intensified against the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed with his own hand in the way of Allah. The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The molar tooth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was struck, his cheek was split open, and his lip was wounded. The one who inflicted it was 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas.

Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to me, from one who had narrated to him, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: I never desired to kill anyone as much as I desired to kill 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas, though as far as I knew he was ill-tempered and hated among his people. The saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sufficed me concerning him: "The anger of Allah has intensified against the one who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." (Sirat Ibn Ishaq, Zahiriyyah manuscript, folio 172.)

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Uthman al-Jazari, from Miqsam, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invoked against 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas on the day of Uhud, when he broke his molar tooth and wounded his face, saying: "O Allah, let not the year pass over him until he dies a disbeliever." He had not completed a year before he died a disbeliever, bound for the Fire. (Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq, 1/136.)

Al-Waqidi reported from Ibn Abi Sabra, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Farwa, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard a man from the Muhajirun say: "I was present at Uhud, and I saw the arrows coming from every direction, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the middle of them, and every one of them was turned away from him. I also saw Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri saying that day: 'Show me Muhammad! I will not be saved if he is saved.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was beside him with no one else with him. Then he passed by him and was rebuked for this by Safwan, who said: 'By Allah, I did not see him. I swear by Allah that he is protected from us.' We set out four men, made a pact and agreed to kill him, but we did not get close to that."

Al-Waqidi said: "What is established according to us is that the one who struck the cheek of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was Ibn Qami'a, and the one who wounded his lip and struck his front tooth (ruba'iyyah) was Utba ibn Abi Waqqas."

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, who said: Isa ibn Talha informed me, from Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), whenever he mentioned the Day of Uhud, would say: 'That whole day belonged to Talha.' Then he began to narrate: 'I was the first to return on the Day of Uhud, and I saw a man fighting alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), defending him' - and I think he said 'out of zeal' - 'and I said: Be Talha! Since what I missed has escaped me, I said: a man from my own people would be dearer to me. Between me and the polytheists there was a man whom I did not recognize, and I was closer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than he was, and he was moving swiftly in a manner I cannot describe. Then it turned out to be Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah. We reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and his front tooth had been broken and his face was wounded, and two rings of the helmet had entered his cheek. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Attend to your companion," meaning Talha, who was bleeding profusely, but we did not pay attention to his words. He said: I went to pull that out of his face, but Abu Ubayda said: I adjure you by my right over you that you leave me. So I left him. He disliked to take hold of them with his hand lest he hurt the Prophet (ﷺ), so he clenched them with his teeth and pulled out one of the two rings, and his tooth fell out with the ring. I went to do what he had done, but he said: I adjure you by my right over you that you leave me. He did the same as he had done the first time, and his other front tooth fell out with the ring. Abu Ubayda (may Allah be pleased with him) was the most graceful of people in losing his teeth. Then we tended to the affairs of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then we came to Talha in one of those ditches, and he had more than seventy wounds, or fewer or more, from stabbing, shooting and striking, and his finger had been cut off, so we tended to his condition."

Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb and al-Tabarani also narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Yahya. In al-Haytham's version: Abu Ubayda said: "I beseech you, O Abu Bakr, by Allah, to leave me?" Then Abu Ubayda took the arrowhead with his mouth and began to move it gently, out of dislike that it would hurt the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he pulled the arrowhead out with his mouth, and Abu Ubayda's tooth was dislodged.

He mentioned its full text, and al-Hafiz Diya al-Maqdisi chose it in his book. (Musnad al-Tayalisi, p. 3, and al-Mukhtarah of Diya al-Maqdisi, no. 49, through the route of al-Haytham ibn Kulayb. al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. 63, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 4941 (al-Ihsan), narrated it through the route of Ishaq ibn Yahya. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6/112): "In it is Ishaq ibn Yahya, who is matruk (abandoned).")

Ali ibn al-Madini declared this hadith weak because of this Ishaq ibn Yahya, for Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, Ahmad, Yahya ibn Ma'in, al-Bukhari, Abu Zur'a, Abu Hatim, Muhammad ibn Sa'd, al-Nasa'i and others criticized him.

Ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Umar ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to him that it reached him that Malik, the father (Abi) of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was wounded on the Day of Uhud, sucked the wound until he cleaned it and it shone white. He was told: "Spit it out." He said: "No, by Allah, I will never spit it out." Then he turned back to fight. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to look at a man of the people of Paradise, let him look at this one." And he was martyred. (Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/266) through the route of Ibn Wahb.)

It is established in the two Sahihs, through the route of Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim, from his father, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that he was asked about the wound of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was wounded, his front tooth was broken, and the helmet was crushed on his head. Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was washing the blood, and Ali was pouring water on it with a shield. When Fatimah saw that the water only increased the blood, she took a piece of mat and burned it, and when it became ash, she pressed it onto the wound, and the blood stopped." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2911, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1790.)

* *

His saying: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾ means: He repaid you with grief for grief, as the Arabs say: "I stayed among the family of so-and-so" and "I stayed upon the family of so-and-so."

Ibn Jarir said: Likewise His saying: ﴿And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71], meaning upon the trunks of palm trees.

Ibn Abbas said: "The first grief was because of the defeat and when it was said: Muhammad (ﷺ) has been killed. The second was when the polytheists overcame them from above the mountain, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O Allah, they must not be allowed to prevail over us.'"

From Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: "The first grief was because of the defeat, and the second was when it was said: Muhammad (ﷺ) has been killed, and that was greater in their view than the defeat."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated both of these. Something similar was reported from Umar ibn al-Khattab. Ibn Abi Hatim also mentioned something similar from Qatadah.

Al-Suddi said: "The first grief was because of what they missed of the spoils and the victory, and the second was the enemy's looking down upon them."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾ means: one distress after another, the killing of those of your brothers who were killed, the enemy's rising over you, and what fell upon your hearts from the words of those who said: "Your Prophet has been killed." So that was successive upon you, grief upon grief.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: "The first grief was hearing of the killing of Muhammad, and the second was what befell them of killing and wounds." From Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, the reverse was reported.

From al-Suddi: "The first was what they missed of victory and spoils, and the second was the enemy's looking down upon them." This has already been mentioned from al-Suddi.

Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of these views is the view of the one who said: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾, meaning: He repaid you, O believers, with your grief at Allah's depriving you of the spoils of the polytheists, of victory over them and of triumph against them, and with what befell you of killing and wounds that day, after He had shown you in all that what you love, because of your disobedience to your Lord and your opposition to the command of the Prophet (ﷺ) - the grief of your thinking that your Prophet had been killed, and the enemy's advantage over you after your retreat from them.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that you would not grieve over what escaped you, nor over what befell you﴾ means: over what escaped you of the spoils from your enemy, ﴿nor over what befell you﴾ of killing and wounds. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi. ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾.

Allah warns His believing servants against obeying the disbelievers and the hypocrites, for obeying them brings ruin in this world and in the Hereafter. Therefore He says: ﴿If you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will turn about as losers.﴾

Then He commanded them to obey Him, to take Him as their Protector, to seek His help, and to rely upon Him. So He says: ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers.﴾

Then He gave them good news that He will cast fear of them into the hearts of their enemies, and humiliation before them, because of their disbelief and their association of partners with Allah, along with what He has stored up for them in the Hereafter of punishment and retribution. So He says: ﴿We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾

It is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things that were not given to any prophet before me: I was helped with terror (cast into the hearts of the enemy) over a distance of one month's journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration (masjid) and a means of purification (tahur); spoils of war have been made lawful for me; I have been given intercession; and every prophet was sent only to his own people, whereas I have been sent to all mankind."

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us from Sulayman, that is al-Taymi, from Sayyar, from Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My Lord has favoured me over the prophets, or he said: over the nations, with four things: I have been sent to all people; the whole earth has been made for me and for my community a place of prostration and a means of purification, so wherever a man of my community is overtaken by the prayer, his place of prostration is there and his purification is there; I have been helped with terror, which He casts into the hearts of my enemies over a distance of one month's journey; and the spoils have been made lawful for me."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it through Sulayman al-Taymi, from Sayyar al-Qurashi al-Umawi, their client, the Damascene, who settled in Basra, from Abu Umamah Suday ibn 'Ajlan, may Allah be pleased with him, with the same wording. He said: "Hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Abu Yunus narrated to him, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been helped with terror against the enemy."

Muslim also narrated it through Ibn Wahb.

Imam Ahmad narrated: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from his father, Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things: I have been sent to the red and the black (people); the earth has been made for me a means of purification and a place of prostration; spoils have been made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; I have been helped with terror over a distance of one month's journey; and I have been given intercession. Every prophet has asked for his intercession, but I have kept my intercession hidden, and I have made it for those among my community who die without associating anything with Allah."

Ahmad alone narrated it.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve﴾ that he said: Allah cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan, so he returned to Makkah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abu Sufyan has taken from you a portion, but he has returned, and Allah has cast terror into his heart." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah had promised them victory.

This verse may be used as evidence for one of the two opinions mentioned earlier concerning His words: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord supports you with three thousand angels sent down?" Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will support you with five thousand angels marked for battle.﴾ That this (promise) was on the day of Uhud, because their enemy was three thousand fighters. When they met them, victory and triumph belonged to Islam at the beginning of the day. But when what happened occurred, namely the disobedience of the archers and the failure of some of the fighters, the promise that had been conditioned upon steadfastness and obedience was postponed. Therefore He says: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you﴾, that is, at the beginning of the day, ﴿when you were killing them﴾, that is, you were slaying them, ﴿by His permission﴾, that is, by His empowering you over them. ﴿Until, when you lost courage﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: al-fashal means cowardice. ﴿And you disputed about the matter and disobeyed﴾, as occurred with the archers, ﴿after He had shown you that which you love﴾, which is victory over them. ﴿Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾, that is, then He gave them power over you in order to try you and examine you. ﴿And certainly He has pardoned you﴾, that is, He forgave you that act. And that, Allah knows best, was due to the large number and equipment of the enemy and the small number and equipment of the Muslims.

Ibn Jurayj said concerning His words: ﴿And certainly He has pardoned you﴾: He did not annihilate you. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said likewise. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated both. ﴿And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad informed us, from his father, from 'Ubaydullah, (in some copies "Abi 'Ubaydullah," but the correct form is what we have recorded from the Musnad), from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: Allah has not given victory in any battle as He gave it on the day of Uhud. He said: We denied that, so Ibn 'Abbas said: Between me and whoever denies that is the Book of Allah. Indeed Allah says concerning the day of Uhud: ﴿And certainly Allah fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-hass means killing. ﴿Until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed, after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world and among you are some who desire the Hereafter﴾, to the end of the verse. He meant by this only the archers. That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) had stationed them in one place and said: "Protect our backs. If you see us being killed, do not come to our aid; and if you see us gaining spoils, do not share them with us." When the Prophet (ﷺ) gained spoils and they (the Muslims) had routed the camp of the polytheists, the archers all rushed in and entered the camp, plundering. The lines of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came together, they were thus (and he interlaced his fingers before him) and they engaged. When the archers abandoned that gap in which they had been stationed, the cavalry entered through that spot upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and some of them struck others and they became confused. Many of the Muslims were killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions had been (dominant) at the beginning of the day, until seven or nine of the standard-bearers of the polytheists were killed. The Muslims withdrew in a retreat toward the mountain, but they did not reach the cave, as people say; rather they were under al-Mihras. Satan shouted: "Muhammad has been killed!" It was not doubted that this was true, and we continued in that state, not doubting that it was true, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appeared between the two Sa'ds. We recognized him by his gait when he walked. He said: So we rejoiced until it was as if no harm had befallen us. He said: He climbed toward us saying: "The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah." And he said again: "O Allah, they have no right to prevail over us." Until he reached us, he remained for a while, and then Abu Sufyan was shouting at the foot of the mountain: "Exalt Hubal!" twice, meaning his idol. "Where is the son of Abu Kabshah? Where is the son of Abu Quhafah? Where is the son of al-Khattab?" 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not answer him?" He said: "Yes." So when he said: "Exalt Hubal!", 'Umar said: "Allah is higher and greater!" Abu Sufyan said: "Our idol has been gratified, so turn away from it," or: "Be silent!" Then he said: "Where is the son of Abu Kabshah? Where is the son of Abu Quhafah? Where is the son of al-Khattab?" 'Umar said: "This is the Messenger of Allah, this is Abu Bakr, and here I am, 'Umar." He said: Abu Sufyan said: "A day for a day of Badr! The days are alternating, and war is a matter of turns." He said: 'Umar said: "No, they are not equal: our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire." He said: Abu Sufyan said: "You claim that, but we have indeed then lost and failed." Then Abu Sufyan said: "You will find among your slain mutilation, and that was not by the opinion of our leaders." He said: Then the zeal of the Jahiliyyah overtook him, and he said: "Indeed, if that happened, we did not dislike it."

This is a strange (gharib) report with a remarkable chain and context, and it is a mursal narration from Ibn 'Abbas, for he did not witness Uhud, nor did his father.

Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak from Abu al-Nadr al-Faqih, from 'Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Sulayman ibn Dawud ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, with the same wording. Thus Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah narrated it from the report of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi, with the same wording. Some of it has supporting reports in the Sahih collections and elsewhere. Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The women were on the day of Uhud behind the Muslims, finishing off the wounded of the polytheists. Had I sworn on that day, I would have hoped to be truthful that none of us desired this world, until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾. When the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) opposed and disobeyed what they had been commanded, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone with nine men: seven from the Ansar and two from Quraysh, and he was the tenth of them. When they overtook him, he said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who turns them back from us." A man from the Ansar stood up and fought for a while until he was killed. When they overtook him again, he said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who turns them back from us." He kept saying this until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companion: "We have not been fair to our companions."

Then Abu Sufyan came and said: "Exalted is Hubal!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is most high and most majestic!" They said: "Allah is most high and most majestic!" Abu Sufyan said: "We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is our Protector, and the disbelievers have no protector." Then Abu Sufyan said: "A day for a day of Badr: a day for us and a day against us, and a day of distress and a day of victory. Hanzalah for Hanzalah, and so-and-so for so-and-so, and so-and-so for so-and-so." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Not equal. Our dead are alive, being provided for, and your dead are in the Fire, being tormented." Abu Sufyan said: "There was mutilation among the people, and though it was not by my command, nor did I forbid it, nor did I like it or dislike it, nor did it grieve me or please me." He said: They looked and saw that Hamzah's belly had been ripped open, and Hind had taken his liver and chewed it but could not swallow it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Did she eat anything?" They said: "No." He said: "Allah would not have allowed any part of Hamzah to enter the Fire."

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed Hamzah and prayed over him. A man from the Ansar was brought and placed beside him, and he prayed over him; then the Ansari was lifted and Hamzah was left, then another was brought and placed beside Hamzah, and he prayed over him; then he was lifted and Hamzah was left, until he prayed over him that day seventy times.

Ahmad alone narrated it also (al-Musnad 1/462).

Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "We met the polytheists that day, and the Prophet (ﷺ) seated a group of archers and appointed over them 'Abdullah (meaning Ibn Jubayr), and said: 'Do not leave your position if you see us gaining the upper hand over them, and do not leave it if you see them gaining the upper hand over us, so do not come to our aid.' When we met them, they fled, until we saw the women running up the mountain, lifting their skirts, and their anklets were visible, so they began to say: 'The spoils! The spoils!' 'Abdullah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined me not to leave. But they refused, and when they refused, he turned their faces, and seventy were killed. Abu Sufyan looked over and said: 'Is Muhammad among the people?' He said: 'Do not answer him.' He said: 'Is Ibn Abi Quhafa among the people?' He said: 'Do not answer him.' He said: 'Is Ibn al-Khattab among the people?' He said: 'These have been killed, and if they were alive they would have answered.' 'Umar could not contain himself and said: 'You lie, enemy of Allah! Allah has left for you what will grieve you.' Abu Sufyan said: 'Exalted is Hubal!' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Answer him.' They said: 'What should we say?' He said: 'Say: Allah is most high and most majestic.' Abu Sufyan said: 'We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Answer him.' They said: 'What should we say?' He said: 'Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector.' Abu Sufyan said: 'A day for a day of Badr, and war is in turns (sijal), and you will find mutilation that I did not order, and it did not displease me.'"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this chain, and he also narrated it from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', with similar wording (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4043 and 3986). It will come later in more detail.

Al-Bukhari also said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: When the day of Uhud came, the polytheists were defeated, and Iblis shouted: "O servants of Allah, behind you!" So their first ranks turned back and fought against their last ranks. Hudhayfah looked and saw his father al-Yaman, and said: "O servants of Allah, my father, my father!" She said: By Allah, they did not stop until they killed him. Hudhayfah said: "May Allah forgive you." 'Urwah said: By Allah, goodness remained in Hudhayfah until he met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4065).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam said: "By Allah, I saw myself looking at the female servants of Hind and her companions, lifting their skirts and fleeing; nothing was taken by them, neither much nor little. The archers turned toward the camp when we had driven the people away from it, desiring the plunder, and they left our backs open to the cavalry, which came at us from behind. A crier cried out: 'Beware, Muhammad has been killed!'
