Thus Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah narrated it from the report of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi, with the same wording. Some of it has supporting reports in the Sahih collections and elsewhere. Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The women were on the day of Uhud behind the Muslims, finishing off the wounded of the polytheists. Had I sworn on that day, I would have hoped to be truthful that none of us desired this world, until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾. When the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) opposed and disobeyed what they had been commanded, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone with nine men: seven from the Ansar and two from Quraysh, and he was the tenth of them. When they overtook him, he said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who turns them back from us." A man from the Ansar stood up and fought for a while until he was killed. When they overtook him again, he said: "May Allah have mercy on a man who turns them back from us." He kept saying this until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companion: "We have not been fair to our companions."

Then Abu Sufyan came and said: "Exalted is Hubal!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is most high and most majestic!" They said: "Allah is most high and most majestic!" Abu Sufyan said: "We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is our Protector, and the disbelievers have no protector." Then Abu Sufyan said: "A day for a day of Badr: a day for us and a day against us, and a day of distress and a day of victory. Hanzalah for Hanzalah, and so-and-so for so-and-so, and so-and-so for so-and-so." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Not equal. Our dead are alive, being provided for, and your dead are in the Fire, being tormented." Abu Sufyan said: "There was mutilation among the people, and though it was not by my command, nor did I forbid it, nor did I like it or dislike it, nor did it grieve me or please me." He said: They looked and saw that Hamzah's belly had been ripped open, and Hind had taken his liver and chewed it but could not swallow it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Did she eat anything?" They said: "No." He said: "Allah would not have allowed any part of Hamzah to enter the Fire."

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed Hamzah and prayed over him. A man from the Ansar was brought and placed beside him, and he prayed over him; then the Ansari was lifted and Hamzah was left, then another was brought and placed beside Hamzah, and he prayed over him; then he was lifted and Hamzah was left, until he prayed over him that day seventy times.

Ahmad alone narrated it also (al-Musnad 1/462).

Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "We met the polytheists that day, and the Prophet (ﷺ) seated a group of archers and appointed over them 'Abdullah (meaning Ibn Jubayr), and said: 'Do not leave your position if you see us gaining the upper hand over them, and do not leave it if you see them gaining the upper hand over us, so do not come to our aid.' When we met them, they fled, until we saw the women running up the mountain, lifting their skirts, and their anklets were visible, so they began to say: 'The spoils! The spoils!' 'Abdullah said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined me not to leave. But they refused, and when they refused, he turned their faces, and seventy were killed. Abu Sufyan looked over and said: 'Is Muhammad among the people?' He said: 'Do not answer him.' He said: 'Is Ibn Abi Quhafa among the people?' He said: 'Do not answer him.' He said: 'Is Ibn al-Khattab among the people?' He said: 'These have been killed, and if they were alive they would have answered.' 'Umar could not contain himself and said: 'You lie, enemy of Allah! Allah has left for you what will grieve you.' Abu Sufyan said: 'Exalted is Hubal!' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Answer him.' They said: 'What should we say?' He said: 'Say: Allah is most high and most majestic.' Abu Sufyan said: 'We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Answer him.' They said: 'What should we say?' He said: 'Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector.' Abu Sufyan said: 'A day for a day of Badr, and war is in turns (sijal), and you will find mutilation that I did not order, and it did not displease me.'"

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this chain, and he also narrated it from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', with similar wording (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4043 and 3986). It will come later in more detail.

Al-Bukhari also said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: When the day of Uhud came, the polytheists were defeated, and Iblis shouted: "O servants of Allah, behind you!" So their first ranks turned back and fought against their last ranks. Hudhayfah looked and saw his father al-Yaman, and said: "O servants of Allah, my father, my father!" She said: By Allah, they did not stop until they killed him. Hudhayfah said: "May Allah forgive you." 'Urwah said: By Allah, goodness remained in Hudhayfah until he met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4065).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam said: "By Allah, I saw myself looking at the female servants of Hind and her companions, lifting their skirts and fleeing; nothing was taken by them, neither much nor little. The archers turned toward the camp when we had driven the people away from it, desiring the plunder, and they left our backs open to the cavalry, which came at us from behind. A crier cried out: 'Beware, Muhammad has been killed!' So we turned back, and the people turned back upon us after we had struck the bearers of the banner, so that none of the people could come near it."

Ibn Ishaq said: The banner of the polytheists remained fallen until 'Amrah bint 'Alqamah al-Harithiyyah took it, and she gave it to Quraysh, and they rallied around it (Sirah Ibn Ishaq, Zahiriyyah MS, folio 170).

And al-Suddi narrated from 'Abd Khayr, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "I did not think that any of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) desired the world until there was revealed concerning us what was revealed on the day of Uhud: ﴿Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾."

It has been narrated through other chains from Ibn Mas'ud, and likewise from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and Abu Talhah, which Ibn Mardawayh recorded in his tafsir.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾. Ibn Ishaq said: al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi', one of the Banu 'Adi ibn al-Najjar, narrated to me, saying: Anas ibn al-Nadr, the uncle of Anas ibn Malik, passed by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah, among men of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, who had laid down their arms. He said: "What keeps you (here)?" They said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been killed." He said: "What is the point of life after him? Get up and die as he died." Then he faced the people and fought until he was killed.

Al-Bukhari said: Hassan ibn Hassan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Talhah narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik: that his uncle (meaning Anas ibn al-Nadr) was absent from Badr and said: "I was absent from the first battle the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought. If Allah lets me witness a battle with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah will see what I do." Then at Uhud the people fled, and he said: "O Allah, I apologize to You for what these people have done (meaning the Muslims), and I disown to You what the polytheists have brought." He advanced with his sword and met Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and said: "Where, O Sa'd? Indeed I smell the fragrance of Paradise beyond Uhud." He went on and was killed. He was not recognized until his sister recognized him by his fingertips, with a mark, and he had more than eighty wounds from stabbing, striking and arrow shots.

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Thabit from Anas, with similar wording (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4048; Sahih Muslim, no. 1903).

Al-Bukhari also said: 'Abdan narrated to us, Abu Hamzah informed us, from 'Uthman ibn Mawhab, who said: A man who had performed Hajj to the House saw a group sitting, and said: "Who are these sitters?" They said: "These are Quraysh." He said: "Who is the elder?" They said: "Ibn 'Umar." He came to him and said: "I will ask you about something, so tell me. I adjure you by the sanctity of this House: do you know that 'Uthman ibn 'Affan fled on the day of Uhud?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know that he was absent from Badr and did not witness it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know that he stayed away from the Pledge of al-Ridwan and did not witness it?" He said: "Yes." He said: Then he exclaimed Allahu akbar. Ibn 'Umar said: "Come, I will inform you and explain to you what you asked me about. As for his fleeing on the day of Uhud, I bear witness that Allah has pardoned him. As for his absence from Badr, he had under him the daughter of the Prophet (ﷺ), who was ill, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'You have the reward of a man who witnessed Badr, and his share.' As for his staying away from the Pledge of al-Ridwan, if anyone was more honored in the valley of Makkah than 'Uthman, he would have sent him instead of him. So he sent 'Uthman, and the Pledge of al-Ridwan took place after 'Uthman had gone to Makkah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said with his right hand: "This is the hand of 'Uthman," and struck it upon his other hand, and said: "This is the hand of 'Uthman; go with it now."

Then al-Bukhari narrated it through another chain, from Abu 'Awanah, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mawhab (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4066 and 3698).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿When you were going up and not turning back for anyone﴾, that is, He turned you away from them, ﴿when you were going up﴾, that is, up the mountain, fleeing from your enemies.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah read: ﴿When you were going up﴾, that is, up the mountain, ﴿and not turning back for anyone﴾, that is, while you did not turn back for anyone out of bewilderment, fear and terror, ﴿while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾, that is, while he was behind you, calling you to stop fleeing from the enemies, and to return, come back and charge again.

Al-Suddi said: When the polytheists attacked the Muslims at Uhud and routed them, some of them entered Madinah, and some of them went up the mountain to the rock and stood upon it, while the Messenger (ﷺ) was calling the people: "Come to me, servants of Allah! Come to me, servants of Allah!" So Allah mentioned their going up the mountain, then mentioned the Prophet's (ﷺ) calling to them, saying: ﴿When you were going up and not turning back for anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, al-Rabi' and Ibn Zayd said likewise.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ari, who was still a polytheist and had not yet embraced Islam, composed a poem describing the defeat of the Muslims at Uhud, whose opening is:

O crow of separation, have you heard? Then say, for you speak only of what has already happened...
Indeed for good and for evil there is an end, and both are a direction and a turn...

Then he said:

Would that my elders had witnessed Badr, the Khazraj's dismay at the striking of spears,
When their camels knelt at Quba' and the slaughter raged among the 'Abd al-Ashhal;
Then they hurried away at that moment, dancing like the young camels dance, rising upon the hill.
We killed double of their nobles, and the scale of Badr was balanced.

Al-Hiffan: the young of camels.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 149–153 (part 3 of 4):

The Prophet (ﷺ) had been left with only twelve men of his Companions, as al-Imam Ahmad related: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abu Ishaq narrated to us that al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: On the day of Uhud, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr over the archers, who were fifty men, and he placed them in a position and said: "If you see us being snatched by the birds, do not leave your position until I send for you. And if you see us gaining the upper hand over the enemy and trampling them, do not leave your position until I send for you." He said: They routed them. He said: By Allah, I saw the women running up the mountain, their ankles and anklets showing, their garments raised. The companions of 'Abd Allah said: The spoils! O people, the spoils! Your companions have prevailed, so what are you waiting for? 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr said: Have you forgotten what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to you? They said: By Allah, we will go to the people and take a share of the spoils. When they reached them, their faces were turned away and they retreated in defeat. That is what the Messenger called them back to, from behind them. Only twelve men remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They inflicted seventy casualties upon us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions had inflicted on the polytheists at Badr one hundred and forty: seventy captives and seventy killed. Abu Sufyan said: Is Muhammad among the people? Is Muhammad among the people? Is Muhammad among the people? (three times). He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade them from answering him. Then he said: Is the son of Abu Quhafah among the people? Is the son of Abu Quhafah among the people? Is the son of al-Khattab among the people? Is the son of al-Khattab among the people? Then he turned to his companions and said: As for these, they have been killed; you have been spared them. 'Umar could not restrain himself and said: You lie, by Allah, O enemy of Allah! Those whom you named are all alive, and what will grieve you still remains. Abu Sufyan said: A day for a day of Badr, and war is a matter of turns (sijal). Indeed, you will find among the people mutilation which I did not order, and which did not displease me. Then he began to chant rhythmically, saying: "Exalt Hubal! Exalt Hubal!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Will you not answer him?" They said: O Messenger of Allah, what should we say? He said: "Say: Allah is higher and more majestic." He said: We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Will you not answer him?" They said: O Messenger of Allah, what should we say? He said: "Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector." (Al-Musnad, 4/293.)

Al-Bukhari related it from the hadith (prophetic report) of Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah in an abridged form, and he related it from the hadith of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, in a more detailed form, as has already passed. And Allah knows best.

Al-Bayhaqi related in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, from the hadith of 'Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The people fled from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, and there remained with him eleven men from the Ansar and Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah, while he was climbing the mountain. The polytheists came upon them, and he (ﷺ) said: "Is there anyone for these?" Talhah said: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Stay where you are, O Talhah." A man from the Ansar said: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He fought on his behalf and was killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those with him then ascended. Then the Ansari was killed, and they came upon him. He said: "Is there a man for these?" Talhah said the same as before, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said the same as before. A man from the Ansar said: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He fought on his behalf, and his companions went up. Then he was killed, and they came upon him. He kept saying the same as his first words, and Talhah would say: I am, O Messenger of Allah. He would hold him back, and a man from the Ansar would ask his permission to fight, and he would permit him, and he would fight as those before him had fought, until none remained with him except Talhah, and they were surrounded. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who will take care of these?" Talhah said: I am. He fought with the fighting of all who had been before him, and his fingertips were injured. He said: "Hiss!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you had said, 'In the name of Allah,' and mentioned the name of Allah, the angels would have lifted you up while the people looked at you, until you vanished into the air of the sky." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went up to his Companions, who were gathered together.

Al-Bukhari related from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Waki', from Isma'il, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: I saw the hand of Talhah paralysed, with which he shielded the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning on the day of Uhud.

In the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: On some of those days in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought, there remained with him none except Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah and Sa'd, according to their report.

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from 'Ali ibn Zayd and Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was left alone on the day of Uhud with seven men from the Ansar and two men from Quraysh. When they overwhelmed him, he said: "Who will repel them from us, and he will have Paradise?" or "and he will be my companion in Paradise?" A man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. Then they overwhelmed him again, and he said: "Who will repel them from us, and he will have Paradise?" A man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. And so it continued until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his two companions: "We have not dealt justly with our companions."

Muslim related it from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same meaning.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: Ibn Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hashim ibn Hashim al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: I heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him) say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) emptied his quiver for me on the day of Uhud, and said: "Shoot, may my father and mother be your ransom."

(Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: nathala, meaning he shook out for me, i.e., the Messenger of Allah emptied out for me.)

Al-Bukhari related it from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah. (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4055.)

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to me, from some of the family of Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he shot on the day of Uhud in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Sa'd said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) handing me arrows and saying: "Shoot, may my father and mother be your ransom," until he would hand me an arrow with no head on it, and I would shoot with it.

It is firmly established in the Sahihayn, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from his grandfather, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: On the day of Uhud I saw, to the right and left of the Prophet (ﷺ), two men in white garments, fighting on his behalf with the utmost fierceness. I had not seen them before that day or after it. He meant Jibril and Mika'il (peace be upon them). (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4054; Sahih Muslim, no. 2306.)

Abu al-Aswad said, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf, brother of Banu Jumah, had sworn while in Makkah that he would kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When his oath reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Rather, I will kill him, if Allah wills." When the day of Uhud came, Ubayy approached in his armour, his face covered, saying: "I shall not survive if Muhammad survives!" He charged at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), intending to kill him. Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, brother of Banu 'Abd al-Dar, confronted him, shielding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with his own self, and Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr was killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the collarbone of Ubayy ibn Khalaf through a gap between the coat of mail and the helmet, and he struck him there with his spear. He fell from his horse to the ground, and no blood came out from his wound. His companions came to him and carried him, while he was bellowing like a bull. They said to him: Why are you so distressed? It is only a scratch! He mentioned to them the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I will kill Ubayy." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, if this which I have were distributed among the people of Dhu al-Majaz, they would all die." He died on the way to Hell, so far away be the companions of the Blaze.

Musa ibn 'Uqbah related it in his Maghazi (Military Campaigns), from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, in similar wording.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was propped up in the mountain pass, Ubayy ibn Khalaf reached him, saying: "I shall not survive if you survive!" The people said: O Messenger of Allah, shall one of us turn against him? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave him." When he drew near, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the spear from al-Harith ibn al-Simmah. One of the people said what was related to me: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it from him, he (Ubayy) shook violently, and we scattered away from him like hair scattering from the back of a camel when it shakes. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) approached him and struck him in the neck with a blow, from which he fell from his horse several times.

Al-Waqidi mentioned, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Amr ibn Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, something similar to this. (Sirat Ibn Ishaq, Zahiriyyah manuscript, folio 171, in the recension of Muhammad ibn Salamah.)

Al-Waqidi said: Ibn 'Umar used to say: Ubayy ibn Khalaf died at Batn Raghigh. I was traveling through Batn Raghigh after part of the night had passed, when I suddenly saw a fire blazing. I was frightened by it, and then a man came out of it, dragged by a chain, while thirst was tormenting him, and a man was saying: "Do not give him water, for this is the slain of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), this is Ubayy ibn Khalaf."

It is firmly established in the Sahihayn, from the narration of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who did this to the Messenger of Allah" (and at that time he was pointing to his molar tooth), "The anger of Allah has intensified against a man whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kills in the way of Allah." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4073; Sahih Muslim, no. 1793.)

Al-Bukhari also related it (Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4074, 4076) from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The anger of Allah has intensified against the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed with his own hand in the way of Allah. The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The molar tooth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was struck, his cheek was split open, and his lip was wounded. The one who inflicted it was 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas.

Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to me, from one who had narrated to him, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: I never desired to kill anyone as much as I desired to kill 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas, though as far as I knew he was ill-tempered and hated among his people. The saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sufficed me concerning him: "The anger of Allah has intensified against the one who wounded the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." (Sirat Ibn Ishaq, Zahiriyyah manuscript, folio 172.)

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Uthman al-Jazari, from Miqsam, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invoked against 'Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas on the day of Uhud, when he broke his molar tooth and wounded his face, saying: "O Allah, let not the year pass over him until he dies a disbeliever." He had not completed a year before he died a disbeliever, bound for the Fire. (Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq, 1/136.)

Al-Waqidi reported from Ibn Abi Sabra, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Farwa, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard a man from the Muhajirun say: "I was present at Uhud, and I saw the arrows coming from every direction, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the middle of them, and every one of them was turned away from him. I also saw Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri saying that day: 'Show me Muhammad! I will not be saved if he is saved.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was beside him with no one else with him. Then he passed by him and was rebuked for this by Safwan, who said: 'By Allah, I did not see him. I swear by Allah that he is protected from us.' We set out four men, made a pact and agreed to kill him, but we did not get close to that."

Al-Waqidi said: "What is established according to us is that the one who struck the cheek of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was Ibn Qami'a, and the one who wounded his lip and struck his front tooth (ruba'iyyah) was Utba ibn Abi Waqqas."

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, who said: Isa ibn Talha informed me, from Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), whenever he mentioned the Day of Uhud, would say: 'That whole day belonged to Talha.' Then he began to narrate: 'I was the first to return on the Day of Uhud, and I saw a man fighting alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), defending him' - and I think he said 'out of zeal' - 'and I said: Be Talha! Since what I missed has escaped me, I said: a man from my own people would be dearer to me. Between me and the polytheists there was a man whom I did not recognize, and I was closer to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than he was, and he was moving swiftly in a manner I cannot describe. Then it turned out to be Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah. We reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and his front tooth had been broken and his face was wounded, and two rings of the helmet had entered his cheek. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Attend to your companion," meaning Talha, who was bleeding profusely, but we did not pay attention to his words. He said: I went to pull that out of his face, but Abu Ubayda said: I adjure you by my right over you that you leave me. So I left him. He disliked to take hold of them with his hand lest he hurt the Prophet (ﷺ), so he clenched them with his teeth and pulled out one of the two rings, and his tooth fell out with the ring. I went to do what he had done, but he said: I adjure you by my right over you that you leave me. He did the same as he had done the first time, and his other front tooth fell out with the ring. Abu Ubayda (may Allah be pleased with him) was the most graceful of people in losing his teeth. Then we tended to the affairs of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then we came to Talha in one of those ditches, and he had more than seventy wounds, or fewer or more, from stabbing, shooting and striking, and his finger had been cut off, so we tended to his condition."

Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb and al-Tabarani also narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Yahya. In al-Haytham's version: Abu Ubayda said: "I beseech you, O Abu Bakr, by Allah, to leave me?" Then Abu Ubayda took the arrowhead with his mouth and began to move it gently, out of dislike that it would hurt the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he pulled the arrowhead out with his mouth, and Abu Ubayda's tooth was dislodged.

He mentioned its full text, and al-Hafiz Diya al-Maqdisi chose it in his book. (Musnad al-Tayalisi, p. 3, and al-Mukhtarah of Diya al-Maqdisi, no. 49, through the route of al-Haytham ibn Kulayb. al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. 63, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 4941 (al-Ihsan), narrated it through the route of Ishaq ibn Yahya. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6/112): "In it is Ishaq ibn Yahya, who is matruk (abandoned).")

Ali ibn al-Madini declared this hadith weak because of this Ishaq ibn Yahya, for Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, Ahmad, Yahya ibn Ma'in, al-Bukhari, Abu Zur'a, Abu Hatim, Muhammad ibn Sa'd, al-Nasa'i and others criticized him.

Ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Umar ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to him that it reached him that Malik, the father (Abi) of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was wounded on the Day of Uhud, sucked the wound until he cleaned it and it shone white. He was told: "Spit it out." He said: "No, by Allah, I will never spit it out." Then he turned back to fight. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to look at a man of the people of Paradise, let him look at this one." And he was martyred. (Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (3/266) through the route of Ibn Wahb.)

It is established in the two Sahihs, through the route of Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim, from his father, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, that he was asked about the wound of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was wounded, his front tooth was broken, and the helmet was crushed on his head. Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was washing the blood, and Ali was pouring water on it with a shield. When Fatimah saw that the water only increased the blood, she took a piece of mat and burned it, and when it became ash, she pressed it onto the wound, and the blood stopped." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2911, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1790.)

* *

His saying: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾ means: He repaid you with grief for grief, as the Arabs say: "I stayed among the family of so-and-so" and "I stayed upon the family of so-and-so."

Ibn Jarir said: Likewise His saying: ﴿And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71], meaning upon the trunks of palm trees.

Ibn Abbas said: "The first grief was because of the defeat and when it was said: Muhammad (ﷺ) has been killed. The second was when the polytheists overcame them from above the mountain, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O Allah, they must not be allowed to prevail over us.'"

From Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: "The first grief was because of the defeat, and the second was when it was said: Muhammad (ﷺ) has been killed, and that was greater in their view than the defeat."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated both of these. Something similar was reported from Umar ibn al-Khattab. Ibn Abi Hatim also mentioned something similar from Qatadah.

Al-Suddi said: "The first grief was because of what they missed of the spoils and the victory, and the second was the enemy's looking down upon them."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾ means: one distress after another, the killing of those of your brothers who were killed, the enemy's rising over you, and what fell upon your hearts from the words of those who said: "Your Prophet has been killed." So that was successive upon you, grief upon grief.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: "The first grief was hearing of the killing of Muhammad, and the second was what befell them of killing and wounds." From Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, the reverse was reported.

From al-Suddi: "The first was what they missed of victory and spoils, and the second was the enemy's looking down upon them." This has already been mentioned from al-Suddi.

Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of these views is the view of the one who said: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾, meaning: He repaid you, O believers, with your grief at Allah's depriving you of the spoils of the polytheists, of victory over them and of triumph against them, and with what befell you of killing and wounds that day, after He had shown you in all that what you love, because of your disobedience to your Lord and your opposition to the command of the Prophet (ﷺ) - the grief of your thinking that your Prophet had been killed, and the enemy's advantage over you after your retreat from them.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that you would not grieve over what escaped you, nor over what befell you﴾ means: over what escaped you of the spoils from your enemy, ﴿nor over what befell you﴾ of killing and wounds. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi. ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾.

Allah the Exalted says, bestowing favour upon His servants regarding what He sent down upon them of tranquillity (sakinah) and security (amanah), which is the drowsiness (nu'as) that overtook them while they were clad in their weapons, in the midst of their distress and grief. Drowsiness in such a state is a sign of safety (amn), as Allah the Exalted said in Surat al-Anfal, concerning the story of Badr: ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him, and sent down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it, to remove from you the evil of Satan, to strengthen your hearts and to make your feet firm﴾ [al-Anfal: 11].

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman, said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym and Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Drowsiness in battle is from Allah, and drowsiness in prayer is from Satan."

Al-Bukhari said: Khalifah narrated to me: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from Abu Talhah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I was among those who were overcome by drowsiness on the Day of Uhud, until my sword kept falling from my hand repeatedly; it would fall and I would pick it up, and it would fall and I would pick it up."

He narrated it thus in the Maghazi as a mu'allaq (suspended narration). He narrated it in the Book of Tafsir as a musnad (connected narration) from Shayban, from Qatadah, from Anas, from Abu Talhah, who said: "Drowsiness overtook us while we were in our battle lines on the Day of Uhud." He said: "My sword kept falling from my hand, and I would pick it up, and it would fall and I would pick it up."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, from Abu Talhah, who said: "I raised my head on the Day of Uhud and began to look, and there was not one of them that day but was swaying beneath his shield from drowsiness." This is the wording of al-Tirmidhi, who said: "Hasan sahih."

al-Nasa'i also narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Khalid ibn al-Harith, from Abu Qutaybah, from Ibn Abi 'Adi, all of them from Humayd, from Anas, who said: Abu Talhah said: "I was among those upon whom drowsiness was cast..." and the hadith follows.

Similarly it has been narrated from al-Zubayr and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, may Allah be pleased with him [them both].

Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed me, Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Thaqafi informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak al-Makhzumi narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shaybân narrated to us, from Qatadah, Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, that Abu Talhah said: "Drowsiness overtook us while we were in our battle lines on the Day of Uhud, and my sword kept falling from my hand, and I would pick it up, and it would fall and I would pick it up." He said: "The other group, the hypocrites, had no concern except for themselves, the most cowardly and most foolish of people, and most forsaking of the truth, ﴿thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah﴾, liars, people of doubt and suspicion regarding Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

He narrated it with this addition, and it seems to be from the words of Qatadah, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is as he said. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then after the distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness overcoming a group of you﴾, meaning: the people of faith, certainty, steadfastness, and true reliance upon Allah, who were certain that Allah would help His Messenger and fulfil his hope. For this reason He said: ﴿And another group, whose own selves had concerned them﴾, meaning: drowsiness did not overcome them due to anxiety, panic and fear, ﴿thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Jahiliyyah﴾, as He said in another verse: ﴿Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made attractive in your hearts, and you thought an evil thought, and you were a corrupt people﴾ [al-Fath: 12]. Likewise these people believed that when the polytheists prevailed at that moment, that would be the decisive end, and that Islam and its people had been destroyed. This is the condition of people of doubt and suspicion: when a dreadful matter occurs, these abominable suspicions arise in them.

Then Allah informed about them that they ﴿say﴾ in that state: ﴿Is there anything for us in the affair?﴾ Allah said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the affair is entirely for Allah.﴾ ﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you.﴾ Then He explained what they concealed within themselves by His saying: ﴿They say: If there had been anything for us in the affair, we would not have been killed here.﴾ That is, they would secretly say this statement about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Yahya ibn 'Abbad ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: al-Zubayr said: "I saw myself with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when fear intensified upon us; Allah sent sleep upon us, and none of us was there but his chin was on his chest. He said: By Allah, I was hearing the words of Mu'tab ibn Qushayr, which I heard only as in a dream: ﴿If there had been anything for us in the affair, we would not have been killed here.﴾ So I memorised it from him, and concerning that Allah sent down ﴿If there had been anything for us in the affair, we would not have been killed here﴾, in reference to the saying of Mu'tab." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Allah said: ﴿Say: Even if you had been in your houses, those decreed to be killed would have gone forth to their resting places.﴾ That is: this is a predestined decree from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and a definite judgment that cannot be averted, and there is no escape from it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts﴾, that is: He tests you by what befell you, to distinguish the bad from the good, and to make manifest to the people the condition of the believer and the hypocrite in words and deeds. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, that is: of what is hidden in the innermost thoughts and consciences.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned﴾, that is: because of some of their earlier sins. As some of the Salaf said: "Indeed, among the reward of a good deed is a good deed after it, and among the recompense of an evil deed is an evil deed after it."

Then Allah said: ﴿And Allah has certainly pardoned them﴾, that is: for what they did of fleeing, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾, that is: He forgives sins, shows forbearance toward His creation, and overlooks their faults. The hadith of Ibn 'Umar concerning 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, and his turning away on the Day of Uhud, and that Allah had pardoned them, has already been mentioned at His saying: ﴿And Allah had certainly pardoned you﴾, and its mention is fitting here.

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Shaqiq, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf met al-Walid ibn 'Uqbah, and al-Walid said to him: "Why do I see you have shunned the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman?" 'Abd al-Rahman said to him: "Convey to him that I did not flee on the Day of 'Aynayn" ('Asim said: he means the Day of Uhud), "nor did I stay away from Badr, and I did not abandon the Sunnah of 'Umar." He said: So he went and informed 'Uthman of that. He said: "As for his saying that I did not flee on the Day of 'Aynayn, how can he reproach me for a sin which Allah has pardoned? He said: ﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned, and Allah has certainly pardoned them﴾. As for his saying that I stayed away from Badr, I was nursing Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until she died, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ allotted a share to me, and whoever was allotted a share by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has attended. As for his saying 'I did not abandon the Sunnah of 'Umar,' I am not able to follow it, and neither is he. So go to him and tell him this."

He, exalted is He, forbids His believing servants from resembling the disbelievers in their corrupt belief, which is indicated by their saying about their brothers who died while traveling or [[In J, R, and W: "or"]] in battles: "If they had not done that, what befell them would not have befallen them." So He said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers﴾, meaning concerning their brothers, ﴿when they traveled through the land﴾, meaning traveled for trade and the like [[In J: "and others."]], ﴿or were raiders﴾, meaning in a raid, ﴿"Had they been with us, they would not have died or been killed"﴾ [[In R: "nor"]], meaning they would not have died while traveling or been killed in a raid.

* *

His saying: ﴿So that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts﴾ means: He created this belief in their souls so that they would increase in regret over their dead and their slain [[In J, R, A, and W: "their dead and their slain."]]. Then He, exalted is He, said in refutation of them: ﴿And Allah gives life and causes death﴾, meaning the creation is in His hand and the matter returns to Him. No one lives or dies except by His will and decree, and no one's lifespan is lengthened or shortened except by His decree and destiny. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, meaning His knowledge and sight penetrate all His creation, and nothing about their affairs is hidden from Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you are killed in the cause of Allah or die, then forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they accumulate﴾ includes that being killed in the cause of Allah, and dying as well, is a means to attaining Allah's mercy, His pardon, and His good pleasure, and that is better than remaining in this world and gathering its perishing trash.

Then He informed that everyone who dies or is killed, his destination and return is to Allah, mighty and majestic, and He will recompense him for his deed: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil. So He said: ﴿And if you die or are killed, indeed to Allah you will be gathered.﴾

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 159–164 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), bestowing favour upon him and upon the believers regarding how He softened his heart toward his community, those who follow his command and abandon opposing his rebuke, and He made his speech gentle toward them: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them﴾, meaning: what made you gentle toward them? Had it not been for the mercy of Allah upon you and upon them.

Qatadah said: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them﴾ means: "So it was by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them." And "mā" (مَا) is a *ṣila* (a particle that adds no meaning and serves to connect and emphasise). The Arabs attach it to a definite noun, as in His saying ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾ (An-Nisa 155; Al-Ma'idah 13), and to an indefinite noun, as in His saying ﴿After a little while﴾ (Al-Mu'minun 40). Likewise here, He said ﴿So by mercy from Allah﴾, meaning: "by a mercy from Allah."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "This is the character of Muhammad (ﷺ) with which Allah sent him."

This noble verse resembles His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; he is zealous over you; for the believers he is kind and merciful﴾ (At-Tawbah 128).

Imam Ahmad said: Haywah narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Abu Rashid al-Hubrani narrated to me, saying: Abu Umamah al-Bahili took hold of my hand and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of my hand and said: "O Abu Umamah, among the believers are those whose hearts soften toward me." Ahmad alone narrated it.

Then He said: ﴿And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you﴾. *Fazz* (فَظّ) means harsh, coarse. The intended meaning here is coarse speech, as shown by His words after it, ﴿hard-hearted﴾. That is: "If you had been bad in speech and hard-hearted toward them, they would have dispersed from you and abandoned you. But Allah gathered them around you and made you gentle toward them, to win their hearts." This is like what 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: that he saw the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the earlier scriptures: that he was not harsh, nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, and he did not repay evil with evil, but pardoned and overlooked. [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4838.]

Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Tirmidhi narrated, Bishr ibn 'Ubayd al-Darimi informed us, 'Ammar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah commanded me to be patient and gentle with people, just as He commanded me to establish the obligatory duties." Gharib (a strange narration). [Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in *Thalatha Majalis min al-Amali* no. 42, Ibn 'Adi in *al-Kamil* (2/15), and al-Daylami in *Musnad al-Firdaws* no. 659, through Bishr ibn 'Ubayd. Ibn 'Adi said: Bishr ibn 'Ubayd is "munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected) regarding the imams. al-Dhahabi cited hadiths from him, including this one, then said: "These hadiths are not authentic, so Allah is the one to seek help from."]

Therefore He said: ﴿So pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter﴾. Accordingly, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would consult his companions on matters when they arose, to comfort their hearts, so that they would be more eager to carry out what they were doing. He consulted them on the day of Badr regarding going out to the caravan. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you were to lead us across the sea, we would cross it with you; if you were to take us to Bark al-Ghimad, we would go with you. We will not say to you what the people of Musa said to Musa: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will sit here.' Rather we say: Go forward, and we are with you, before you, behind you, on your right and on your left, fighting."

He also consulted them about where the camp should be, until al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr al-Mu'tiq suggested that they advance ahead of the people. He consulted them at Uhud about whether to remain in Madinah or go out to the enemy. The majority of them advised going out to meet them, so he went out to them.

He consulted them on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) about reconciling with the confederates by giving them a third of Madinah's produce that year. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah refused this, so he abandoned it.

He consulted them at Hudaybiyyah about attacking the children of the polytheists. Abu Bakr said to him: "We did not come to fight anyone; we only came as pilgrims (for 'umrah)." So he agreed to what he said.

He (ﷺ) also said, in the matter of the slander (al-ifk): "Advise me, O assembly of Muslims, concerning people who have slandered my family and accused them. By Allah, I know nothing but good about my family, and they have slandered a man of whom, by Allah, I know nothing but good." He consulted 'Ali and Usamah concerning separating from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

So he would consult them in wars and similar matters. The jurists have differed as to whether this was obligatory upon him or was a recommended practice to comfort their hearts, on two views.

Al-Hakim said in his *Mustadrak*: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub al-'Allaf narrated to us in Egypt, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and consult them in the matter﴾, he said: "Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both." Then he said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [*al-Mustadrak* (3/70).]

Similarly, al-Kalbi narrated it from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and they were the closest companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his two ministers, and the two fathers of the Muslims.

Imam Ahmad also narrated: Waki' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and 'Umar: "If you two were to agree on a consultation, I would not oppose you both." [*al-Musnad* (4/227).]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about *al-'azm* (determination/resolve), and he said: "Consulting the people of opinion, then following them." [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in *al-Durr* (2/360), attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh.]

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Shaybān, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who is consulted is trustworthy (mu'taman)."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, and al-Nasa'i graded it *hasan*, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, with more detail than this.

Then Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who is consulted is trustworthy." Narrated by him alone.

[And he also said:] Abu Bakr narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah and 'Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of you seeks counsel from his brother, let him advise him." Narrated by him alone as well.

* * *

His saying: ﴿Then when you have decided, rely upon Allah﴾, meaning: when you have consulted them on the matter and resolved upon it, then rely upon Allah in it. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him.﴾

* * *

His saying: ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾. This is as previously stated in His saying: ﴿And victory is only from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (Al 'Imran 126). Then He commanded them to rely upon Him, saying: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

* * *

His saying: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate (an-yaghull)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and others said: It is not befitting for a prophet to betray (yakhun).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Musayyab ibn Wadih narrated to us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khasif, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A cloak (qatifah) was missing on the day of Badr, and they said: "Perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, meaning: to betray.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Khasif narrated to us, Miqsam narrated to us, Ibn 'Abbas told me that this verse, ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, was revealed concerning a red cloak that went missing on the day of Badr. Some people said: "He took it." He said: They spoke a great deal about it, so Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate. And whoever misappropriates will bring what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it, from Qutaybah, from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, with the same chain. al-Tirmidhi said: *hasan gharib*. Some of them narrated it from Khasif, from Miqsam, as a *mursal* (a report missing a companion from its chain).

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The hypocrites accused the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of something that went missing, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate.﴾

This has been narrated from other routes from Ibn 'Abbas, similar to what has preceded. This is a clearing of him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, from all forms of treachery in the discharge of the trust, the division of the spoils, and other matters.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, meaning: by giving a share to some of the expeditions (*sarāyā*) and withholding from others. Al-Dahhak said likewise.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾ means by withholding part of what was revealed to him, so he does not convey it to his community.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, Tawus, Mujahid and al-Dahhak recited it: ﴿yughalla﴾ with a *damma* on the *ya'* (*yughall*), meaning: he is betrayed (*yukhan*).

Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: This verse was revealed on the day of Badr, when some of his companions had misappropriated. Ibn Jarir narrated it from both of them. Then he related from some of them that he explained this reading in the sense of "being accused of betrayal."

Then He said: ﴿And whoever misappropriates will bring what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ This is a severe warning and a firm threat. The Sunnah has also come with the prohibition of this in numerous hadiths.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, Zuhayr (meaning Ibn Muhammad) narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The gravest misappropriation before Allah is a cubit of land. You find two men who are neighbours in land, or in a house, and one of them takes a cubit from the share of his companion. When he takes it, it will be hung around his neck from seven earths until the Day of Resurrection." [*al-Musnad* (4/140).]

In the Two Sahihs, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wrongfully takes even a span of land, it will be hung around his neck from the seven earths on the Day of Resurrection." [Addition from A and W.] [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2452; Sahih Muslim, no. 1610.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Ibn Hubayrah and al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is appointed over a task for us and has no dwelling, let him acquire a dwelling; or if he has no wife, let him marry; or if he has no servant, let him acquire a servant; or if he has no mount, let him acquire a mount. Whoever takes anything beyond that is a embezzler (ghall)." [Al-Musnad (4/229).]

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it. Abu Dawud narrated it with a different chain and different wording, saying:

Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqqi related to us, al-Mu'afa related to us, al-Awza'i related to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid [in G and A: Shurayk], from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is a worker for us, let him acquire a wife; if he has no servant, let him acquire a servant; if he has no dwelling, let him acquire a dwelling." He said: Abu Bakr said: I was informed that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes other than that is an embezzler (ghall), or a thief." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2945.]

Our shaykh, the hafiz al-Mizzi [may Allah have mercy on him] [addition from W], said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated it from Musa ibn Marwan and said: "from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr" instead of "Jubayr ibn Nufayr," and this is closer to the correct version.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Hafs ibn Bishr related to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, Hafs ibn Humayd related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a sheep that bleats, calling out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.' And I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel that roars, calling out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.' And I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a horse that neighs, calling out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.' And I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying pieces of leather [addition from G, R and Tabari; in A and W: "two pieces"] that call out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.'"

No one among the authors of the Six Books narrated it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (7/358).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Zuhri, who heard Urwah say: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi informed us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed a man from the Azd called Ibn al-Lutbiyyah over the zakat. He came and said: "This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on the pulpit and said: "What is the matter with the worker whom we send, and he comes and says: 'This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift'? Why did he not sit in the house of his father and mother and see whether a gift would be given to him or not? By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you takes anything from it but that he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection upon his neck: if it is a camel, it will have a roar; if a cow, it will have a low; or if a sheep, it will bleat." Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits, and said: "O Allah, have I conveyed?" three times.

Hisham ibn Urwah added: Abu Humayd said: "My eyes saw it and my ears heard it; and ask Zayd ibn Thabit."

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah [Al-Musnad (5/423); Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2597, 7174; Sahih Muslim, no. 1832.] — and in al-Bukhari: "and ask Zayd ibn Thabit." — and by other routes from al-Zuhri, and by a route from Hisham ibn Urwah, both of them from Urwah, with the same text.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Isa related to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Humayd that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The gifts of workers are embezzlement (ghulul)."

This hadith is one that Ahmad alone narrated; its chain is weak, and it appears to be an abridged version of the preceding one, and Allah knows best. [Al-Musnad (5/424).]

Another hadith: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said in the Book of Judgments: Abu Kurayb related to us, Abu Usamah related to us, from Dawud ibn Yazid al-Awdi, from al-Mughirah ibn Shibl, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to Yemen. When I had set out, he sent after me and I was brought back, and he said: "Do you know why I sent for you? Do not take anything without my permission, for that is embezzlement (ghulul), and: '...whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection' [Qur'an 3:161]. For this I called you; now go to your work."

This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route. In the chapter there are also narrations from Adi ibn Umayrah, Buraydah, al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, Abu Humayd, and Ibn Umar. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1335.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Ulayyah related to us, Abu Hayyan Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Taymi related to us, from Abu Zur'ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us one day and mentioned embezzlement, magnifying it and magnifying its matter. Then he said: "Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck that roars, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed it to you.' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse on his neck that neighs, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed it to you.' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with pieces of cloth on his neck that flutter, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed it to you.' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with gold or silver on his neck, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have conveyed it to you.'"

Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hayyan, with the same text. [Al-Musnad (2/426); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3073; Sahih Muslim, no. 1831.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: Qays related to me, from Adi ibn Umayrah al-Kindi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, whoever among you works for us at a task and conceals from us a needle or anything larger than it, it is embezzlement (ghull) which he will bring on the Day of Resurrection." A black man from the Ansar, [Mujalid said: he was Sa'id ibn Ubadah] as though I am looking at him, stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, accept back your work from me." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "I heard you say such-and-such." He said: "And I say it now: whoever we appoint over a task, let him bring its little and its much; what he is given from it, he takes, and what he is forbidden, he refrains from."

Muslim and Abu Dawud also narrated it similarly by several routes from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid. [Al-Musnad (4/192); Sahih Muslim, no. 1833.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Manbudh, a man from the family of Abu Rafi', related to me, from al-Fadl ibn Ubayd Allah [in G, R, A: "Abd Allah"] ibn Abi Rafi', from Abu Rafi', who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the afternoon prayer, he would sometimes go to the Banu Abd al-Ashhal and talk with them until the sun set [in G, R, A, W: "for the maghrib"]. Abu Rafi' said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was hurrying toward the maghrib, he passed by al-Baqi' and said: "Uff to you... uff to you," twice. I felt it [in G, R: "it was heavy on me"] and I drew back, thinking that he meant me. He said: "What is wrong with you? Walk on." I said: "Have you done something, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "What is that?" I said: "You said 'uff' to me." He said: "No, but this is the grave of so-and-so, whom we sent as a collector over the family of so-and-so, and he embezzled a striped cloak, and he is now being struck with the like of it from fire."

Another hadith: Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Salim al-Kufi, the paralysed one, who was in Makkah, related to us: Ubaydah ibn al-Aswad related to us, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from Abu Sadiq, from Rabi'ah ibn Nadid, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to take a tuft of hair from the side of a camel from the spoils, then say: "I have no more in it than one of you has. Beware of embezzlement, for embezzlement is a disgrace upon its owner on the Day of Resurrection. Return the thread and the needle and whatever is above that. Strive in the way of Allah against the near and the far, in the settled and the travelling, for jihad is a gate of the gates of Paradise; through it Allah relieves worry and grief. Establish the limits of Allah regarding the near and the far, and let not the blame of any blamer deter you in the matter of Allah." Ibn Majah narrated part of it from al-Maflub, with the same chain. [Al-Musnad (5/330), and this hadith is among the additions of Abdullah ibn Ahmad to his father's Musnad; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2540.]

Another hadith: From Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Return the thread and the needle, for embezzlement is shame, fire and disgrace upon its people on the Day of Resurrection." [Al-Musnad (2/184).]

Another hadith: Abu Dawud said: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Jarir related to us, from Mutarrif, from Abu al-Jahm, from Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me as a collector, then said: "Go, Abu Mas'ud; let me not find you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel of the zakat camels on your back, roaring, which you have embezzled." He said: "In that case I will not go." He said: "In that case I will not compel you." Abu Dawud alone narrated it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2947.]

Another hadith: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim informed us, Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Abd al-Hamid ibn Salih informed us, Ahmad ibn Aban informed us, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed a stone is hurled into Jahannam and it falls for seventy autumns without reaching its bottom; and embezzlement is brought and cast into it along with it." Then it is said to the one who embezzled: "Bring it," and that is His saying: ﴿Whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection﴾. [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/21), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 4334, by way of Muhammad ibn Aban, from Alqamah ibn Marthad; in its chain is Muhammad ibn Aban al-Ja'fi, who is weak.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 159–164 (part 3 of 3):

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hashim [[In C: "Hisham".]] ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar narrated to us, Simak al-Hanafi Abu Zumayl narrated to me, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas narrated to me, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, saying: When the Day of Khaybar came, a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) came and said: "So-and-so is a martyr, and so-and-so is a martyr," until they came upon a man and said: "So-and-so is a martyr?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No! I saw him in the Fire, in a cloak he had misappropriated [ghalla], or a cloak." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ibn al-Khattab, go and proclaim among the people: Indeed, none will enter Paradise except the believers." He said: So I went out and proclaimed: "Indeed, none will enter Paradise except the believers."

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in the same way from the hadith of ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. [[Al-Musnad (1/30), Sahih Muslim no. (114), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1574).]]

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Saʿid ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah as a tax collector [musaddiq], and he said: "Beware, O Saʿd, of coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel carrying on its back a bellowing." He said: "I will neither take it nor bring it." So he excused him. Then he narrated it through another route, from ʿUbayd Allah [[In C, R, A: "ʿAbd Allah".]], from Nafiʿ, with the same meaning. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/361).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saʿid narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Zaʾidah narrated to us, from Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah, that he was with Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik in the land of the Romans, and something misappropriated [ghulul] was found in the belongings of a man. He said: So Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah was asked, and he said: My father ʿAbd Allah narrated to me, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever you find misappropriated goods in his belongings, burn them." He said: I think he also said: "And strike him." He said: So his belongings were taken out to the market, and in them was a mushaf [copy of the Qur'an]. So Salim was asked, and he said: "Sell it and give its price in charity."

This was also narrated by ʿAli ibn al-Madini, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi [[In C, R, A: "al-Dawardi".]]. Abu Dawud added: and Abu Ishaq al-Fazari. Both of them narrated from Abu Waqid al-Laythi al-Saghir, Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Zaʾidah, with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (1/22), Sunan Abi Dawud nos. (2713, 2714), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1461), where he said: "Gharib hadith."]]

ʿAli ibn al-Madini, may Allah have mercy on him, al-Bukhari, and others said: This is a munkar hadith [a weak report contradicting stronger ones] from the narration of this Abu Waqid. Al-Daraqutni said: The correct view is that it is only a fatwa of Salim. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, and those who followed him among his companions adopted the position according to the implication of this hadith. But Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and the majority disagreed with him and said: The belongings of the one who misappropriated [al-ghall] are not burned; rather he is disciplined with a discipline appropriate to his case. Al-Bukhari said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refrained from praying over the one who misappropriated, and he did not burn his belongings. And Allah knows best.

Another route from ʿUmar: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me that Musa ibn Jubayr narrated to him that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Hubab al-Ansari narrated to him that ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays narrated to him that he and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab once discussed charity [sadaqah, obligatory alms]. He said: Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he mentioned the misappropriation of charity: "Whoever misappropriates from it a camel or a sheep, he will carry it on the Day of Resurrection"? ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays said: Yes.

Ibn Majah also narrated it from ʿAmr ibn Sawwad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb, with the same meaning. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/360) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1810). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawaʾid (2/56): "This chain contains weakness: Musa ibn Jubayr. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: He makes mistakes and contradicts. Al-Dhahabi said in al-Kashif: Trustworthy (thiqah), and I have not seen any other comment on him. ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman was mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat, and the rest of the chain's narrators are trustworthy."]]

It was also narrated by al-Umawi from Muʿawiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, who said: The punishment of the one who misappropriates is that his baggage is taken out and burned along with what is in it.

Then it was narrated from Muʿawiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿUthman ibn ʿAta, from his father, from ʿAli [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from R.]], who said: The one who misappropriates, his baggage is gathered and burned, and he is flogged short of the legal limit [for a slave], and he is deprived of his share. Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and the majority disagreed and said: The belongings of the one who misappropriates are not burned; rather he is disciplined with a discipline appropriate to his case. Al-Bukhari said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refrained from praying over the one who misappropriated and did not burn his belongings. And Allah knows best. [[Addition from W.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, Israʾil informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Khumayr [[In H, C, R: "Jubayr", which is an error; the correct form is what we have written, from al-Musnad (1/414). See Ahmad Shakir's comment on hadith no. (3929).]] ibn Malik, who said: It was ordered that the mushafs be altered. He said: So Ibn Masʿud said: Whoever among you can misappropriate a mushaf, let him misappropriate it, for whoever misappropriates something will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. Then he said: "I recited seventy surahs from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Shall I abandon what I took from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" [[Al-Musnad (1/414), and Ibn Abi Dawud narrated it in al-Masahif (p. 21) from the route of Israʾil, from Abu Ishaq.]]

Waki' narrated in his tafsir from Sharik, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Ibrahim, who said: When the mushafs were ordered to be burned [in C, R, A: "torn up"], ʿAbd Allah said: O people, misappropriate the mushafs, for whoever misappropriates will come on the Day of Resurrection with what he misappropriated, and what a fine misappropriation is the mushaf! One of you will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. [[Also narrated by Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Masahif (p. 22) from the route of Waki'.]]

Abu Dawud said, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) acquired spoils of war, he would order Bilal, and he would proclaim among the people, and they would bring their spoils, and he would take out the fifth and distribute it. Then a man came one day after the proclamation with a rope of hair and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this was among what we obtained from the spoils." He said: "Did you hear Bilal proclaim three times?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what prevented you from bringing it?" So he apologized to him, and he said: "No! You will bring it on the Day of Resurrection, and I will not accept it from you." [[Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan no. (2712) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs. The statement of al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, that it is from Samurah ibn Jundub is an error. Al-Hafiz al-Mizzi mentioned this hadith in the musnad of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr in his valuable book Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has earned wrath from Allah, and whose refuge is Hell? And wretched is the destination.﴾ That is: One who follows the pleasure of Allah in what He has legislated is not equal to one who deserves Allah's pleasure, His abundant reward, and protection from His severe punishment; and one who deserves Allah's anger and is bound by it has no escape from it. His refuge on the Day of Resurrection is Hell, and wretched is the destination.

There are many parallels to this in the Qur'an, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [al-Raʿd: 19]. And His saying: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise, and he will meet it, like one whom We have given the enjoyment of the worldly life, then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth?﴾ [al-Qasas: 61].

Then He said: ﴿They are degrees with Allah.﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: That is, the people of good and the people of evil are degrees. Abu ʿUbaydah and al-Kisaʾi said: "Stations," that is, they vary in their stations and degrees in Paradise and their levels in the Fire, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And for each there are degrees according to what they did﴾ [al-Anʿam: 132], and therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, that is: He will repay them for it. He does not wrong them by reducing their good, nor does He add to their evil, but He recompenses each according to his deed.

* *

His saying: ﴿Certainly did Allah confer favor upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾, that is: from their own kind, so that they could converse with him, ask him, sit with him, and benefit from him, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you from yourselves spouses that you might find tranquility in them﴾ [al-Rum: 21], that is: from your own kind. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Say: I am only a man like you to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the cities﴾ [Yusuf: 109]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-Anʿam: 130]. So this is more eloquent in showing favor: that the messengers sent to them are from among them, such that it is possible for them to address him, to refer back to him for understanding the speech. Therefore He said: ﴿He recites to them His verses﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and purifies them﴾, that is: He commands them to good and forbids them from evil, so that their souls may be purified and cleansed of the filth and corruption in which they were entangled during their polytheism and ignorance [in A: "their polytheism and their ignorance"]. ﴿And teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the Sunnah. ﴿And indeed, they were before that﴾, that is: before this messenger, ﴿in clear error﴾, that is: in manifest, evident, plain misguidance and ignorance, clear to everyone.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 159–164 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), bestowing favour upon him and upon the believers regarding how He softened his heart toward his community, those who follow his command and abandon opposing his rebuke, and He made his speech gentle toward them: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them﴾, meaning: what made you gentle toward them? Had it not been for the mercy of Allah upon you and upon them.

Qatadah said: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them﴾ means: "So it was by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them." And "mā" (مَا) is a *ṣila* (a particle that adds no meaning and serves to connect and emphasise). The Arabs attach it to a definite noun, as in His saying ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾ (An-Nisa 155; Al-Ma'idah 13), and to an indefinite noun, as in His saying ﴿After a little while﴾ (Al-Mu'minun 40). Likewise here, He said ﴿So by mercy from Allah﴾, meaning: "by a mercy from Allah."
