Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "This is the character of Muhammad (ﷺ) with which Allah sent him."

This noble verse resembles His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; he is zealous over you; for the believers he is kind and merciful﴾ (At-Tawbah 128).

Imam Ahmad said: Haywah narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Abu Rashid al-Hubrani narrated to me, saying: Abu Umamah al-Bahili took hold of my hand and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of my hand and said: "O Abu Umamah, among the believers are those whose hearts soften toward me." Ahmad alone narrated it.

Then He said: ﴿And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you﴾. *Fazz* (فَظّ) means harsh, coarse. The intended meaning here is coarse speech, as shown by His words after it, ﴿hard-hearted﴾. That is: "If you had been bad in speech and hard-hearted toward them, they would have dispersed from you and abandoned you. But Allah gathered them around you and made you gentle toward them, to win their hearts." This is like what 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: that he saw the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the earlier scriptures: that he was not harsh, nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, and he did not repay evil with evil, but pardoned and overlooked. [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4838.]

Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Tirmidhi narrated, Bishr ibn 'Ubayd al-Darimi informed us, 'Ammar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah commanded me to be patient and gentle with people, just as He commanded me to establish the obligatory duties." Gharib (a strange narration). [Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in *Thalatha Majalis min al-Amali* no. 42, Ibn 'Adi in *al-Kamil* (2/15), and al-Daylami in *Musnad al-Firdaws* no. 659, through Bishr ibn 'Ubayd. Ibn 'Adi said: Bishr ibn 'Ubayd is "munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected) regarding the imams. al-Dhahabi cited hadiths from him, including this one, then said: "These hadiths are not authentic, so Allah is the one to seek help from."]

Therefore He said: ﴿So pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter﴾. Accordingly, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would consult his companions on matters when they arose, to comfort their hearts, so that they would be more eager to carry out what they were doing. He consulted them on the day of Badr regarding going out to the caravan. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you were to lead us across the sea, we would cross it with you; if you were to take us to Bark al-Ghimad, we would go with you. We will not say to you what the people of Musa said to Musa: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will sit here.' Rather we say: Go forward, and we are with you, before you, behind you, on your right and on your left, fighting."

He also consulted them about where the camp should be, until al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr al-Mu'tiq suggested that they advance ahead of the people. He consulted them at Uhud about whether to remain in Madinah or go out to the enemy. The majority of them advised going out to meet them, so he went out to them.

He consulted them on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) about reconciling with the confederates by giving them a third of Madinah's produce that year. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah refused this, so he abandoned it.

He consulted them at Hudaybiyyah about attacking the children of the polytheists. Abu Bakr said to him: "We did not come to fight anyone; we only came as pilgrims (for 'umrah)." So he agreed to what he said.

He (ﷺ) also said, in the matter of the slander (al-ifk): "Advise me, O assembly of Muslims, concerning people who have slandered my family and accused them. By Allah, I know nothing but good about my family, and they have slandered a man of whom, by Allah, I know nothing but good." He consulted 'Ali and Usamah concerning separating from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

So he would consult them in wars and similar matters. The jurists have differed as to whether this was obligatory upon him or was a recommended practice to comfort their hearts, on two views.

Al-Hakim said in his *Mustadrak*: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub al-'Allaf narrated to us in Egypt, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and consult them in the matter﴾, he said: "Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both." Then he said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [*al-Mustadrak* (3/70).]

Similarly, al-Kalbi narrated it from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and they were the closest companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his two ministers, and the two fathers of the Muslims.

Imam Ahmad also narrated: Waki' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and 'Umar: "If you two were to agree on a consultation, I would not oppose you both." [*al-Musnad* (4/227).]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about *al-'azm* (determination/resolve), and he said: "Consulting the people of opinion, then following them." [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in *al-Durr* (2/360), attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh.]

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Shaybān, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who is consulted is trustworthy (mu'taman)."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, and al-Nasa'i graded it *hasan*, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, with more detail than this.

Then Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who is consulted is trustworthy." Narrated by him alone.

[And he also said:] Abu Bakr narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah and 'Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of you seeks counsel from his brother, let him advise him." Narrated by him alone as well.

* * *

His saying: ﴿Then when you have decided, rely upon Allah﴾, meaning: when you have consulted them on the matter and resolved upon it, then rely upon Allah in it. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him.﴾

* * *

His saying: ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾. This is as previously stated in His saying: ﴿And victory is only from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (Al 'Imran 126). Then He commanded them to rely upon Him, saying: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

* * *

His saying: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate (an-yaghull)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and others said: It is not befitting for a prophet to betray (yakhun).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Musayyab ibn Wadih narrated to us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khasif, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A cloak (qatifah) was missing on the day of Badr, and they said: "Perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, meaning: to betray.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Khasif narrated to us, Miqsam narrated to us, Ibn 'Abbas told me that this verse, ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, was revealed concerning a red cloak that went missing on the day of Badr. Some people said: "He took it." He said: They spoke a great deal about it, so Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate. And whoever misappropriates will bring what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it, from Qutaybah, from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, with the same chain. al-Tirmidhi said: *hasan gharib*. Some of them narrated it from Khasif, from Miqsam, as a *mursal* (a report missing a companion from its chain).

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The hypocrites accused the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of something that went missing, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate.﴾

This has been narrated from other routes from Ibn 'Abbas, similar to what has preceded. This is a clearing of him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, from all forms of treachery in the discharge of the trust, the division of the spoils, and other matters.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, meaning: by giving a share to some of the expeditions (*sarāyā*) and withholding from others. Al-Dahhak said likewise.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾ means by withholding part of what was revealed to him, so he does not convey it to his community.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, Tawus, Mujahid and al-Dahhak recited it: ﴿yughalla﴾ with a *damma* on the *ya'* (*yughall*), meaning: he is betrayed (*yukhan*).

Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: This verse was revealed on the day of Badr, when some of his companions had misappropriated. Ibn Jarir narrated it from both of them. Then he related from some of them that he explained this reading in the sense of "being accused of betrayal."

Then He said: ﴿And whoever misappropriates will bring what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ This is a severe warning and a firm threat. The Sunnah has also come with the prohibition of this in numerous hadiths.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, Zuhayr (meaning Ibn Muhammad) narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The gravest misappropriation before Allah is a cubit of land. You find two men who are neighbours in land, or in a house, and one of them takes a cubit from the share of his companion. When he takes it, it will be hung around his neck from seven earths until the Day of Resurrection." [*al-Musnad* (4/140).]

In the Two Sahihs, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wrongfully takes even a span of land, it will be hung around his neck from the seven earths on the Day of Resurrection." [Addition from A and W.] [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2452; Sahih Muslim, no. 1610.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Ibn Hubayrah and al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is appointed over a task for us and has no dwelling, let him acquire a dwelling; or if he has no wife, let him marry; or if he has no servant, let him acquire a servant; or if he has no mount, let him acquire a mount. Whoever takes anything beyond that is a embezzler (ghall)." [Al-Musnad (4/229).]

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it. Abu Dawud narrated it with a different chain and different wording, saying:

Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqqi related to us, al-Mu'afa related to us, al-Awza'i related to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid [in G and A: Shurayk], from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is a worker for us, let him acquire a wife; if he has no servant, let him acquire a servant; if he has no dwelling, let him acquire a dwelling." He said: Abu Bakr said: I was informed that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes other than that is an embezzler (ghall), or a thief." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2945.]

Our shaykh, the hafiz al-Mizzi [may Allah have mercy on him] [addition from W], said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated it from Musa ibn Marwan and said: "from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr" instead of "Jubayr ibn Nufayr," and this is closer to the correct version.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Hafs ibn Bishr related to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, Hafs ibn Humayd related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a sheep that bleats, calling out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.' And I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel that roars, calling out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.' And I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a horse that neighs, calling out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.' And I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying pieces of leather [addition from G, R and Tabari; in A and W: "two pieces"] that call out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.'"

No one among the authors of the Six Books narrated it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (7/358).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Zuhri, who heard Urwah say: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi informed us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed a man from the Azd called Ibn al-Lutbiyyah over the zakat. He came and said: "This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on the pulpit and said: "What is the matter with the worker whom we send, and he comes and says: 'This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift'? Why did he not sit in the house of his father and mother and see whether a gift would be given to him or not? By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you takes anything from it but that he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection upon his neck: if it is a camel, it will have a roar; if a cow, it will have a low; or if a sheep, it will bleat." Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits, and said: "O Allah, have I conveyed?" three times.

Hisham ibn Urwah added: Abu Humayd said: "My eyes saw it and my ears heard it; and ask Zayd ibn Thabit."

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah [Al-Musnad (5/423); Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2597, 7174; Sahih Muslim, no. 1832.] — and in al-Bukhari: "and ask Zayd ibn Thabit." — and by other routes from al-Zuhri, and by a route from Hisham ibn Urwah, both of them from Urwah, with the same text.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Isa related to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Humayd that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The gifts of workers are embezzlement (ghulul)."

This hadith is one that Ahmad alone narrated; its chain is weak, and it appears to be an abridged version of the preceding one, and Allah knows best. [Al-Musnad (5/424).]

Another hadith: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said in the Book of Judgments: Abu Kurayb related to us, Abu Usamah related to us, from Dawud ibn Yazid al-Awdi, from al-Mughirah ibn Shibl, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to Yemen. When I had set out, he sent after me and I was brought back, and he said: "Do you know why I sent for you? Do not take anything without my permission, for that is embezzlement (ghulul), and: '...whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection' [Qur'an 3:161]. For this I called you; now go to your work."

This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route. In the chapter there are also narrations from Adi ibn Umayrah, Buraydah, al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, Abu Humayd, and Ibn Umar. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1335.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Ulayyah related to us, Abu Hayyan Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Taymi related to us, from Abu Zur'ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us one day and mentioned embezzlement, magnifying it and magnifying its matter. Then he said: "Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck that roars, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed it to you.' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse on his neck that neighs, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed it to you.' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with pieces of cloth on his neck that flutter, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed it to you.' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with gold or silver on his neck, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have conveyed it to you.'"

Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hayyan, with the same text. [Al-Musnad (2/426); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3073; Sahih Muslim, no. 1831.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: Qays related to me, from Adi ibn Umayrah al-Kindi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, whoever among you works for us at a task and conceals from us a needle or anything larger than it, it is embezzlement (ghull) which he will bring on the Day of Resurrection." A black man from the Ansar, [Mujalid said: he was Sa'id ibn Ubadah] as though I am looking at him, stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, accept back your work from me." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "I heard you say such-and-such." He said: "And I say it now: whoever we appoint over a task, let him bring its little and its much; what he is given from it, he takes, and what he is forbidden, he refrains from."

Muslim and Abu Dawud also narrated it similarly by several routes from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid. [Al-Musnad (4/192); Sahih Muslim, no. 1833.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Manbudh, a man from the family of Abu Rafi', related to me, from al-Fadl ibn Ubayd Allah [in G, R, A: "Abd Allah"] ibn Abi Rafi', from Abu Rafi', who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the afternoon prayer, he would sometimes go to the Banu Abd al-Ashhal and talk with them until the sun set [in G, R, A, W: "for the maghrib"]. Abu Rafi' said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was hurrying toward the maghrib, he passed by al-Baqi' and said: "Uff to you... uff to you," twice. I felt it [in G, R: "it was heavy on me"] and I drew back, thinking that he meant me. He said: "What is wrong with you? Walk on." I said: "Have you done something, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "What is that?" I said: "You said 'uff' to me." He said: "No, but this is the grave of so-and-so, whom we sent as a collector over the family of so-and-so, and he embezzled a striped cloak, and he is now being struck with the like of it from fire."

Another hadith: Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Salim al-Kufi, the paralysed one, who was in Makkah, related to us: Ubaydah ibn al-Aswad related to us, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from Abu Sadiq, from Rabi'ah ibn Nadid, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to take a tuft of hair from the side of a camel from the spoils, then say: "I have no more in it than one of you has. Beware of embezzlement, for embezzlement is a disgrace upon its owner on the Day of Resurrection. Return the thread and the needle and whatever is above that. Strive in the way of Allah against the near and the far, in the settled and the travelling, for jihad is a gate of the gates of Paradise; through it Allah relieves worry and grief. Establish the limits of Allah regarding the near and the far, and let not the blame of any blamer deter you in the matter of Allah." Ibn Majah narrated part of it from al-Maflub, with the same chain. [Al-Musnad (5/330), and this hadith is among the additions of Abdullah ibn Ahmad to his father's Musnad; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2540.]

Another hadith: From Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Return the thread and the needle, for embezzlement is shame, fire and disgrace upon its people on the Day of Resurrection." [Al-Musnad (2/184).]

Another hadith: Abu Dawud said: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Jarir related to us, from Mutarrif, from Abu al-Jahm, from Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me as a collector, then said: "Go, Abu Mas'ud; let me not find you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel of the zakat camels on your back, roaring, which you have embezzled." He said: "In that case I will not go." He said: "In that case I will not compel you." Abu Dawud alone narrated it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2947.]

Another hadith: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim informed us, Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Abd al-Hamid ibn Salih informed us, Ahmad ibn Aban informed us, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed a stone is hurled into Jahannam and it falls for seventy autumns without reaching its bottom; and embezzlement is brought and cast into it along with it." Then it is said to the one who embezzled: "Bring it," and that is His saying: ﴿Whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection﴾. [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/21), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 4334, by way of Muhammad ibn Aban, from Alqamah ibn Marthad; in its chain is Muhammad ibn Aban al-Ja'fi, who is weak.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 159–164 (part 3 of 3):

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hashim [[In C: "Hisham".]] ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar narrated to us, Simak al-Hanafi Abu Zumayl narrated to me, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas narrated to me, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, saying: When the Day of Khaybar came, a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) came and said: "So-and-so is a martyr, and so-and-so is a martyr," until they came upon a man and said: "So-and-so is a martyr?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No! I saw him in the Fire, in a cloak he had misappropriated [ghalla], or a cloak." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ibn al-Khattab, go and proclaim among the people: Indeed, none will enter Paradise except the believers." He said: So I went out and proclaimed: "Indeed, none will enter Paradise except the believers."

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in the same way from the hadith of ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. [[Al-Musnad (1/30), Sahih Muslim no. (114), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1574).]]

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Saʿid ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah as a tax collector [musaddiq], and he said: "Beware, O Saʿd, of coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel carrying on its back a bellowing." He said: "I will neither take it nor bring it." So he excused him. Then he narrated it through another route, from ʿUbayd Allah [[In C, R, A: "ʿAbd Allah".]], from Nafiʿ, with the same meaning. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/361).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saʿid narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Zaʾidah narrated to us, from Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah, that he was with Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik in the land of the Romans, and something misappropriated [ghulul] was found in the belongings of a man. He said: So Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah was asked, and he said: My father ʿAbd Allah narrated to me, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever you find misappropriated goods in his belongings, burn them." He said: I think he also said: "And strike him." He said: So his belongings were taken out to the market, and in them was a mushaf [copy of the Qur'an]. So Salim was asked, and he said: "Sell it and give its price in charity."

This was also narrated by ʿAli ibn al-Madini, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi [[In C, R, A: "al-Dawardi".]]. Abu Dawud added: and Abu Ishaq al-Fazari. Both of them narrated from Abu Waqid al-Laythi al-Saghir, Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Zaʾidah, with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (1/22), Sunan Abi Dawud nos. (2713, 2714), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1461), where he said: "Gharib hadith."]]

ʿAli ibn al-Madini, may Allah have mercy on him, al-Bukhari, and others said: This is a munkar hadith [a weak report contradicting stronger ones] from the narration of this Abu Waqid. Al-Daraqutni said: The correct view is that it is only a fatwa of Salim. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, and those who followed him among his companions adopted the position according to the implication of this hadith. But Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and the majority disagreed with him and said: The belongings of the one who misappropriated [al-ghall] are not burned; rather he is disciplined with a discipline appropriate to his case. Al-Bukhari said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refrained from praying over the one who misappropriated, and he did not burn his belongings. And Allah knows best.

Another route from ʿUmar: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me that Musa ibn Jubayr narrated to him that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Hubab al-Ansari narrated to him that ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays narrated to him that he and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab once discussed charity [sadaqah, obligatory alms]. He said: Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he mentioned the misappropriation of charity: "Whoever misappropriates from it a camel or a sheep, he will carry it on the Day of Resurrection"? ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays said: Yes.

Ibn Majah also narrated it from ʿAmr ibn Sawwad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb, with the same meaning. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/360) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1810). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawaʾid (2/56): "This chain contains weakness: Musa ibn Jubayr. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: He makes mistakes and contradicts. Al-Dhahabi said in al-Kashif: Trustworthy (thiqah), and I have not seen any other comment on him. ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman was mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat, and the rest of the chain's narrators are trustworthy."]]

It was also narrated by al-Umawi from Muʿawiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, who said: The punishment of the one who misappropriates is that his baggage is taken out and burned along with what is in it.

Then it was narrated from Muʿawiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿUthman ibn ʿAta, from his father, from ʿAli [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from R.]], who said: The one who misappropriates, his baggage is gathered and burned, and he is flogged short of the legal limit [for a slave], and he is deprived of his share. Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and the majority disagreed and said: The belongings of the one who misappropriates are not burned; rather he is disciplined with a discipline appropriate to his case. Al-Bukhari said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refrained from praying over the one who misappropriated and did not burn his belongings. And Allah knows best. [[Addition from W.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, Israʾil informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Khumayr [[In H, C, R: "Jubayr", which is an error; the correct form is what we have written, from al-Musnad (1/414). See Ahmad Shakir's comment on hadith no. (3929).]] ibn Malik, who said: It was ordered that the mushafs be altered. He said: So Ibn Masʿud said: Whoever among you can misappropriate a mushaf, let him misappropriate it, for whoever misappropriates something will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. Then he said: "I recited seventy surahs from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Shall I abandon what I took from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" [[Al-Musnad (1/414), and Ibn Abi Dawud narrated it in al-Masahif (p. 21) from the route of Israʾil, from Abu Ishaq.]]

Waki' narrated in his tafsir from Sharik, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Ibrahim, who said: When the mushafs were ordered to be burned [in C, R, A: "torn up"], ʿAbd Allah said: O people, misappropriate the mushafs, for whoever misappropriates will come on the Day of Resurrection with what he misappropriated, and what a fine misappropriation is the mushaf! One of you will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. [[Also narrated by Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Masahif (p. 22) from the route of Waki'.]]

Abu Dawud said, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) acquired spoils of war, he would order Bilal, and he would proclaim among the people, and they would bring their spoils, and he would take out the fifth and distribute it. Then a man came one day after the proclamation with a rope of hair and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this was among what we obtained from the spoils." He said: "Did you hear Bilal proclaim three times?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what prevented you from bringing it?" So he apologized to him, and he said: "No! You will bring it on the Day of Resurrection, and I will not accept it from you." [[Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan no. (2712) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs. The statement of al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, that it is from Samurah ibn Jundub is an error. Al-Hafiz al-Mizzi mentioned this hadith in the musnad of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr in his valuable book Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has earned wrath from Allah, and whose refuge is Hell? And wretched is the destination.﴾ That is: One who follows the pleasure of Allah in what He has legislated is not equal to one who deserves Allah's pleasure, His abundant reward, and protection from His severe punishment; and one who deserves Allah's anger and is bound by it has no escape from it. His refuge on the Day of Resurrection is Hell, and wretched is the destination.

There are many parallels to this in the Qur'an, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [al-Raʿd: 19]. And His saying: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise, and he will meet it, like one whom We have given the enjoyment of the worldly life, then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth?﴾ [al-Qasas: 61].

Then He said: ﴿They are degrees with Allah.﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: That is, the people of good and the people of evil are degrees. Abu ʿUbaydah and al-Kisaʾi said: "Stations," that is, they vary in their stations and degrees in Paradise and their levels in the Fire, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And for each there are degrees according to what they did﴾ [al-Anʿam: 132], and therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, that is: He will repay them for it. He does not wrong them by reducing their good, nor does He add to their evil, but He recompenses each according to his deed.

* *

His saying: ﴿Certainly did Allah confer favor upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾, that is: from their own kind, so that they could converse with him, ask him, sit with him, and benefit from him, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you from yourselves spouses that you might find tranquility in them﴾ [al-Rum: 21], that is: from your own kind. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Say: I am only a man like you to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the cities﴾ [Yusuf: 109]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-Anʿam: 130]. So this is more eloquent in showing favor: that the messengers sent to them are from among them, such that it is possible for them to address him, to refer back to him for understanding the speech. Therefore He said: ﴿He recites to them His verses﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and purifies them﴾, that is: He commands them to good and forbids them from evil, so that their souls may be purified and cleansed of the filth and corruption in which they were entangled during their polytheism and ignorance [in A: "their polytheism and their ignorance"]. ﴿And teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the Sunnah. ﴿And indeed, they were before that﴾, that is: before this messenger, ﴿in clear error﴾, that is: in manifest, evident, plain misguidance and ignorance, clear to everyone.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 159–164 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), bestowing favour upon him and upon the believers regarding how He softened his heart toward his community, those who follow his command and abandon opposing his rebuke, and He made his speech gentle toward them: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them﴾, meaning: what made you gentle toward them? Had it not been for the mercy of Allah upon you and upon them.

Qatadah said: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them﴾ means: "So it was by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them." And "mā" (مَا) is a *ṣila* (a particle that adds no meaning and serves to connect and emphasise). The Arabs attach it to a definite noun, as in His saying ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾ (An-Nisa 155; Al-Ma'idah 13), and to an indefinite noun, as in His saying ﴿After a little while﴾ (Al-Mu'minun 40). Likewise here, He said ﴿So by mercy from Allah﴾, meaning: "by a mercy from Allah."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "This is the character of Muhammad (ﷺ) with which Allah sent him."

This noble verse resembles His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; he is zealous over you; for the believers he is kind and merciful﴾ (At-Tawbah 128).

Imam Ahmad said: Haywah narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Abu Rashid al-Hubrani narrated to me, saying: Abu Umamah al-Bahili took hold of my hand and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of my hand and said: "O Abu Umamah, among the believers are those whose hearts soften toward me." Ahmad alone narrated it.

Then He said: ﴿And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you﴾. *Fazz* (فَظّ) means harsh, coarse. The intended meaning here is coarse speech, as shown by His words after it, ﴿hard-hearted﴾. That is: "If you had been bad in speech and hard-hearted toward them, they would have dispersed from you and abandoned you. But Allah gathered them around you and made you gentle toward them, to win their hearts." This is like what 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: that he saw the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the earlier scriptures: that he was not harsh, nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, and he did not repay evil with evil, but pardoned and overlooked. [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4838.]

Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Tirmidhi narrated, Bishr ibn 'Ubayd al-Darimi informed us, 'Ammar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah commanded me to be patient and gentle with people, just as He commanded me to establish the obligatory duties." Gharib (a strange narration). [Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in *Thalatha Majalis min al-Amali* no. 42, Ibn 'Adi in *al-Kamil* (2/15), and al-Daylami in *Musnad al-Firdaws* no. 659, through Bishr ibn 'Ubayd. Ibn 'Adi said: Bishr ibn 'Ubayd is "munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected) regarding the imams. al-Dhahabi cited hadiths from him, including this one, then said: "These hadiths are not authentic, so Allah is the one to seek help from."]

Therefore He said: ﴿So pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter﴾. Accordingly, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would consult his companions on matters when they arose, to comfort their hearts, so that they would be more eager to carry out what they were doing. He consulted them on the day of Badr regarding going out to the caravan. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you were to lead us across the sea, we would cross it with you; if you were to take us to Bark al-Ghimad, we would go with you. We will not say to you what the people of Musa said to Musa: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will sit here.' Rather we say: Go forward, and we are with you, before you, behind you, on your right and on your left, fighting."

He also consulted them about where the camp should be, until al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr al-Mu'tiq suggested that they advance ahead of the people. He consulted them at Uhud about whether to remain in Madinah or go out to the enemy. The majority of them advised going out to meet them, so he went out to them.

He consulted them on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) about reconciling with the confederates by giving them a third of Madinah's produce that year. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah refused this, so he abandoned it.

He consulted them at Hudaybiyyah about attacking the children of the polytheists. Abu Bakr said to him: "We did not come to fight anyone; we only came as pilgrims (for 'umrah)." So he agreed to what he said.

He (ﷺ) also said, in the matter of the slander (al-ifk): "Advise me, O assembly of Muslims, concerning people who have slandered my family and accused them. By Allah, I know nothing but good about my family, and they have slandered a man of whom, by Allah, I know nothing but good." He consulted 'Ali and Usamah concerning separating from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

So he would consult them in wars and similar matters. The jurists have differed as to whether this was obligatory upon him or was a recommended practice to comfort their hearts, on two views.

Al-Hakim said in his *Mustadrak*: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub al-'Allaf narrated to us in Egypt, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and consult them in the matter﴾, he said: "Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both." Then he said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [*al-Mustadrak* (3/70).]

Similarly, al-Kalbi narrated it from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and they were the closest companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his two ministers, and the two fathers of the Muslims.

Imam Ahmad also narrated: Waki' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and 'Umar: "If you two were to agree on a consultation, I would not oppose you both." [*al-Musnad* (4/227).]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about *al-'azm* (determination/resolve), and he said: "Consulting the people of opinion, then following them." [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in *al-Durr* (2/360), attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh.]

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Shaybān, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who is consulted is trustworthy (mu'taman)."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, and al-Nasa'i graded it *hasan*, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, with more detail than this.

Then Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who is consulted is trustworthy." Narrated by him alone.

[And he also said:] Abu Bakr narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah and 'Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of you seeks counsel from his brother, let him advise him." Narrated by him alone as well.

* * *

His saying: ﴿Then when you have decided, rely upon Allah﴾, meaning: when you have consulted them on the matter and resolved upon it, then rely upon Allah in it. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him.﴾

* * *

His saying: ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾. This is as previously stated in His saying: ﴿And victory is only from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (Al 'Imran 126). Then He commanded them to rely upon Him, saying: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

* * *

His saying: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate (an-yaghull)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and others said: It is not befitting for a prophet to betray (yakhun).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Musayyab ibn Wadih narrated to us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khasif, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A cloak (qatifah) was missing on the day of Badr, and they said: "Perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, meaning: to betray.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Khasif narrated to us, Miqsam narrated to us, Ibn 'Abbas told me that this verse, ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, was revealed concerning a red cloak that went missing on the day of Badr. Some people said: "He took it." He said: They spoke a great deal about it, so Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate. And whoever misappropriates will bring what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it, from Qutaybah, from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, with the same chain. al-Tirmidhi said: *hasan gharib*. Some of them narrated it from Khasif, from Miqsam, as a *mursal* (a report missing a companion from its chain).

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The hypocrites accused the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of something that went missing, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate.﴾

This has been narrated from other routes from Ibn 'Abbas, similar to what has preceded. This is a clearing of him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, from all forms of treachery in the discharge of the trust, the division of the spoils, and other matters.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, meaning: by giving a share to some of the expeditions (*sarāyā*) and withholding from others. Al-Dahhak said likewise.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾ means by withholding part of what was revealed to him, so he does not convey it to his community.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, Tawus, Mujahid and al-Dahhak recited it: ﴿yughalla﴾ with a *damma* on the *ya'* (*yughall*), meaning: he is betrayed (*yukhan*).

Qatadah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: This verse was revealed on the day of Badr, when some of his companions had misappropriated. Ibn Jarir narrated it from both of them. Then he related from some of them that he explained this reading in the sense of "being accused of betrayal."

Then He said: ﴿And whoever misappropriates will bring what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ This is a severe warning and a firm threat. The Sunnah has also come with the prohibition of this in numerous hadiths.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, Zuhayr (meaning Ibn Muhammad) narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The gravest misappropriation before Allah is a cubit of land. You find two men who are neighbours in land, or in a house, and one of them takes a cubit from the share of his companion. When he takes it, it will be hung around his neck from seven earths until the Day of Resurrection." [*al-Musnad* (4/140).]

In the Two Sahihs, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wrongfully takes even a span of land, it will be hung around his neck from the seven earths on the Day of Resurrection." [Addition from A and W.] [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2452; Sahih Muslim, no. 1610.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Ibn Hubayrah and al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is appointed over a task for us and has no dwelling, let him acquire a dwelling; or if he has no wife, let him marry; or if he has no servant, let him acquire a servant; or if he has no mount, let him acquire a mount. Whoever takes anything beyond that is a embezzler (ghall)." [Al-Musnad (4/229).]

Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it. Abu Dawud narrated it with a different chain and different wording, saying:

Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqqi related to us, al-Mu'afa related to us, al-Awza'i related to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid [in G and A: Shurayk], from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is a worker for us, let him acquire a wife; if he has no servant, let him acquire a servant; if he has no dwelling, let him acquire a dwelling." He said: Abu Bakr said: I was informed that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes other than that is an embezzler (ghall), or a thief." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2945.]

Our shaykh, the hafiz al-Mizzi [may Allah have mercy on him] [addition from W], said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated it from Musa ibn Marwan and said: "from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr" instead of "Jubayr ibn Nufayr," and this is closer to the correct version.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Hafs ibn Bishr related to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, Hafs ibn Humayd related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a sheep that bleats, calling out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.' And I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel that roars, calling out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.' And I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a horse that neighs, calling out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.' And I will not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying pieces of leather [addition from G, R and Tabari; in A and W: "two pieces"] that call out: 'O Muhammad, O Muhammad!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have delivered the message to you.'"

No one among the authors of the Six Books narrated it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (7/358).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Zuhri, who heard Urwah say: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi informed us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed a man from the Azd called Ibn al-Lutbiyyah over the zakat. He came and said: "This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on the pulpit and said: "What is the matter with the worker whom we send, and he comes and says: 'This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift'? Why did he not sit in the house of his father and mother and see whether a gift would be given to him or not? By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you takes anything from it but that he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection upon his neck: if it is a camel, it will have a roar; if a cow, it will have a low; or if a sheep, it will bleat." Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits, and said: "O Allah, have I conveyed?" three times.

Hisham ibn Urwah added: Abu Humayd said: "My eyes saw it and my ears heard it; and ask Zayd ibn Thabit."

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah [Al-Musnad (5/423); Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2597, 7174; Sahih Muslim, no. 1832.] — and in al-Bukhari: "and ask Zayd ibn Thabit." — and by other routes from al-Zuhri, and by a route from Hisham ibn Urwah, both of them from Urwah, with the same text.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Isa related to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Humayd that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The gifts of workers are embezzlement (ghulul)."

This hadith is one that Ahmad alone narrated; its chain is weak, and it appears to be an abridged version of the preceding one, and Allah knows best. [Al-Musnad (5/424).]

Another hadith: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said in the Book of Judgments: Abu Kurayb related to us, Abu Usamah related to us, from Dawud ibn Yazid al-Awdi, from al-Mughirah ibn Shibl, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to Yemen. When I had set out, he sent after me and I was brought back, and he said: "Do you know why I sent for you? Do not take anything without my permission, for that is embezzlement (ghulul), and: '...whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection' [Qur'an 3:161]. For this I called you; now go to your work."

This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route. In the chapter there are also narrations from Adi ibn Umayrah, Buraydah, al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, Abu Humayd, and Ibn Umar. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1335.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il ibn Ulayyah related to us, Abu Hayyan Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Taymi related to us, from Abu Zur'ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us one day and mentioned embezzlement, magnifying it and magnifying its matter. Then he said: "Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck that roars, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed it to you.' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse on his neck that neighs, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed it to you.' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with pieces of cloth on his neck that flutter, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed it to you.' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with gold or silver on his neck, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' and I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have conveyed it to you.'"

Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hayyan, with the same text. [Al-Musnad (2/426); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3073; Sahih Muslim, no. 1831.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: Qays related to me, from Adi ibn Umayrah al-Kindi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, whoever among you works for us at a task and conceals from us a needle or anything larger than it, it is embezzlement (ghull) which he will bring on the Day of Resurrection." A black man from the Ansar, [Mujalid said: he was Sa'id ibn Ubadah] as though I am looking at him, stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, accept back your work from me." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "I heard you say such-and-such." He said: "And I say it now: whoever we appoint over a task, let him bring its little and its much; what he is given from it, he takes, and what he is forbidden, he refrains from."

Muslim and Abu Dawud also narrated it similarly by several routes from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid. [Al-Musnad (4/192); Sahih Muslim, no. 1833.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Manbudh, a man from the family of Abu Rafi', related to me, from al-Fadl ibn Ubayd Allah [in G, R, A: "Abd Allah"] ibn Abi Rafi', from Abu Rafi', who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the afternoon prayer, he would sometimes go to the Banu Abd al-Ashhal and talk with them until the sun set [in G, R, A, W: "for the maghrib"]. Abu Rafi' said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was hurrying toward the maghrib, he passed by al-Baqi' and said: "Uff to you... uff to you," twice. I felt it [in G, R: "it was heavy on me"] and I drew back, thinking that he meant me. He said: "What is wrong with you? Walk on." I said: "Have you done something, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "What is that?" I said: "You said 'uff' to me." He said: "No, but this is the grave of so-and-so, whom we sent as a collector over the family of so-and-so, and he embezzled a striped cloak, and he is now being struck with the like of it from fire."

Another hadith: Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Salim al-Kufi, the paralysed one, who was in Makkah, related to us: Ubaydah ibn al-Aswad related to us, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from Abu Sadiq, from Rabi'ah ibn Nadid, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to take a tuft of hair from the side of a camel from the spoils, then say: "I have no more in it than one of you has. Beware of embezzlement, for embezzlement is a disgrace upon its owner on the Day of Resurrection. Return the thread and the needle and whatever is above that. Strive in the way of Allah against the near and the far, in the settled and the travelling, for jihad is a gate of the gates of Paradise; through it Allah relieves worry and grief. Establish the limits of Allah regarding the near and the far, and let not the blame of any blamer deter you in the matter of Allah." Ibn Majah narrated part of it from al-Maflub, with the same chain. [Al-Musnad (5/330), and this hadith is among the additions of Abdullah ibn Ahmad to his father's Musnad; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2540.]

Another hadith: From Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Return the thread and the needle, for embezzlement is shame, fire and disgrace upon its people on the Day of Resurrection." [Al-Musnad (2/184).]

Another hadith: Abu Dawud said: Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Jarir related to us, from Mutarrif, from Abu al-Jahm, from Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me as a collector, then said: "Go, Abu Mas'ud; let me not find you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel of the zakat camels on your back, roaring, which you have embezzled." He said: "In that case I will not go." He said: "In that case I will not compel you." Abu Dawud alone narrated it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2947.]

Another hadith: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim informed us, Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Abd al-Hamid ibn Salih informed us, Ahmad ibn Aban informed us, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed a stone is hurled into Jahannam and it falls for seventy autumns without reaching its bottom; and embezzlement is brought and cast into it along with it." Then it is said to the one who embezzled: "Bring it," and that is His saying: ﴿Whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection﴾. [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/21), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 4334, by way of Muhammad ibn Aban, from Alqamah ibn Marthad; in its chain is Muhammad ibn Aban al-Ja'fi, who is weak.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 159–164 (part 3 of 3):

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hashim [[In C: "Hisham".]] ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar narrated to us, Simak al-Hanafi Abu Zumayl narrated to me, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas narrated to me, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, saying: When the Day of Khaybar came, a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) came and said: "So-and-so is a martyr, and so-and-so is a martyr," until they came upon a man and said: "So-and-so is a martyr?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No! I saw him in the Fire, in a cloak he had misappropriated [ghalla], or a cloak." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Ibn al-Khattab, go and proclaim among the people: Indeed, none will enter Paradise except the believers." He said: So I went out and proclaimed: "Indeed, none will enter Paradise except the believers."

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in the same way from the hadith of ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. [[Al-Musnad (1/30), Sahih Muslim no. (114), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1574).]]

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Saʿid ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah as a tax collector [musaddiq], and he said: "Beware, O Saʿd, of coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel carrying on its back a bellowing." He said: "I will neither take it nor bring it." So he excused him. Then he narrated it through another route, from ʿUbayd Allah [[In C, R, A: "ʿAbd Allah".]], from Nafiʿ, with the same meaning. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/361).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saʿid narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Zaʾidah narrated to us, from Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah, that he was with Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik in the land of the Romans, and something misappropriated [ghulul] was found in the belongings of a man. He said: So Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah was asked, and he said: My father ʿAbd Allah narrated to me, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever you find misappropriated goods in his belongings, burn them." He said: I think he also said: "And strike him." He said: So his belongings were taken out to the market, and in them was a mushaf [copy of the Qur'an]. So Salim was asked, and he said: "Sell it and give its price in charity."

This was also narrated by ʿAli ibn al-Madini, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi [[In C, R, A: "al-Dawardi".]]. Abu Dawud added: and Abu Ishaq al-Fazari. Both of them narrated from Abu Waqid al-Laythi al-Saghir, Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Zaʾidah, with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (1/22), Sunan Abi Dawud nos. (2713, 2714), and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1461), where he said: "Gharib hadith."]]

ʿAli ibn al-Madini, may Allah have mercy on him, al-Bukhari, and others said: This is a munkar hadith [a weak report contradicting stronger ones] from the narration of this Abu Waqid. Al-Daraqutni said: The correct view is that it is only a fatwa of Salim. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, and those who followed him among his companions adopted the position according to the implication of this hadith. But Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and the majority disagreed with him and said: The belongings of the one who misappropriated [al-ghall] are not burned; rather he is disciplined with a discipline appropriate to his case. Al-Bukhari said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refrained from praying over the one who misappropriated, and he did not burn his belongings. And Allah knows best.

Another route from ʿUmar: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me that Musa ibn Jubayr narrated to him that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Hubab al-Ansari narrated to him that ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays narrated to him that he and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab once discussed charity [sadaqah, obligatory alms]. He said: Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he mentioned the misappropriation of charity: "Whoever misappropriates from it a camel or a sheep, he will carry it on the Day of Resurrection"? ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays said: Yes.

Ibn Majah also narrated it from ʿAmr ibn Sawwad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb, with the same meaning. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/360) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1810). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawaʾid (2/56): "This chain contains weakness: Musa ibn Jubayr. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: He makes mistakes and contradicts. Al-Dhahabi said in al-Kashif: Trustworthy (thiqah), and I have not seen any other comment on him. ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman was mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat, and the rest of the chain's narrators are trustworthy."]]

It was also narrated by al-Umawi from Muʿawiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan, who said: The punishment of the one who misappropriates is that his baggage is taken out and burned along with what is in it.

Then it was narrated from Muʿawiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿUthman ibn ʿAta, from his father, from ʿAli [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from R.]], who said: The one who misappropriates, his baggage is gathered and burned, and he is flogged short of the legal limit [for a slave], and he is deprived of his share. Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and the majority disagreed and said: The belongings of the one who misappropriates are not burned; rather he is disciplined with a discipline appropriate to his case. Al-Bukhari said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refrained from praying over the one who misappropriated and did not burn his belongings. And Allah knows best. [[Addition from W.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, Israʾil informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Khumayr [[In H, C, R: "Jubayr", which is an error; the correct form is what we have written, from al-Musnad (1/414). See Ahmad Shakir's comment on hadith no. (3929).]] ibn Malik, who said: It was ordered that the mushafs be altered. He said: So Ibn Masʿud said: Whoever among you can misappropriate a mushaf, let him misappropriate it, for whoever misappropriates something will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. Then he said: "I recited seventy surahs from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Shall I abandon what I took from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" [[Al-Musnad (1/414), and Ibn Abi Dawud narrated it in al-Masahif (p. 21) from the route of Israʾil, from Abu Ishaq.]]

Waki' narrated in his tafsir from Sharik, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Ibrahim, who said: When the mushafs were ordered to be burned [in C, R, A: "torn up"], ʿAbd Allah said: O people, misappropriate the mushafs, for whoever misappropriates will come on the Day of Resurrection with what he misappropriated, and what a fine misappropriation is the mushaf! One of you will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. [[Also narrated by Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Masahif (p. 22) from the route of Waki'.]]

Abu Dawud said, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) acquired spoils of war, he would order Bilal, and he would proclaim among the people, and they would bring their spoils, and he would take out the fifth and distribute it. Then a man came one day after the proclamation with a rope of hair and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this was among what we obtained from the spoils." He said: "Did you hear Bilal proclaim three times?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what prevented you from bringing it?" So he apologized to him, and he said: "No! You will bring it on the Day of Resurrection, and I will not accept it from you." [[Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan no. (2712) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs. The statement of al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, that it is from Samurah ibn Jundub is an error. Al-Hafiz al-Mizzi mentioned this hadith in the musnad of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr in his valuable book Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has earned wrath from Allah, and whose refuge is Hell? And wretched is the destination.﴾ That is: One who follows the pleasure of Allah in what He has legislated is not equal to one who deserves Allah's pleasure, His abundant reward, and protection from His severe punishment; and one who deserves Allah's anger and is bound by it has no escape from it. His refuge on the Day of Resurrection is Hell, and wretched is the destination.

There are many parallels to this in the Qur'an, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ [al-Raʿd: 19]. And His saying: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise, and he will meet it, like one whom We have given the enjoyment of the worldly life, then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth?﴾ [al-Qasas: 61].

Then He said: ﴿They are degrees with Allah.﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: That is, the people of good and the people of evil are degrees. Abu ʿUbaydah and al-Kisaʾi said: "Stations," that is, they vary in their stations and degrees in Paradise and their levels in the Fire, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And for each there are degrees according to what they did﴾ [al-Anʿam: 132], and therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, that is: He will repay them for it. He does not wrong them by reducing their good, nor does He add to their evil, but He recompenses each according to his deed.

* *

His saying: ﴿Certainly did Allah confer favor upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾, that is: from their own kind, so that they could converse with him, ask him, sit with him, and benefit from him, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you from yourselves spouses that you might find tranquility in them﴾ [al-Rum: 21], that is: from your own kind. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Say: I am only a man like you to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the cities﴾ [Yusuf: 109]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-Anʿam: 130]. So this is more eloquent in showing favor: that the messengers sent to them are from among them, such that it is possible for them to address him, to refer back to him for understanding the speech. Therefore He said: ﴿He recites to them His verses﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and purifies them﴾, that is: He commands them to good and forbids them from evil, so that their souls may be purified and cleansed of the filth and corruption in which they were entangled during their polytheism and ignorance [in A: "their polytheism and their ignorance"]. ﴿And teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the Sunnah. ﴿And indeed, they were before that﴾, that is: before this messenger, ﴿in clear error﴾, that is: in manifest, evident, plain misguidance and ignorance, clear to everyone.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah Al 'Imran, verses 159–164 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says, addressing His Messenger (ﷺ), bestowing favour upon him and upon the believers regarding how He softened his heart toward his community, those who follow his command and abandon opposing his rebuke, and He made his speech gentle toward them: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them﴾, meaning: what made you gentle toward them? Had it not been for the mercy of Allah upon you and upon them.

Qatadah said: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were gentle with them﴾ means: "So it was by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them." And "mā" (مَا) is a *ṣila* (a particle that adds no meaning and serves to connect and emphasise). The Arabs attach it to a definite noun, as in His saying ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾ (An-Nisa 155; Al-Ma'idah 13), and to an indefinite noun, as in His saying ﴿After a little while﴾ (Al-Mu'minun 40). Likewise here, He said ﴿So by mercy from Allah﴾, meaning: "by a mercy from Allah."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "This is the character of Muhammad (ﷺ) with which Allah sent him."

This noble verse resembles His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; he is zealous over you; for the believers he is kind and merciful﴾ (At-Tawbah 128).

Imam Ahmad said: Haywah narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Abu Rashid al-Hubrani narrated to me, saying: Abu Umamah al-Bahili took hold of my hand and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of my hand and said: "O Abu Umamah, among the believers are those whose hearts soften toward me." Ahmad alone narrated it.

Then He said: ﴿And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you﴾. *Fazz* (فَظّ) means harsh, coarse. The intended meaning here is coarse speech, as shown by His words after it, ﴿hard-hearted﴾. That is: "If you had been bad in speech and hard-hearted toward them, they would have dispersed from you and abandoned you. But Allah gathered them around you and made you gentle toward them, to win their hearts." This is like what 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said: that he saw the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the earlier scriptures: that he was not harsh, nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, and he did not repay evil with evil, but pardoned and overlooked. [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4838.]

Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Tirmidhi narrated, Bishr ibn 'Ubayd al-Darimi informed us, 'Ammar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah commanded me to be patient and gentle with people, just as He commanded me to establish the obligatory duties." Gharib (a strange narration). [Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in *Thalatha Majalis min al-Amali* no. 42, Ibn 'Adi in *al-Kamil* (2/15), and al-Daylami in *Musnad al-Firdaws* no. 659, through Bishr ibn 'Ubayd. Ibn 'Adi said: Bishr ibn 'Ubayd is "munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected) regarding the imams. al-Dhahabi cited hadiths from him, including this one, then said: "These hadiths are not authentic, so Allah is the one to seek help from."]

Therefore He said: ﴿So pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter﴾. Accordingly, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would consult his companions on matters when they arose, to comfort their hearts, so that they would be more eager to carry out what they were doing. He consulted them on the day of Badr regarding going out to the caravan. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you were to lead us across the sea, we would cross it with you; if you were to take us to Bark al-Ghimad, we would go with you. We will not say to you what the people of Musa said to Musa: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will sit here.' Rather we say: Go forward, and we are with you, before you, behind you, on your right and on your left, fighting."

He also consulted them about where the camp should be, until al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr al-Mu'tiq suggested that they advance ahead of the people. He consulted them at Uhud about whether to remain in Madinah or go out to the enemy. The majority of them advised going out to meet them, so he went out to them.

He consulted them on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) about reconciling with the confederates by giving them a third of Madinah's produce that year. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah refused this, so he abandoned it.

He consulted them at Hudaybiyyah about attacking the children of the polytheists. Abu Bakr said to him: "We did not come to fight anyone; we only came as pilgrims (for 'umrah)." So he agreed to what he said.

He (ﷺ) also said, in the matter of the slander (al-ifk): "Advise me, O assembly of Muslims, concerning people who have slandered my family and accused them. By Allah, I know nothing but good about my family, and they have slandered a man of whom, by Allah, I know nothing but good." He consulted 'Ali and Usamah concerning separating from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

So he would consult them in wars and similar matters. The jurists have differed as to whether this was obligatory upon him or was a recommended practice to comfort their hearts, on two views.

Al-Hakim said in his *Mustadrak*: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub al-'Allaf narrated to us in Egypt, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and consult them in the matter﴾, he said: "Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both." Then he said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [*al-Mustadrak* (3/70).]

Similarly, al-Kalbi narrated it from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and they were the closest companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his two ministers, and the two fathers of the Muslims.

Imam Ahmad also narrated: Waki' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and 'Umar: "If you two were to agree on a consultation, I would not oppose you both." [*al-Musnad* (4/227).]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about *al-'azm* (determination/resolve), and he said: "Consulting the people of opinion, then following them." [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in *al-Durr* (2/360), attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh.]

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Shaybān, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who is consulted is trustworthy (mu'taman)."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, and al-Nasa'i graded it *hasan*, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, with more detail than this.

Then Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who is consulted is trustworthy." Narrated by him alone.

[And he also said:] Abu Bakr narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah and 'Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of you seeks counsel from his brother, let him advise him." Narrated by him alone as well.

* * *

His saying: ﴿Then when you have decided, rely upon Allah﴾, meaning: when you have consulted them on the matter and resolved upon it, then rely upon Allah in it. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him.﴾

* * *

His saying: ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾. This is as previously stated in His saying: ﴿And victory is only from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (Al 'Imran 126). Then He commanded them to rely upon Him, saying: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

* * *

His saying: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate (an-yaghull)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and others said: It is not befitting for a prophet to betray (yakhun).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Musayyab ibn Wadih narrated to us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khasif, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A cloak (qatifah) was missing on the day of Badr, and they said: "Perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, meaning: to betray.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Khasif narrated to us, Miqsam narrated to us, Ibn 'Abbas told me that this verse, ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, was revealed concerning a red cloak that went missing on the day of Badr. Some people said: "He took it." He said: They spoke a great deal about it, so Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate. And whoever misappropriates will bring what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it, from Qutaybah, from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, with the same chain. al-Tirmidhi said: *hasan gharib*. Some of them narrated it from Khasif, from Miqsam, as a *mursal* (a report missing a companion from its chain).

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala', from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The hypocrites accused the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of something that went missing, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate.﴾

This has been narrated from other routes from Ibn 'Abbas, similar to what has preceded. This is a clearing of him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, from all forms of treachery in the discharge of the trust, the division of the spoils, and other matters.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, meaning: by giving a share to some of the expeditions (*sarāyā*) and withholding from others. Al-Dahhak said likewise.
