Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, Isma'il ibn Umayyah ibn Amr ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When your brothers were struck at Uhud, Allah placed their spirits in the bodies of green birds that come to the rivers of Paradise, eat from its fruits, and return to lamps of gold in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their drink and food and the excellence of their resting place, they said: 'Would that our brothers knew what Allah has done for us, so that they would not lose their desire for jihad and would not shrink from war.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I will convey it to them on your behalf.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead...﴾ and what follows."

Ahmad related it in this way, and Ibn Jarir likewise related it from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash [[In A: "Abbas".]], from Muhammad ibn Ishaq with the same chain [[Musnad (1/265) and Tafsir al-Tabari (7/385).]]. Abu Dawud and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (Sahih collection) related it from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, and mentioned it, and this is more firmly established [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2520), and al-Mustadrak (2/297), where he said: "This hadith is sahih according to the conditions of Muslim," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]. Likewise Sufyan al-Thawri related it from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak related from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Sufyan [[In R: "Abu Sufyan," which is an error. See al-Mustadrak (2/387).]], from Isma'il [[In W: "Abu Isma'il," which is an error.]] ibn Abi Khalid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning Hamzah and his companions: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾." Then he said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it" [[Al-Mustadrak (2/387).]].

Qatadah, al-Rabi' and al-Dahhak likewise said: it was revealed concerning those killed at Uhud.

Another hadith: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Harun ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Madini informed us, Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir ibn Bashir ibn al-Fakih al-Ansari informed us, I heard Talhah ibn Khirash ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khirash ibn al-Simmah al-Ansari say: I heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: "One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at me and said: 'O Jabir, why do I see you worried?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my father has been martyred and has left behind debt and dependants.' He said: 'Shall I not inform you? Allah has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil, but He spoke to your father face to face (kifah).' Ali said: Kifah means direct confrontation. He said: 'Ask Me and I will give you.' He said: 'I ask You to return me to the world so that I may be killed for You a second time.' The Lord, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'It has already gone forth from Me that they will not return to it.' He said: 'O Lord, then convey to those behind me.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ to the end of the verse [[In A, W: "until I complete the verse."]]."

He related it again through another route, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Subayt al-Ansari, from his father, from Jabir, with similar wording. Al-Bayhaqi likewise related it in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah" through the route of Ali ibn al-Madini, with the same chain [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (3/299).]].

Al-Bayhaqi also related it from the hadith of Abu Ubadah al-Ansari, who is Isa ibn Abd al-Rahman, God willing, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah [may Allah be pleased with her] [[Addition from R.]], who said: The Prophet ﷺ said to Jabir: "O Jabir, shall I not give you good news?" He said: "Yes. May Allah give you good tidings of goodness." He said: "I perceive that Allah gave life to your father and said: 'Ask of Me, My servant, whatever you wish and I will give it to you.' He said: 'O Lord, I did not worship You as You deserve to be worshipped. I ask You to return me to the world so that I may fight alongside Your Prophet and be killed for You once more.' He said: 'It has already passed from Me that they will not return to it'" [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (3/298).]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, al-Harith ibn Fudayl al-Ansari narrated to us, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The martyrs are on the bank of a river at the gate of Paradise, in a green dome. Their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening."

Ahmad alone related it, and Ibn Jarir related it from Abu Kurayb: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, and Ubaydah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with the same chain. This is a good chain (isnad jayyid) [[Musnad (1/266) and Tafsir al-Tabari (7/387).]].

The martyrs are of several categories: among them are those whose spirits roam in Paradise, and among them are those who are at this river at the gate of Paradise. It is possible that the final destination of their journey is this river, where they gather, and their provision is brought to them there in the morning and evening. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 170–175 (part 2 of 4):

We have related in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad a hadith containing good news for every believer, that his soul will be in Paradise, grazing there as well, eating of its fruits, seeing the beauty and joy within it, and witnessing the honour that Allah has prepared for it. Its chain of narration is sound, strong and great, for it brings together three of the four Imams, the founders of the followed schools of law. Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated it from [the Imam] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, from Malik ibn Anas al-Asbahi, may Allah have mercy on him, from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The soul of the believer is a bird that hangs [[In manuscripts J and R: "ta'allaqa" (it hangs).]] on the trees of Paradise until Allah returns it to its body on the Day He raises him up." [[Al-Musnad (3/455).]]

His saying "ya'luqu" [[In manuscripts J and R: "ta'allaqa"; in manuscript A: "yata'allaqu".]] means: it eats.

And in this hadith: "The soul of the believer takes the form of a bird in Paradise."

As for the souls of the martyrs, as has preceded, they are in the crops of green birds. They are like the riders [[In manuscripts J and R: "al-rakib" (the rider).]] in comparison with the souls of believers in general, for they fly by themselves. So we ask Allah, the Generous, the Bestower, to keep us firm upon faith.

* *

His saying: ﴿Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that there is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve﴾ [[Addition in manuscripts J, R, A, and W; in manuscript H: "to the end of the verse".]]. That is, the martyrs who were killed in the cause of Allah are alive with their Lord, rejoicing in the blessing and happiness they are in, and rejoicing for their brothers who will be killed after them in the cause of Allah, that they will come to them, and that they will not fear what is before them, nor grieve over what they left behind them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "wa-yastabshiruna" means: they are gladdened by the joining of those behind them of their brothers in the way they went in jihad, so that they may share with them in the reward of Allah which He gave them.

[And] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, and W.]] al-Suddi said: The martyr is brought a book in which it is written: "So-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day, and so-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day," and he rejoices at this just as the people of this world rejoice at the arrival of their absent ones. [[In manuscripts J, R, A, and W: "ghayyabihim" (their absent ones) was written as "ghayib".]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When they entered Paradise and saw the honour there prepared for the martyrs, they said: "Would that our brothers in the world knew what we have come to know of this honour! For when they go out to fight, they would engage in it themselves, and be martyred, and obtain what we have obtained of good." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of their matter and of what they were in of honour, and their Lord informed them: "I have sent down to your Prophet and informed him of your matter and of your state." So they rejoiced at that, and this is His saying: ﴿And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾, and so on.

It is established in the two Sahihs from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the story of the seventy men of the Ansar at Bi'r Ma'unah, who were killed in a single morning, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made qunut against those who killed them, supplicating against them and cursing them. Anas said: "A Qur'an was revealed concerning them, which we recited, until it was lifted: 'Inform our people that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and has made us pleased.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2801, 4095) and Sahih Muslim, no. (677).]]

Then He said: ﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and a bounty, and that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They rejoiced and were gladdened by what they witnessed of the fulfilment of the promise and the abundant reward.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: This verse encompasses all the believers, both the martyrs and others. Allah rarely mentions a bounty or a reward He gave to the Prophets without mentioning what He gave to the believers after them.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them﴾. This was the day of Hamra' al-Asad. When the polytheists had inflicted what they inflicted upon the Muslims, they turned back toward their lands. Then, when they continued on their journey, they regretted that they had not finished off the people of Madinah, and they considered that a missed opportunity. When this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he called the Muslims to go after them, to terrify them and to show them that he had strength and resolve. He did not permit anyone except those who had been present at the battle of Uhud, except Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, for a reason we will mention. So the Muslims responded, despite their wounds and their severe injuries, in obedience to Allah [Mighty and Majestic] [[Addition from manuscript W.]] and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Ikrimah who said: When the polytheists returned from Uhud, they said: "You have not killed Muhammad, nor have you taken the young women captive. Evil is what you have done. Return!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard of this and called the Muslims, and they responded, until they reached Hamra' al-Asad, or the Well of Abu Uyaynah [[In manuscripts J, A, and W: "Utbah".]] (the doubt is from Sufyan). The polytheists said: "We will return next year." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, and this was counted as a military expedition. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them, for those among them who did good and were mindful of Allah there is a great reward﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Mansur, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, and mentioned it. [[Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11083), through the chain of Sufyan from Amr with the same wording.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The day of Uhud was a Saturday, the fifteenth of Shawwal. When the next day, a Sunday, came, sixteen nights had passed from Shawwal, the caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called among the people to pursue the enemy, and his caller announced: "None shall go out with us except those who were present at our battle yesterday." Jabir ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Haram spoke to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my father had left me in charge of seven sisters, and he said: 'My son, it is not fitting for me or for you that we leave these women without any man among them. I am not the one who would prefer you over myself in jihad alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So remain behind to look after your sisters.' So I remained behind to look after them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him permission, and he went out with him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out only to strike terror into the enemy, and to let them know that he had set out in pursuit of them, so that they would think he had strength, and that what had befallen them had not weakened them against their enemy.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abd Allah ibn Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to me, from Abu al-Sa'ib, the freedman of Aishah bint Uthman, that a man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Banu Abd al-Ashhal, who had witnessed Uhud, said: "I witnessed Uhud with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I and my brother, and we returned wounded. When the caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) announced the departure in pursuit of the enemy, I said to my brother, or he said to me: 'Will you miss an expedition with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? By Allah, we have no mount to ride, and none of us is anything but badly wounded.' So we went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I was less severely wounded than he was. Whenever he tired, I would carry him for one stretch and he would walk for another, until we reached where the Muslims had reached." [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/101) and Tafsir al-Tabari (7/399, 400), both through the chain of Ibn Ishaq.]]

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Sallam narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger [after the wound had befallen them, for those among them who did good and were mindful of Allah there is a great reward] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, and W; in manuscript H: "the verse".]]﴾. She said to Urwah: "O son of my sister, your two fathers were among them: al-Zubayr and Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both. When what befell the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) at Uhud happened, and the polytheists withdrew from him, he feared that they would return, and he said: 'Who will go after them?' Seventy men from among them responded, including Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both."

This is how al-Bukhari narrated it, uniquely, with this wording. Al-Hakim also narrated it in his al-Mustadrak from al-Asamm, from al-Abbas al-Duri, from Abu al-Nadr, from Abu Sa'id al-Mu'addib, from Hisham ibn Urwah, with it, and then said: "Sahih, though they did not record it." Thus he said. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4077) and al-Mustadrak (2/298), in which the one addressed by Aishah's words is Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, not Urwah, as in the narration of al-Bukhari.]]

It was also narrated from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Bahi, from Urwah who said: Aishah said to me: "O my son, your father is among those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them." Then he said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it." [[Al-Mustadrak (3/363).]]

Ibn Majah narrated from Hisham ibn Ammar and Hudbah ibn Abd al-Wahhab, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Hisham ibn Urwah, with it. Likewise Sa'id ibn Mansur and Abu Bakr al-Humaydi in his Musnad narrated it from Sufyan, with it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (124).]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us from the original of his book, Samawayh informed us, Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr informed us, Sufyan informed us, Hisham informed us, from his father, from Aishah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "If your two fathers were among those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them, they are Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both." [[This hadith is not sound when attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ), for it is confused (mudtarib). The Hafiz Ibn Kathir has explained the reason for its confusion. Al-Tabari, in his Tafsir (7/402), narrated that Aishah said this to Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr with this very wording, so the error may lie with one of the narrators or in his book.]]

Its attribution as a marfu' (prophetic) report is a plain error in terms of its chain, since it contradicts the reports of the trustworthy narrators that it stopped at Aishah as already mentioned, and in terms of its meaning, for al-Zubayr is not one of Aishah's fathers. Aishah only said this to Urwah ibn al-Zubayr because he was the son of her sister Asma' bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verse 170–175 (part 3 of 4):

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, my father narrated to me, [my father narrated to me] [[Addition from ج and al-Tabari.]] my paternal uncle, my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan on the Day of Uhud after what had happened from him, and he returned to Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Abu Sufyan has inflicted some harm upon you, and he has returned, and Allah has cast terror into his heart." The Battle of Uhud took place in Shawwal, and the merchants used to come to Madinah in Dhu al-Qa'dah and camp at Badr al-Sughra once every year. They came after the Battle of Uhud [[In أ: "Uhud in Shawwal."]] and the wound had afflicted the believers, and they complained of that to the Prophet ﷺ, and what had befallen them weighed heavily upon them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the people to set out with him and to pursue what they had been pursuing, and he said: "They are only setting out now, and they will go to Hajj, and they will not be able to do the like of this until next year." Then Satan came and frightened his allies, saying: "The people have gathered against you." The people refused to follow him, so he said: "I am going, even if no one follows me," in order to rouse the people. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, Talhah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah responded to him with seventy men, and they set out in pursuit of Abu Sufyan. They pursued until they reached al-Safra', and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them—for those among them who did good and were mindful of Allah there is a great reward﴾ [[Addition from ج، ر، أ، و، and in هـ: "the verse."]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/402).]].

Then Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he reached Hamra' al-Asad, which is eight miles from Madinah.

Ibn Hisham said: He appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Madinah, and he stayed there on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, then returned to Madinah. Ma'bad ibn Abi Ma'bad al-Khuza'i passed by him, as 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, and the Khuza'ah—its Muslims and its polytheists—were a trustworthy confidant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Tihamah; their dealings with him were sincere, and they did not conceal from him anything that happened there. Ma'bad was a polytheist at that time. He said: "O Muhammad, by Allah, what has befallen you among your companions has grieved us, and we wished that Allah had granted you well-being through them." Then he left, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at Hamra' al-Asad, until he met Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those with him at al-Rawha', and they had resolved to return to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions. They said: "We have struck the best of his companions, his leaders and his nobles. Then we return before we have uprooted them... we shall certainly attack their remnant, and we shall finish them off." When Abu Sufyan saw Ma'bad, he said: "What is behind you, O Ma'bad?" He said: "Muhammad has gone out with his companions seeking you, with a host the like of which I have never seen. They are burning with rage against you, a burning. Those who had stayed behind from him on your day have joined him, and they regret what they did; among them is a rage against you the like of which I have never seen." He said: "Woe to you! What are you saying?" He said: "By Allah, I do not think you should depart until you see the forelocks of the horses." He said: "By Allah, we have resolved to return against them to uproot their remnant." He said: "I forbid you from that. By Allah, what I have seen has moved me to say verses of poetry about them." He said: "And what did you say?" He said: I said:

It nearly broke my mount with the clamour,
when the earth flowed with the dark, massed horses...

They came with noble lions, not cowardly, nor inclined and weak in encounter, nor fleeing...

So I went on running, thinking the earth was tilting,
when they rose with a leader who was not forsaken...

So I said: Woe to Ibn Harb from your encounter,
when al-Batha' roars with the cavalry...

I am a warner to the people of al-Basl, a clear warning,
to everyone of them who has understanding and reason...

From the army of Ahmad, not cowards, not ..., and what I have warned of is not to be described as mere talk...

He said: That turned Abu Sufyan and those with him back.

A party of the Banu 'Abd al-Qays passed by him, and he said: "Where do you intend to go?" They said: "We intend Madinah." He said: "For what?" They said: "For the market of 'Ukaz, when you come to us." They said: "Yes." He said: "When you meet him, tell him that we have resolved to march against him and his companions to uproot their remnant." The party passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at Hamra' al-Asad, and they informed him of what Abu Sufyan and his companions had said. They said: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾.

Ibn Hisham also mentioned from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said when news of their return reached him: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, stones had been prepared for them, and if they had been attacked with them, they would have been like yesterday, gone."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said, regarding His words ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them﴾: Abu Sufyan and his companions inflicted upon the Muslims what they inflicted and then returned. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Abu Sufyan has returned, and Allah has cast terror into his heart. Who will volunteer to pursue him?" The Prophet ﷺ stood, with Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, and some of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ [[In ج، أ، و: "Messenger of Allah."]], and they followed them. News reached Abu Sufyan that the Prophet ﷺ was pursuing him, so he met a caravan of merchants and said: "Turn back Muhammad, and for you is such-and-such a reward, and inform them that I have gathered great forces against them, and that I am returning to them." The merchants came and informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of that, and the Prophet ﷺ said: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾. Then Allah revealed this verse.

Likewise 'Ikrimah and Qatadah and others said: This context was revealed concerning the expedition of Hamra' al-Asad [[Addition from ج، أ، و.]]. It was said: It was revealed concerning Badr al-Maw'id, but the sound view is the first.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it increased them in faith, and they said, "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs"﴾ [[Addition from ج، ر، أ، و، and in هـ: "the verse."]]: meaning, those whom the people threatened [with the gatherings] [[Addition from ج، ر.]] and frightened with the multitude of enemies, yet they were not moved by that, but relied upon Allah and sought His help, and said: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾.

Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, I think he said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abu Hasin, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾ was said by Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad ﷺ said it when they said: ﴿Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them,” but it increased them in faith, and they said, “Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim and Harun ibn 'Abd Allah, both from Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, from Abu Bakr, namely Ibn 'Ayyash, with the same chain. Strangely, al-Hakim [Abu 'Abd Allah] [[Addition from و.]] narrated it from the hadith of Ahmad ibn Yunus with the same chain, then said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4563, 4564), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11081), and al-Mustadrak (2/298), which al-Dhahabi affirmed, although al-Bukhari had narrated this hadith by this route.]]

Then [[In ج: "and."]] al-Bukhari narrated it from Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il, from Isra'il, from Abu Hasin, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The last words of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the fire, were: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4564).]].

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn 'Uyaynah said: Zakariyya informed me, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: It is the word of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the furnace. Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Thawri [[In أ، و: "al-Tawzi."]] informed us, 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Sukkari informed us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash informed us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, that it was said to him on the Day of Uhud: "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them." So Allah revealed this verse [[Also narrated by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad (11/86) through the route of Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Jawzi, who is al-Thawri, from 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad al-Sukkari with the same.]].

He also narrated with his chain from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Rafi'i, from his father, from his grandfather Abu Rafi', that the Prophet ﷺ sent 'Ali with a group of men in pursuit of Abu Sufyan. A Bedouin of Khuza'ah met them and said: "Indeed the people have gathered against you." They said: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." So this verse was revealed concerning them.

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Da'laj ibn Ahmad narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, Abu Khaythamah Mus'ab ibn Sa'id informed us, Musa ibn A'yan informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you fall into a great matter, say: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/390) and in al-Jami' al-Saghir, attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh; al-Manawi graded it as weak, and al-Albani weakened it in Da'if al-Jami' no. (829).]]

This is a strange hadith through this route.

Imam Ahmad said: Haywah ibn Shurayh and Ibrahim ibn Abi al-'Abbas narrated to us, both said: Baqiyyah narrated to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Sayf, from 'Awf ibn Malik, that he told them: The Prophet ﷺ judged between two men, and the one judged against said as he turned away: "Hasbi Allah wa ni'ma al-wakil" (Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bring the man back to me." He said: "What did you say?" He said: "I said: Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah blames helplessness, but upon you is resourcefulness. So when a matter overcomes you, say: Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

Likewise Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Baqiyyah, from Bahir, from Khalid, from Sayf, who was al-Shami and was not attributed, from 'Awf ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, in similar words [[Musnad (6/24), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3627), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (10462).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Asbat narrated to us, Mutarrif narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, [regarding His words: ﴿So when the trumpet is sounded﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 8]] he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "How can I be at ease when the one with the horn has put the horn to his mouth and bowed his forehead, listening for when he will be commanded so that he blows?" The companions of Muhammad ﷺ said: "Then what should we say?" He said: "Say: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs; in Allah we have put our trust."

Ibn Kathir said: This has been related through more than one chain, and it is a sound hadith. [[Al-Musnad (1/326).]] We have also been told, from the Mother of the Believers 'Aishah and Zaynab [bint Jahsh] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W.]] (may Allah be pleased with them both), that they boasted to one another. Zaynab said: "Allah married me, and your families married you." 'Aishah said: "My innocence was revealed from heaven in the Qur'an." Zaynab conceded to her. Then she asked: "How did you say it when you mounted the riding-beast of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal?" 'Aishah replied: "I said: Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." Zaynab said: "You spoke the word of the believers." [[Related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (10/88, 89), ed. al-Fikr, through Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jahsh. It will come, Allah willing, in the tafsir of Surat al-Nur.]]

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they returned with blessing from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them﴾. That is, when they put their trust in Allah, He sufficed them for what concerned them and repelled from them the might of whoever intended to scheme against them. So they returned to their land ﴿with blessing from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them﴾ from what their enemy had concealed for them. ﴿And they followed the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾

Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Dawud al-Zahid related to us: Muhammad ibn Nu'aym related to us: Bishr ibn al-Hakam related to us: Mubashshir ibn Abdullah ibn Razin related to us: Sufyan ibn Husayn related to us, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted [[In R: "Mighty and Majestic."]]: ﴿So they returned with blessing from Allah and bounty﴾. He said: "The blessing is that they were kept safe, and the bounty is that a caravan passed by, and it was during the days of the season (of trade). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bought it, made a profit in it, and distributed the wealth among his companions."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them"﴾: "This refers to Abu Sufyan, who said to Muhammad ﷺ: 'Our appointment is at Badr, where you killed our companions.' Muhammad ﷺ said: 'Perhaps.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for his appointment until he alighted at Badr. They happened upon the market there and traded, and that is the meaning of Allah's words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So they returned with blessing from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them [and they followed the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W; in H: "the verse."]]." He said: "This was the Lesser Battle of Badr."

Ibn Jarir related it. He also related, [too] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W.]] from al-Qasim, from al-Husayn, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the appointment with Abu Sufyan, the Muslims began meeting the polytheists and asking them about Quraysh. They would say: "They have gathered against you, intending to scheme against them by this, wanting to terrify them." The believers would say: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾, until they reached Badr and found its markets untroubled, with no one contesting them there. A man from among the polytheists [[In J, R, A: "He said: A man came."]] came and informed the people of Makkah about Muhammad's horsemen, and he said concerning that:

My she-camel shied away from the horses of Muhammad,
and from a date of Yathrib, scattered like the 'unjud (a dark fruit);
she goes after the religion of her ancient father,
she has made the water of Qudayd my appointment,
and the water of Dajnan for her, at the morning of tomorrow.

Ibn Jarir then said: "This is how al-Qasim recited it to us, and it is wrong. It is actually:

My she-camel shied away from my companions, Muhammad's people,
and from a date of Yathrib like the 'unjud,
she goes after [the religion of] her ancient father,
she has made the water of Qudayd my appointment,
and the water of Dajnan for her at the morning of tomorrow." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/411, 412).]]

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is only Satan frightening his allies﴾. That is, he frightens you with his allies and makes you imagine that they have might and power. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers﴾. [That is: ] [[Addition from manuscripts R, A, W.]] when he adorns (a matter) for you and makes you imagine it, then put your trust in Me and turn to Me, for I am sufficient for you and will help you against them, just as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those other than Him…﴾ until His words: ﴿Say, "Allah is sufficient for me; in Him the trusting put their trust"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 36–38]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So fight the allies of Satan; indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾ [An-Nisa: 76]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾ [Al-Mujadila: 19]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might"﴾ [Al-Mujadila: 21]. And [the Exalted] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W.]] said: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him﴾ [Al-Hajj: 40]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts J, A, W; in H: "the verse."]] [Muhammad: 7]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who have believed in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand, the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers. For them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51–52].

The Most High informs us about the martyrs: even though they are killed in this world, their spirits are living and provided for in the abode of permanence.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Ikrimah, Ibn Ishaq ibn Abi Talha narrated to us, Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, concerning the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ [[In A: "al-ladhi" (the one who).]] whom the Prophet of Allah ﷺ sent to the people of Bir Ma'unah. He said: "I do not know whether they were forty or seventy." Over that water was Amir ibn al-Tufayl al-Ja'fari. Those men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out until they came [[In R: "until when they came".]] to a cave overlooking the water, and they sat in it. Then some of them said to others: "Which of you will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the people of this water?" One of them, I think he was Ibn Milhan al-Ansari, said: "I will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He set out until he came to a tribe [[In H, J, R, A, W: "around" (hawl), but the text here follows al-Tabari.]] [among them] [[Addition from J and R.]], and he hid in front of the tents, then said: "O people of Bir Ma'unah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, so believe in Allah and His Messenger." A man came out to him from behind the tent with a spear and struck him in the side with it until it passed out through the other side. He said: "Allahu Akbar! I have succeeded, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" Then they followed his trail until they reached his companions in the cave, and Amir ibn al-Tufayl killed them all.

Ishaq said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that Allah [Most High] [[Addition from A.]] revealed a Qur'an concerning them: "Convey on our behalf to our people that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and we are pleased with Him." Then it was abrogated (naskh) and removed after we had recited it for a time [[In A, W: "zamanan" (a time).]]. And Allah revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/392, 393). Al-Bukhari also narrated it in his Sahih, no. (2801), through the route of Hammam, from Ishaq ibn Abi Talha, with the same wording.]].

Imam Abu al-Husayn Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Qushayri said in his Sahih: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, who said: "We asked Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) about this verse: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾." He said: "We too asked about that, and he said: 'Their spirits are in the bodies of green birds that have lamps suspended beneath the Throne. They roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, then they return to those lamps. Their Lord looked down upon them with a look and said: Do you desire anything? They said: What could we desire, when we roam freely in Paradise wherever we wish? He did this with them three times. When they saw that they would not be left alone unless they were asked, they said: O Lord, we wish that You return our spirits to our bodies so that we may be killed in Your way once more. When He saw that they had no need, they were left alone.'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1887).]] Similar reports have been narrated from Anas and Abu Sa'id.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No soul dies that has with Allah something good, and would love to return to the world, except the martyr, for he loves to return to the world and be killed again, because of what he sees of the excellence of martyrdom."

Muslim alone related it through the route of Hammad [[Musnad (3/126) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1877), but through the route of Humayd and Qatadah, from Anas.]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Madini narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Rabi'ah al-Sulami, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Did you not know that Allah gave life to your father, and said to him: Ask of Me? He said: I wish to be returned to the world so that I may be killed again. He said: I have already decreed that they will not return to it."

Ahmad alone related it by this route [[Musnad (3/361).]]. It is established in the two Sahihs and others that Abu Jabir, namely Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Haram al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, was killed as a martyr on the day of Uhud. Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid said, from Shu'bah, from Ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir say: "When my father was killed, I began to weep and uncover the cloth from his face, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to forbid me, but the Prophet ﷺ did not forbid me. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Do not weep for him, or: Do not let him be wept for; the angels continued to shade him with their wings until he was raised.'" He and Muslim and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through another route, from Shu'bah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: "When my father was killed on the day of Uhud, I began to uncover the cloth from his face and weep..." and mentioned its full text in similar wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4080), Sahih Muslim, no. (2471), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (4/13).]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, Isma'il ibn Umayyah ibn Amr ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When your brothers were struck at Uhud, Allah placed their spirits in the bodies of green birds that come to the rivers of Paradise, eat from its fruits, and return to lamps of gold in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their drink and food and the excellence of their resting place, they said: 'Would that our brothers knew what Allah has done for us, so that they would not lose their desire for jihad and would not shrink from war.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I will convey it to them on your behalf.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead...﴾ and what follows."

Ahmad related it in this way, and Ibn Jarir likewise related it from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash [[In A: "Abbas".]], from Muhammad ibn Ishaq with the same chain [[Musnad (1/265) and Tafsir al-Tabari (7/385).]]. Abu Dawud and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (Sahih collection) related it from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, and mentioned it, and this is more firmly established [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2520), and al-Mustadrak (2/297), where he said: "This hadith is sahih according to the conditions of Muslim," and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]. Likewise Sufyan al-Thawri related it from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak related from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Sufyan [[In R: "Abu Sufyan," which is an error. See al-Mustadrak (2/387).]], from Isma'il [[In W: "Abu Isma'il," which is an error.]] ibn Abi Khalid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning Hamzah and his companions: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾." Then he said: "It is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it" [[Al-Mustadrak (2/387).]].

Qatadah, al-Rabi' and al-Dahhak likewise said: it was revealed concerning those killed at Uhud.

Another hadith: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Harun ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Madini informed us, Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir ibn Bashir ibn al-Fakih al-Ansari informed us, I heard Talhah ibn Khirash ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khirash ibn al-Simmah al-Ansari say: I heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: "One day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at me and said: 'O Jabir, why do I see you worried?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my father has been martyred and has left behind debt and dependants.' He said: 'Shall I not inform you? Allah has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil, but He spoke to your father face to face (kifah).' Ali said: Kifah means direct confrontation. He said: 'Ask Me and I will give you.' He said: 'I ask You to return me to the world so that I may be killed for You a second time.' The Lord, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'It has already gone forth from Me that they will not return to it.' He said: 'O Lord, then convey to those behind me.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ to the end of the verse [[In A, W: "until I complete the verse."]]."

He related it again through another route, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Subayt al-Ansari, from his father, from Jabir, with similar wording. Al-Bayhaqi likewise related it in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah" through the route of Ali ibn al-Madini, with the same chain [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (3/299).]].

Al-Bayhaqi also related it from the hadith of Abu Ubadah al-Ansari, who is Isa ibn Abd al-Rahman, God willing, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah [may Allah be pleased with her] [[Addition from R.]], who said: The Prophet ﷺ said to Jabir: "O Jabir, shall I not give you good news?" He said: "Yes. May Allah give you good tidings of goodness." He said: "I perceive that Allah gave life to your father and said: 'Ask of Me, My servant, whatever you wish and I will give it to you.' He said: 'O Lord, I did not worship You as You deserve to be worshipped. I ask You to return me to the world so that I may fight alongside Your Prophet and be killed for You once more.' He said: 'It has already passed from Me that they will not return to it'" [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (3/298).]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, al-Harith ibn Fudayl al-Ansari narrated to us, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The martyrs are on the bank of a river at the gate of Paradise, in a green dome. Their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening."

Ahmad alone related it, and Ibn Jarir related it from Abu Kurayb: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, and Ubaydah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with the same chain. This is a good chain (isnad jayyid) [[Musnad (1/266) and Tafsir al-Tabari (7/387).]].

The martyrs are of several categories: among them are those whose spirits roam in Paradise, and among them are those who are at this river at the gate of Paradise. It is possible that the final destination of their journey is this river, where they gather, and their provision is brought to them there in the morning and evening. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verses 170–175 (part 2 of 4):

We have related in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad a hadith containing good news for every believer, that his soul will be in Paradise, grazing there as well, eating of its fruits, seeing the beauty and joy within it, and witnessing the honour that Allah has prepared for it. Its chain of narration is sound, strong and great, for it brings together three of the four Imams, the founders of the followed schools of law. Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated it from [the Imam] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, from Malik ibn Anas al-Asbahi, may Allah have mercy on him, from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The soul of the believer is a bird that hangs [[In manuscripts J and R: "ta'allaqa" (it hangs).]] on the trees of Paradise until Allah returns it to its body on the Day He raises him up." [[Al-Musnad (3/455).]]

His saying "ya'luqu" [[In manuscripts J and R: "ta'allaqa"; in manuscript A: "yata'allaqu".]] means: it eats.

And in this hadith: "The soul of the believer takes the form of a bird in Paradise."

As for the souls of the martyrs, as has preceded, they are in the crops of green birds. They are like the riders [[In manuscripts J and R: "al-rakib" (the rider).]] in comparison with the souls of believers in general, for they fly by themselves. So we ask Allah, the Generous, the Bestower, to keep us firm upon faith.

* *

His saying: ﴿Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that there is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve﴾ [[Addition in manuscripts J, R, A, and W; in manuscript H: "to the end of the verse".]]. That is, the martyrs who were killed in the cause of Allah are alive with their Lord, rejoicing in the blessing and happiness they are in, and rejoicing for their brothers who will be killed after them in the cause of Allah, that they will come to them, and that they will not fear what is before them, nor grieve over what they left behind them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "wa-yastabshiruna" means: they are gladdened by the joining of those behind them of their brothers in the way they went in jihad, so that they may share with them in the reward of Allah which He gave them.

[And] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, and W.]] al-Suddi said: The martyr is brought a book in which it is written: "So-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day, and so-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day," and he rejoices at this just as the people of this world rejoice at the arrival of their absent ones. [[In manuscripts J, R, A, and W: "ghayyabihim" (their absent ones) was written as "ghayib".]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When they entered Paradise and saw the honour there prepared for the martyrs, they said: "Would that our brothers in the world knew what we have come to know of this honour! For when they go out to fight, they would engage in it themselves, and be martyred, and obtain what we have obtained of good." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of their matter and of what they were in of honour, and their Lord informed them: "I have sent down to your Prophet and informed him of your matter and of your state." So they rejoiced at that, and this is His saying: ﴿And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾, and so on.

It is established in the two Sahihs from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the story of the seventy men of the Ansar at Bi'r Ma'unah, who were killed in a single morning, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made qunut against those who killed them, supplicating against them and cursing them. Anas said: "A Qur'an was revealed concerning them, which we recited, until it was lifted: 'Inform our people that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and has made us pleased.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2801, 4095) and Sahih Muslim, no. (677).]]

Then He said: ﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and a bounty, and that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They rejoiced and were gladdened by what they witnessed of the fulfilment of the promise and the abundant reward.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: This verse encompasses all the believers, both the martyrs and others. Allah rarely mentions a bounty or a reward He gave to the Prophets without mentioning what He gave to the believers after them.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them﴾. This was the day of Hamra' al-Asad. When the polytheists had inflicted what they inflicted upon the Muslims, they turned back toward their lands. Then, when they continued on their journey, they regretted that they had not finished off the people of Madinah, and they considered that a missed opportunity. When this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he called the Muslims to go after them, to terrify them and to show them that he had strength and resolve. He did not permit anyone except those who had been present at the battle of Uhud, except Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, for a reason we will mention. So the Muslims responded, despite their wounds and their severe injuries, in obedience to Allah [Mighty and Majestic] [[Addition from manuscript W.]] and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Ikrimah who said: When the polytheists returned from Uhud, they said: "You have not killed Muhammad, nor have you taken the young women captive. Evil is what you have done. Return!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard of this and called the Muslims, and they responded, until they reached Hamra' al-Asad, or the Well of Abu Uyaynah [[In manuscripts J, A, and W: "Utbah".]] (the doubt is from Sufyan). The polytheists said: "We will return next year." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, and this was counted as a military expedition. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them, for those among them who did good and were mindful of Allah there is a great reward﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Mansur, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, and mentioned it. [[Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11083), through the chain of Sufyan from Amr with the same wording.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The day of Uhud was a Saturday, the fifteenth of Shawwal. When the next day, a Sunday, came, sixteen nights had passed from Shawwal, the caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called among the people to pursue the enemy, and his caller announced: "None shall go out with us except those who were present at our battle yesterday." Jabir ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Haram spoke to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my father had left me in charge of seven sisters, and he said: 'My son, it is not fitting for me or for you that we leave these women without any man among them. I am not the one who would prefer you over myself in jihad alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So remain behind to look after your sisters.' So I remained behind to look after them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him permission, and he went out with him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out only to strike terror into the enemy, and to let them know that he had set out in pursuit of them, so that they would think he had strength, and that what had befallen them had not weakened them against their enemy.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abd Allah ibn Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to me, from Abu al-Sa'ib, the freedman of Aishah bint Uthman, that a man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Banu Abd al-Ashhal, who had witnessed Uhud, said: "I witnessed Uhud with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I and my brother, and we returned wounded. When the caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) announced the departure in pursuit of the enemy, I said to my brother, or he said to me: 'Will you miss an expedition with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? By Allah, we have no mount to ride, and none of us is anything but badly wounded.' So we went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I was less severely wounded than he was. Whenever he tired, I would carry him for one stretch and he would walk for another, until we reached where the Muslims had reached." [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/101) and Tafsir al-Tabari (7/399, 400), both through the chain of Ibn Ishaq.]]

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Sallam narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger [after the wound had befallen them, for those among them who did good and were mindful of Allah there is a great reward] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, and W; in manuscript H: "the verse".]]﴾. She said to Urwah: "O son of my sister, your two fathers were among them: al-Zubayr and Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both. When what befell the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) at Uhud happened, and the polytheists withdrew from him, he feared that they would return, and he said: 'Who will go after them?' Seventy men from among them responded, including Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both."

This is how al-Bukhari narrated it, uniquely, with this wording. Al-Hakim also narrated it in his al-Mustadrak from al-Asamm, from al-Abbas al-Duri, from Abu al-Nadr, from Abu Sa'id al-Mu'addib, from Hisham ibn Urwah, with it, and then said: "Sahih, though they did not record it." Thus he said. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4077) and al-Mustadrak (2/298), in which the one addressed by Aishah's words is Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, not Urwah, as in the narration of al-Bukhari.]]

It was also narrated from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Bahi, from Urwah who said: Aishah said to me: "O my son, your father is among those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them." Then he said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it." [[Al-Mustadrak (3/363).]]

Ibn Majah narrated from Hisham ibn Ammar and Hudbah ibn Abd al-Wahhab, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Hisham ibn Urwah, with it. Likewise Sa'id ibn Mansur and Abu Bakr al-Humaydi in his Musnad narrated it from Sufyan, with it. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (124).]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us from the original of his book, Samawayh informed us, Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr informed us, Sufyan informed us, Hisham informed us, from his father, from Aishah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "If your two fathers were among those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them, they are Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both." [[This hadith is not sound when attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ), for it is confused (mudtarib). The Hafiz Ibn Kathir has explained the reason for its confusion. Al-Tabari, in his Tafsir (7/402), narrated that Aishah said this to Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr with this very wording, so the error may lie with one of the narrators or in his book.]]

Its attribution as a marfu' (prophetic) report is a plain error in terms of its chain, since it contradicts the reports of the trustworthy narrators that it stopped at Aishah as already mentioned, and in terms of its meaning, for al-Zubayr is not one of Aishah's fathers. Aishah only said this to Urwah ibn al-Zubayr because he was the son of her sister Asma' bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 3, verse 170–175 (part 3 of 4):

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, my father narrated to me, [my father narrated to me] [[Addition from ج and al-Tabari.]] my paternal uncle, my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan on the Day of Uhud after what had happened from him, and he returned to Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Abu Sufyan has inflicted some harm upon you, and he has returned, and Allah has cast terror into his heart." The Battle of Uhud took place in Shawwal, and the merchants used to come to Madinah in Dhu al-Qa'dah and camp at Badr al-Sughra once every year. They came after the Battle of Uhud [[In أ: "Uhud in Shawwal."]] and the wound had afflicted the believers, and they complained of that to the Prophet ﷺ, and what had befallen them weighed heavily upon them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the people to set out with him and to pursue what they had been pursuing, and he said: "They are only setting out now, and they will go to Hajj, and they will not be able to do the like of this until next year." Then Satan came and frightened his allies, saying: "The people have gathered against you." The people refused to follow him, so he said: "I am going, even if no one follows me," in order to rouse the people. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, Talhah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah responded to him with seventy men, and they set out in pursuit of Abu Sufyan. They pursued until they reached al-Safra', and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them—for those among them who did good and were mindful of Allah there is a great reward﴾ [[Addition from ج، ر، أ، و، and in هـ: "the verse."]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/402).]].

Then Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he reached Hamra' al-Asad, which is eight miles from Madinah.

Ibn Hisham said: He appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Madinah, and he stayed there on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, then returned to Madinah. Ma'bad ibn Abi Ma'bad al-Khuza'i passed by him, as 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, and the Khuza'ah—its Muslims and its polytheists—were a trustworthy confidant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Tihamah; their dealings with him were sincere, and they did not conceal from him anything that happened there. Ma'bad was a polytheist at that time. He said: "O Muhammad, by Allah, what has befallen you among your companions has grieved us, and we wished that Allah had granted you well-being through them." Then he left, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at Hamra' al-Asad, until he met Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those with him at al-Rawha', and they had resolved to return to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions. They said: "We have struck the best of his companions, his leaders and his nobles. Then we return before we have uprooted them... we shall certainly attack their remnant, and we shall finish them off." When Abu Sufyan saw Ma'bad, he said: "What is behind you, O Ma'bad?" He said: "Muhammad has gone out with his companions seeking you, with a host the like of which I have never seen. They are burning with rage against you, a burning. Those who had stayed behind from him on your day have joined him, and they regret what they did; among them is a rage against you the like of which I have never seen." He said: "Woe to you! What are you saying?" He said: "By Allah, I do not think you should depart until you see the forelocks of the horses." He said: "By Allah, we have resolved to return against them to uproot their remnant." He said: "I forbid you from that. By Allah, what I have seen has moved me to say verses of poetry about them." He said: "And what did you say?" He said: I said:

It nearly broke my mount with the clamour,
when the earth flowed with the dark, massed horses...

They came with noble lions, not cowardly, nor inclined and weak in encounter, nor fleeing...

So I went on running, thinking the earth was tilting,
when they rose with a leader who was not forsaken...

So I said: Woe to Ibn Harb from your encounter,
when al-Batha' roars with the cavalry...

I am a warner to the people of al-Basl, a clear warning,
to everyone of them who has understanding and reason...

From the army of Ahmad, not cowards, not ..., and what I have warned of is not to be described as mere talk...

He said: That turned Abu Sufyan and those with him back.

A party of the Banu 'Abd al-Qays passed by him, and he said: "Where do you intend to go?" They said: "We intend Madinah." He said: "For what?" They said: "For the market of 'Ukaz, when you come to us." They said: "Yes." He said: "When you meet him, tell him that we have resolved to march against him and his companions to uproot their remnant." The party passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at Hamra' al-Asad, and they informed him of what Abu Sufyan and his companions had said. They said: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾.

Ibn Hisham also mentioned from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said when news of their return reached him: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, stones had been prepared for them, and if they had been attacked with them, they would have been like yesterday, gone."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said, regarding His words ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them﴾: Abu Sufyan and his companions inflicted upon the Muslims what they inflicted and then returned. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Abu Sufyan has returned, and Allah has cast terror into his heart. Who will volunteer to pursue him?" The Prophet ﷺ stood, with Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, and some of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ [[In ج، أ، و: "Messenger of Allah."]], and they followed them. News reached Abu Sufyan that the Prophet ﷺ was pursuing him, so he met a caravan of merchants and said: "Turn back Muhammad, and for you is such-and-such a reward, and inform them that I have gathered great forces against them, and that I am returning to them." The merchants came and informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of that, and the Prophet ﷺ said: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾. Then Allah revealed this verse.

Likewise 'Ikrimah and Qatadah and others said: This context was revealed concerning the expedition of Hamra' al-Asad [[Addition from ج، أ، و.]]. It was said: It was revealed concerning Badr al-Maw'id, but the sound view is the first.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it increased them in faith, and they said, "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs"﴾ [[Addition from ج، ر، أ، و، and in هـ: "the verse."]]: meaning, those whom the people threatened [with the gatherings] [[Addition from ج، ر.]] and frightened with the multitude of enemies, yet they were not moved by that, but relied upon Allah and sought His help, and said: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾.

Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, I think he said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abu Hasin, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾ was said by Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad ﷺ said it when they said: ﴿Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them,” but it increased them in faith, and they said, “Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim and Harun ibn 'Abd Allah, both from Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, from Abu Bakr, namely Ibn 'Ayyash, with the same chain. Strangely, al-Hakim [Abu 'Abd Allah] [[Addition from و.]] narrated it from the hadith of Ahmad ibn Yunus with the same chain, then said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4563, 4564), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11081), and al-Mustadrak (2/298), which al-Dhahabi affirmed, although al-Bukhari had narrated this hadith by this route.]]

Then [[In ج: "and."]] al-Bukhari narrated it from Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il, from Isra'il, from Abu Hasin, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The last words of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the fire, were: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4564).]].

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn 'Uyaynah said: Zakariyya informed me, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: It is the word of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the furnace. Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Thawri [[In أ، و: "al-Tawzi."]] informed us, 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Sukkari informed us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash informed us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, that it was said to him on the Day of Uhud: "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them." So Allah revealed this verse [[Also narrated by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad (11/86) through the route of Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Jawzi, who is al-Thawri, from 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad al-Sukkari with the same.]].

He also narrated with his chain from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Rafi'i, from his father, from his grandfather Abu Rafi', that the Prophet ﷺ sent 'Ali with a group of men in pursuit of Abu Sufyan. A Bedouin of Khuza'ah met them and said: "Indeed the people have gathered against you." They said: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." So this verse was revealed concerning them.

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Da'laj ibn Ahmad narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, Abu Khaythamah Mus'ab ibn Sa'id informed us, Musa ibn A'yan informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you fall into a great matter, say: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/390) and in al-Jami' al-Saghir, attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh; al-Manawi graded it as weak, and al-Albani weakened it in Da'if al-Jami' no. (829).]]

This is a strange hadith through this route.

Imam Ahmad said: Haywah ibn Shurayh and Ibrahim ibn Abi al-'Abbas narrated to us, both said: Baqiyyah narrated to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Sayf, from 'Awf ibn Malik, that he told them: The Prophet ﷺ judged between two men, and the one judged against said as he turned away: "Hasbi Allah wa ni'ma al-wakil" (Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bring the man back to me." He said: "What did you say?" He said: "I said: Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah blames helplessness, but upon you is resourcefulness. So when a matter overcomes you, say: Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

Likewise Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Baqiyyah, from Bahir, from Khalid, from Sayf, who was al-Shami and was not attributed, from 'Awf ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ, in similar words [[Musnad (6/24), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3627), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (10462).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Asbat narrated to us, Mutarrif narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, [regarding His words: ﴿So when the trumpet is sounded﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 8]] he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "How can I be at ease when the one with the horn has put the horn to his mouth and bowed his forehead, listening for when he will be commanded so that he blows?" The companions of Muhammad ﷺ said: "Then what should we say?" He said: "Say: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs; in Allah we have put our trust."

Ibn Kathir said: This has been related through more than one chain, and it is a sound hadith. [[Al-Musnad (1/326).]] We have also been told, from the Mother of the Believers 'Aishah and Zaynab [bint Jahsh] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W.]] (may Allah be pleased with them both), that they boasted to one another. Zaynab said: "Allah married me, and your families married you." 'Aishah said: "My innocence was revealed from heaven in the Qur'an." Zaynab conceded to her. Then she asked: "How did you say it when you mounted the riding-beast of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal?" 'Aishah replied: "I said: Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." Zaynab said: "You spoke the word of the believers." [[Related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (10/88, 89), ed. al-Fikr, through Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jahsh. It will come, Allah willing, in the tafsir of Surat al-Nur.]]

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they returned with blessing from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them﴾. That is, when they put their trust in Allah, He sufficed them for what concerned them and repelled from them the might of whoever intended to scheme against them. So they returned to their land ﴿with blessing from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them﴾ from what their enemy had concealed for them. ﴿And they followed the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾

Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Dawud al-Zahid related to us: Muhammad ibn Nu'aym related to us: Bishr ibn al-Hakam related to us: Mubashshir ibn Abdullah ibn Razin related to us: Sufyan ibn Husayn related to us, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted [[In R: "Mighty and Majestic."]]: ﴿So they returned with blessing from Allah and bounty﴾. He said: "The blessing is that they were kept safe, and the bounty is that a caravan passed by, and it was during the days of the season (of trade). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bought it, made a profit in it, and distributed the wealth among his companions."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them"﴾: "This refers to Abu Sufyan, who said to Muhammad ﷺ: 'Our appointment is at Badr, where you killed our companions.' Muhammad ﷺ said: 'Perhaps.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for his appointment until he alighted at Badr. They happened upon the market there and traded, and that is the meaning of Allah's words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So they returned with blessing from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them [and they followed the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W; in H: "the verse."]]." He said: "This was the Lesser Battle of Badr."

Ibn Jarir related it. He also related, [too] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W.]] from al-Qasim, from al-Husayn, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the appointment with Abu Sufyan, the Muslims began meeting the polytheists and asking them about Quraysh. They would say: "They have gathered against you, intending to scheme against them by this, wanting to terrify them." The believers would say: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾, until they reached Badr and found its markets untroubled, with no one contesting them there. A man from among the polytheists [[In J, R, A: "He said: A man came."]] came and informed the people of Makkah about Muhammad's horsemen, and he said concerning that:

My she-camel shied away from the horses of Muhammad,
and from a date of Yathrib, scattered like the 'unjud (a dark fruit);
she goes after the religion of her ancient father,
she has made the water of Qudayd my appointment,
and the water of Dajnan for her, at the morning of tomorrow.

Ibn Jarir then said: "This is how al-Qasim recited it to us, and it is wrong. It is actually:

My she-camel shied away from my companions, Muhammad's people,
and from a date of Yathrib like the 'unjud,
she goes after [the religion of] her ancient father,
she has made the water of Qudayd my appointment,
and the water of Dajnan for her at the morning of tomorrow." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/411, 412).]]

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is only Satan frightening his allies﴾. That is, he frightens you with his allies and makes you imagine that they have might and power. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers﴾. [That is: ] [[Addition from manuscripts R, A, W.]] when he adorns (a matter) for you and makes you imagine it, then put your trust in Me and turn to Me, for I am sufficient for you and will help you against them, just as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those other than Him…﴾ until His words: ﴿Say, "Allah is sufficient for me; in Him the trusting put their trust"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 36–38]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So fight the allies of Satan; indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾ [An-Nisa: 76]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾ [Al-Mujadila: 19]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might"﴾ [Al-Mujadila: 21]. And [the Exalted] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W.]] said: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him﴾ [Al-Hajj: 40]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts J, A, W; in H: "the verse."]] [Muhammad: 7]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who have believed in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand, the Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers. For them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51–52].

The Most High informs us about the martyrs: even though they are killed in this world, their spirits are living and provided for in the abode of permanence.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Ikrimah, Ibn Ishaq ibn Abi Talha narrated to us, Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, concerning the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ [[In A: "al-ladhi" (the one who).]] whom the Prophet of Allah ﷺ sent to the people of Bir Ma'unah. He said: "I do not know whether they were forty or seventy." Over that water was Amir ibn al-Tufayl al-Ja'fari. Those men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out until they came [[In R: "until when they came".]] to a cave overlooking the water, and they sat in it. Then some of them said to others: "Which of you will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the people of this water?" One of them, I think he was Ibn Milhan al-Ansari, said: "I will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He set out until he came to a tribe [[In H, J, R, A, W: "around" (hawl), but the text here follows al-Tabari.]] [among them] [[Addition from J and R.]], and he hid in front of the tents, then said: "O people of Bir Ma'unah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, so believe in Allah and His Messenger." A man came out to him from behind the tent with a spear and struck him in the side with it until it passed out through the other side. He said: "Allahu Akbar! I have succeeded, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" Then they followed his trail until they reached his companions in the cave, and Amir ibn al-Tufayl killed them all.

Ishaq said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that Allah [Most High] [[Addition from A.]] revealed a Qur'an concerning them: "Convey on our behalf to our people that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and we are pleased with Him." Then it was abrogated (naskh) and removed after we had recited it for a time [[In A, W: "zamanan" (a time).]].
