And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 105–106] And He praised His believing servants: ﴿Who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth,﴾ saying, ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain.﴾ That is: You did not create this creation in vain, but in truth, so that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best. Then they glorified Him above futility and the creation of vanity, saying: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, that is, far above creating anything in vain. ﴿So protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾, meaning: O You who created creation with truth and justice, O You who are free from deficiencies, defects and futility, protect us from the punishment of the Fire by Your power and strength, and facilitate for us deeds with which You will be pleased with us, and grant us success in righteous deeds by which You guide us to the Gardens of Bliss and protect us through them from Your painful punishment.

Then they said: ﴿Our Lord, indeed whomever You admit to the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him﴾, meaning: You have humiliated him and displayed his disgrace before the assembled. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there will be no helpers﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection there will be no protector for them from You, nor anyone to turn them away from what You intend for them.

﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith﴾, meaning: a summoner calling to faith, and he is the Messenger ﷺ, ﴿Believe in your Lord,﴾ meaning he says: "Believe in your Lord," so we believed, meaning: we responded to him and followed him. ﴿Our Lord, so forgive us our sins﴾, meaning: by our faith and our following of Your Prophet, so forgive us our sins, that is, cover them. ﴿And remove from us our misdeeds﴾, meaning: concerning what is between us and You. ﴿And take us in death with the righteous﴾, meaning: join us with the righteous. ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾. It was said: its meaning is: [what You promised] upon belief in Your messengers. And it was said: its meaning is: upon the tongues of Your messengers. And this is more apparent.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Iqal, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Asqalan is one of the two brides. From it Allah will raise on the Day of Resurrection seventy thousand people who will have no reckoning, and from it He will raise fifty thousand martyrs, delegations to Allah, and there are the ranks of the martyrs, their heads severed and held in their hands, their veins gushing blood, saying: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break Your promise.﴾ Then He will say: 'My servant has spoken the truth. Wash them in the river of al-Bayda.' They will come out from it pure and white, and they will roam in Paradise wherever they wish."

This hadith is counted among the strange narrations of the Musnad, and some consider it fabricated, and Allah knows best. [[Al-Musnad (3/225). Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it in al-Mawdu'at (2/54) and said: "This hadith is not authentic from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. All its chains revolve around Abu 'Iqal, whose name is Hilal ibn Zayd ibn Yasar. Ibn Hibban said: He narrates from Anas things that are fabricated, which Anas never related at all; it is not permissible to argue with him in any way." Al-Dhahabi mentioned it in al-Mizan (4/313) and said: "False." See also the words of al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in al-Qawl al-Musaddad, no. (8), where he mentions that the hadith is about virtues of deeds and encouragement to garrison duty in the way of Allah, and that leniency in narrating such material is the method of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him. He then cited supporting evidence for it, so consult it if you wish.]]

﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: before the assembled creation. ﴿Indeed, You do not break the promise﴾, meaning: there must be the appointment which You informed Your messengers about, which is standing before You on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: al-Harith ibn Surayj narrated to us; al-Mu'tamir narrated to us; al-Fadl ibn 'Isa narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, that Jabir ibn 'Abdullah told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shame and disgrace will reach the son of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, in the standing before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to the point that the servant wishes he would be ordered to the Fire." This is a strange hadith. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/311). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/350): "In it is al-Fadl ibn 'Isa al-Raqqashi, on whom there is consensus of weakness."]]

It is established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite these ten verses at the end of Al 'Imran when he rose at night for his tahajjud (night prayer). Then al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shuraik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Namir informed me, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I spent the night at the house of my maternal aunt Maymunah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) talked with his family for a while, then slept. When the last third of the night came, he sat up, looked at the sky, and said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding.﴾ Then he got up, performed ablution and used the siwak. He prayed eleven rak'ahs. Then Bilal called the adhan, and he prayed two rak'ahs, then went out and led the people in the dawn prayer."

Muslim also related it similarly from Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq al-Sana'ani, from Ibn Abi Maryam, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4569; Sahih Muslim, no. 763.]

Then al-Bukhari related it through several routes from Malik, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas [in some manuscripts: "Ibn Abbas informed him"], that he spent the night at the house of Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who was his aunt. He said: "I lay down across the width of the pillow, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his family lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slept until midnight, or a little before it or a little after it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) woke from his sleep and began to wipe the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the last ten verses of Surah Al 'Imran. Then he got up to a hanging water-skin, performed ablution from it, and did it well [in some manuscripts: 'the ablution'], then stood to pray. Ibn Abbas said: 'So I got up and did what he did, then I went and stood beside him.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his right hand on my head and took hold of my right ear, twisting it. He prayed two rak'ahs, then two, then two, then two, then two, then two, then two, then he performed Witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He got up and prayed two light rak'ahs, then went out and led the dawn prayer."

The rest of the collectors related it in various routes from Malik with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4570, 4571; Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1367; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/210); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1363; as for al-Tirmidhi, he related it in al-Shama'il, no. 252.] Muslim and Abu Dawud also related it from other routes, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1364.]

Another route for this hadith from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both).

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us: Abu Yahya ibn Abi Misarra [in some manuscripts: "Maysara"] informed us: Khallad ibn Yahya informed us: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq informed us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Abbas [in some manuscripts: "from his father" and in others "from Ibn Abbas"], who said: "Al-Abbas ordered me to spend the night with the family of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to observe his prayer. He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led the people in the night prayer, the 'Isha, until no one remained in the mosque except him. Then he stood and passed by me and said: "Who is this? Abdullah?" I said: "Yes." He said: "What is it?" I said: "Al-Abbas ordered me to spend the night with you tonight." He said: "Then stay with us." When he entered [the house] he said: "Shall I spread out a bed for Abdullah?" So a pillow of coarse wool was brought, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slept on it until I heard his snoring. Then he sat up on his bed, raised his head to the sky and said: "Glory be to the King, the Holy" three times. Then he recited these verses from the end of Surah Al 'Imran until he finished them.'"

Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also related a hadith in this regard from the narration of Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from his father. [Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1353; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/236).]

Another route, related by Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of Asim ibn Bahdalah, from one of his companions, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out one night after part of the night had passed, looked at the sky, and recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾ to the end of the Surah. Then he said: "O Allah, place in my heart light, in my hearing light, in my sight light, on my right light, on my left light, before me light, behind me light, above me light, below me light, and make light great for me on the Day of Resurrection." This supplication is established in some sound routes, from the narration of Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him). [The chain contains Asim, who has been criticized, and his shaykh is unknown. Al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih, no. 4569, and Muslim, no. 763, through Kurayb from Ibn Abbas, in similar wording.]

Then Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim related, from the hadith of Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Quraysh came to the Jews and said: 'What signs did Musa bring you?' They said: 'His staff and his white hand, for the onlookers.' They came to the Christians and said: 'How was Isa among you?' They said: 'He healed the blind and the leper, and brought the dead to life.' Then they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Ask your Lord to turn the Safa into gold for us.' So he supplicated to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾." He said: "Let them reflect upon them." This is the wording of Ibn Mardawayh. [Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn al-Mundhir related it as in al-Durr (2/407). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (8/235): "Its narrators are trustworthy except al-Hammani, who is criticized; and al-Hasan ibn Musa contradicted him, relating it from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, as a mursal (broken) report, and this is more likely. Even if it is preserved as connected, there is a difficulty: this surah is Madani, while the Quraysh were people of Makkah. It may be that their question was after the Prophet (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, especially during the time of the truce."]

The narration of al-Tabarani for this hadith has already been cited at the beginning of the verse, and this implies that these verses are Makki. However, what is well known is that they are Madani, and the evidence for this is another hadith. Ibn Mardawayh said:

Isma'il ibn Ali ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Harrani informed us: Shuja' ibn Ashras narrated to us: Hashraj ibn Nabata al-Wasiti, Abu Mukram narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, who is Abu Janab [in some manuscripts: "Hibban"; "al-Kalbi" added from another manuscript], from Ata', who said: "Myself, Ibn Umar and Ubayd ibn Umayr set out to visit Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her). We entered upon her with a screen between us and her, and she said: 'O Ubayd, what prevents you from visiting us?' He said: the saying of the poet:

'Visit occasionally, and your love will grow.'

Ibn Umar said: 'Leave us, and tell us the most wondrous thing you saw from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' She wept and said: 'All of his affairs were wondrous. He came to me one night until his skin touched my skin, then he said: "Leave me, so that I may worship my Lord [Mighty and Majestic]."' She said: 'I said: "By Allah, I love your nearness, and I love that you worship your Lord."' So he got up to the water-skin, performed ablution, and did not pour much water. Then he stood to pray and wept until his beard was wet. Then he prostrated and wept until the ground was wet. Then he lay on his side and wept, until Bilal came to call him to the dawn prayer. She said: Bilal said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what makes you weep, when Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins?' He said: 'Woe to you, O Bilal! What prevents me from weeping, when this was revealed to me on this night: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾.'" Then he said: "Woe to whoever recites it and does not reflect upon it."

Abd ibn Humayd also related it in his tafsir: Ja'far ibn Awn informed us, from Abu Janab al-Kalbi, from Ata', with a longer and more complete narration. [Ibn Mardawayh's route was also related by al-Asbahani in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib, no. 666. Its chain contains Abu Janab al-Kalbi, who is weak and is alone in this narration.]

Likewise, Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih, from Imran ibn Musa, from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya, from Ibrahim ibn Suwayd al-Nakha'i, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ata', who said: "Myself, Abdullah ibn Umar and Ubayd ibn Umayr entered upon Aishah [in one manuscript: "upon the Mother of the Believers"], and he mentioned something similar."

Likewise, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya related it in his book "al-Tafakkur wa al-I'tibar", from Shuja' ibn Ashras, with the same chain. Then he said: al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to me: I heard Sunayd mention, from Sufyan (al-Thawri), with a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report, that he said: "Whoever recites the last of Al 'Imran and does not reflect upon it, woe to him," counting ten on his fingers. Al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Aziz said: Ubayd ibn al-Sa'ib informed me: It was said to al-Awza'i: "What is the ultimate extent of reflection upon them?" He said: "That one recites them while understanding them."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Qasim ibn Hashim narrated to me: Ali ibn Ayyash narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: "I asked al-Awza'i about the least that one who reflects upon them must attain, and what saves him from this woe? He lowered his head for a moment, then said: 'That one recites them while understanding them.'"

[Another hadith with a strange element: Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir ibn Numayr informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Busti informed us, and he said (ḥ): Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd informed us, and Ahmad ibn Amr said: Hisham ibn Ammar informed us: Sulayman ibn Musa al-Zuhri informed us: Mazahir ibn Aslam al-Makhzumi informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqbari informed us, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite ten verses from the end of Surah Al 'Imran every night. Mazahir ibn Aslam is weak.]

Al-Tabarani said: Al-Hasan ibn Ishaq al-Tustari narrated to us, Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Quraysh went to the Jews and said, "With what did Musa come to you?" They said, "His staff and his hand, white for the onlookers." Then they went to the Christians and said, "How was 'Isa?" They said, "He healed the blind and the leper, and raised the dead." So they came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Ask your Lord to make Safa turn to gold for us." He prayed to his Lord, and this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding.﴾ So let them reflect upon it. [[Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12322). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/332): "In it is Yahya al-Himmani, who is weak."]] This is problematic, for this verse is Medinan, whereas their request that Safa become gold was in Makkah. And Allah knows best.

The meaning of the verse: He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning, these in their height and vastness, and those in their lowness and density and their being spread out, and what is in them of great observable signs: wandering planets, fixed stars, seas, mountains, deserts, trees, plants, crops, fruits, animals, minerals and benefits, differing in colors, tastes, scents and properties. ﴿And the alternation of the night and the day﴾, meaning their succession and their exchanging of length and shortness: at times this one lengthens and that one shortens, then they become equal, then this one takes from that one, so that what was short becomes long and what was long becomes short. All of this is the decree of the Mighty, the Wise [in some copies: "the All-Knowing"]. Therefore He said: ﴿for those of understanding﴾, meaning, those of complete and sharp intellects, who perceive things in their realities as they truly are. They are not like the deaf and dumb who do not reason, concerning whom Allah said: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it. And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 105–106]

Then the Exalted described those of understanding, saying: ﴿Who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾, as it is established in Sahih al-Bukhari from 'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (1115). In some copies: "side" (jamb).]] Meaning: they do not cease to remember Him in all their states, with their inner selves, their consciences and their tongues. ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: they understand the wisdoms in them that indicate the greatness of the Creator, His power, His knowledge, His wisdom, His choice and His mercy.

Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: "I go out from my house, and my gaze does not fall upon anything without my seeing in it a blessing from Allah upon me, or a lesson for me." Narrated by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in his book "al-Tafakkur wal-I'tibar" [[In the manuscripts: "al-Tawakkul", but the correct reading is what we have adopted, as mentioned by al-Dhahabi in Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (13/402) and in the catalogue of Ibn Abi al-Dunya's works held at the Zahiriyya library. It will come later in the section with full vocalization. See p. 189.]].

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he said: "An hour of reflection is better than a night of standing in prayer." Al-Fudayl said: Al-Hasan said: "Reflection is a mirror that shows you your good deeds and your bad deeds." Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: "Reflection is a light that enters your heart." He often quoted this verse:

"When a person has the faculty of reflection,
then in everything there is a lesson for him."

And from 'Isa, peace be upon him, that he said: "Blessed is the one whose speech is remembrance, whose silence is reflection, and whose gaze is lessons."

Luqman the Wise said: "Long solitude is most conducive to reflection, and long reflection is a sign of knocking on the door of Paradise."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "A person's reflection never lengthens except that he understands; no one understands except that he knows; and no one knows except that he acts."

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: "Speech about the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is good, and reflection upon the blessings of Allah is the best of worship."

Mughith al-Aswad said: "Visit the graves every day so that they make you reflect; witness the place of standing with your hearts; look at the two groups departing, to Paradise or to the Fire; and make your hearts and bodies aware of the remembrance of the Fire, its chains and its layers." He would weep at that until he was carried away fainting from among his companions, his mind gone.

'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: A man passed by a monk beside a graveyard and a rubbish heap, and he called out to him: "O monk, you have two treasures of the treasures of this world, in which there is a lesson for you: the treasure of men and the treasure of wealth."

From Ibn 'Umar: whenever he wished to examine his heart, he would come to a ruined house, stand at its door, call out in a sorrowful voice, and say: "Where are its people?" Then he would return to himself and say: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face.﴾ [al-Qasas: 88]

From Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "Two moderate rak'ahs with reflection are better than a night of standing in prayer while the heart is heedless."

Al-Hasan said: "O son of Adam, eat with one third of your stomach, drink with one third, and leave the last third for breathing and for reflection."

Some of the wise said: "Whoever looks at this world without taking heed has his heart's sight blinded to the degree of that heedlessness."

Bishr ibn al-Harith al-Hafi said: "If people reflected upon the greatness of Allah, they would not disobey Him."

Al-Hasan, from 'Amir ibn 'Abd Qays, who said: "I heard more than one, not two or three, of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ say: Indeed, the radiance of faith, or the light of faith, is reflection."

From 'Isa, peace be upon him, that he said: "O weak son of Adam, fear Allah wherever you are; be a guest in this world; take the mosques as your house; teach your eyes weeping, your body patience, and your heart reflection; and do not worry about tomorrow's provision."

From the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, that one day he wept among his companions. When he was asked about that, he said: "I reflected upon this world, its pleasures and its desires, and I took a lesson from it through itself. Its desires hardly end before its bitterness spoils them. If there is no lesson in it for the one who takes lessons, there are indeed admonitions in it for the one who remembers."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Al-Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman recited to me:

"The believer's recreation is reflection;
the believer's pleasure is lessons.
We praise Allah alone;
we are all on a precipice.
Many a heedless man whose life
has passed without his noticing.
Many a life that was above all hopes,
radiant in its blossoming,
amid streams from the springs
and shade from the trees,
and joy from the plants
and sweetness from the fruits,
which the swift passing of time changed, and its people with it, by change.
We praise Allah alone;
indeed in this there is a lesson.
Indeed in this is a lesson
for the intelligent one, if he takes heed."

Allah the Exalted has censured those who do not take lessons from His creatures, which point to His essence, His attributes, His law, His decree and His signs. He said: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it. And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 105–106] And He praised His believing servants: ﴿Who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth,﴾ saying, ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain.﴾ That is: You did not create this creation in vain, but in truth, so that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best. Then they glorified Him above futility and the creation of vanity, saying: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, that is, far above creating anything in vain. ﴿So protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾, meaning: O You who created creation with truth and justice, O You who are free from deficiencies, defects and futility, protect us from the punishment of the Fire by Your power and strength, and facilitate for us deeds with which You will be pleased with us, and grant us success in righteous deeds by which You guide us to the Gardens of Bliss and protect us through them from Your painful punishment.

Then they said: ﴿Our Lord, indeed whomever You admit to the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him﴾, meaning: You have humiliated him and displayed his disgrace before the assembled. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there will be no helpers﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection there will be no protector for them from You, nor anyone to turn them away from what You intend for them.

﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith﴾, meaning: a summoner calling to faith, and he is the Messenger ﷺ, ﴿Believe in your Lord,﴾ meaning he says: "Believe in your Lord," so we believed, meaning: we responded to him and followed him. ﴿Our Lord, so forgive us our sins﴾, meaning: by our faith and our following of Your Prophet, so forgive us our sins, that is, cover them. ﴿And remove from us our misdeeds﴾, meaning: concerning what is between us and You. ﴿And take us in death with the righteous﴾, meaning: join us with the righteous. ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾. It was said: its meaning is: [what You promised] upon belief in Your messengers. And it was said: its meaning is: upon the tongues of Your messengers. And this is more apparent.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Iqal, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Asqalan is one of the two brides. From it Allah will raise on the Day of Resurrection seventy thousand people who will have no reckoning, and from it He will raise fifty thousand martyrs, delegations to Allah, and there are the ranks of the martyrs, their heads severed and held in their hands, their veins gushing blood, saying: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break Your promise.﴾ Then He will say: 'My servant has spoken the truth. Wash them in the river of al-Bayda.' They will come out from it pure and white, and they will roam in Paradise wherever they wish."

This hadith is counted among the strange narrations of the Musnad, and some consider it fabricated, and Allah knows best. [[Al-Musnad (3/225). Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it in al-Mawdu'at (2/54) and said: "This hadith is not authentic from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. All its chains revolve around Abu 'Iqal, whose name is Hilal ibn Zayd ibn Yasar. Ibn Hibban said: He narrates from Anas things that are fabricated, which Anas never related at all; it is not permissible to argue with him in any way." Al-Dhahabi mentioned it in al-Mizan (4/313) and said: "False." See also the words of al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in al-Qawl al-Musaddad, no. (8), where he mentions that the hadith is about virtues of deeds and encouragement to garrison duty in the way of Allah, and that leniency in narrating such material is the method of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him. He then cited supporting evidence for it, so consult it if you wish.]]

﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: before the assembled creation. ﴿Indeed, You do not break the promise﴾, meaning: there must be the appointment which You informed Your messengers about, which is standing before You on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: al-Harith ibn Surayj narrated to us; al-Mu'tamir narrated to us; al-Fadl ibn 'Isa narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, that Jabir ibn 'Abdullah told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shame and disgrace will reach the son of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, in the standing before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to the point that the servant wishes he would be ordered to the Fire." This is a strange hadith. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/311). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/350): "In it is al-Fadl ibn 'Isa al-Raqqashi, on whom there is consensus of weakness."]]

It is established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite these ten verses at the end of Al 'Imran when he rose at night for his tahajjud (night prayer). Then al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shuraik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Namir informed me, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I spent the night at the house of my maternal aunt Maymunah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) talked with his family for a while, then slept. When the last third of the night came, he sat up, looked at the sky, and said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding.﴾ Then he got up, performed ablution and used the siwak. He prayed eleven rak'ahs. Then Bilal called the adhan, and he prayed two rak'ahs, then went out and led the people in the dawn prayer."

Muslim also related it similarly from Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq al-Sana'ani, from Ibn Abi Maryam, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4569; Sahih Muslim, no. 763.]

Then al-Bukhari related it through several routes from Malik, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas [in some manuscripts: "Ibn Abbas informed him"], that he spent the night at the house of Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who was his aunt. He said: "I lay down across the width of the pillow, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his family lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slept until midnight, or a little before it or a little after it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) woke from his sleep and began to wipe the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the last ten verses of Surah Al 'Imran. Then he got up to a hanging water-skin, performed ablution from it, and did it well [in some manuscripts: 'the ablution'], then stood to pray. Ibn Abbas said: 'So I got up and did what he did, then I went and stood beside him.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his right hand on my head and took hold of my right ear, twisting it. He prayed two rak'ahs, then two, then two, then two, then two, then two, then two, then he performed Witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He got up and prayed two light rak'ahs, then went out and led the dawn prayer."

The rest of the collectors related it in various routes from Malik with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4570, 4571; Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1367; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/210); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1363; as for al-Tirmidhi, he related it in al-Shama'il, no. 252.] Muslim and Abu Dawud also related it from other routes, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1364.]

Another route for this hadith from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both).

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us: Abu Yahya ibn Abi Misarra [in some manuscripts: "Maysara"] informed us: Khallad ibn Yahya informed us: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq informed us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Abbas [in some manuscripts: "from his father" and in others "from Ibn Abbas"], who said: "Al-Abbas ordered me to spend the night with the family of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to observe his prayer. He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led the people in the night prayer, the 'Isha, until no one remained in the mosque except him. Then he stood and passed by me and said: "Who is this? Abdullah?" I said: "Yes." He said: "What is it?" I said: "Al-Abbas ordered me to spend the night with you tonight." He said: "Then stay with us." When he entered [the house] he said: "Shall I spread out a bed for Abdullah?" So a pillow of coarse wool was brought, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slept on it until I heard his snoring. Then he sat up on his bed, raised his head to the sky and said: "Glory be to the King, the Holy" three times. Then he recited these verses from the end of Surah Al 'Imran until he finished them.'"

Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also related a hadith in this regard from the narration of Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from his father. [Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1353; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/236).]

Another route, related by Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of Asim ibn Bahdalah, from one of his companions, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out one night after part of the night had passed, looked at the sky, and recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾ to the end of the Surah. Then he said: "O Allah, place in my heart light, in my hearing light, in my sight light, on my right light, on my left light, before me light, behind me light, above me light, below me light, and make light great for me on the Day of Resurrection." This supplication is established in some sound routes, from the narration of Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him). [The chain contains Asim, who has been criticized, and his shaykh is unknown. Al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih, no. 4569, and Muslim, no. 763, through Kurayb from Ibn Abbas, in similar wording.]

Then Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim related, from the hadith of Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Quraysh came to the Jews and said: 'What signs did Musa bring you?' They said: 'His staff and his white hand, for the onlookers.' They came to the Christians and said: 'How was Isa among you?' They said: 'He healed the blind and the leper, and brought the dead to life.' Then they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Ask your Lord to turn the Safa into gold for us.' So he supplicated to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾." He said: "Let them reflect upon them." This is the wording of Ibn Mardawayh. [Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn al-Mundhir related it as in al-Durr (2/407). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (8/235): "Its narrators are trustworthy except al-Hammani, who is criticized; and al-Hasan ibn Musa contradicted him, relating it from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, as a mursal (broken) report, and this is more likely. Even if it is preserved as connected, there is a difficulty: this surah is Madani, while the Quraysh were people of Makkah. It may be that their question was after the Prophet (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, especially during the time of the truce."]

The narration of al-Tabarani for this hadith has already been cited at the beginning of the verse, and this implies that these verses are Makki. However, what is well known is that they are Madani, and the evidence for this is another hadith. Ibn Mardawayh said:

Isma'il ibn Ali ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Harrani informed us: Shuja' ibn Ashras narrated to us: Hashraj ibn Nabata al-Wasiti, Abu Mukram narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, who is Abu Janab [in some manuscripts: "Hibban"; "al-Kalbi" added from another manuscript], from Ata', who said: "Myself, Ibn Umar and Ubayd ibn Umayr set out to visit Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her). We entered upon her with a screen between us and her, and she said: 'O Ubayd, what prevents you from visiting us?' He said: the saying of the poet:

'Visit occasionally, and your love will grow.'

Ibn Umar said: 'Leave us, and tell us the most wondrous thing you saw from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' She wept and said: 'All of his affairs were wondrous. He came to me one night until his skin touched my skin, then he said: "Leave me, so that I may worship my Lord [Mighty and Majestic]."' She said: 'I said: "By Allah, I love your nearness, and I love that you worship your Lord."' So he got up to the water-skin, performed ablution, and did not pour much water. Then he stood to pray and wept until his beard was wet. Then he prostrated and wept until the ground was wet. Then he lay on his side and wept, until Bilal came to call him to the dawn prayer. She said: Bilal said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what makes you weep, when Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins?' He said: 'Woe to you, O Bilal! What prevents me from weeping, when this was revealed to me on this night: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾.'" Then he said: "Woe to whoever recites it and does not reflect upon it."

Abd ibn Humayd also related it in his tafsir: Ja'far ibn Awn informed us, from Abu Janab al-Kalbi, from Ata', with a longer and more complete narration. [Ibn Mardawayh's route was also related by al-Asbahani in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib, no. 666. Its chain contains Abu Janab al-Kalbi, who is weak and is alone in this narration.]

Likewise, Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih, from Imran ibn Musa, from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya, from Ibrahim ibn Suwayd al-Nakha'i, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ata', who said: "Myself, Abdullah ibn Umar and Ubayd ibn Umayr entered upon Aishah [in one manuscript: "upon the Mother of the Believers"], and he mentioned something similar."

Likewise, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya related it in his book "al-Tafakkur wa al-I'tibar", from Shuja' ibn Ashras, with the same chain. Then he said: al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to me: I heard Sunayd mention, from Sufyan (al-Thawri), with a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report, that he said: "Whoever recites the last of Al 'Imran and does not reflect upon it, woe to him," counting ten on his fingers. Al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Aziz said: Ubayd ibn al-Sa'ib informed me: It was said to al-Awza'i: "What is the ultimate extent of reflection upon them?" He said: "That one recites them while understanding them."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Qasim ibn Hashim narrated to me: Ali ibn Ayyash narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: "I asked al-Awza'i about the least that one who reflects upon them must attain, and what saves him from this woe? He lowered his head for a moment, then said: 'That one recites them while understanding them.'"

[Another hadith with a strange element: Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir ibn Numayr informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Busti informed us, and he said (ḥ): Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd informed us, and Ahmad ibn Amr said: Hisham ibn Ammar informed us: Sulayman ibn Musa al-Zuhri informed us: Mazahir ibn Aslam al-Makhzumi informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqbari informed us, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite ten verses from the end of Surah Al 'Imran every night. Mazahir ibn Aslam is weak.]

Al-Tabarani said: Al-Hasan ibn Ishaq al-Tustari narrated to us, Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Quraysh went to the Jews and said, "With what did Musa come to you?" They said, "His staff and his hand, white for the onlookers." Then they went to the Christians and said, "How was 'Isa?" They said, "He healed the blind and the leper, and raised the dead." So they came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Ask your Lord to make Safa turn to gold for us." He prayed to his Lord, and this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding.﴾ So let them reflect upon it. [[Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12322). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/332): "In it is Yahya al-Himmani, who is weak."]] This is problematic, for this verse is Medinan, whereas their request that Safa become gold was in Makkah. And Allah knows best.

The meaning of the verse: He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning, these in their height and vastness, and those in their lowness and density and their being spread out, and what is in them of great observable signs: wandering planets, fixed stars, seas, mountains, deserts, trees, plants, crops, fruits, animals, minerals and benefits, differing in colors, tastes, scents and properties. ﴿And the alternation of the night and the day﴾, meaning their succession and their exchanging of length and shortness: at times this one lengthens and that one shortens, then they become equal, then this one takes from that one, so that what was short becomes long and what was long becomes short. All of this is the decree of the Mighty, the Wise [in some copies: "the All-Knowing"]. Therefore He said: ﴿for those of understanding﴾, meaning, those of complete and sharp intellects, who perceive things in their realities as they truly are. They are not like the deaf and dumb who do not reason, concerning whom Allah said: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it. And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 105–106]

Then the Exalted described those of understanding, saying: ﴿Who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾, as it is established in Sahih al-Bukhari from 'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (1115). In some copies: "side" (jamb).]] Meaning: they do not cease to remember Him in all their states, with their inner selves, their consciences and their tongues. ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: they understand the wisdoms in them that indicate the greatness of the Creator, His power, His knowledge, His wisdom, His choice and His mercy.

Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: "I go out from my house, and my gaze does not fall upon anything without my seeing in it a blessing from Allah upon me, or a lesson for me." Narrated by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in his book "al-Tafakkur wal-I'tibar" [[In the manuscripts: "al-Tawakkul", but the correct reading is what we have adopted, as mentioned by al-Dhahabi in Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (13/402) and in the catalogue of Ibn Abi al-Dunya's works held at the Zahiriyya library. It will come later in the section with full vocalization. See p. 189.]].

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he said: "An hour of reflection is better than a night of standing in prayer." Al-Fudayl said: Al-Hasan said: "Reflection is a mirror that shows you your good deeds and your bad deeds." Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: "Reflection is a light that enters your heart." He often quoted this verse:

"When a person has the faculty of reflection,
then in everything there is a lesson for him."

And from 'Isa, peace be upon him, that he said: "Blessed is the one whose speech is remembrance, whose silence is reflection, and whose gaze is lessons."

Luqman the Wise said: "Long solitude is most conducive to reflection, and long reflection is a sign of knocking on the door of Paradise."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "A person's reflection never lengthens except that he understands; no one understands except that he knows; and no one knows except that he acts."

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: "Speech about the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is good, and reflection upon the blessings of Allah is the best of worship."

Mughith al-Aswad said: "Visit the graves every day so that they make you reflect; witness the place of standing with your hearts; look at the two groups departing, to Paradise or to the Fire; and make your hearts and bodies aware of the remembrance of the Fire, its chains and its layers." He would weep at that until he was carried away fainting from among his companions, his mind gone.

'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: A man passed by a monk beside a graveyard and a rubbish heap, and he called out to him: "O monk, you have two treasures of the treasures of this world, in which there is a lesson for you: the treasure of men and the treasure of wealth."

From Ibn 'Umar: whenever he wished to examine his heart, he would come to a ruined house, stand at its door, call out in a sorrowful voice, and say: "Where are its people?" Then he would return to himself and say: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face.﴾ [al-Qasas: 88]

From Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "Two moderate rak'ahs with reflection are better than a night of standing in prayer while the heart is heedless."

Al-Hasan said: "O son of Adam, eat with one third of your stomach, drink with one third, and leave the last third for breathing and for reflection."

Some of the wise said: "Whoever looks at this world without taking heed has his heart's sight blinded to the degree of that heedlessness."

Bishr ibn al-Harith al-Hafi said: "If people reflected upon the greatness of Allah, they would not disobey Him."

Al-Hasan, from 'Amir ibn 'Abd Qays, who said: "I heard more than one, not two or three, of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ say: Indeed, the radiance of faith, or the light of faith, is reflection."

From 'Isa, peace be upon him, that he said: "O weak son of Adam, fear Allah wherever you are; be a guest in this world; take the mosques as your house; teach your eyes weeping, your body patience, and your heart reflection; and do not worry about tomorrow's provision."

From the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, that one day he wept among his companions. When he was asked about that, he said: "I reflected upon this world, its pleasures and its desires, and I took a lesson from it through itself. Its desires hardly end before its bitterness spoils them. If there is no lesson in it for the one who takes lessons, there are indeed admonitions in it for the one who remembers."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Al-Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman recited to me:

"The believer's recreation is reflection;
the believer's pleasure is lessons.
We praise Allah alone;
we are all on a precipice.
Many a heedless man whose life
has passed without his noticing.
Many a life that was above all hopes,
radiant in its blossoming,
amid streams from the springs
and shade from the trees,
and joy from the plants
and sweetness from the fruits,
which the swift passing of time changed, and its people with it, by change.
We praise Allah alone;
indeed in this there is a lesson.
Indeed in this is a lesson
for the intelligent one, if he takes heed."

Allah the Exalted has censured those who do not take lessons from His creatures, which point to His essence, His attributes, His law, His decree and His signs. He said: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it. And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 105–106] And He praised His believing servants: ﴿Who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth,﴾ saying, ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain.﴾ That is: You did not create this creation in vain, but in truth, so that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best. Then they glorified Him above futility and the creation of vanity, saying: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, that is, far above creating anything in vain. ﴿So protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾, meaning: O You who created creation with truth and justice, O You who are free from deficiencies, defects and futility, protect us from the punishment of the Fire by Your power and strength, and facilitate for us deeds with which You will be pleased with us, and grant us success in righteous deeds by which You guide us to the Gardens of Bliss and protect us through them from Your painful punishment.

Then they said: ﴿Our Lord, indeed whomever You admit to the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him﴾, meaning: You have humiliated him and displayed his disgrace before the assembled. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there will be no helpers﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection there will be no protector for them from You, nor anyone to turn them away from what You intend for them.

﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith﴾, meaning: a summoner calling to faith, and he is the Messenger ﷺ, ﴿Believe in your Lord,﴾ meaning he says: "Believe in your Lord," so we believed, meaning: we responded to him and followed him. ﴿Our Lord, so forgive us our sins﴾, meaning: by our faith and our following of Your Prophet, so forgive us our sins, that is, cover them. ﴿And remove from us our misdeeds﴾, meaning: concerning what is between us and You. ﴿And take us in death with the righteous﴾, meaning: join us with the righteous. ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾. It was said: its meaning is: [what You promised] upon belief in Your messengers. And it was said: its meaning is: upon the tongues of Your messengers. And this is more apparent.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Iqal, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Asqalan is one of the two brides. From it Allah will raise on the Day of Resurrection seventy thousand people who will have no reckoning, and from it He will raise fifty thousand martyrs, delegations to Allah, and there are the ranks of the martyrs, their heads severed and held in their hands, their veins gushing blood, saying: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break Your promise.﴾ Then He will say: 'My servant has spoken the truth. Wash them in the river of al-Bayda.' They will come out from it pure and white, and they will roam in Paradise wherever they wish."

This hadith is counted among the strange narrations of the Musnad, and some consider it fabricated, and Allah knows best. [[Al-Musnad (3/225). Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it in al-Mawdu'at (2/54) and said: "This hadith is not authentic from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. All its chains revolve around Abu 'Iqal, whose name is Hilal ibn Zayd ibn Yasar. Ibn Hibban said: He narrates from Anas things that are fabricated, which Anas never related at all; it is not permissible to argue with him in any way." Al-Dhahabi mentioned it in al-Mizan (4/313) and said: "False." See also the words of al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in al-Qawl al-Musaddad, no. (8), where he mentions that the hadith is about virtues of deeds and encouragement to garrison duty in the way of Allah, and that leniency in narrating such material is the method of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him. He then cited supporting evidence for it, so consult it if you wish.]]

﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: before the assembled creation. ﴿Indeed, You do not break the promise﴾, meaning: there must be the appointment which You informed Your messengers about, which is standing before You on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: al-Harith ibn Surayj narrated to us; al-Mu'tamir narrated to us; al-Fadl ibn 'Isa narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, that Jabir ibn 'Abdullah told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shame and disgrace will reach the son of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, in the standing before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to the point that the servant wishes he would be ordered to the Fire." This is a strange hadith. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/311). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/350): "In it is al-Fadl ibn 'Isa al-Raqqashi, on whom there is consensus of weakness."]]

It is established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite these ten verses at the end of Al 'Imran when he rose at night for his tahajjud (night prayer). Then al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shuraik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Namir informed me, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I spent the night at the house of my maternal aunt Maymunah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) talked with his family for a while, then slept. When the last third of the night came, he sat up, looked at the sky, and said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding.﴾ Then he got up, performed ablution and used the siwak. He prayed eleven rak'ahs. Then Bilal called the adhan, and he prayed two rak'ahs, then went out and led the people in the dawn prayer."

Muslim also related it similarly from Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq al-Sana'ani, from Ibn Abi Maryam, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4569; Sahih Muslim, no. 763.]

Then al-Bukhari related it through several routes from Malik, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas [in some manuscripts: "Ibn Abbas informed him"], that he spent the night at the house of Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who was his aunt. He said: "I lay down across the width of the pillow, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his family lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slept until midnight, or a little before it or a little after it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) woke from his sleep and began to wipe the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the last ten verses of Surah Al 'Imran. Then he got up to a hanging water-skin, performed ablution from it, and did it well [in some manuscripts: 'the ablution'], then stood to pray. Ibn Abbas said: 'So I got up and did what he did, then I went and stood beside him.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his right hand on my head and took hold of my right ear, twisting it. He prayed two rak'ahs, then two, then two, then two, then two, then two, then two, then he performed Witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He got up and prayed two light rak'ahs, then went out and led the dawn prayer."

The rest of the collectors related it in various routes from Malik with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4570, 4571; Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1367; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/210); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1363; as for al-Tirmidhi, he related it in al-Shama'il, no. 252.] Muslim and Abu Dawud also related it from other routes, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1364.]

Another route for this hadith from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both).

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us: Abu Yahya ibn Abi Misarra [in some manuscripts: "Maysara"] informed us: Khallad ibn Yahya informed us: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq informed us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Abbas [in some manuscripts: "from his father" and in others "from Ibn Abbas"], who said: "Al-Abbas ordered me to spend the night with the family of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to observe his prayer. He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led the people in the night prayer, the 'Isha, until no one remained in the mosque except him. Then he stood and passed by me and said: "Who is this? Abdullah?" I said: "Yes." He said: "What is it?" I said: "Al-Abbas ordered me to spend the night with you tonight." He said: "Then stay with us." When he entered [the house] he said: "Shall I spread out a bed for Abdullah?" So a pillow of coarse wool was brought, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slept on it until I heard his snoring. Then he sat up on his bed, raised his head to the sky and said: "Glory be to the King, the Holy" three times. Then he recited these verses from the end of Surah Al 'Imran until he finished them.'"

Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also related a hadith in this regard from the narration of Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from his father. [Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1353; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/236).]

Another route, related by Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of Asim ibn Bahdalah, from one of his companions, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out one night after part of the night had passed, looked at the sky, and recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾ to the end of the Surah. Then he said: "O Allah, place in my heart light, in my hearing light, in my sight light, on my right light, on my left light, before me light, behind me light, above me light, below me light, and make light great for me on the Day of Resurrection." This supplication is established in some sound routes, from the narration of Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him). [The chain contains Asim, who has been criticized, and his shaykh is unknown. Al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih, no. 4569, and Muslim, no. 763, through Kurayb from Ibn Abbas, in similar wording.]

Then Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim related, from the hadith of Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Quraysh came to the Jews and said: 'What signs did Musa bring you?' They said: 'His staff and his white hand, for the onlookers.' They came to the Christians and said: 'How was Isa among you?' They said: 'He healed the blind and the leper, and brought the dead to life.' Then they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Ask your Lord to turn the Safa into gold for us.' So he supplicated to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾." He said: "Let them reflect upon them." This is the wording of Ibn Mardawayh. [Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn al-Mundhir related it as in al-Durr (2/407). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (8/235): "Its narrators are trustworthy except al-Hammani, who is criticized; and al-Hasan ibn Musa contradicted him, relating it from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, as a mursal (broken) report, and this is more likely. Even if it is preserved as connected, there is a difficulty: this surah is Madani, while the Quraysh were people of Makkah. It may be that their question was after the Prophet (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, especially during the time of the truce."]

The narration of al-Tabarani for this hadith has already been cited at the beginning of the verse, and this implies that these verses are Makki. However, what is well known is that they are Madani, and the evidence for this is another hadith. Ibn Mardawayh said:

Isma'il ibn Ali ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Harrani informed us: Shuja' ibn Ashras narrated to us: Hashraj ibn Nabata al-Wasiti, Abu Mukram narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, who is Abu Janab [in some manuscripts: "Hibban"; "al-Kalbi" added from another manuscript], from Ata', who said: "Myself, Ibn Umar and Ubayd ibn Umayr set out to visit Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her). We entered upon her with a screen between us and her, and she said: 'O Ubayd, what prevents you from visiting us?' He said: the saying of the poet:

'Visit occasionally, and your love will grow.'

Ibn Umar said: 'Leave us, and tell us the most wondrous thing you saw from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' She wept and said: 'All of his affairs were wondrous. He came to me one night until his skin touched my skin, then he said: "Leave me, so that I may worship my Lord [Mighty and Majestic]."' She said: 'I said: "By Allah, I love your nearness, and I love that you worship your Lord."' So he got up to the water-skin, performed ablution, and did not pour much water. Then he stood to pray and wept until his beard was wet. Then he prostrated and wept until the ground was wet. Then he lay on his side and wept, until Bilal came to call him to the dawn prayer. She said: Bilal said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what makes you weep, when Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins?' He said: 'Woe to you, O Bilal! What prevents me from weeping, when this was revealed to me on this night: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding﴾.'" Then he said: "Woe to whoever recites it and does not reflect upon it."

Abd ibn Humayd also related it in his tafsir: Ja'far ibn Awn informed us, from Abu Janab al-Kalbi, from Ata', with a longer and more complete narration. [Ibn Mardawayh's route was also related by al-Asbahani in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib, no. 666. Its chain contains Abu Janab al-Kalbi, who is weak and is alone in this narration.]

Likewise, Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih, from Imran ibn Musa, from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya, from Ibrahim ibn Suwayd al-Nakha'i, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ata', who said: "Myself, Abdullah ibn Umar and Ubayd ibn Umayr entered upon Aishah [in one manuscript: "upon the Mother of the Believers"], and he mentioned something similar."

Likewise, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya related it in his book "al-Tafakkur wa al-I'tibar", from Shuja' ibn Ashras, with the same chain. Then he said: al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to me: I heard Sunayd mention, from Sufyan (al-Thawri), with a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report, that he said: "Whoever recites the last of Al 'Imran and does not reflect upon it, woe to him," counting ten on his fingers. Al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Aziz said: Ubayd ibn al-Sa'ib informed me: It was said to al-Awza'i: "What is the ultimate extent of reflection upon them?" He said: "That one recites them while understanding them."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Qasim ibn Hashim narrated to me: Ali ibn Ayyash narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: "I asked al-Awza'i about the least that one who reflects upon them must attain, and what saves him from this woe? He lowered his head for a moment, then said: 'That one recites them while understanding them.'"

[Another hadith with a strange element: Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir ibn Numayr informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Busti informed us, and he said (ḥ): Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd informed us, and Ahmad ibn Amr said: Hisham ibn Ammar informed us: Sulayman ibn Musa al-Zuhri informed us: Mazahir ibn Aslam al-Makhzumi informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqbari informed us, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite ten verses from the end of Surah Al 'Imran every night. Mazahir ibn Aslam is weak.]

Al-Tabarani said: Al-Hasan ibn Ishaq al-Tustari narrated to us, Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Quraysh went to the Jews and said, "With what did Musa come to you?" They said, "His staff and his hand, white for the onlookers." Then they went to the Christians and said, "How was 'Isa?" They said, "He healed the blind and the leper, and raised the dead." So they came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "Ask your Lord to make Safa turn to gold for us." He prayed to his Lord, and this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding.﴾ So let them reflect upon it. [[Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12322). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/332): "In it is Yahya al-Himmani, who is weak."]] This is problematic, for this verse is Medinan, whereas their request that Safa become gold was in Makkah. And Allah knows best.

The meaning of the verse: He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning, these in their height and vastness, and those in their lowness and density and their being spread out, and what is in them of great observable signs: wandering planets, fixed stars, seas, mountains, deserts, trees, plants, crops, fruits, animals, minerals and benefits, differing in colors, tastes, scents and properties. ﴿And the alternation of the night and the day﴾, meaning their succession and their exchanging of length and shortness: at times this one lengthens and that one shortens, then they become equal, then this one takes from that one, so that what was short becomes long and what was long becomes short. All of this is the decree of the Mighty, the Wise [in some copies: "the All-Knowing"]. Therefore He said: ﴿for those of understanding﴾, meaning, those of complete and sharp intellects, who perceive things in their realities as they truly are. They are not like the deaf and dumb who do not reason, concerning whom Allah said: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it. And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 105–106]

Then the Exalted described those of understanding, saying: ﴿Who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾, as it is established in Sahih al-Bukhari from 'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (1115). In some copies: "side" (jamb).]] Meaning: they do not cease to remember Him in all their states, with their inner selves, their consciences and their tongues. ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: they understand the wisdoms in them that indicate the greatness of the Creator, His power, His knowledge, His wisdom, His choice and His mercy.

Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: "I go out from my house, and my gaze does not fall upon anything without my seeing in it a blessing from Allah upon me, or a lesson for me." Narrated by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in his book "al-Tafakkur wal-I'tibar" [[In the manuscripts: "al-Tawakkul", but the correct reading is what we have adopted, as mentioned by al-Dhahabi in Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (13/402) and in the catalogue of Ibn Abi al-Dunya's works held at the Zahiriyya library. It will come later in the section with full vocalization. See p. 189.]].

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he said: "An hour of reflection is better than a night of standing in prayer." Al-Fudayl said: Al-Hasan said: "Reflection is a mirror that shows you your good deeds and your bad deeds." Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: "Reflection is a light that enters your heart." He often quoted this verse:

"When a person has the faculty of reflection,
then in everything there is a lesson for him."

And from 'Isa, peace be upon him, that he said: "Blessed is the one whose speech is remembrance, whose silence is reflection, and whose gaze is lessons."

Luqman the Wise said: "Long solitude is most conducive to reflection, and long reflection is a sign of knocking on the door of Paradise."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "A person's reflection never lengthens except that he understands; no one understands except that he knows; and no one knows except that he acts."

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: "Speech about the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is good, and reflection upon the blessings of Allah is the best of worship."

Mughith al-Aswad said: "Visit the graves every day so that they make you reflect; witness the place of standing with your hearts; look at the two groups departing, to Paradise or to the Fire; and make your hearts and bodies aware of the remembrance of the Fire, its chains and its layers." He would weep at that until he was carried away fainting from among his companions, his mind gone.

'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: A man passed by a monk beside a graveyard and a rubbish heap, and he called out to him: "O monk, you have two treasures of the treasures of this world, in which there is a lesson for you: the treasure of men and the treasure of wealth."

From Ibn 'Umar: whenever he wished to examine his heart, he would come to a ruined house, stand at its door, call out in a sorrowful voice, and say: "Where are its people?" Then he would return to himself and say: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face.﴾ [al-Qasas: 88]

From Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "Two moderate rak'ahs with reflection are better than a night of standing in prayer while the heart is heedless."

Al-Hasan said: "O son of Adam, eat with one third of your stomach, drink with one third, and leave the last third for breathing and for reflection."

Some of the wise said: "Whoever looks at this world without taking heed has his heart's sight blinded to the degree of that heedlessness."

Bishr ibn al-Harith al-Hafi said: "If people reflected upon the greatness of Allah, they would not disobey Him."

Al-Hasan, from 'Amir ibn 'Abd Qays, who said: "I heard more than one, not two or three, of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ say: Indeed, the radiance of faith, or the light of faith, is reflection."

From 'Isa, peace be upon him, that he said: "O weak son of Adam, fear Allah wherever you are; be a guest in this world; take the mosques as your house; teach your eyes weeping, your body patience, and your heart reflection; and do not worry about tomorrow's provision."

From the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, that one day he wept among his companions. When he was asked about that, he said: "I reflected upon this world, its pleasures and its desires, and I took a lesson from it through itself. Its desires hardly end before its bitterness spoils them. If there is no lesson in it for the one who takes lessons, there are indeed admonitions in it for the one who remembers."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Al-Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman recited to me:

"The believer's recreation is reflection;
the believer's pleasure is lessons.
We praise Allah alone;
we are all on a precipice.
Many a heedless man whose life
has passed without his noticing.
Many a life that was above all hopes,
radiant in its blossoming,
amid streams from the springs
and shade from the trees,
and joy from the plants
and sweetness from the fruits,
which the swift passing of time changed, and its people with it, by change.
We praise Allah alone;
indeed in this there is a lesson.
Indeed in this is a lesson
for the intelligent one, if he takes heed."

Allah the Exalted has censured those who do not take lessons from His creatures, which point to His essence, His attributes, His law, His decree and His signs. He said: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it. And most of them do not believe in Allah except while they associate others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 105–106] And He praised His believing servants: ﴿Who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth,﴾ saying, ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain.﴾ That is: You did not create this creation in vain, but in truth, so that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best. Then they glorified Him above futility and the creation of vanity, saying: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, that is, far above creating anything in vain. ﴿So protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾, meaning: O You who created creation with truth and justice, O You who are free from deficiencies, defects and futility, protect us from the punishment of the Fire by Your power and strength, and facilitate for us deeds with which You will be pleased with us, and grant us success in righteous deeds by which You guide us to the Gardens of Bliss and protect us through them from Your painful punishment.

Then they said: ﴿Our Lord, indeed whomever You admit to the Fire, You have certainly disgraced him﴾, meaning: You have humiliated him and displayed his disgrace before the assembled. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there will be no helpers﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection there will be no protector for them from You, nor anyone to turn them away from what You intend for them.

﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith﴾, meaning: a summoner calling to faith, and he is the Messenger ﷺ, ﴿Believe in your Lord,﴾ meaning he says: "Believe in your Lord," so we believed, meaning: we responded to him and followed him. ﴿Our Lord, so forgive us our sins﴾, meaning: by our faith and our following of Your Prophet, so forgive us our sins, that is, cover them. ﴿And remove from us our misdeeds﴾, meaning: concerning what is between us and You. ﴿And take us in death with the righteous﴾, meaning: join us with the righteous. ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾. It was said: its meaning is: [what You promised] upon belief in Your messengers. And it was said: its meaning is: upon the tongues of Your messengers. And this is more apparent.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Iqal, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Asqalan is one of the two brides. From it Allah will raise on the Day of Resurrection seventy thousand people who will have no reckoning, and from it He will raise fifty thousand martyrs, delegations to Allah, and there are the ranks of the martyrs, their heads severed and held in their hands, their veins gushing blood, saying: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break Your promise.﴾ Then He will say: 'My servant has spoken the truth. Wash them in the river of al-Bayda.' They will come out from it pure and white, and they will roam in Paradise wherever they wish."

This hadith is counted among the strange narrations of the Musnad, and some consider it fabricated, and Allah knows best. [[Al-Musnad (3/225). Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it in al-Mawdu'at (2/54) and said: "This hadith is not authentic from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. All its chains revolve around Abu 'Iqal, whose name is Hilal ibn Zayd ibn Yasar. Ibn Hibban said: He narrates from Anas things that are fabricated, which Anas never related at all; it is not permissible to argue with him in any way." Al-Dhahabi mentioned it in al-Mizan (4/313) and said: "False." See also the words of al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in al-Qawl al-Musaddad, no. (8), where he mentions that the hadith is about virtues of deeds and encouragement to garrison duty in the way of Allah, and that leniency in narrating such material is the method of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him. He then cited supporting evidence for it, so consult it if you wish.]]

﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: before the assembled creation. ﴿Indeed, You do not break the promise﴾, meaning: there must be the appointment which You informed Your messengers about, which is standing before You on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: al-Harith ibn Surayj narrated to us; al-Mu'tamir narrated to us; al-Fadl ibn 'Isa narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, that Jabir ibn 'Abdullah told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shame and disgrace will reach the son of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, in the standing before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to the point that the servant wishes he would be ordered to the Fire." This is a strange hadith. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/311). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/350): "In it is al-Fadl ibn 'Isa al-Raqqashi, on whom there is consensus of weakness."]]

It is established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite these ten verses at the end of Al 'Imran when he rose at night for his tahajjud (night prayer). Then al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shuraik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Namir informed me, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I spent the night at the house of my maternal aunt Maymunah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) talked with his family for a while, then slept. When the last third of the night came, he sat up, looked at the sky, and said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for those of understanding.﴾ Then he got up, performed ablution and used the siwak. He prayed eleven rak'ahs. Then Bilal called the adhan, and he prayed two rak'ahs, then went out and led the people in the dawn prayer."

Muslim also related it similarly from Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq al-Sana'ani, from Ibn Abi Maryam, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4569; Sahih Muslim, no. 763.]

Then al-Bukhari related it through several routes from Malik, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, from Ibn Abbas [in some manuscripts: "Ibn Abbas informed him"], that he spent the night at the house of Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who was his aunt. He said: "I lay down across the width of the pillow, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his family lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) slept until midnight, or a little before it or a little after it. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) woke from his sleep and began to wipe the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the last ten verses of Surah Al 'Imran. Then he got up to a hanging water-skin, performed ablution from it, and did it well [in some manuscripts: 'the ablution'], then stood to pray. Ibn Abbas said: 'So I got up and did what he did, then I went and stood beside him.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his right hand on my head and took hold of my right ear, twisting it. He prayed two rak'ahs, then two, then two, then two, then two, then two, then two, then he performed Witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He got up and prayed two light rak'ahs, then went out and led the dawn prayer."

The rest of the collectors related it in various routes from Malik with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4570, 4571; Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1367; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/210); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1363; as for al-Tirmidhi, he related it in al-Shama'il, no. 252.] Muslim and Abu Dawud also related it from other routes, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim, no. 763; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1364.]

Another route for this hadith from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both).

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us: Abu Yahya ibn Abi Misarra [in some manuscripts: "Maysara"] informed us: Khallad ibn Yahya informed us: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq informed us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Abbas [in some manuscripts: "from his father" and in others "from Ibn Abbas"], who said: "Al-Abbas ordered me to spend the night with the family of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to observe his prayer. He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led the people in the night prayer, the 'Isha, until no one remained in the mosque except him. Then he stood and passed by me and said: "Who is this? Abdullah?" I said: "Yes." He said: "What is it?" I said: "Al-Abbas ordered me to spend the night with you tonight." He said: "Then stay with us."
