Ibn Adi said: "Extremely weak; his weakness is evident from his narrations."]]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Hisham al-Dastawai narrated to us, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: "The righteous (al-abrar) are those who do not harm an ant."

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Khaythama, from al-Aswad, who said: Abd Allah (meaning Ibn Mas'ud) said: "No soul, whether righteous or wicked, but death is better for it. If it is righteous, Allah has said: ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾."

Similarly, Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from al-A'mash, from al-Thawri, with the same wording, and he recited: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite so that they increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:178].

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me: Ishaq narrated to us: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Faraj ibn Fadala, from Luqman, from Abu al-Darda', that he used to say: "There is no believer but that death is better for him, and there is no disbeliever but that death is better for him. Whoever does not believe me, then Allah says: ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾, and He says: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite so that they increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾."

Ibn Kathir said: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do not be deceived by the free movement of those who disbelieve in the land﴾. That is, do not look at what these disbelievers enjoy of blessings, ease and pleasure. All of this will soon depart from them, and they will become held captive by their evil deeds. What they have is only a means of gradual enticement (istidraj), so we extend to them what they have. ﴿It is a little enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and it is an evil resting place﴾.

This verse is like His saying: ﴿None dispute the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not let their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾ [Ghafir 40:4]. He also said: ﴿Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed. [Theirs is] enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus 10:69-70]. He said: ﴿We give them enjoyment for a little; then We will compel them to a severe punishment﴾ [Luqman 31:24]. He said: ﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; give them time, a little﴾ [al-Tariq 86:17], meaning, a little. He said: ﴿Is one to whom We have made a good promise, which he will meet, like one We have given enjoyment of the worldly life and then, on the Day of Resurrection, he will be among those brought forward [for punishment]?﴾ [al-Qasas 28:61].

Thus, when He mentioned the state of the disbelievers in this world and their final destination in the Fire, He said after it: ﴿But those who fear their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally as a welcome provision from Allah. And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾. That is, a hospitality from Allah. ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Nasr narrated to us: Abu Tahir Sahl ibn Abd Allah informed us: Hisham ibn Ammar informed us: Sa'id ibn Yahya informed us: Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "They were only called 'the righteous' (al-abrar) because they were dutiful to fathers and sons, just as your parents have a right over you, so your child has a right over you."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated this from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As as a marfu' report. [[It is not preserved; what is preserved is from Ibn Umar, and Abu Tahir Sahl ibn Abd Allah alone transmitted it.]] Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Janab narrated to us: Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn Umar, who said: "Allah only named them 'the righteous' because they were dutiful to fathers and sons, just as your parents have a right over you, so your child has a right over you. And this is more likely, and Allah knows best." [[Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (4/323) through Muhammad ibn Khuraym, from Hisham ibn Ammar, from Sa'id ibn Yahya, from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab, as a marfu' report. Al-Bukhari narrated it in al-Adab al-Mufrad, no. 94, through Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab, as a mawquf report. Al-Suyuti said in al-Durr (2/416): "Its stopping (waqf) is more authentic." Its chain includes Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, who is agreed to be weak. Ibn Adi said: "Extremely weak; his weakness is evident from his narrations."]]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Hisham al-Dastawai narrated to us, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: "The righteous (al-abrar) are those who do not harm an ant."

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Khaythama, from al-Aswad, who said: Abd Allah (meaning Ibn Mas'ud) said: "No soul, whether righteous or wicked, but death is better for it. If it is righteous, Allah has said: ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾."

Similarly, Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from al-A'mash, from al-Thawri, with the same wording, and he recited: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite so that they increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:178].

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me: Ishaq narrated to us: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Faraj ibn Fadala, from Luqman, from Abu al-Darda', that he used to say: "There is no believer but that death is better for him, and there is no disbeliever but that death is better for him. Whoever does not believe me, then Allah says: ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾, and He says: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite so that they increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾."

Ibn Kathir (may God have mercy on him) reports that a group of the People of the Book believe in God with true belief, and in what was revealed to Muhammad, alongside what they believe of the earlier scriptures. They are also humble before God (khashi'un), meaning obedient to Him, submissive and humbling themselves before Him. ﴿They do not sell the signs of God for a small price﴾, meaning they do not conceal with their hands the good tidings about Muhammad ﷺ, his description, his attributes, his mission and the description of his community. These are the choicest of the People of the Book and their elite, whether they were Jews or Christians. God the Exalted has said in Surah al-Qasas: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believe in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it." Those will be given their reward twice for what they patienced﴾ up to the verse [Al-Qasas 52-54]. He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recite it with its true recitation; those believe in it﴾ up to the verse [Al-Baqarah 121]. He said: ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it establish justice﴾ [Al-A'raf 159]. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They are not all alike. Among the People of the Book is a standing community who recite the verses of God during the night and prostrate﴾ [Ali 'Imran 113]. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall on their faces in prostration, and they say, 'Glory be to our Lord; indeed the promise of our Lord is ever fulfilled.' And they fall on their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility"﴾ [Al-Isra' 107-109]. These qualities are found among the Jews, but few of them, as was the case with 'Abdullah ibn Salam and those like him from the Jewish rabbis who believed, and they did not reach ten persons. As for the Christians, many of them are guided and submit to the truth, as God the Exalted said: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of the people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God; and you will find the nearest of them in affection toward the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears from what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses. And why would we not believe in God and what has come to us of the truth, while we aspire that our Lord would admit us among the righteous people?" So God rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein﴾ up to the verse [Al-Ma'idah 82-85]. Likewise He said here: ﴿Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account﴾, and so on.

It has been established in a hadith that Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, when he recited Surah Maryam (﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾) in the presence of al-Najashi, the king of Abyssinia, and with him were the patriarchs and the priests (qasawisa), wept and they wept with him, until they dyed their beards with their tears.

It is established in the two Sahihs that when al-Najashi died, the Prophet ﷺ informed his companions of it and said: "Indeed, a brother of yours in Abyssinia has died, so pray over him." So he went out with them to the open ground, arranged them in rows, and prayed over him.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When al-Najashi died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask forgiveness for your brother." Some people said: "He orders us to ask forgiveness for a non-Arab (ilj) who died in the land of Abyssinia." Then this was revealed: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submitting to God﴾ up to the verse.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through another route from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet ﷺ. Then Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through several routes from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, similar to what preceded.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said when al-Najashi died: "Indeed, your brother Ashamah has died." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and prayed as one prays over funerals, and he said four takbirs over him. The hypocrites said: "He prays over a non-Arab who died in the land of Abyssinia." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submitting to God, not selling the signs of God for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account﴾.

Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abdullah al-Hakim also narrated in his Mustadrak, informing us Abu al-'Abbas al-Sayyari in Marw, that 'Abdullah ibn 'Ali al-Ghazzal told us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit informed us, from 'Amir ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, who said: An enemy from their land attacked al-Najashi, so the emigrants came to him and said: "We wish to go out to them so that we may fight alongside you, and that you may see our courage, and that we may repay you for what you did for us." He said: "The aid of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is better than the aid of people." He said: And concerning this it was revealed: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submitting to God﴾ up to the verse. Then he said: This is a hadith whose chain is sound, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it. [Al-Mustadrak 2/300, and al-Dhahabi affirmed it.]

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Razi told us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Yazid ibn Ruman told me, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: When al-Najashi died, we used to hear that a light would still be seen upon his grave.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book﴾: it means the Muslims among the People of the Book.

'Abbad ibn Mansur said: I asked al-Hasan al-Basri about the saying of God the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submitting to God﴾ up to the verse. He said: They are the People of the Book who were before Muhammad ﷺ, then they followed him and recognized Islam, so God gave them the reward of two: for what they had upon faith before Muhammad ﷺ, and for what they followed of Muhammad ﷺ. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both.

It is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will be given their reward twice," and he mentioned among them: "A man of the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and believed in me."

* *

His saying: ﴿They do not sell the signs of God for a small price﴾ means they do not conceal what knowledge they have, as the despised group among them did, but rather they give it freely without payment. Therefore He said: ﴿Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.﴾

Mujahid said: ﴿Swift in account﴾ means swift in counting. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and others.

* *

His saying: ﴿O you who believe, persevere and endure and be stationed (rabitu)﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said: They were commanded to persevere in their religion which Allah has chosen for them, which is Islam, so that they do not abandon it in times of ease or hardship, in prosperity or adversity, until they die as Muslims, and to endure against the enemies who conceal their religion. Likewise said more than one of the scholars of the early generations.

As for murabatah (rabitah), it is constancy and steadfastness in a place of worship. It was also said: waiting for the prayer after the prayer. This was said by Mujahid, Ibn 'Abbas, Sahl ibn Hunayf, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here the hadith that Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated from the hadith of Malik ibn Anas, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, client of al-Huraqah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Shall I not inform you of what Allah erases sins by and raises ranks by? Completing ablution in difficult conditions, many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer. That is ribat, that is ribat, that is ribat." [Malik in al-Muwatta, Muslim, and al-Nasa'i.]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad told us, Musa ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Juhayfah 'Ali ibn Yazid al-Kufi told us, Ibn Abi Karimah informed us, from Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: Abu Hurayrah turned to me one day and said: "Do you know, nephew, concerning what this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, persevere and endure and be stationed﴾?" I said: "No." He said: "Indeed, there was no campaign in the time of the Prophet ﷺ in which they stationed themselves, but it was revealed concerning a people who maintain the mosques, who pray the prayer at its appointed times, then remember God in them. So upon them was revealed: ﴿Persevere﴾, i.e., in the five prayers; ﴿and endure﴾ against yourselves and your desires; ﴿and be stationed﴾ in your mosques; ﴿and fear God﴾ regarding what is incumbent upon you; ﴿that you may succeed﴾." [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr, attributed to Ibn Mardawayh.]

Al-Hakim narrated it similarly in his Mustadrak through the route of Sa'id ibn Mansur ibn al-Mubarak, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from Dawud ibn Salih, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, in similar wording.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa'ib told me, Ibn Fudayl told me, from 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his grandfather, from Shurahbil, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I direct you to what expiates sins and wrongs? Completing ablution in difficult conditions, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer. That is ribat."

Ibn Jarir also said: Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Muhajir narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, from Shurahbil, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not guide you to that by which Allah erases sins and expiates wrongdoings?" We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Perfecting the wudu' (ablution) in its proper places, walking much to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer. That is ribat (frontier vigilance)." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/505, 506). Al-Bazzar also narrated it (1/223) in Kashf al-Astar, and said: "We do not know this to be narrated from Jabir except through this chain." Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, no. (161) in Mawarid, both from the route of Muhammad ibn Salama, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Salama, with the same.]]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn [[In manuscripts J, R, A, W: "Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Salam".]] al-Salam al-Bayruti informed us, Muhammad ibn Ghalib al-Antaki informed us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us, al-Wazi' ibn Nafi' informed us, from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Ayyub, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stopped before us and said: "Shall [[In manuscripts J, A: "Shall I guide you".]] I [[Text variant as given.]] direct you to that by which Allah erases sins and multiplies the reward?" We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, what is it?" He said: "Perfecting the wudu' despite hardships, walking much to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer."

He said: "And it is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, be patient, endure together, remain stationed, and fear Allah that you may succeed﴾. That is ribat in the mosques." This is a very strange (gharib) hadith through this route. [[In its chain is al-Wazi' ibn Nafi'. Ibn Ma'in said: "He is not trustworthy." Al-Bukhari said: "Munkar al-hadith," and al-Nasa'i abandoned him. Ibn Adi said: "Most of what al-Wazi' narrates is not preserved." Mizan al-I'tidal (4/327).]]

Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: Dawud ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman said to me: "O nephew, do you know concerning what this verse was revealed: ﴿Be patient, endure together, and remain stationed﴾?" I said: "No." He said: "Indeed, O nephew, there was no military campaign in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) in which one would stand guard (yurabitu), but it was the waiting for the prayer after the prayer." Al-Tabari narrated it. The wording of Ibn Mardawayh has already been mentioned, and that it is from the words of Abu Hurayra. And Allah knows best.

It has been said: What is meant here by ribat (murabata) is the ribat of military campaign at the enemy's frontier, and guarding the borders of Islam and protecting them from the entry of enemies into the territory of the Muslim lands. Reports have come encouraging this and mentioning its great reward. Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him [[In manuscripts A, W: "with both of them".]], that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better than the world and whatever is in it." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2892).]]

Another hadith: Muslim narrated from Salman al-Farisi, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "A day and a night of ribat is better than a month of fasting and its night prayer. If he dies, his deed that he used to do continues for him, his provision continues for him, and he is safe from the tester (al-fattan)." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1913).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Haywa ibn Shurayh, Abu Hani' al-Khawlani informed me, that Amr ibn Malik al-Janbi [[In manuscript A: "al-Khatani".]] informed him that he heard Fudala ibn Ubayd say: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Every dead person is sealed upon his deed, except the one who dies while on ribat in the way of Allah, for his deed continues to grow for him until the Day of Resurrection, and he is safe from the trial of the grave.'"

Likewise Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hani' al-Khawlani. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih. [[Musnad (6/20); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2500); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1621); Sahih Ibn Hibban (7/69), al-Ihsan.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad also narrated from Yahya ibn Ishaq, Hasan ibn Musa, Abu Sa'id [and Abd Allah ibn Yazid] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W.]] - they said: "[All of them from Abd Allah ibn Lahi'a]" [[In manuscripts J, R, A, W: "all from Abd Allah ibn Lahi'a".]] Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Mashraḥ ibn Ha'an narrated to us, I heard Uqba ibn Amir saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every dead person is sealed for him upon his deed, except the one on ribat in the way of Allah, for his deed continues for him [[In manuscript A: "for him".]] until he is resurrected, and he is safe from the tester (al-fattan)." [[Musnad (3/157). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/289): "In it is Ibn Lahi'a, and his hadith is good."]]

Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Usama narrated in his Musnad, from al-Maqburi, who is Abd Allah ibn Yazid, with it, up to his words "until he is resurrected," without the mention of "al-fattan." [[Musnad al-Harith, no. (627), Bughyat al-Baहith. The narration of Abd Allah ibn Yazid from Ibn Lahi'a is sound, as he is among those who narrated from him before the confusion (ikhtilat).]] And Ibn Lahi'a, when he explicitly states hearing (al-tahdith), is good, especially with the supporting narrations mentioned earlier.

Another hadith: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah said in his Sunan: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, al-Layth informed me, from Zuhra ibn Ma'bad [[In manuscript R: "and Ibn Sa'id".]], from his father, from Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam), who said: "Whoever dies while on ribat in the way of Allah, his righteous deed that he used to do continues to be recorded for him, his provision continues for him, he is safe from the tester, and Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection safe from terror." [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2767). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/391): "This chain is sahih, its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a informed us, from Musa ibn Wardan, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies on ribat is protected from the trial of the grave, safe from the greatest terror, his provision is brought to him in the morning and evening from Paradise, and the reward of the one on ribat is written for him until the Day of Resurrection." [[Musnad (2/404).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Halhala al-Du'ali, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah, from Umm al-Darda', raising the hadith, she said: "Whoever performs ribat on any of the coasts of the Muslims for three days, it suffices him for a year's ribat." [[Musnad (6/362). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/289): "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it through Isma'il ibn Ayyash from the Medinans, and its remaining narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Kahmas narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, who said: Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said while delivering a sermon from his pulpit: "I am going to narrate to you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What prevented me from narrating it to you was nothing but my concern for you. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'A night's guard in the way of Allah is better than a thousand nights in which its night is spent in prayer and its day in fasting.'" [[Musnad (1/64).]]

Likewise Ahmad narrated it from Rawh, from Kahmas, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from Uthman. [[Musnad (1/61).]] Ibn Majah narrated it from Hisham ibn Ammar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Uthman ibn Affan addressed the people and said: "O people, I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What prevented me from narrating it to you was nothing but my concern for you and your companions. Let whoever chooses for himself choose, or leave it. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever performs ribat for a night in the way of Allah, it is as if he had fasted and prayed for a thousand nights.'" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2766). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/390): "Its chain is weak."]]

Another route from Uthman [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from manuscript W.]]: al-Tirmidhi said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khallal narrated to us, Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to us, al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Abu Aqil Zuhra ibn Ma'bad narrated to us, from Abu Salih, the freedman of Uthman ibn Affan, who said: I heard Uthman - while he was on the pulpit - saying: "I concealed from you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), out of dislike that you would scatter away from me. Then it occurred to me to narrate it to you, so that a person may choose for himself what seems right to him. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better than a thousand days spent in any other station.'"

Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith through this route." Muhammad [i.e., al-Bukhari] said: "Abu Salih, the freedman of Uthman, his name is Burkan." [[In manuscripts J, A: "Turkan".]] Other than al-Tirmidhi mentioned that his name is al-Harith. And Allah knows best. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1667); al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Sunan (6/39).]] Likewise Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Abd Allah ibn Lahi'a, and in his version there is an addition at the end: he [i.e., Uthman] said: "Let a person perform ribat however he wishes. Have I conveyed?" They said: "Yes." He said: "O Allah, bear witness." [[Musnad (1/62).]]

Another hadith: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, who said: Salman al-Farisi passed by Shurahbil ibn al-Simt, while he was on his ribat, and it had become burdensome upon him and his companions. He said: "Shall I not narrate to you, O son of al-Simt, a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes." He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better - or he said: "is superior" - to a month of fasting and its night prayer. Whoever dies in it is protected from the trial of the grave, and his deed continues to grow for him until the Day of Resurrection.'"

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated it through this route, and said: "This is a hasan hadith." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1665).]] In some copies there is an addition: "Its chain is not connected, and Ibn al-Munkadir did not meet Salman."

I say: The apparent view is that Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir heard it from Shurahbil ibn al-Simt. Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Makhul and Abu Ubayda ibn Uqba, both from Shurahbil ibn al-Simt - and he has companionship (suhba) - from Salman al-Farisi, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "A day and a night of ribat is better than a month of fasting and its night prayer. If he dies, his deed that he used to do continues for him, his provision continues for him, and he is safe from the tester." The wording of Muslim alone has already been mentioned. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1913); Sunan al-Nasa'i (3916).]]

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Samura narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ya'la al-Sulami narrated to us, Umar ibn Subayh narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr, from Makhul, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A day of ribat in the way of Allah, guarding the frontier of the Muslims, seeking reward, outside the month of Ramadan, is greater in reward than the worship of a hundred years, its fasting and its night prayer. And a day of ribat in the way of Allah, guarding the frontier of the Muslims, seeking reward, during the month of Ramadan, is superior with Allah and greater in reward - I think he said - than the worship of a thousand years, its fasting and its night prayer. If Allah, the Exalted, returns him safely to his family, there will not be recorded against him the sin of a thousand years, the good deeds will be recorded for him, and the reward of ribat will continue to be given to him until the Day of Resurrection."

This is a gharib hadith, rather munkar through this route, and Umar ibn Subayh is accused (muttaham). [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2768).]]

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Isa ibn Yunus al-Ramli narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Shapur narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Khalid ibn Abi Tawil, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Guarding one night in the cause of Allah is better than the fasting and standing in prayer of a man among his family for a thousand years: the year is three hundred and sixty days, and the day is like a thousand years."

This is also a strange (gharib) hadith. Sa'id ibn Khalid is weakened by Abu Zur'ah and other imams. Al-Uqayli said: "None follows him in his narration." Ibn Hibban said: "It is not permissible to use him as proof." Al-Hakim said: "He narrated false (mawdu') hadiths from Anas."

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad informed us, from Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Za'idah, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on the guard of the guards."

In it there is a break (inqita') between Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and Uqbah ibn Amir, for he did not meet him. And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Abu Dawud said: Abu Tawbah narrated to us, Mu'awiyah narrated to us—meaning Ibn Salam—from Zayd—meaning Ibn Salam—that he heard Abu Salam say: al-Sulami narrated to me that Sahl ibn al-Hanzaliyyah narrated to him that they travelled with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn, and they travelled until evening. The Prayer was due with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a horseman came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I went ahead of you until I climbed the mountain of such and such, and there I saw Hawazin, all of them, with their women, camels and sheep, gathered at Hunayn." The Prophet (ﷺ) smiled and said: "That will be the spoils of the Muslims tomorrow, if Allah wills." Then he said: "Who will guard us tonight?" Anas ibn Abi Martha said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Then mount." So he mounted his horse and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Go to the head of this pass until you are at its top, and let no one surprise us from your direction tonight." When we woke in the morning, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to his place of prayer, prayed two rak'ahs, then said: "Did you sense your horseman?" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, we did not sense him." The iqamah for the prayer was called, and the Prophet (ﷺ), while praying, kept turning towards the pass until he finished his prayer, then said: "Rejoice, for your horseman has come." We began looking through the gaps of the trees in the pass, and there he was, coming, until he stood before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I went on until I was at the top of this pass, where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had commanded me. When I woke, I looked over both passes and saw no one." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Did you descend during the night?" He said: "No, except to pray or to relieve myself." He said to him: "You have earned it (awjabta), so there is no harm for you if you do not work after this."

al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir al-Harrani, from Abu Tawbah, who is al-Rabi' ibn Nafi', with this chain.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh narrated to us: I heard Muhammad ibn Shumayr al-Ru'ayni say: I heard Abu Amir al-Tujibi say. Imam Ahmad said: Others than Zayd said: Abu Ali al-Janbi said: I heard Abu Rayhanah say: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a campaign, and one night we came to a height and spent the night on it. A severe cold struck us, until I saw people digging a hole in the ground, entering it, and placing the shield over it—meaning the shield." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw this among the people, he called out: "Who will guard us this night, so that I may invoke a supplication for him that will be of merit for him?" A man from the Ansar said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Come near." He came near. He said: "Who are you?" The Ansari named himself to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began the supplication and made it lengthy. Abu Rayhanah said: "When I heard what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had prayed for, I said: 'I am another man.' He said: 'Come near.' I came near. He said: 'Who are you?' I said: 'I am Abu Rayhanah.' He prayed a supplication less than what he had prayed for the Ansari, then said: 'The Fire is forbidden to an eye that wept—or cried—out of fear of Allah, and the Fire is forbidden to an eye that stayed awake in the cause of Allah.'"

al-Nasa'i narrated from it: "The Fire is forbidden..." to the end, from Isma ibn al-Fadl, from Zayd ibn al-Hubab with it, and from al-Harith ibn Miskin, from Ibn Wahb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh, with it, and more completely; and in both narrations he said: "from Abu Ali al-Janbi."

Another hadith: al-Tirmidhi said: Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us, Bishr ibn Umar narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn Ruzayq Abu Shaybah narrated to us, Ata al-Khurasani narrated to us, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Two eyes will not be touched by the Fire: an eye that wept out of fear of Allah, and an eye that stayed awake guarding in the cause of Allah."

Then he said: "Hasan gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Shu'ayb ibn Ruzayq." He said: "And in the chapter there is also a narration from Uthman and Abu Rayhanah." I say: these have already passed, and praise be to Allah.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, from Zabban, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh, from his father Mu'adh ibn Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever guards behind the Muslims in the cause of Allah, voluntarily, not for a wage from a ruler, will not see the Fire with his eyes except as the fulfilment of the oath, for Allah says: 'And there is none of you but will pass over it' (Maryam 19:71)."

Ahmad alone narrated it (may Allah have mercy on him).

Another hadith: al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Wretched is the slave of the dinar, the slave of the dirham, and the slave of the velvet garment: if he is given, he is pleased, and if he is not given, he is displeased. Wretched and failing is he; and if he is pricked with a thorn, may he not find its removal. Blessed is the servant who takes hold of the bridle of his horse in the cause of Allah, his hair disheveled, his feet dusty: if he is in the guard, he is in the guard, and if he is in the rear, he is in the rear; if he asks permission, it is not granted, and if he intercedes, it is not accepted."

This is what has been easily presented of the hadiths related to this topic, and praise be to Allah for His abundant blessings, through the succession of years and days.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah al-Madani narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Abu Ubaydah, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioning to him gatherings of the Romans and what he feared from them. Umar wrote back to him: "To proceed: whenever a believing servant is struck by a hardship, Allah will bring relief after it, and indeed one hardship will never overcome two ease. Allah the Exalted says in His Book: 'O you who believe, endure and outlast, and stand guard, and fear Allah, that you may succeed' (Al 'Imran 3:200)."

Ibn Asakir, in the biography of Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, narrated through the chain of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi Sukaynah, who said: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak dictated these verses to me at Tarsus, when I bade him farewell for departure, and he recited them with me to al-Fudayl ibn Iyad in the year 170 AH; and in another narration, the year 177 AH:

O worshipper of the two Harams, if you saw us, you would know that you are playing in worship.
Whoever stains his cheek with his tears, our throats are stained with our blood.
Or whoever tires his horse in vanity, our horses tire on the morning of battle.
The fragrance of musk is for you, and we have our fragrance: the blaze of hooves and the best dust.
There has come to us from the speech of our Prophet a saying, true and sincere, that does not lie:
It is not equal—the dust of Allah's horses in the nostril of a man, and the smoke of a blazing fire.
This is the Book of Allah speaking among us: the martyr is not dead, and it does not lie.

He said: So I met al-Fudayl ibn Iyad with his book in the Masjid al-Haram, and when he read it, his eyes shed tears, and he said: "Abu Abd al-Rahman has spoken the truth, and advised me." Then he said: "Are you one who writes down hadith?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then write this hadith in return for your carrying Abu Abd al-Rahman's book to us." Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad dictated to me: Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me a deed by which I may attain the reward of the warriors in the cause of Allah." He said: "Can you pray without slackening and fast without breaking your fast?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am too weak to be able to do that." The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if you could do that, you would not reach the warriors in the cause of Allah. Do you not know that the warrior's horse prances on its tether and good deeds are recorded for him for that?"

Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, meaning: in all your affairs and conditions, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, when he sent him to Yemen: "Fear Allah wherever you are, follow an evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and treat people with good character."

﴿That you may succeed﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Sakhr informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: that he used to say concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And fear Allah that you may succeed﴾: "And fear Allah regarding what is between me and you, that you may succeed tomorrow when you meet me."

End of the tafsir of Surat Al 'Imran. Praise and blessings are Allah's, and we ask Him for death upon the Book and the Sunnah.

Ibn Kathir (may God have mercy on him) reports that a group of the People of the Book believe in God with true belief, and in what was revealed to Muhammad, alongside what they believe of the earlier scriptures. They are also humble before God (khashi'un), meaning obedient to Him, submissive and humbling themselves before Him. ﴿They do not sell the signs of God for a small price﴾, meaning they do not conceal with their hands the good tidings about Muhammad ﷺ, his description, his attributes, his mission and the description of his community. These are the choicest of the People of the Book and their elite, whether they were Jews or Christians. God the Exalted has said in Surah al-Qasas: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believe in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it." Those will be given their reward twice for what they patienced﴾ up to the verse [Al-Qasas 52-54]. He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recite it with its true recitation; those believe in it﴾ up to the verse [Al-Baqarah 121]. He said: ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it establish justice﴾ [Al-A'raf 159]. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They are not all alike. Among the People of the Book is a standing community who recite the verses of God during the night and prostrate﴾ [Ali 'Imran 113]. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall on their faces in prostration, and they say, 'Glory be to our Lord; indeed the promise of our Lord is ever fulfilled.' And they fall on their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility"﴾ [Al-Isra' 107-109]. These qualities are found among the Jews, but few of them, as was the case with 'Abdullah ibn Salam and those like him from the Jewish rabbis who believed, and they did not reach ten persons. As for the Christians, many of them are guided and submit to the truth, as God the Exalted said: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of the people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God; and you will find the nearest of them in affection toward the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears from what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses. And why would we not believe in God and what has come to us of the truth, while we aspire that our Lord would admit us among the righteous people?" So God rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein﴾ up to the verse [Al-Ma'idah 82-85]. Likewise He said here: ﴿Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account﴾, and so on.

It has been established in a hadith that Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, when he recited Surah Maryam (﴿Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad﴾) in the presence of al-Najashi, the king of Abyssinia, and with him were the patriarchs and the priests (qasawisa), wept and they wept with him, until they dyed their beards with their tears.

It is established in the two Sahihs that when al-Najashi died, the Prophet ﷺ informed his companions of it and said: "Indeed, a brother of yours in Abyssinia has died, so pray over him." So he went out with them to the open ground, arranged them in rows, and prayed over him.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When al-Najashi died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask forgiveness for your brother." Some people said: "He orders us to ask forgiveness for a non-Arab (ilj) who died in the land of Abyssinia." Then this was revealed: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submitting to God﴾ up to the verse.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through another route from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet ﷺ. Then Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through several routes from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, similar to what preceded.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said when al-Najashi died: "Indeed, your brother Ashamah has died." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and prayed as one prays over funerals, and he said four takbirs over him. The hypocrites said: "He prays over a non-Arab who died in the land of Abyssinia." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submitting to God, not selling the signs of God for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account﴾.

Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abdullah al-Hakim also narrated in his Mustadrak, informing us Abu al-'Abbas al-Sayyari in Marw, that 'Abdullah ibn 'Ali al-Ghazzal told us, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit informed us, from 'Amir ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, who said: An enemy from their land attacked al-Najashi, so the emigrants came to him and said: "We wish to go out to them so that we may fight alongside you, and that you may see our courage, and that we may repay you for what you did for us." He said: "The aid of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is better than the aid of people." He said: And concerning this it was revealed: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submitting to God﴾ up to the verse. Then he said: This is a hadith whose chain is sound, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it. [Al-Mustadrak 2/300, and al-Dhahabi affirmed it.]

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Razi told us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Yazid ibn Ruman told me, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: When al-Najashi died, we used to hear that a light would still be seen upon his grave.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book﴾: it means the Muslims among the People of the Book.

'Abbad ibn Mansur said: I asked al-Hasan al-Basri about the saying of God the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submitting to God﴾ up to the verse. He said: They are the People of the Book who were before Muhammad ﷺ, then they followed him and recognized Islam, so God gave them the reward of two: for what they had upon faith before Muhammad ﷺ, and for what they followed of Muhammad ﷺ. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both.

It is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will be given their reward twice," and he mentioned among them: "A man of the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and believed in me."

* *

His saying: ﴿They do not sell the signs of God for a small price﴾ means they do not conceal what knowledge they have, as the despised group among them did, but rather they give it freely without payment. Therefore He said: ﴿Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.﴾

Mujahid said: ﴿Swift in account﴾ means swift in counting. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and others.

* *

His saying: ﴿O you who believe, persevere and endure and be stationed (rabitu)﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, said: They were commanded to persevere in their religion which Allah has chosen for them, which is Islam, so that they do not abandon it in times of ease or hardship, in prosperity or adversity, until they die as Muslims, and to endure against the enemies who conceal their religion. Likewise said more than one of the scholars of the early generations.

As for murabatah (rabitah), it is constancy and steadfastness in a place of worship. It was also said: waiting for the prayer after the prayer. This was said by Mujahid, Ibn 'Abbas, Sahl ibn Hunayf, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here the hadith that Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated from the hadith of Malik ibn Anas, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, client of al-Huraqah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Shall I not inform you of what Allah erases sins by and raises ranks by? Completing ablution in difficult conditions, many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer. That is ribat, that is ribat, that is ribat." [Malik in al-Muwatta, Muslim, and al-Nasa'i.]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad told us, Musa ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Juhayfah 'Ali ibn Yazid al-Kufi told us, Ibn Abi Karimah informed us, from Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: Abu Hurayrah turned to me one day and said: "Do you know, nephew, concerning what this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, persevere and endure and be stationed﴾?" I said: "No." He said: "Indeed, there was no campaign in the time of the Prophet ﷺ in which they stationed themselves, but it was revealed concerning a people who maintain the mosques, who pray the prayer at its appointed times, then remember God in them. So upon them was revealed: ﴿Persevere﴾, i.e., in the five prayers; ﴿and endure﴾ against yourselves and your desires; ﴿and be stationed﴾ in your mosques; ﴿and fear God﴾ regarding what is incumbent upon you; ﴿that you may succeed﴾." [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr, attributed to Ibn Mardawayh.]

Al-Hakim narrated it similarly in his Mustadrak through the route of Sa'id ibn Mansur ibn al-Mubarak, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from Dawud ibn Salih, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, in similar wording.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa'ib told me, Ibn Fudayl told me, from 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his grandfather, from Shurahbil, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I direct you to what expiates sins and wrongs? Completing ablution in difficult conditions, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer. That is ribat."

Ibn Jarir also said: Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Muhajir narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa, from Shurahbil, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not guide you to that by which Allah erases sins and expiates wrongdoings?" We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Perfecting the wudu' (ablution) in its proper places, walking much to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer. That is ribat (frontier vigilance)." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (7/505, 506). Al-Bazzar also narrated it (1/223) in Kashf al-Astar, and said: "We do not know this to be narrated from Jabir except through this chain." Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, no. (161) in Mawarid, both from the route of Muhammad ibn Salama, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Salama, with the same.]]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn [[In manuscripts J, R, A, W: "Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Salam".]] al-Salam al-Bayruti informed us, Muhammad ibn Ghalib al-Antaki informed us, Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us, al-Wazi' ibn Nafi' informed us, from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Ayyub, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stopped before us and said: "Shall [[In manuscripts J, A: "Shall I guide you".]] I [[Text variant as given.]] direct you to that by which Allah erases sins and multiplies the reward?" We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, what is it?" He said: "Perfecting the wudu' despite hardships, walking much to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer."

He said: "And it is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, be patient, endure together, remain stationed, and fear Allah that you may succeed﴾. That is ribat in the mosques." This is a very strange (gharib) hadith through this route. [[In its chain is al-Wazi' ibn Nafi'. Ibn Ma'in said: "He is not trustworthy." Al-Bukhari said: "Munkar al-hadith," and al-Nasa'i abandoned him. Ibn Adi said: "Most of what al-Wazi' narrates is not preserved." Mizan al-I'tidal (4/327).]]

Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: Dawud ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman said to me: "O nephew, do you know concerning what this verse was revealed: ﴿Be patient, endure together, and remain stationed﴾?" I said: "No." He said: "Indeed, O nephew, there was no military campaign in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) in which one would stand guard (yurabitu), but it was the waiting for the prayer after the prayer." Al-Tabari narrated it. The wording of Ibn Mardawayh has already been mentioned, and that it is from the words of Abu Hurayra. And Allah knows best.

It has been said: What is meant here by ribat (murabata) is the ribat of military campaign at the enemy's frontier, and guarding the borders of Islam and protecting them from the entry of enemies into the territory of the Muslim lands. Reports have come encouraging this and mentioning its great reward. Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him [[In manuscripts A, W: "with both of them".]], that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better than the world and whatever is in it." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2892).]]

Another hadith: Muslim narrated from Salman al-Farisi, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "A day and a night of ribat is better than a month of fasting and its night prayer. If he dies, his deed that he used to do continues for him, his provision continues for him, and he is safe from the tester (al-fattan)." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1913).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Haywa ibn Shurayh, Abu Hani' al-Khawlani informed me, that Amr ibn Malik al-Janbi [[In manuscript A: "al-Khatani".]] informed him that he heard Fudala ibn Ubayd say: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Every dead person is sealed upon his deed, except the one who dies while on ribat in the way of Allah, for his deed continues to grow for him until the Day of Resurrection, and he is safe from the trial of the grave.'"

Likewise Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hani' al-Khawlani. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih. [[Musnad (6/20); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2500); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1621); Sahih Ibn Hibban (7/69), al-Ihsan.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad also narrated from Yahya ibn Ishaq, Hasan ibn Musa, Abu Sa'id [and Abd Allah ibn Yazid] [[Addition from manuscripts J, R, A, W.]] - they said: "[All of them from Abd Allah ibn Lahi'a]" [[In manuscripts J, R, A, W: "all from Abd Allah ibn Lahi'a".]] Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Mashraḥ ibn Ha'an narrated to us, I heard Uqba ibn Amir saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every dead person is sealed for him upon his deed, except the one on ribat in the way of Allah, for his deed continues for him [[In manuscript A: "for him".]] until he is resurrected, and he is safe from the tester (al-fattan)." [[Musnad (3/157). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/289): "In it is Ibn Lahi'a, and his hadith is good."]]

Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Usama narrated in his Musnad, from al-Maqburi, who is Abd Allah ibn Yazid, with it, up to his words "until he is resurrected," without the mention of "al-fattan." [[Musnad al-Harith, no. (627), Bughyat al-Baहith. The narration of Abd Allah ibn Yazid from Ibn Lahi'a is sound, as he is among those who narrated from him before the confusion (ikhtilat).]] And Ibn Lahi'a, when he explicitly states hearing (al-tahdith), is good, especially with the supporting narrations mentioned earlier.

Another hadith: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah said in his Sunan: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, al-Layth informed me, from Zuhra ibn Ma'bad [[In manuscript R: "and Ibn Sa'id".]], from his father, from Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam), who said: "Whoever dies while on ribat in the way of Allah, his righteous deed that he used to do continues to be recorded for him, his provision continues for him, he is safe from the tester, and Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection safe from terror." [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2767). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/391): "This chain is sahih, its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a informed us, from Musa ibn Wardan, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies on ribat is protected from the trial of the grave, safe from the greatest terror, his provision is brought to him in the morning and evening from Paradise, and the reward of the one on ribat is written for him until the Day of Resurrection." [[Musnad (2/404).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Halhala al-Du'ali, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah, from Umm al-Darda', raising the hadith, she said: "Whoever performs ribat on any of the coasts of the Muslims for three days, it suffices him for a year's ribat." [[Musnad (6/362). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/289): "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it through Isma'il ibn Ayyash from the Medinans, and its remaining narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Kahmas narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, who said: Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, said while delivering a sermon from his pulpit: "I am going to narrate to you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What prevented me from narrating it to you was nothing but my concern for you. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'A night's guard in the way of Allah is better than a thousand nights in which its night is spent in prayer and its day in fasting.'" [[Musnad (1/64).]]

Likewise Ahmad narrated it from Rawh, from Kahmas, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from Uthman. [[Musnad (1/61).]] Ibn Majah narrated it from Hisham ibn Ammar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Uthman ibn Affan addressed the people and said: "O people, I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What prevented me from narrating it to you was nothing but my concern for you and your companions. Let whoever chooses for himself choose, or leave it. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever performs ribat for a night in the way of Allah, it is as if he had fasted and prayed for a thousand nights.'" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2766). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/390): "Its chain is weak."]]

Another route from Uthman [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from manuscript W.]]: al-Tirmidhi said: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khallal narrated to us, Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to us, al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Abu Aqil Zuhra ibn Ma'bad narrated to us, from Abu Salih, the freedman of Uthman ibn Affan, who said: I heard Uthman - while he was on the pulpit - saying: "I concealed from you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), out of dislike that you would scatter away from me. Then it occurred to me to narrate it to you, so that a person may choose for himself what seems right to him. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better than a thousand days spent in any other station.'"

Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith through this route." Muhammad [i.e., al-Bukhari] said: "Abu Salih, the freedman of Uthman, his name is Burkan." [[In manuscripts J, A: "Turkan".]] Other than al-Tirmidhi mentioned that his name is al-Harith. And Allah knows best. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1667); al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Sunan (6/39).]] Likewise Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Abd Allah ibn Lahi'a, and in his version there is an addition at the end: he [i.e., Uthman] said: "Let a person perform ribat however he wishes. Have I conveyed?" They said: "Yes." He said: "O Allah, bear witness." [[Musnad (1/62).]]

Another hadith: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, who said: Salman al-Farisi passed by Shurahbil ibn al-Simt, while he was on his ribat, and it had become burdensome upon him and his companions. He said: "Shall I not narrate to you, O son of al-Simt, a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "Yes." He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better - or he said: "is superior" - to a month of fasting and its night prayer. Whoever dies in it is protected from the trial of the grave, and his deed continues to grow for him until the Day of Resurrection.'"

Al-Tirmidhi alone narrated it through this route, and said: "This is a hasan hadith." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1665).]] In some copies there is an addition: "Its chain is not connected, and Ibn al-Munkadir did not meet Salman."

I say: The apparent view is that Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir heard it from Shurahbil ibn al-Simt. Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Makhul and Abu Ubayda ibn Uqba, both from Shurahbil ibn al-Simt - and he has companionship (suhba) - from Salman al-Farisi, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "A day and a night of ribat is better than a month of fasting and its night prayer. If he dies, his deed that he used to do continues for him, his provision continues for him, and he is safe from the tester." The wording of Muslim alone has already been mentioned. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1913); Sunan al-Nasa'i (3916).]]

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Samura narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ya'la al-Sulami narrated to us, Umar ibn Subayh narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr, from Makhul, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A day of ribat in the way of Allah, guarding the frontier of the Muslims, seeking reward, outside the month of Ramadan, is greater in reward than the worship of a hundred years, its fasting and its night prayer. And a day of ribat in the way of Allah, guarding the frontier of the Muslims, seeking reward, during the month of Ramadan, is superior with Allah and greater in reward - I think he said - than the worship of a thousand years, its fasting and its night prayer. If Allah, the Exalted, returns him safely to his family, there will not be recorded against him the sin of a thousand years, the good deeds will be recorded for him, and the reward of ribat will continue to be given to him until the Day of Resurrection."

This is a gharib hadith, rather munkar through this route, and Umar ibn Subayh is accused (muttaham). [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (2768).]]

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Isa ibn Yunus al-Ramli narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Shapur narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Khalid ibn Abi Tawil, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Guarding one night in the cause of Allah is better than the fasting and standing in prayer of a man among his family for a thousand years: the year is three hundred and sixty days, and the day is like a thousand years."

This is also a strange (gharib) hadith. Sa'id ibn Khalid is weakened by Abu Zur'ah and other imams. Al-Uqayli said: "None follows him in his narration." Ibn Hibban said: "It is not permissible to use him as proof." Al-Hakim said: "He narrated false (mawdu') hadiths from Anas."

Another hadith: Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad informed us, from Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Za'idah, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on the guard of the guards."

In it there is a break (inqita') between Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and Uqbah ibn Amir, for he did not meet him. And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Abu Dawud said: Abu Tawbah narrated to us, Mu'awiyah narrated to us—meaning Ibn Salam—from Zayd—meaning Ibn Salam—that he heard Abu Salam say: al-Sulami narrated to me that Sahl ibn al-Hanzaliyyah narrated to him that they travelled with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn, and they travelled until evening. The Prayer was due with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a horseman came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I went ahead of you until I climbed the mountain of such and such, and there I saw Hawazin, all of them, with their women, camels and sheep, gathered at Hunayn." The Prophet (ﷺ) smiled and said: "That will be the spoils of the Muslims tomorrow, if Allah wills." Then he said: "Who will guard us tonight?" Anas ibn Abi Martha said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Then mount." So he mounted his horse and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Go to the head of this pass until you are at its top, and let no one surprise us from your direction tonight." When we woke in the morning, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to his place of prayer, prayed two rak'ahs, then said: "Did you sense your horseman?" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, we did not sense him." The iqamah for the prayer was called, and the Prophet (ﷺ), while praying, kept turning towards the pass until he finished his prayer, then said: "Rejoice, for your horseman has come." We began looking through the gaps of the trees in the pass, and there he was, coming, until he stood before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I went on until I was at the top of this pass, where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had commanded me. When I woke, I looked over both passes and saw no one." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Did you descend during the night?" He said: "No, except to pray or to relieve myself." He said to him: "You have earned it (awjabta), so there is no harm for you if you do not work after this."

al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir al-Harrani, from Abu Tawbah, who is al-Rabi' ibn Nafi', with this chain.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh narrated to us: I heard Muhammad ibn Shumayr al-Ru'ayni say: I heard Abu Amir al-Tujibi say. Imam Ahmad said: Others than Zayd said: Abu Ali al-Janbi said: I heard Abu Rayhanah say: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a campaign, and one night we came to a height and spent the night on it. A severe cold struck us, until I saw people digging a hole in the ground, entering it, and placing the shield over it—meaning the shield." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw this among the people, he called out: "Who will guard us this night, so that I may invoke a supplication for him that will be of merit for him?" A man from the Ansar said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Come near." He came near. He said: "Who are you?" The Ansari named himself to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began the supplication and made it lengthy. Abu Rayhanah said: "When I heard what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had prayed for, I said: 'I am another man.' He said: 'Come near.' I came near. He said: 'Who are you?' I said: 'I am Abu Rayhanah.' He prayed a supplication less than what he had prayed for the Ansari, then said: 'The Fire is forbidden to an eye that wept—or cried—out of fear of Allah, and the Fire is forbidden to an eye that stayed awake in the cause of Allah.'"

al-Nasa'i narrated from it: "The Fire is forbidden..." to the end, from Isma ibn al-Fadl, from Zayd ibn al-Hubab with it, and from al-Harith ibn Miskin, from Ibn Wahb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh, with it, and more completely; and in both narrations he said: "from Abu Ali al-Janbi."

Another hadith: al-Tirmidhi said: Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us, Bishr ibn Umar narrated to us, Shu'ayb ibn Ruzayq Abu Shaybah narrated to us, Ata al-Khurasani narrated to us, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Two eyes will not be touched by the Fire: an eye that wept out of fear of Allah, and an eye that stayed awake guarding in the cause of Allah."

Then he said: "Hasan gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Shu'ayb ibn Ruzayq." He said: "And in the chapter there is also a narration from Uthman and Abu Rayhanah." I say: these have already passed, and praise be to Allah.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, from Zabban, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh, from his father Mu'adh ibn Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever guards behind the Muslims in the cause of Allah, voluntarily, not for a wage from a ruler, will not see the Fire with his eyes except as the fulfilment of the oath, for Allah says: 'And there is none of you but will pass over it' (Maryam 19:71)."

Ahmad alone narrated it (may Allah have mercy on him).

Another hadith: al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Wretched is the slave of the dinar, the slave of the dirham, and the slave of the velvet garment: if he is given, he is pleased, and if he is not given, he is displeased. Wretched and failing is he; and if he is pricked with a thorn, may he not find its removal. Blessed is the servant who takes hold of the bridle of his horse in the cause of Allah, his hair disheveled, his feet dusty: if he is in the guard, he is in the guard, and if he is in the rear, he is in the rear; if he asks permission, it is not granted, and if he intercedes, it is not accepted."

This is what has been easily presented of the hadiths related to this topic, and praise be to Allah for His abundant blessings, through the succession of years and days.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah al-Madani narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Abu Ubaydah, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioning to him gatherings of the Romans and what he feared from them. Umar wrote back to him: "To proceed: whenever a believing servant is struck by a hardship, Allah will bring relief after it, and indeed one hardship will never overcome two ease. Allah the Exalted says in His Book: 'O you who believe, endure and outlast, and stand guard, and fear Allah, that you may succeed' (Al 'Imran 3:200)."

Ibn Asakir, in the biography of Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, narrated through the chain of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi Sukaynah, who said: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak dictated these verses to me at Tarsus, when I bade him farewell for departure, and he recited them with me to al-Fudayl ibn Iyad in the year 170 AH; and in another narration, the year 177 AH:

O worshipper of the two Harams, if you saw us, you would know that you are playing in worship.
Whoever stains his cheek with his tears, our throats are stained with our blood.
Or whoever tires his horse in vanity, our horses tire on the morning of battle.
The fragrance of musk is for you, and we have our fragrance: the blaze of hooves and the best dust.
There has come to us from the speech of our Prophet a saying, true and sincere, that does not lie:
It is not equal—the dust of Allah's horses in the nostril of a man, and the smoke of a blazing fire.
This is the Book of Allah speaking among us: the martyr is not dead, and it does not lie.

He said: So I met al-Fudayl ibn Iyad with his book in the Masjid al-Haram, and when he read it, his eyes shed tears, and he said: "Abu Abd al-Rahman has spoken the truth, and advised me." Then he said: "Are you one who writes down hadith?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then write this hadith in return for your carrying Abu Abd al-Rahman's book to us." Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad dictated to me: Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me a deed by which I may attain the reward of the warriors in the cause of Allah." He said: "Can you pray without slackening and fast without breaking your fast?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am too weak to be able to do that." The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if you could do that, you would not reach the warriors in the cause of Allah. Do you not know that the warrior's horse prances on its tether and good deeds are recorded for him for that?"

Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, meaning: in all your affairs and conditions, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, when he sent him to Yemen: "Fear Allah wherever you are, follow an evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and treat people with good character."

﴿That you may succeed﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Sakhr informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: that he used to say concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And fear Allah that you may succeed﴾: "And fear Allah regarding what is between me and you, that you may succeed tomorrow when you meet me."

End of the tafsir of Surat Al 'Imran. Praise and blessings are Allah's, and we ask Him for death upon the Book and the Sunnah.
